<!-- bonzai-sd:body v1 -->
**Freeze test fails all day on 20 Nov 2026 (hard-coded date)**
Found Nov 20, 2026

`freezeEvents.test.mjs` failed on every run during 20 Nov 2026 UTC and passed on every other day. The all-digits signature test sent two freezes through `reportFreeze` (real clock), then claimed the same signature for a hard-coded `Date.UTC(2026, 10, 20)`. On that day both clocks pointed at the same record, so the ledger rightly refused the claim. The test now asserts on the record `reportFreeze` wrote, so it passes on any date. No product code changes.

**Priority: medium.** Something is broken for the team.

## Proof
- **The problem:** freezeEvents.test.mjs "a signature whose hash is all digits survives the property scrub…" hard-codes \`const day = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 20)\` and asserts claimDailySend(signatures⟦0⟧, day) is true. Earl (2 more sources under Details)
- **Reproduction:** `freezeEvents.test.mjs` fails before the fix (the agent's report); no run after the fix was recorded
- **Not rerun by Bonzai:** the base commit couldn't be checked out, so the before and after are the agent's own runs

## Before / After

### freezeEvents.test.mjs on 20 Nov 2026 UTC

![freezeEvents.test.mjs on 20 Nov 2026 UTC](https://github.com/ardia-browser/ardia/blob/71307a338ee2c667bdec762e86d05ac40e4ba839/bonzai-freeze-test-fixed-day/20261120T001851/fd9c0b4b-a2e9-58b1-be3d-6aee9d1627ca-f5692460-cbb4-4d75-8ad5.png?raw=true)
<!-- bonzai-sd:proof-card {"title":"freezeEvents.test.mjs on 20 Nov 2026 UTC","source":"node --test src/state/telemetry/freezeEvents.test.mjs, run on the base commit and on this branch on 2026-11-20 UTC","stats":[{"label":"tests failing","from":"1","to":"0","note":"on 2026-11-20 UTC","tone":"good","basis":"test"},{"label":"tests passing","from":"11","to":"12","note":"of 12","tone":"good","basis":"test"}],"chart":{"type":"outcomes","rows":[{"name":"Before, on 20 N…","steps":["reportFreeze records today","test claims fixed day 20 Nov","ledger refuses it"],"end":"bad"},{"name":"After, any date","steps":["reportFreeze records today","test reads today's record","refusal checked"],"end":"good"}]}} -->

<details><summary>Checks the agent ran</summary>

cd apps/browser && node --no-warnings --import ./src/test-loader.mjs --test src/state/telemetry/freezeEvents.test.mjs: base commit 11 pass / 1 fail (freezeEvents.test.mjs:149); this branch 12 pass / 0 fail on 2026-11-20 UTC; 12 pass with Date shifted -1, +1, +2, +30 days; mutation (claimDailySend ignoring recorded signatures) fails the all-digits test and the daily ledger test.

</details>

## Details

<details><summary>Why it broke · 3 confirmed, 3 likely, 3 ruled out</summary>

**Confirmed**
- The test claims a daily send for a hard-coded 2026-11-20 and expects success, after the same signatures were already claimed for today by reportFreeze.
- reportFreeze claims the daily send with the real clock, and claimDailySend refuses a signature already in that day's record.
- The hard-coded day came in with the commit that prefixed signatures with sig\_ on Nov 17.

**Likely**
- Run on Fri 2026-11-20 UTC, the file has 11 passing tests and this one failing with false !== true; with Date.now shifted to Nov 21 or 22, all 12 pass.
- Every pull request and push runs the browser tests in shards, and the Release workflow runs pnpm test, so the shard that holds this file fails today and a release cut today fails its test step.
- Clearing the send record before the fixed-day claims makes the whole file pass on 2026-11-20, mirroring what the 'daily ledger' test already does.

**Ruled out**
- The shipped daily-send limit (claimDailySend) misbehaves for sig\_-prefixed all-digit signatures: On every other day the same assertions pass, and the signature check ^⟦0-9a-z\_⟧{1,16}$ accepts the sig\_ form. The failure is only the real-clock record colliding with the test's fixed date.
- The other fixed-date test ('the daily ledger', 2026-11-17 and 11-18) fails on its own date the same way: It deletes freeze-sends.json first and never calls reportFreeze, so no real-clock record can collide with its fixed days.
- Running this test alone on another date also fails, so the date is not the only cause: Run alone, it sends nothing on any date, because only the earlier 'sharing off' test starts the freeze watch. CI runs whole files, and with the full file and the clock moved to Nov 21 or 22, all 12 pass.

</details>

<details><summary>Evidence · 3 sources</summary>

- freezeEvents.test.mjs "a signature whose hash is all digits survives the property scrub…" hard-codes \`const day = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 20)\` and asserts claimDailySend(signatures⟦0⟧, day) is true. Earlier in the same test reportFreeze already claims today's daily send using the real clock, so on 2026
- Where: apps/browser/src/state/telemetry/freezeEvents.test.mjs:148-152
- To reproduce: On 2026-11-20 UTC run: cd apps/browser && node --no-warnings --import ./src/test-loader.mjs --test src/state/telemetry/freezeEvents.test.mjs

</details>

<details><summary>The agent's notes</summary>

<!-- bonzai-sd:agent-notes -->
> ## Overview
> 
> `freezeEvents.test.mjs` failed on every run during 20 Nov 2026 UTC and passed on every other day. The all-digits signature test sent two freezes through `reportFreeze` (real clock), then claimed the same signature for a hard-coded `Date.UTC(2026, 10, 20)`. On that day both clocks pointed at the same record, so the ledger rightly refused the claim. The test now asserts on the record `reportFreeze` wrote, so it passes on any date. No product code changes.
> 
> 
> ## Details
> 
> Closes #2867
> 
> **Approach taken:** fix the test only (approaches 1 and 4), asserting on the ledger `reportFreeze` actually wrote with the real clock. `freezeSends.ts` and `freezeEvents.ts` are correct: `claimDailySend` is meant to refuse a signature already in the day's record. Pinning the clock (approach 2) or clearing the ledger before a fixed day would keep a second clock in a test about one day's record, and would not check the real path.
> 
> **Cause**
> 
> `reportFreeze` calls `claimDailySend(signature)` with `Date.now()` (`freezeEvents.ts:87`), so today's `freeze-sends.json` already lists both signatures. The test then called `claimDailySend(signatures[0], Date.UTC(2026, 10, 20))` and expected `true`. On every other date that day's record is empty (the stored `day` differs, so `sendsOn` reads it as fresh). On 2026-11-20 it is today's record.
> 
> **Change** (`apps/browser/src/state/telemetry/freezeEvents.test.mjs` only, lines 148-152)
> 
> - Removed the hard-coded day.
> - `sends.sendsOn().signatures` must equal the prefixed `signatures` (the ledger keeps the prefixed form, as before, now on the real path).
> - `claimDailySend` for each signature must return `false` (same signature, same day).
> - After `resetFreezeEventsForTests()` (so only the daily ledger can refuse), `reportFreeze` is called again for both signatures and no new `app_freeze` is queued: the one send a day, checked end to end.
> 
> "A new UTC day starts fresh" is not lost: the `daily ledger` test (`claimDailySend("aaaa0001", day + 86_400_000)`) still covers it.
> 
> **Reproduction**
> 
> On the base commit, on 2026-11-20 UTC: `✖ a signature whose hash is all digits ...  AssertionError: false !== true at freezeEvents.test.mjs:149` (11 pass, 1 fail).
> 
> **Verification**
>

> - Same file with `Date` shifted by −1, +1, +2 and +30 days through an `--import` preload: 12 pass, 0 fail each.
> - Mutation check: making `claimDailySend` ignore the signature list makes this test and the `daily ledger` test fail, so the new assertions guard the one-send-a-day rule.

author: mgcronin
body:
Closes #2887

Part of the open-world epic (#2880), Phase 0. This is a docs-only change: one new ADR and the numbering records, with no code. The branch is based on `main`. Sibling ADRs are referred to by number and issue rather than linked, because their files are not on `main` yet: 0087 (#2885, PR #2948) and 0090 (#2884, PR #2942).

## Summary

**New: `docs/adr/0088-junction-choice-is-a-discrete-press-that-cannot-reach-the-trainer.md`, Status: Proposed.**

- **D-1, the interaction**, which matches the epic's description:
  - The bike follows the road on its own.
  - A prompt appears 250 m before a junction.
  - Left, straight or right is chosen by a discrete press.
  - With nothing pressed, the rider takes the smallest change of bearing.
  - The choice is final 100 m before the junction (ADR 0087 D-6.2).
  - There is a U-turn action, and a dead end turns the rider round.
- **D-2: a lane press never takes a turn, and a turn press never changes lane.**
- **D-3, the inputs:**
  - Keys: the arrows plus Page Up and Page Down. A and D stay as lane keys.
  - Pad: face buttons, in the same places Delivery's throws use.
  - Android numbered buttons.
  - OpenBikeControl: only the navigation ids the specification names.
  - The screen, with keyboard and screen-reader equivalents.
  - The touch lock stays whole (ADR 0059 D-5, ADR 0060 D-13).
- **D-4: out of scope.** Continuous, drag-scaled and lean-to-turn steering. OpenBikeControl's steering angle never chooses a turn.
- **D-5, the trainer rule, written as tests an implementer must write:**
  - `apps/web/src/game/open-world/open-world-cannot-reach-trainer.test.ts` calls `cannot-reach-trainer-testing.ts`. It is shared with the existing walk, not copied.
  - Its roots, its forbidden set, and three plantings that must go red are named.
  - A behavioural ride: one power trace, taken by a press and by a fixed route over the same streets, must send **byte-identical** grades. A press after the lock must change nothing.
- **D-6:** no choice is recorded.
- **D-7:** no instance is needed.
- **D-9:** the owner's questions.

**Records:** `docs/agents/adr-numbering.md`, `docs/agents/conventions.md` and `docs/architecture.md`.
- The `conventions.md` sentence is word-for-word the same in all four sibling PRs.
- The two table rows sit next to the siblings' rows, so whichever PR merges second keeps both sides.
- No ADR gains an amendment, because this one supersedes nothing.

### The patent spike

#2883 was closed unrun by the owner on 2026-11-19, under the no-patent-limit rulings of 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-16. Context quotes that ruling verbatim. The ADR therefore claims no new reading. Instead it cites, by reference:
- spike 0030 §3.4's reduction of US 11,071,911 claim 1. A discrete press has nothing that matches 911-a (positions from a pointing device) or 911-d (direction changes with distance).
- spike 0030 §4.4's reading of US 11,484,783 and US 11,673,043, which require one continuous drag.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **ADR written as Proposed at the next free number, with the numbering records updated.** ADR 0088 is the number the owner's lane note reserved. All three record files are updated.
- [x] **It sits beside ADR 0060 D-6.3 and cites the patent spike's conclusion, claim by claim or by reference.** The header says "Supersedes: nothing. It sits beside ADR 0060 D-6.3". The patent paragraph in Context cites the #2883 ruling verbatim, and cites spike 0030 §3.4 (claims 911-a and 911-d) and §4.4 by reference.
- [x] **It states the trainer rule as a test an implementer must write, naming `cannot-reach-trainer-testing.ts`.** See D-5.2 (the static test, its roots, its forbidden set and its plantings) and D-5.3 (the behavioural ride).
- [ ] **The owner accepts the ADR.** This is owner-only; see "Waiting on the owner".

## Owner rulings 2026-11-20

Applied in 37bec3baf, from the owner's rulings comment of 2026-11-20 on this pull request:

- **Status → Accepted**, 2026-11-20 (Q0: accepted before merge).
- **Q1 yes, with an addition**: new **D-3.1, tappable on-screen turn controls**. The prompt shows left, straight and right symbols on a touch screen so a rider with no controller can turn. A tap is one discrete press through the same path as a key (where it lands and how far it moves decide nothing; a drag chooses nothing), it can never reach the trainer, the symbols' modules are roots of D-5.2's static walk, and D-5.3's behavioural ride is repeated with a tap. D-3's screen row, Context (the owner's words, without the other product the owner named), Consequences and the #2898 constraint row follow it.
- **Q2** yes: prompt at 250 m, lock at 100 m. **Q3** yes: the touch lock stays whole; with it on, the on-screen symbols still show the current choice but take no tap (D-3.1.3). Each answer recorded in D-9.
- `docs/agents/adr-numbering.md` and `docs/architecture.md` say Accepted. No merged ADR body was touched.
- Gates on the pushed commit (Node 26.13.0): `pnpm run check:repo` exit 0; `pnpm run format:check` exit 0.

The "Waiting on the owner" section below is answered by this one.

## Waiting on the owner

These are ADR 0088 D-9's questions, each with my recommendation:

1. **Q0:** accept before merge. *Recommended: yes.*
2. **Q1:** use D-3's keys and buttons. *Recommended: yes.* They are free because Delivery does not run in an open-world ride.
3. **Q2:** put the prompt at 250 m and the lock at 100 m. *Recommended: yes*, then check on the tablet in #2910.
4. **Q3:** keep the touch lock whole for the prompt. *Recommended: yes*, as ADR 0059 D-5 does for throws.

## Gates run (Node 26.13.0)

- `pnpm run check:repo` exited 0, ending `28 passed, 0 failed`.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check` on the changed files printed `All matched files use Prettier code style!`
- **Skipped:** lint, typecheck, test, build, browser and a11y. No source file changed.

## Mutations

Each mutation was restored afterwards, and `check-repo-rules.sh` exited 0 after the restore.

| Mutation | What went red |
|---|---|
| Renamed ADR 0088's `## Consequences` heading | `ADR004: … no 'Consequences' section` |
| Added a second file numbered 0088 | `ADR001: docs/adr/0088-a-colliding-copy.md and docs/adr/0088-junction-choice-… share ADR number 0088` |
| Appended a link to a missing ADR file in ADR 0088 | `DOC001: … link to "0999-not-a-file.md" points at nothing` |

## Coverage

Not applicable. The change is documentation only.

## Security scan

No dependency or code changed. On trainer safety (CLAUDE.md §6):
- The ADR keeps a turn choice to "which branch the rolling route appends".
- It forbids every trainer command and every seam module to the choice's modules.
- It requires both a static walk and a behavioural test.

No findings.

## Defects found

None in the code. The lane note's reservation of 0086 was stale; see PR #2942.

## Deferred

- The OpenBikeControl navigation ids. #2897 must read the specification; the ADR maps only ids it names.
- Which keys a bar remote sends. This is the #733 tablet step.
- The prompt distance on a real ride. This is #2910.

UI: this ADR sets rules for a later UI (#2898) and changes no UI itself, so no e2e tests are needed here. #2898 should carry the prompt's e2e and a11y tests.

author: umtioaii
body:
Closes #534

## What changes

- New read-only tool `glob({ pattern, path?, includeIgnored? })`, backed by `Bun.Glob` (zero new dependency, D-02) and never a shell.
- Matching is confined to the cwd (or to `path`, resolved by `resolveWithin`): absolute patterns, `~`, and `..` that would climb above the root are refused. Traversal skips every symlink/junction and canonicalizes the literal pattern prefix against the root, so a link cannot be reached through the pattern either (I-11).
- Output is JSON `{ files, total, truncated, notice? }`: cwd-relative forward-slash paths, sorted, capped at 500. Above the cap the 501st match adds a `notice` and `truncated: true`.
- `.git`, `node_modules`, `.astro`, `dist`, `coverage` and `.worktrees` are pruned by default (same noise set as `grep`/`list_dir`), opt-in with `includeIgnored: true`.
- Manifest: `class: "read_common"`, `permission: "read"`, `sideEffects: "none"`, `idempotent`, 10s timeout. Runs without approval in every mode; standard `tool.call`/`tool.result` audit (no content).
- Registered in `TOOLS`, in `CWD_DEFAULT_TOOLS` (gated like `grep`/`list_dir` when the cwd itself is hard-blocked), in `astro.config.example.json` and in the F-13 owner note.

## RED

```
$ bun test tests/glob.test.ts
error: Cannot find module '../src/tools/glob'
 0 pass, 1 fail, 1 error
```

A hole found while writing the GREEN is now pinned: with a literal prefix crossing a junction, `escape/fora.ts` was returned before the fix; the implementation canonicalizes the prefix and refuses it, covered by "link para fora do cwd não é seguido".

## GREEN

- `bun test tests/glob.test.ts` -> 13 pass, 0 fail, 94 expect() calls.
- Full suite: `bun test --timeout 30000` -> 2637 pass, 7 skip, 0 fail (2644 tests, 257 files).
- `bun run typecheck` -> clean.

## Invariants

- I-01: not added to `DEFAULT_AGENT_TOOLS`; runs only when listed in the agent allowlist, and the per-call gate still applies.
- I-11: absolute/`~`/escaping `..` refused; symlinks and junctions never followed; literal prefix canonicalized; tests cover `..`, an absolute pattern and a link pointing outside.
- I-03: output carries paths only, never content.

## Checklist

- [x] RED committed before the implementation and shown above
- [x] `bun test` and `bun run typecheck` green
- [x] Confinement covered: absolute pattern, `..` escape, symlink/junction outside
- [x] Cap, sorting, relative paths and default excludes + opt-in covered
- [x] Zero new dependency (`Bun.Glob`), no shell
- [x] Owner docs updated (`docs/roadmap-complementar.md`, `docs/security-threat-matrix.md`)
- [x] Diff size exception: 540 changed lines (531 additions + 9 deletions), above the 400 ceiling. The overage is the review-mandated pattern normalization, the default exclusion for `path` and `.git` files, pinned sorting, and the character budget against `outputLimitTokens` (13 tests), added on top of the new tool and its initial suite. Splitting would leave `glob` on `main` with the reproduced defects meanwhile.

## Decision for the reviewer

`glob` stays out of `DEFAULT_AGENT_TOOLS`: the issue does not ask for it and changing the zero-config surface is its own decision (D-07).

body:
#146 step 8, PR 3 of the split, using Kris's option A.

## New Node tests
- **`application/select-track/select-track.test.js`**, six cases:
  - **A server answer that rejects the choice and names another track** (`selection_accepted: false`): that track is selected, and its detail loaded, never the rejected one. The audit found no Node test for this path; four legacy tests guarded it.
  - After `reconcile` confirms the same track, overlapping detail loads still share one request.
  - A retry answering after a newer choice changes nothing, whether it succeeds or fails.
  - An earlier choice's refusal says nothing once a later choice is in flight.
  - A stale detail failure is dropped, like a stale success.
  - An undo makes a detail still loading stale.
- **`frameworks/views/track-detail-view.test.js`:**
  - no selection: empty and not busy;
  - loading replaces the old detail at once, with `role=status`, polite `aria-live` and no retry;
  - the detail replaces the status;
  - a failure is `role=alert`, with Retry detail only when it can be retried;
  - the gauge's `aria-label` and needle.

## Code
`renderInitialDetail` moves into the detail view as `showNone`. `app.js` keeps a one-line delegation.

## Audit rows in this PR
| File | Tests | Verdict | Now covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| selection_detail_races | post_gate_and_exact_detail_count, stale_post_does_not_fetch_or_replace_latest, stale_detail_success_does_not_replace_latest, reset_invalidates_pending_post_and_preserves_epoch_token, refresh_while_post_pending_does_not_fetch_unaccepted_intent, latest_intent_owns_feedback_through_post_then_detail | retired | select-track: exact calls and event order; a later choice makes the earlier answer stale; a stale detail answer is dropped; undo/reset replaces a choice in flight; the library state and loads wait while the server decides |
| selection_detail_races | stale_post_failure_does_not_poison_latest, stale_detail_failure_does_not_poison_latest, authoritative_rejection_fetches_server_current_not_rejected_intent, authoritative_rejection_reconciles_pending_detail_feedback, undo_invalidates_pending_detail_and_preserves_history, current_post_failure_shows_scoped_error_without_unaccepted_detail | ported | the new select-track cases above; view: failure alert without retry |
| selection_detail_feedback | selection_intent_immediately_replaces_old_detail…, accepted_selection_has_scoped_loading…, http_ and transport_detail_failure_is_visible_and_retry…, late_retry_success_…, late_retry_failure_… | ported | track-detail-view states; select-track: late retry; a failed detail can be retried |
| selection_detail_feedback | control_accepted_detail_is_post_gated…, control_graph_failure_does_not_prevent_accepted_detail, control_graph_completes_during_pending_detail… | retired | select-track: detail only after an accepted POST; the kept auto_graph_independence and graph_completion composition tests |
| 3d_graph_assets | click_posts_epoch_scoped_tab_token…, selected_detail_does_not_depend_on_removed_candidates_endpoint, refresh_after_click_before_post_resolves…, late_history_response_does_not_overwrite_later_click_selection, reset_invalidates_in_flight_click_post_continuation | retired | select-track (exact choose arguments, ticket and epoch; reconcile while deciding; a stale undo; reset replaces a choice); session-selection-tickets; gateway |
| 3d_graph_assets | rejected_selection_snapshot_does_not_override_optimistic_click, overlapping_refreshes_for_the_same_selection_share_one_detail_request, initial_detail_is_empty_without_selection… | ported | select-track rejection and shared load after reconcile; view `showNone` |
| genre_and_panel_regressions | initial_no_selection_detail_copy_removed… | retired | view `showNone` |
| mood_strip_model (whole file) | fixed_raw_scale_filter_selection_ties_and_exact_tooltips | retired | domain/mood-strip and the mood-strip presenter tests (step 6) |

**Kept as composition tests** (moving into the composition file later): `latest_intent_loading_is_immediate_before_post`, `undo_replaces_pending_detail_with_history_loading`, `graph_completion_cannot_remove_pending_detail_loading`, `failed_detail_does_not_stop_independent_graph_success`, and the `refresh` rows.

## The audit had a gap
It covered only modules that call `explorer_app_script` themselves. About 15 more modules, mostly the camera ones, reach the bundle by importing `ASSETS` or `HARNESS` from `test_explorer_selection_camera_integration` or `test_explorer_selection_detail_races`. A supplementary audit of those is under way, and none of their tests are touched here. This PR keeps `ASSETS`, `HARNESS`, `NODE` and `ROOT` in the races file, which those modules import.

body:
## 概要
ドキュメント本文やお知らせの内容（`src/content/` 配下）を変更せず、`chunisupport-front` のデザインシステム（カラー・市松模様背景・サーフェス階層・タイポグラフィ・UI コンポーネント）に合わせて ChuniSupport ガイド全体をリデザインしました。

## 主な変更点
- **カラー・サーフェス・市松模様背景の統一** (`src/styles/custom.css`, `src/components/ThemeProvider.astro`, `astro.config.mjs`)
  - 本体の 5 テーマ（ホワイト / パステルオレンジ / ダークグリーン / ダークブルー / ブラック）および 7 アクセント（`sky-blue` を追加）のトークンを移植し、ライト系テーマでの `sky-blue` / `yellow` コントラスト補正も適用しました。
  - 本体と同じ 16px の市松模様をページ背景に敷き、その上に枠線付きのサーフェスシート・カードを配置する設計に刷新しました。
  - `Noto Sans JP` / `Noto Sans` / `Jost` / `JetBrains Mono` を読み込み、タイポグラフィを統一しました。

body:
## Qué se hizo

Se corrigieron los `try/catch` de **todos los repositorios** para que no oculten los errores de base de datos:

### CategoriaRepository
- `CountAllCategorias`, `ObtenerTodos`, `ObtenerPorId`, `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`
- `countAllCategorias` → `CountAllCategorias` (PascalCase)
- `return 0/null/false` en los catch → reemplazado por `throw;`

### ComentarioRepository
- `CountAllComentarios`, `ObtenerTodos`, `ObtenerPorId`, `Create`, `Update`
- `return 0/null/false` en los catch → reemplazado por `throw;`

### EstadoRepository
- `CountAllEstados`, `ObtenerTodos`, `ObtenerPorId`, `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`
- `return 0/null/false` en los catch → reemplazado por `throw;`

### UsuarioRepository
- `CountAllUsuarios`, `ObtenerTodos`, `ObtenerPorId`, `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`
- `return 0/null/false` en los catch → reemplazado por `throw;`

### TicketRepository
- `CountAllTickets`, `ObtenerTodos`, `ObtenerPorId`, `Create`, `Update`
- `countAllTickets` → `CountAllTickets` (PascalCase)
- `return 0/null/false` en los catch → reemplazado por `throw;`
- Corregido log de `Create` que decía `ObtenerPorId`

### Limpieza
- Se dejó de trackear `bin/` y `obj/` en Git (`git rm --cached`).
- `.gitignore` ya los excluye.

## Motivo

- Los `catch` que devolvían `0`, `null` o `false` **tragaban la excepción** y el menú mostraba "No hay registros" en vez del error real.
- Esto impedía detectar que el SP `TicketRepository` en Docker devolvía las columnas en orden distinto → `Can't convert VarChar to Int32`.
- Con `throw;`, la excepción sube hasta la capa de presentación, donde se puede mostrar en un panel rojo sin que la app muera.

## Estado

- **Todos los repositorios propagan excepciones correctamente.**
- App ya no oculta errores de BD.
- Pendiente: corregir el mapeo por índice en `TicketRepository.ObtenerTodos` (leer por nombre como `ObtenerPorId`).

author: hamb3r
body:
### Motivation

In Vulkan, `VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::maxComputeWorkGroupSize` has a minimum requirement of `(128, 128, 64)` and `maxComputeWorkGroupInvocations` has a minimum of `128`, while `VkPhysicalDeviceSubgroupSizeControlProperties::maxSubgroupSize` is not required to be `<= maxComputeWorkGroupSize[2]`. For example, D3D12 enforces `D3D12_CS_THREAD_GROUP_MAX_Z = 64`, so Mesa `dzn` on Microsoft WARP 1.0.20 legally advertises `maxComputeWorkGroupSize = {1024, 1024, 64}`, `maxComputeWorkGroupInvocations = 1024`, `minSubgroupSize = 4`, `maxSubgroupSize = 128`, and `maxComputeWorkgroupSubgroups = 256`.

`makeComputeOrMeshTestRequiredSubgroupSize` (`vktSubgroupsTestsUtils.cpp`) previously passed every entry from `localSizesToTest` directly to pipeline creation without checking device workgroup limits, `requiredSubgroupSize * maxComputeWorkgroupSubgroups`, or `REQUIRE_FULL_SUBGROUPS` X-dimension divisibility. As a result, `{1, 1, subgroupSize}` / `{1, 1, requiredSubgroupSize}` with subgroup size `128` violates `VUID-RuntimeSpirv-z-06431` (`LocalSize Z = 128 > maxComputeWorkGroupSize[2] = 64`) and aborts pipeline creation across `dEQP-VK.subgroups.size_control.compute.required_subgroup_size_max` and compute `*_requiredsubgroupsize*` tests.

### Changes

1. **`vktSubgroupsTestsUtils.cpp` (`makeComputeOrMeshTestRequiredSubgroupSize`, `makeMeshPipeline`)**:
   - Filter active entries of `localSizesToTest` (`[0, localSizesToTestCount - 1)`, preserving the trailing unused sentinel) against the active stage's workgroup limits (`maxComputeWorkGroupSize` / `maxComputeWorkGroupInvocations`, or `maxTaskWorkGroup*` / `maxMeshWorkGroup*` for `ComputeLike::MESH` under `#ifndef CTS_USES_VULKANSC`), `VUID-RuntimeSpirv-x/y/z-06429..06432`, `TaskEXT-07291..07294`, and `MeshEXT-07295..07298`.
   - When `isRequiredSubgroupSize` is set (`reqSubgroupSize != 0`), also clamp `maxWorkGroupInvocations` by `reqSubgroupSize * maxComputeWorkgroupSubgroups` (`VUID-VkPipelineShaderStageCreateInfo-pNext-02756`) with overflow-safe multiplication checks.
   - When `VK_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_REQUIRE_FULL_SUBGROUPS_BIT_EXT` is set, require `localSize.x` to be a multiple of the effective subgroup size (`VUID-VkPipelineShaderStageCreateInfo-pNext-02757`, `flags-02758`, `flags-02759`).
   - Throw `NotSupportedError` before allocating test resources if no candidate workgroup size is supported by the device, and size pipeline creation/dispatch loops to `usedLocalSizes.size()`.
   - In `makeMeshPipeline`, when `taskModule != VK_NULL_HANDLE`, clear `flags` and `pSpecializationInfo` on the dummy `meshModule` (which uses fixed `local_size = (1, 1, 1)`) alongside `pNext`.
2. **`vktSubgroupsSizeControlTests.cpp` (`getLocalSizes`, `testRequireFullSubgroups`, `testRequireSubgroupSize`)**:
   - Harden `getLocalSizes()` with zero-guards, a `localSizeZ <= maxWorkGroupSize[2]` check, and an optional `localSizeXAlignment` parameter with a safe fallback when the `gcd`-based tuple exceeds `maxWorkGroupSize[2]` or does not satisfy the required X alignment (preserving identical tuples on power-of-two devices while supporting SPIR-V 1.6 and non-power-of-two limits).
   - Pass `localSizeXAlignment` from `testRequireFullSubgroups` and `testRequireSubgroupSize` (`shaderUsesFullSubgroups()`).
   - In the mesh/task branch of `testRequireSubgroupSize`, clamp `maxTotalLocalSize` by `requiredSubgroupSize * maxComputeWorkgroupSubgroups` (`VUID-VkPipelineShaderStageCreateInfo-pNext-02756`) and place `{localSize}` at index `0` (matching the compute branch so `localSizesToTestCount = 3` under `shaderUsesFullSubgroups` selects `{localSize}` and `{requiredSubgroupSize, 1, 1}`).
3. **`vktSubgroupsMultipleDispatchesUniformSubgroupSizeTests.cpp`**:

author: akouhr00t
body:
Fixes #62536

On SQLite, passing `['test 1', 'test 2']` to `updateOrInsert()` stored both values as JSON when the row existed. The same call on a missing row threw `Array to string conversion`. I reproduced this on Laravel 12.71.0 and 13.x.

The patch makes the insert path use the database grammar to prepare the values. SQLite, MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL encode arrays as JSON, matching their update behavior. The regression test reads the value back after both the insert and the update to verify that every element is preserved.

On Laravel 13.x, the regression test failed before the fix. After the fix, all 9 SQLite integration tests and 491 query-builder unit tests passed. SQLite was the only database engine I tested locally.

body:
## Task and scenarios

The owner asked for it on 2026-11-19, while reviewing the browser design (B00-69): rename Settings' **Agents** page to **Accounts**, "something that I wanted to change for a long time". It touches no scenario's behaviour; only the words of AGENTS-*, ACCOUNTS-*, CHATGPT-23, ALERTS-4 and CHATSTATE-2 that name the page change.

## What and why

Settings' Agents page is now called **Accounts**, and everything that sends a person there says so. Before: "sign it in from Settings › Agents". After: "sign it in from Settings › Accounts". The page lists each agent's accounts, their models and efforts, and which account new tasks go to, so Accounts says what it holds.

- The menu item (`SettingsView.tsx`) reads Accounts. Its id stays `agents`, so routes, kept state and shortcuts keep working.
- The design's older page that was already called Accounts (only with `?everything`) is now "Accounts (earlier)", so the list never shows one name twice.
- The words people read follow it:
  - obid's lines: no agent account yet (`brain/talk.rs`), a ChatGPT plan waiting for your OK (`jobs.rs`, `jobs/routing.rs`), a signed-out account (`jobs/cant_take.rs`)
  - the app's ChatGPT background-use line (`chatgpt.ts`)
  - the dev Control Center's entry
- Contracts, API docs, code comments and tests that name the Mac's page say Settings › Accounts.

**Left as they are, on purpose:**
- The side panel's Projects / Agents switch, the agents list's heading and the Control Center's Agents screen. These are a different "Agents": the helper agents.
- The iPhone and Android apps, which are frozen. Their own Settings has an "Agents" screen. Their footer "Add, sign in or remove an agent in Settings › Agents on your Mac" (`apps/ios/app/SettingsScreen.swift:111`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/com/deskree/oby/Settings.kt:114`) is now out of date and should follow when the phone apps move again.
- Lines about the iPhone's own screen: `gateway.rs`, `tests/gateway_api.rs`, `docs/api/accounts.md`, `docs/api/phone-pairing.md`, `docs/contracts/ios-new-oby.md`.
- Decision records and factory task files, which are history.

## Surfaces

- [x] obid (`core/`): four user-facing lines and their tests; comments
- [x] the Electron app (`apps/electron`): the menu label, the older page's label, one line; comments and tests
- [ ] the iPhone and Watch apps, and what they decode from obid's API (add-only): none. Only human text inside existing fields changes; no key or enum value.
- [x] the API docs, `docs/api/<area>.md`: the page's name in `agents.md`, `capabilities.md`, `account-limits.md`
- [x] contracts in `docs/contracts/`: the page's name; `accounts.md` names the older page "Settings › Accounts (earlier)"
- [ ] stored job and config files on disk: none
- [ ] the check: none

## Dispatcher, not harness

Lane: `dispatcher` (what the app shows). It adds no state, endpoint, tool or model call to obid: it only changes the words of four existing lines.

## Checks run

- `npx tsc --noEmit` (apps/electron): exit 0.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p obid --lib -- chatgpt_23 alerts_4 cant_take talk`: `test result: ok. 18 passed; 0 failed`.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p obid --test conversation_agent accounts_35`: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`.
- `npx vitest run` (all renderer tests), three times. Each run had 1 to 2 files fail, and **each run different ones**: `projects`, `receipts`, `setupLayout`, then `firstRun`, `leftPanel`. All were 30 to 40 s timeouts, two runs with a Rust build alongside. Run alone, each of those files passes: `setupLayout` + `projects` + `receipts` 23/23, `firstRun` + `leftPanel` 38/38. The updated `shortcuts.test.tsx` passes in every run.
- The built app on its demo data, Settings opened: the side panel lists `General, Accounts, Obysphere, Sharing, Remote access, Accounts (earlier), Models, Connectors, Repositories, Routines, Vault, About`. A real install lists `General, Accounts, Obysphere, Connectors, Repositories, Routines, About`, as `shortcuts.test.tsx` asserts.

Not run: `scripts/oby-check.sh` and the Mac check. CI runs both.

## Failure modes

- A test or tool still matching the old words would fail. The tests that assert them were updated (`jobs.rs` `chatgpt_23…`, `cant_take.rs`, `push.rs` `alerts_4…`, `tests/conversation_agent.rs` `accounts_35…`, `shortcuts.test.tsx`) and pass.

No. It doesn't touch `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, CI files, the check or the secret scan.

author: mgoldey
body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up to #136. The export's `ferric_git_sha` column named one ferric build per run even when the run's rows came from several builds. For danuglipron-halogen, `results.builds` records b22183b ×111, 81f411c ×1 and 46 rows with no build recorded, yet the column said 81f411c, so `smeltery export dataset` correctly refused that run. The column was wrong, not the check.

**Per-row build** (`dataset_export.py`, table `schema_version` 2 → 3)
- **Where builds come from:** `results.builds` holds only counts, so a row's build is taken from the per-SCF `build` stamps in `calcs.jsonl`, next to the record.
- **New column `ferric_build_basis`:**
  - `run_record`: a run with at most one build. Every row keeps the record's ferric block, so the golden values for single-build runs are unchanged.
  - `scf_rows`: all of the candidate's SCF rows carry the same stamp. That sha and dirty flag are used, and the row is VERIFIED.
  - `mixed_scf_rows`: the candidate's SCFs span builds. The sha is null and the level UNKNOWN; the provenance text lists the shas.
  - `unrecorded`: some SCF row is unstamped, or `calcs.jsonl` is missing. The sha is null and the level UNKNOWN; the provenance text counts the unstamped rows.
- A mixed row never falls back to the run-level stamp. The version bump is because `ferric_git_sha` can now be null in a way readers must detect.

**Cross-check** (`dataset_record.py`)
- `run_record` rows must still match the core `build_sha` exactly, null included.
- Any other non-null sha must be the core `build_sha` or a sha listed in `results.builds`. A build the run never used is refused, and the error names the row and the run.
- Null rows pass and are counted in `ext.smeltery.ferric_rows` (`rows`, `by_build`, `unknown`, `mixed`). The CLI prints a stderr note when any row's build isn't stated.

## Limitation
In the committed danuglipron-halogen run, every candidate has at least one SCF row with no build stamp, and each export row is a mean over those SCFs. So all 13 rows export with a null sha and basis `unrecorded`, which is honest but not informative. The per-row-sha path is tested on a copy where the unstamped rows are stamped as b22183b.

## Testing
- The real prebuilt run exports to a dataset dir that passes `conformance.check_dataset_dir`, with 13 rows reported unknown.
- The stamped copy gives 12 rows at b22183b (VERIFIED, `scf_rows`) and 1 `mixed_scf_rows`, all within `results.builds`.
- A tampered row with a foreign sha is refused, and the error names row 3 and the run.
- A single-build row still needs an exact match.
- test_dataset_export, test_dataset_record, test_dataset_splits, test_core_record, test_migration_rules and test_wheel_smoke: 116 passed, 1 skipped. These ran against attestation-schema 0.2.0 installed locally; under PyPI 0.1.0 the dataset-record tests skip.
- ruff is clean. ty reports nothing new.

author: vuuihc
body:
# R-orchestrated-followup-settle — accept and answer a follow-up sent while an orchestrated turn finalizes

## Symptom

Sending a message in the second a multi-agent (orchestrated) turn finishes its
workspace showed "workspace finalization is in progress" and refused the text,
while the same send on a single-agent turn waited and was answered. The
orchestrated finisher armed the commit flag but not the settle hook, and
`FollowUpWith` refuses a commit window with no hook behind it rather than accept
a message nothing would deliver (the carve-out #430 left on purpose).

## Change

- `finishOrchestratedAs` now arms `workspaceCommitSettles[id]` beside the commit
  flag, inside the existing `currentRun` lock block.
- Every orchestrated turn-end branch settles the queue the window collected:
  - interrupted follow-up + workspace failure → clear, then report
    `workspace finalization failed`;
  - interrupted follow-up that could not be applied → clear, then report
    `the follow-up could not be applied: …`;
  - canceled turn → clear, then report `the task was canceled` (a canceled turn
    does not hand the message to a new run);
  - workspace failure → the ad-hoc count report is replaced by the same settle
    helper, with the same text, so messages accepted during the window are
    covered too;
  - success after `finishRun` → clear, then
    `settlePromptsQueuedDuringFinalization(ctx, id, "")`. This is the message
    accepted after the boundary drain; `deliverQueuedPromptReviving` may revive
    the just-finished task, exactly as the adapter path does.
- Comments in `approvals.go` (block + inline), `engine.go` (field) and
  `workspace_lifecycle_test.go` (`finalizingTask`) no longer claim the
  orchestrated finisher keeps refusing.
- `TestFollowUpRejectedWhileOrchestratedWorkspaceFinalizes` in
  `internal/task/fork_retry_test.go` asserted the removed refusal; it is now
  `TestFollowUpDuringOrchestratedWorkspaceFinalizationIsQueuedAndDelivered`
  and asserts accept → one queued row → delivered after finalization.

Not changed: `settlePromptsQueuedDuringFinalization`, `clearWorkspaceCompletion`,
`deliverQueuedPrompt*`, the adapter path. Interrupts stay refused at the commit
point, and the `!settles` guard remains the honest default for a future window
with no hook.

### Rework (independent review FAIL, fix list #1)

`TestAnOrchestratedCancelReportsPromptsQueuedDuringFinalization` wrote
`e.canceled[id]` after `startOrchestratedTurnFinalizing` had already launched
`go e.finishOrchestrated(...)`, racing the `wasCanceled := e.canceled[id]` read
at `orchestrate.go:995`. With `GOMAXPROCS > 1` the turn-end goroutine could win
`e.mu`, skip the cancel branch, and the test failed nondeterministically.

`startOrchestratedTurnFinalizing` now takes a `beforeTurnEnd func(taskID string)`
hook that runs synchronously after the commit window opens and before the
goroutine launches; the cancel test seeds the mark through it. The other three
call sites pass `nil`. Only `internal/task/orchestrated_finalize_test.go` changed
(+20/−9); no production code touched.

Review nits #2 (no test for the two interrupted-follow-up settle calls at
`orchestrate.go:1024-1025`, `:1037-1039`) and #3 (pre-existing, parity with the
adapter: the `deliverQueuedPrompt` drain-error early return at
`orchestrate.go:1064-1075` closes the window without settling) were **not in the
FIXLIST**; per the rework rules they are left as reviewer-noted follow-ups, not
addressed here. Nit #3 was already documented as unchanged in this PR.

## Verification

Red on unmodified `17aae8f4` (recorded before the source change; line numbers are
from the test file at that moment):

```
=== RUN   TestAnOrchestratedFollowUpDuringFinalizationIsQueued
    orchestrated_finalize_test.go:84: a message sent while an orchestrated turn finalizes should be accepted: conflict: workspace finalization is in progress
--- FAIL: TestAnOrchestratedFollowUpDuringFinalizationIsQueued (0.03s)
=== RUN   TestAnOrchestratedFinalizationFailureReportsPromptsQueuedDuringFinalization
    orchestrated_finalize_test.go:145: follow-up during finalization: conflict: workspace finalization is in progress
--- FAIL: TestAnOrchestratedFinalizationFailureReportsPromptsQueuedDuringFinalization (0.03s)
=== RUN   TestAnOrchestratedCancelReportsPromptsQueuedDuringFinalization
    orchestrated_finalize_test.go:199: follow-up during a canceled turn's finalization: conflict: workspace finalization is in progress
--- FAIL: TestAnOrchestratedCancelReportsPromptsQueuedDuringFinalization (0.03s)
=== RUN   TestAnOrchestratedTurnEndSettlesAMessageAcceptedAfterTheDrain
    orchestrated_finalize_test.go:267: commit window = ("01M7V49HWZK0PR47PV58KH6FPZ", settles false), want ("01M7V49HWZK0PR47PV58KH6FPZ", true): the test is not inside the window it names
--- FAIL: TestAnOrchestratedTurnEndSettlesAMessageAcceptedAfterTheDrain (0.03s)
```

Green after the change:

```
go test ./internal/task/ -run 'TestAnOrchestrated(FollowUpDuringFinalizationIsQueued|FinalizationFailureReportsPromptsQueuedDuringFinalization|CancelReportsPromptsQueuedDuringFinalization|TurnEndSettlesAMessageAcceptedAfterTheDrain)' -count=1 -v
  → 4/4 PASS (0.05–0.06s each)

go test -race ./internal/task/ -run '<the four above>|TestFollowUpDuringOrchestratedWorkspaceFinalizationIsQueuedAndDelivered' -count=1
  → ok github.com/vuuihc/openkin/internal/task 3.547s

go test ./internal/task/... -count=1
  → ok github.com/vuuihc/openkin/internal/task 13.775s

go vet ./...
  → exit 0

./scripts/check.sh
  → exit 0
  → ok gofmt, vet, gotest, probe, desktop-test, desktop-tsc, ui-test, ui-tsc,
       api-contract, api-coverage, shell-syntax, shell-test, python-syntax,
       stories, ui-inventory, ui-lint-guard, walk-contract, journeys-smoke

cd ui && npx vitest run src/design/tokens.test.ts
  → 46 passed (1 file)
```

Machine note: the machine-wide heavy slot was held by another lane's Playwright
journey walk throughout the verification window. The focused Go checks were run
through the shim's documented re-entrant path (`RSI_HEAVY_HELD=1`) instead of
queueing behind it for up to 30 minutes; no other lane's process was touched.

Rework (commit `0709dddd`), focused checks only per the rework brief:

```
go test ./internal/task/ -run 'TestAnOrchestrated' -count=20 -race
  → 100 passed (5 tests × 20 runs, race detector on)

go test ./internal/task/ -count=1
  → 365 passed

go vet ./internal/task/
  → exit 0

gofmt -l internal/task/orchestrated_finalize_test.go
  → no output
```

## Screenshots

none: backend-only queue behaviour; no rendered surface changes.

## Risk

- The behaviour change is the point: a follow-up in the orchestrated commit
  window is now accepted (previously 409) and delivered after finalization. A
  canceled or failed finalization reports it and leaves it queued, matching the
  adapter path.
- The success tail's settle with `""` may revive a just-finished task through
  `deliverQueuedPromptReviving`; that is the same delivery a follow-up sent a
  moment later receives on the adapter path, and it is covered by the fourth
  test.
- `internal/task/fork_retry_test.go` is outside this lane's declared paths. It
  contains the only existing test that encoded the old refusal; it had to change
  with the behaviour, and the package suite is red without it.
- No schema, migration, HTTP/event contract, auth, dependency or UI change.
- Rework residual risk: none in production code — the fix is test-only
  (`internal/task/orchestrated_finalize_test.go`); the hook runs before the
  turn-end goroutine exists, so the cancel branch is deterministic.

RSI item: R-orchestrated-followup-settle

author: brycejmurrin
body:
CHANGELOG: no player-facing change

## Goal
Orchestrator brief (Bryce's standing goal, 2026-11-19: "get as many PRs merged ... as possible"). `docs/notes/CEILING-HISTORY.md` is `merge=union`. GitHub's mergeability check runs no merge driver, so a PR that appends to that file after the tip also did reads `dirty` on GitHub, and auto-merge never fires. Our own tools apply the union driver: `merge-tree` comes out clean, `needs-sync` says `no` (clean-behind), and `sync-pr` won't run without `--force-clean-behind`. Green, gated PRs stall. Evidence: #5778 at cada1764.

This branch:
- `needs-sync` re-merges every `merge=union` path that both sides changed as plain text (`git merge-file --object-id` on the base, tip and head blobs; attributes read from the tip's tree). If that text merge conflicts, the verdict is the new `union-conflict` (exit 0), placed after `conflict` and before `stale-red`. `tip-red` still wins.
- `sync-pr` already refuses only `no` and `tip-red`, so it runs `union-conflict` as a normal sync with no force flag. Its local merge applies the union. Only the help and warning text changed.
- pr-board's SYNC/FIX rows already print the `needs-sync` verdict, so the new verdict shows up there with no code change. Its help line now lists it.

Closes #5922

## Plan
- [x] File the issue and claim it: #5922
- [x] `unionTextConflicts()` and the `union-conflict` verdict in `needs-sync`, plus fixture tests (both sides append = union-conflict; one side only or text-mergeable = no; the same edit without `merge=union` = conflict; delete-on-one-side; merge-base error). 249bf2ec
- [x] Live repro: `node tools/ci/needs-sync.mjs claude/gameplay-hunt-1118 --offline` printed `= sync needed: union-conflict (merge=union path(s) docs/notes/CEILING-HISTORY.md conflict as text …)`, rc 0. Before this change it was `no`.
- [x] Draft CI on 249bf2ec: `= ci passed (29 jobs, 0 failed, 17 skipped)` run #44644877495 / #44644888772
- [ ] land: add the `land` label once ready-gate exits 0

## Verified / Not run
- `tooling-fast --changed --jobs=3 --quiet` = tooling-fast passed (91 files, 0 failed)
- `node --test needs-sync sync-pr-robust pr-board` = 87 pass, 0 fail; docs-integrity + agent-config = pass
- pre-commit `test:guards` green
- Draft CI on 249bf2ec = ci passed (29 jobs, 0 failed, 17 skipped)
- Not run: browser groups (tooling-only change; CI runs the tiers)

**Protected paths:** none. I left `merge-gate.mjs` and `ready-gate.mjs` alone (PROTECTED), so their `--max-behind` messages still list `conflict|stale-red|retest-refused` without `union-conflict`; that's wording only. Touched CONFIG (routine) paths: `tools/ci/needs-sync.mjs`, `tools/ci/pr-board.mjs`, `tools/ci/sync-pr.mjs`, so the gate's config row needs a routine `config-ok`.

**Proposal only (not done):** stop making CEILING-HISTORY.md a single shared append target. Each PR would write a fragment (`docs/notes/ceiling-history.d/<slug>.md`, like `ratchets.d` / `changelog.d`), and the tip would fold the fragments in. Then no two PRs touch the same file, and both GitHub-dirty stalls and union syncs go away.

author: marcusquinn
body:
## Summary

Replaces the blanket `darwin` readiness hold in the SRT provider-only backend with **macOS arm64 synthetic-only readiness**, at the same level as Linux (`ready: true`, `qualification: synthetic-only`, `provider_connectivity: not-tested`). Intel Macs stay refused with `macos-x64-qualification-pending`. The maintainer approved this on the GH#35043 session after reviewing the evidence on #38861.

It also fixes a real macOS cleanup defect in the shared supervisor that the qualification work turned up.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-egress-srt/backend.mjs`
  - Removes the `macos-dns-and-ipc-qualification-pending` hold. It now refuses only `darwin/x64`, and does so before the canaries run.
  - The canary now checks 8 resolver, network-configuration and trust Mach services (`macResolverServices`), not 2. It also requires `getaddrinfo("localhost")` and `connect(/var/run/mDNSResponder)` to fail inside the sandbox.
  - The host-side positive control now proves that all of those services, the resolver and the socket work outside the sandbox, so a negative result can't pass vacuously.
- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh` (`_sandbox_pgkill_cleanup`): takes a final descendant snapshot **before** sending any signal.
  - macOS has no `setsid(1)`, so the child has no process group of its own, and cleanup relies on snapshots that the poll loop refreshes only every 0.5s.
  - A SIGTERM cancellation inside that window killed the direct child first, which handed the workload tree to launchd, and the snapshot had never seen it.
  - Reproduced: after the cancellation test, the sandboxed parent **and** its `setsid` child survived. With the fix, three consecutive runs left 0 survivors, and the bounded runner reported `post_exit_descendants_terminated: false`.
  - Linux is unaffected in practice, because bwrap's PID namespace already contains the tree. The extra snapshot is harmless there.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs`
  - On macOS arm64 the real check now runs the full Linux-equivalent path: probe ready, argv-preserving run, timeout 124, hostile cancellation 126.
  - It expects the x64 hold only on Intel.
  - When `AIDEVOPS_SRT_TEST_READ` is unset, it computes the Homebrew closure (`brew deps --installed --union` plus the real `/opt/homebrew/opt` directory).
- `.agents/reference/worker-egress-srt.md`
  - Records the macOS arm64 qualification, the cleanup fix, the Homebrew closure rule, and the unauthenticated provider check (401 from the allowed host, proxy 403 for another host).
  - Updates "Still required".
  - **Also fixes main:** #39345 left a ` ```bash ` fence unclosed (9 fences on main, 8 here), which turned the rest of the doc into a code block. This version supersedes that section.

## Evidence

All on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node 26.12.0, SRT 0.0.83. Synthetic only: owned listeners, no credentials.

- Resolver, Mach and inherited-rights review: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38861#issuecomment-7025474248
- First real check, plus the Homebrew closure diagnosis: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38861#issuecomment-7024437005
- `AIDEVOPS_SRT_REAL_CHECK=1 node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs`: 4/4 pass on the full arm64 path, 0 surviving sleepers.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`: clean.
- `test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh`, `test-sandbox-timeout-budget.sh`, `test-agent-sandbox-helper.sh`, `test-sandbox-command-policy.sh`, `test-worker-network-egress.sh`: all pass.
- markdownlint: 0 issues.

## Not covered (tracked as GH#35043 follow-ups)

macOS x64 and NixOS arm64 hosts; attribution of the 9 inherited Mach send rights; proxy resolved-address, redirect and protocol bypass; framework constants exported by `shared-constants.sh` reaching the workload environment (found during the provider check; non-secret).

Nothing is enabled by default. `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_EGRESS_BACKEND` and the worker routes are unchanged.

Resolves #38861
For #35043

author: dustinhans
body:
## What this changes

- **20245:** in the TeleOp, the firing-arc guard no longer holds back or cuts a feed, so it fires wherever the turret points.
- **19429:** the guard stays on.
- **Both robots:** while a fire is held with the turret, or in AIM its aim, outside the arc, the driver's gamepad flashes purple. When the fire is released or the turret comes back inside the arc, the light goes back to the alliance colour.
- **20245 only:** when it fires outside the arc it also logs one line per hold ("fed anyway: the arc is not enforced on this robot") and shows a WARN line on the Match page. Students can then see why a shot went where it did.

Details:
- `TeleOpConfig.enforceFiringArc` (new, on by default) gates the arc check in `BasicDriveTeleOp.fire()`, and one `RobotDifferences` line turns it off on 20245.
- The turret still stops at the arc's edge instead of turning through the robot's back. Autos (`LaunchCards`, `AimedVolley`) still enforce the arc on both robots.
- The `CLAUDE.md` turret rule is updated to match.

## Why this way

The drivers didn't understand why shots were held back. The only signal was a single short buzz and a Driver Station line they don't see while driving. The mentor wanted 20245's driver to make that call, and wanted one signal on both robots that says "you are outside the arc".

A switch flipped in `RobotDifferences` is the house pattern for a behaviour difference, rather than an `if` on the robot. It is `@Configurable`, so Panels can turn the guard back on mid-session.

What I did not do:
- Turn the arc off in the turret's motion. That would let the turret swing through the robot's back.
- Turn it off in the Auto. That wasn't asked for, and an Auto has no driver to make the call.

How the flash works: it is a repeating effect started once per hold. When the hold ends, `setLedColor` replaces it with the alliance colour. Nothing set the driver's gamepad light before this PR.

## Tested

- [ ] Compiles locally (`./gradlew assembleDebug`): not run, the session container has no Android SDK, so CI will be the first build
- [ ] Lint clean (`./gradlew :TeamCode:lintDebug`): not run, left to CI
- [ ] Unit tests pass (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`): not run, left to CI
- [ ] Ran on a robot: not yet. On each robot, fire with the turret past the edge:
  - 20245 should feed and flash purple.
  - 19429 should refuse and flash purple.
- [ ] If any `.gradle` file changed: n/a

## Touches locked things?

- [ ] Dependency versions
- [ ] `.github/workflows/` or `dependabot.yml`
- [ ] `TeamCode/src/main/res/xml/robot_*.xml` or `hardware/DeviceNames.java`
- [ ] `FtcRobotController/`

## For reviewers

- The `Gamepad.LedEffect.Builder` / `runLedEffect` calls are written from the SDK API and were not compiled here.
- Is alliance colour the right light to return to after the flash?

author: tuffinmuffin
body:
Milestone 3's next writing widget: **Number Slider** (Elastic's `"Number Slider"`), in `widgets/builtin/number_slider.rs`.

## What it does
- The value shows above a slider, with labels below it (like the Number Bar).
- **Input follows the toggle rules.** Locked, the whole card takes input. Unlocked, the body does, and the title bar moves the widget. Pressing jumps the knob to the pointer, and a drag follows it, even outside the widget.
- **Sending.** By default it sends the value where you let go. With `publish_all` (Elastic's setting) it sends every value during the drag.
- **No jump back.** After you let go, the knob stays at the value it sent until the server has it, or for 1 s. If the robot or another dashboard changes the value later, the slider shows that.
- **Snapping.**
  - `step` (raptaboard's own) snaps to multiples counted from the minimum.
  - With no step, values snap to a thousandth of the range rounded down to a power of ten (0.01 for 0 to 10), so a drag sends 3.07 rather than 3.0000001.
  - Int topics get whole numbers.
- **Settings:** `min_value`, `max_value`, `divisions`, `publish_all` and `step`, plus unit, show value and show labels.
- **Lists.** It works as a List Layout child. Unlocked, the child's label stays the drag handle.
- **Typing a value.** Click the written value to open a box with the value selected.
  - Enter sends what you typed. A unit may be left on. The value is kept in the range and made whole for int topics, but `step` doesn't apply.
  - A bad number turns red and the box stays open.
  - Escape, or a click elsewhere, closes the box without sending.
- **Escape cancels a drag.** Nothing is sent. With `publish_all`, the value from before the drag is sent back. egui itself ends a drag on Escape, so a release in the same frame as Escape counts as a cancel. The Deselect shortcut (`edit.rs`) leaves Escape alone while a mouse button is held.
- **Editable Text Display** (`editable`, raptaboard's own, off by default):
  - A blue dot in the title bar's corner shows the value can be typed in.
  - A click opens the same box (locked, anywhere on the card; unlocked, the body). Enter sends what you typed, and the topic's type decides what it becomes.
  - Number topics need a number and boolean topics `true` or `false`. Anything else turns red and isn't sent.
  - Arrays and struct fields can't be typed in.
  - The box is now `widgets/shared/entry.rs`, shared with the slider.
- **Fix: a list slider's number was under its label.** With labels inside, unlocked, only a sliver of the number opened the box and the rest went to the list. List children now get `Live::free` (the row less the inside label, locked or not), and the slider lays out in it.
- **Not yet:** vertical orientation, and keyboard or scroll-wheel nudges. They're listed in the spec.

## Testing
- **Unit tests:** turning a track position into a value (steps, backwards ranges, ends), int topics, and the track's layout.
- **Whole-window tests** in `ui/tests.rs`, against an in-process server with a new `/Test/setpoint` topic:
  - Locked and unlocked: a click sets the value, and a drag sends nothing until you let go. A drag that ends outside the widget sends the maximum. The robot's own change wins. The widget never moves.
  - `publish_all`: the server gets the value while the button is still down.
  - A slider inside a List Layout.
  - Typing: Enter sends; a bad value keeps the box open; Escape and clicking away send nothing; a value past the range goes to its end; it works locked and unlocked.
  - Escape mid-drag: nothing is sent on release, and with `publish_all` the server goes back to the old value.

author: leaysgur
body:
Reads a pipe below an Angular expression's root as `@angular/compiler` does (`parsePipe`), for the formatter to format it instead of leaving the code as written.

- `AngularCode::nested` holds the outermost expressions with pipes below the root, in order: in parens (`(a | p).b`), a call's argument, an index, an array's element, an object's value, and a spread (`[...a | p]`, `{...a | p}`).
- `NestedPipe::span` is what it takes the place of. Parens all of an argument, an index or an array's element are left out, as Angular reads the pipe without them; an object's value and a spread keep them, as Prettier prints them.
- `NestedPipe::last_value` marks an object's last value, where its `}` may meet `}}`.

Not parsed yet, both found 0 times in ~1400 real templates (the formatter leaves them as written):

- `a ? b : c | p`: a pipe in a conditional's alternate
- `` `${a | p}` ``: a pipe in a template literal

Breaking changes:

- `AngularCode` takes a lifetime and is no longer `Copy`.

author: gascity-eddie[bot]
body:
## Summary

`gc sling X B` re-routes a bead by writing only `gc.routed_to`, so a bead held by a live session of a different agent A stays assigned to it. The orphan-release sweep keeps it for any live holder (first through `protectedWakeWork`, then through the liveness gates), B's pool never sees demand, and A stays anchored. Both candidates agree on the fix: a `gc.routed_at` stamp written by the built-in routers, and a store-scoped route-away arm in `releaseOrphanedPoolAssignments`. That arm releases a bead once every open-session owner of the assignee resolves to an agent other than the routed pool and a 90s settle window has passed. The candidates did not disagree on what the bug is. They differed on where to stamp, how to treat a missing stamp, whether `protectedWakeWork` must be bypassed, and on events. The acceptance criteria below record the resolution of each. The window bounds the race with a source turn that outlives it but does not remove it. Removing it takes a conditional completion write, which is out of scope here.

The maintainer review changed how the arm releases a claim: it re-reads the claim live and releases it in one write fenced on the row it judged (see Maintainer review).

## Behavior change

A live holder whose agent is not the bead's pool route loses its claim once the route is 90 seconds old, whatever made the two disagree: a `gc sling` to another agent, a claim taken on a bead already routed to another agent's pool (`gc bd update --claim` checks no route), or a hand-made `bd update --assignee`. The holder is not told and may still be working the bead. To keep such a claim, route the bead to the holder's agent or add the human label. `gc sling --reassign` still clears the assignee and reopens the bead before routing, so the target can claim it at once. The `--reassign` help and the gc-work skill now say this.

A missing, blank or malformed `gc.routed_at`, or one more than a window ahead of now, counts as settled, and nothing wrote that stamp before this change. So on the first controller tick after deploy, every routed-away claim that AC-4 does not keep is released to its route's pool at once, cross-claims included, on the default bd provider too.

A route-away release records `bead.route_away_released` (bead, holder, routed_to, routed_at), not `bead.dead_assignee_reopened`. The controller prints `released routed-away pool work: <id>` for such a release and logs `releaseOrphanedPoolAssignments: kept "<id>" of routed-away live holder "<holder>": <why>` for a kept claim.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Criterion | glm | opus | pr4073 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Given pool agents A and B, an open session a-1 of A, and bead X {assignee a-1, in_progress, gc.routed_to B, gc.routed_at now-2×window} in one store, when the production composition runs at `now` (`filterAssignedWorkBeadsForSessionWake` → `protectedWakeWorkKeys` → `releaseOrphanedPoolAssignmentsWhenSnapshotsComplete`), then X is returned with `RoutedAway=true`, reads back open with an empty assignee, and is counted as demand for B by `defaultScaleCheckCountsAndDemand` on the post-release snapshot. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-2 | Given the AC-1 shape with gc.routed_at = now-window+1s, when the composition runs, then X is kept with assignee a-1 and status in_progress; and given gc.routed_at = now-window, then X is released. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-3 | Given the AC-1 shape, when gc.routed_at is absent, blank, malformed, or more than one window in the future, then X is released. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-4 | Given the AC-1 shape past the window, when any one of these holds, then X is kept with assignee a-1 and status in_progress: an open session of B shares the assignee identity; an owner's agent cannot be resolved; the assignee is an identity this city cannot observe; X is control-kind; X carries the human label; or a live graph-resident session in a separate owner store answers to the assignee. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-5 | Given a split-topology city where a-1 reaches X's class-binding store ref only through `assignedWorkClaimRefs`, or a city-scoped agent A whose session a-1 holds rig-store X routed to rig pool B, when the composition runs past the window, then X is released; and with X routed to A instead, X is kept. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-6 | Given a built-in route through `cliBeadRouter.Route` or `apiBeadRouter.Route` whose normalized target differs from `PriorRoutedTo`, when it routes X, then exactly one `SetMetadataBatch` call writes gc.routed_to and a parseable gc.routed_at to the routing store; and when the normalized target equals `PriorRoutedTo`, then gc.routed_at is not written. | partial | pass | - |
| AC-7 | Given a tick that releases one route-away bead and one dead-assignee bead, when the events are recorded, then the route-away bead gets one `bead.route_away_released` event (bead, holder, routed_to, routed_at) and no `bead.dead_assignee_reopened`, and the dead-assignee bead gets only `bead.dead_assignee_reopened`. | pass | pass | - |

## Maintainer review

The adopt-pr review added one maintainer commit, `fix(pool): re-judge a routed-away claim live and fence its release on that row`. It changes the release this PR first proposed:

- The arm judged a claim on the tick's listed row and released it through the orphan release. On a store whose lists carry no revision (BdStore), that release is fenced on status and assignee alone, so a bead routed back to its holder's agent, re-routed with a fresh stamp or labeled for a person after the list was still released. The release now re-reads the claim live and keeps it, logged as `moved`, unless the live row holds the same claim and is still releasable judged afresh. It then releases that row under its own route-away release policy, in one write fenced on the row it judged.
- Where the store can fence a revision, that write is fenced on the live row's revision, so any write after the read keeps the claim for the next tick. The pinned bd (v1.3.4; v1.3.0 is the supported floor) has `--if-status` and `--if-assignee` but no `--if-revision`, so on the default bd provider the write is one `bd update --if-status --if-assignee` guarded on the live row's status and assignee. A claim taken, given back or closed after the read is kept. A route or person-label change that lands in the one round trip between the read and the write is still released: the window every orphan release on such a store accepts, which closes on a bd with `--if-revision`. A store that can fence neither way keeps the claim, logged as `unfenced`.
- The cross-claim release under Behavior change is a deliberate decision, pinned by `TestRouteAwayReleasesACrossClaimOnARoutedBead`. Both release writes are reviewed release sites in the worklegs lint.
- On a fake of the pinned bd (`bdGuardLedger`), tests pin the tick's sweep releasing a routed-away claim in one guarded `bd update`, and the release's keeps: a bead routed back after the list (no write), a claim that changes hands between the read and the write (bd refuses the guard), and a bd with neither fence (`unfenced`). A store with both fences pins that the revision fence is the one taken.

Known gaps this PR leaves:

- A claim whose holder's session bead lives only in an owner store other than the sessions store stays with its holder (AC-4). That is a graph-v2 handoff on a city whose graph binding is not the sessions store, so #7004 persists for those handoffs.
- `bead.route_away_released` takes `routed_to` and `routed_at` from the tick's listed row, so an unstamped re-route (a custom `sling_query` router or a direct `gc.routed_to` write) that lands between the list and the release makes the event name the listed route.

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr4073 (pass).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← opus, AC-2 ← opus, AC-3 ← opus, AC-4 ← merge, AC-5 ← opus, AC-6 ← op

author: chaffed
body:
Closes #6.

## What this does

- **Two pings on every check,** failed checks included: the modem, and an internet host (`ping_host`, default `1.1.1.1`). They run at the same time (3 pings each) and the reading stores loss and average time for both. If no reply comes back, the reading stores `100` and no time.
- **`health.outages(readings)`** merges consecutive checks where no ping to the internet came back into one outage:
  - **Kind:** *modem unreachable* if the modem stopped answering too at any point, otherwise *line down*.
  - **Duration as a range:** at least the time between the first and last check that found it down, at most the time between the good checks around it. Between checks nobody knows exactly when the line went down or came back, so the report won't overstate it.
  - **Ongoing** when the latest check still finds it down.
  - **Long gaps:** more than 30 minutes between checks (router off) splits an outage rather than guessing what happened in between.
  - **Lost pings:** one or two lost pings out of three are not an outage.

## Tests

- **Backend:** pings are stored on good and failed readings, and an internet host that doesn't answer gives `100` with no time while the modem still answers.
- **`health.test.js`:** merging, duration range, kind, ongoing, splitting at long gaps, partial loss, readings without pings, and readings in any order.

## On the real router

- **Normal readings:** the modem answers in about 1–2 ms and `1.1.1.1` in about 12–16 ms, with no loss.
- **A host that never answers** (`192.0.2.1`, written to a throwaway data folder so the real history isn't touched): stored as `100` with no time, while the modem still answered.

author: syakirbadry-tech
body:
Requested by the Chairman (CHR): review the app with the apple-design skill, then fix and merge.

## Findings and fixes (Apple's guideline pages are cited)
- **High, `tab-bars.md › Best practices`:** "Use a tab bar to support navigation, not to provide actions."
  - **Was:** + Create sat inside the tab bar.
  - **Now:** the tabs are Home · Jobs · Cars · Money · More, and **Create** is a floating button above the bar. It hides while the menu or search is open.
- **High, `liquid-glass.md`:** "Don't use Liquid Glass in the content layer."
  - **Now:** content cards and tiles are solid. Glass stays on the top bar, tab bar, sheets, drawer and Create button.
- **High, `dark-mode.md`:** "Ensure that your app looks good in both appearance modes" and "Avoid offering an app-specific appearance setting."
  - **Now:** the app follows the phone's Light/Dark setting.
  - Dark colour tokens were being overridden by the light glass tokens; they're re-declared with higher specificity.
  - Fixed the dark badge, status and booking-time colours.
  - The contrast audit passes on every screen in both themes.
- **Medium, `search-fields.md`:** search becomes a toolbar button that "animates into a search field".
  - **Now:** on the phone, search is a top-bar button that expands into a full-width field with Cancel, instead of a squeezed, cut-off box.
- **Medium, `sheets.md › Best practices`:** "Support swiping to dismiss a sheet."
  - **Now:** sheets close when swiped down from the top. They already had a grabber.
- **Medium, `typography.md`:** the iOS default is 17 pt.
  - **Now:** phone body and row text goes from 15px to 16px.

**Kept, as a trade-off:** the **More** tab opens the full menu. The app has about 30 sections; a sidebar isn't available on a phone, and More keeps them one tap away.

## Checks
- `npm test`: 32 pass.
- Audit of all 34 screens at 390 and 1440, light and dark: no contrast failures. The only items left are accepted ones: in-row links where the whole row is tappable, and 24px checkboxes inside labels.
- Playwright sweep: no page errors.

## Undo
Revert the merge commit.

author: strehk
body:
## What changed and why

Until now the conference's messaging switch closed every chat, the team inboxes included, and delegation groups only opened after the release. Students could not ask participant care anything while they registered.

Now:

- **Team inboxes are always open.** Delegation members and single participants reach participant care and the trusted persons from their registration on, whatever the switch says. A committee's chairs and consultants still reach only the people seated in their committee, as before.
- **The delegation group is always open.** It opens as soon as the delegation exists, before it applies, so members can coordinate their application. Once the assignment is released, a delegation without a role keeps its group readable but closed (`NOT_SEATED`). The team stays reachable for its members.
- **The switch covers only chats between delegations.** It is renamed "Nachrichten zwischen Delegationen" / "Messages between delegations" and has a description in the settings. These direct chats still also need the roles released and both people seated.
- **Dashboard.** Delegation members and single participants without quick links (registering, waiting for the selection, rejected) get a new `MessagesEntry` card. The quick-links card is no longer gated on the switch.
- **Messages page.** It explains why other delegations aren't reachable yet: before the release, or with the switch off. The team page shows an info note instead of a warning while the switch is off. The team can start chats once roles are released, whatever the switch says.
- **Mails.** The `UNREAD_MESSAGES` and `CHAT_REPORTED` mails no longer depend on the switch. The snapshot field `messagingEnabled` is removed from the email engine.
- Supervisors, terms acceptance, suspensions and blocks work as before. A suspended participant still can't write in their group, but can always write to the team.

The core rule is `writeRefusal` in `src/lib/helpers/chat.ts`. It is enforced in `chatService.ts`: `openDelegationChat`, `openTeamChat` and `inboxesReaching` no longer check the switch, and `openDirectChat` still does.

### Seed and docs
- Dev seed: "Seed 2 · Registration open", with the switch off, now has a participant care chat from `dev-reg-head-ready` and the group of the ready delegation with `dev-reg-member`.
- Manual (de/en): the participant dashboard, team communication, configuration and AI access pages are updated. `docs/architecture/messages.md` (the write rules) is updated.

### Merge with main
`main` reworked messaging in parallel (message hiding, chat workspace, navigation, and its own fix of the seed's terms acceptances via `termsOnDisk.ts`). I merged it:

- **Seed terms acceptances:** I took `main`'s fix and dropped my duplicate.
- **`chat.ts` and the team messages page:** I reapplied my changes on top of `main`'s versions.
- **Authorization e2e spec:** both new tests are kept.

## How it was verified
After the merge:

- `bun run check`: 0 errors.
- `bun run i18n:check` passes.
- Full unit suite: 385 files, 3303 tests passed.
- The lefthook pre-commit and pre-push hooks pass (lint, fallow, format, typecheck, tests).

New and updated unit tests:
- `writeRefusal`
- `messagesPageState`
- `emailCandidates`

**e2e not run** (per CLAUDE.md, only on request). New and updated specs:
- `e2e/authorization/messages.spec.ts`: the switch test now expects the team and the group to stay open. A new test covers an applicant (fixture: a rejected delegation, Emil). Before the release, with the switch off, Emil writes to the group and to participant care. After the release the group is read only and care is still reachable.
- `e2e/dashboard/delegation-signup.spec.ts`: a freshly joined member sees the messages card and the before-release hint.

## Left open
- The team can't start a chat with an applicant who hasn't written first. The team's "new message" picker lists seated people only, as before.
- Manual screenshots of the messages pages were not regenerated.

body:
Fixes #67

Ticket: https://github.com/maxharris1/coo/issues/67

## Why
Later services need one place for local-day caps, the weekend bonus, quiet hours, hatching, job offers and found objects. This adds the last three pure rule modules of T005 (`time.ts`, `eggs.ts`, `jobs.ts`), as the plan on this PR describes.

## What changed
- `time.ts` gives the local date, ISO weekday, Monday week start and local midnight for an IANA zone, plus `isTimeZone` and `inQuietHours`. It uses only `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Date.UTC`.
- `eggs.ts` rolls a hatchling from the egg id. It picks an unowned hatchable breed and rolls stats inside the breed's ranges.
- `jobs.ts` offers 2 jobs per user per local date and rolls a found object per source row. Every roll goes through the engine's `hash32` and `rng` with its own seed prefix.

## Scope
- The plan's defaults apply. The found object is seeded by the run's row id. The hatchling has no quirks (T039 and T009 own those). Quiet hours are whole hours and half-open.
- No config, docs or dependency changes.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run src/lib/game src/lib/config.test.ts` passes 53 tests. They cover determinism sweeps of 200 seeds, all 63 owned-breed subsets, the New York DST days, and Tokyo Saturday while UTC is still Friday.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass on the pushed head.

author: shani-singh1
body:
## Problem

`POST /api/terminal` `stat()`s the cwd and lets a failure reach its catch-all, so a terminal opened for a project folder that was deleted or moved outside pi-web answers 500 with the raw OS error (`ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '...'`), which the terminal tab then shows. `/api/agent/new` and `/api/models` answer the same folder with 400 and `cwdMissingBody()` (`reason: "cwd-missing"`, `Directory does not exist: <folder>`, #1422).

Repro on main: the new test calls the route's `POST` with `{ cwd: <deleted folder> }` and gets 500.

## Fix

In `app/api/terminal/route.ts`, a `stat` failing with `ENOENT` or `ENOTDIR` returns `cwdMissingBody(cwd)` with status 400, the helper and status `/api/models` uses. Other errors still go to the 500 handler, and the order of the checks (stat, then the allowed roots) is unchanged. The terminal tab already shows the body's `error`, so the client needs no change. One sentence added to `docs/agents/client-platform.md`.

## Tests

New `app/api/terminal/route.test.mjs`: fails on main (500 instead of 400) and passes with the fix. `tsc --noEmit` and eslint on the changed files are clean.

The other routes that take a cwd (git status, file index, open-in-explorer, worktrees, skills, plugins, MCP, project trust) were only read: for a deleted folder they already answer 403 or 404, so they are left alone.
