body:
**Work item:** closes #197 (part of #193). #198 and #199 are later leaves; L3 stays unfiled.

**Result.** On a pull request, `proofs-shard-0..2` run only the native mutation modes the change can affect, through the real CI caller, with an exact-tuple planned/executed audit. Every doubt schedules the full shards. Native and proof statements, pins, budgets and rejection rules are unchanged.

**Change**
- **`scripts/edit-native-plans.mjs`:** the shared enumeration, moved out of `check-edit-proofs.mjs`.
  - It holds the modes, mutation table, owners and migrations, `proofRoot`, cargo arguments, and the positive's roots and baselines.
  - `check-edit-proofs.mjs` executes exactly these units; `export-plans` exports them.
  - The enumeration is **byte-identical** to the previous inline code: an old-vs-new capture of every mode's owner, mutated-source digest, `proofRoot` and cargo arguments, plus the positive roots and `mutation-owners`, has sha256 `0f8172c2…` both before and after.
- **`scripts/check-edit-proofs.mjs`:**
  - **Exact-tuple audit.** Each executed unit records what it actually ran: roots passed to the verifier, cargo arguments and baselines, the digest of the mutated file in its crate, the owner it judged, and the outcome it asserted. At the end, executed equals planned field for field, in both directions. Preflight controls cover a hidden unit, an unexecuted plan, changed roots, wrong expectation (both kinds), mutation digest, cargo arguments, baselines and owner.
  - **`export-plans`:** exclusive; takes no checkout lock (it runs on read-only store trees); needs no toolchain.
  - **`selection:<file> shard:i/n` consumer.** The record must match this tree's own plan export *and* the recorded native-code file digests.
    - `full` runs the plain shard.
    - `none` writes empty planned/results files and runs nothing ("not affected; no result is claimed").
    - `selected` runs this shard's share of the selected modes, plus this job's own positive seed.
  - **Runtime load audit** in selected runs: a resolve hook records every module loaded after startup, and the run fails if any gate script lies outside the recorded native-code set.
- **`scripts/text-families.mjs`:** the families, their Remaining locator controls and cache-safety. The runner imports it by a literal only when a family or cache-safety runs (or in gatepreflight), so shard runs never load family modules. The Remaining locator PASS line now prints in jobs that run Remaining (core-a) and in gatepreflight, not in shards.
- **`scripts/select-affected.mjs`: per-tuple text selection, both refs.** A native tuple is selected when:
  - it is new or changed;
  - a changed module is in the dependency closure of its actual roots or owner;
  - a crate or test input changed (`src/`, `tests/`, `Cargo.*`, `proof-smoke/`);
  - or a native-path code input changed.

  Native-path code is the literal import closure of `check-edit-proofs.mjs`, computed with `check-gate-inputs.mjs`'s own parser (any unsupported form refuses), minus the one named module `text-families.mjs`.

  An invariant check routes **full** if any owner module is outside its roots' dependency closure (a graph edge missing). **Full** also follows from: the runner, shared machinery (`proof-cache`, `negative-proof-evidence`, `mutation-scope`, `fstar-mutation-scope`, `proof-reform`, `gate-scripts.json`, `flake.nix`), toolchain changes, unmapped paths, unreadable inputs, and malformed or missing exports at either ref.
- **Boundary, flake, CI:**
  - `selection-boundary.mjs --gate=text`; flake `text-selection` and `proofs-selected-shard-i`;
  - a separate PR route for `proofs-shard-*` in `ci.yml`, plus `text-selection-<target>` evidence (identity, planned, results, loaded modules). The register route is byte-identical;
  - skip-plan accounting: 20 new reviewed lines, two build rules, and `SELECTION_PATHS` (plus `check-gate-inputs.mjs` and `edit-native-plans.mjs`) now also applying to text shards.

**Local evidence** (Node 22.23.2; x86 sandbox builds for the flake)
- **Real executions:**
  - the positive alone (audit: 1 unit);
  - two modes plus the identity control: `stream-admission-skips-predecessor` (whole test set) and `plan-skips-validation` (owner `EditAtomic`, root `EditWellFormed`); audit: 3 units;
  - a selected consumer run with the positive seed, the identity control and one mode: tuple audit passed, load audit passed with 4 scripts, all in the native set.

  That consumer run also caught two real bugs **before publication**:
  - families were loaded unconditionally;
  - the selector's first import regex missed bare `import './x.mjs'`.

  Both are fixed. The second is why the selector now uses `check-gate-inputs`' parser.
- **Sandbox:** `nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.text-selection` with real overrides gives mode `selected`, text `none`; `proofs-selected-shard-0` then runs nothing in the sandbox.
- **Fixtures** (real git trees; each tree exports with its own runner; head selector):

  | Change | Text verdict |
  |---|---|
  | family script only | none |
  | `text-families.mjs` only | none |
  | `check-basis-reform.mjs` (native code input) | all 100 |
  | `EditWellFormed` view | 68 (40 of them only by root; e.g. `plan-skips-validation`, owner `EditAtomic`) |
  | `EditBasis.lt` comment plus receipt | 10 (3 basis, 7 replay) |
  | positive-only (`Spec` view) | none, positive flagged |
  | crate `src/event_shell.rs` | all 100 |
  | `tests/` only | all 100 |
  | `Canonical.lt` (shared with register) | 28 |

- **Selector mutants:**

- gate-inputs closure check OK; gatepreflight 7 PASS lines; skip-plan self-test 13 groups.

author: daniel-ospina
body:
### Review Scope Contract

- **Class:** `code` (one `tools/` instrument + its DB-free pins + CI-manifest registration + a research/evidence doc, and **one production file**: a behaviour-preserving extraction in `tortoise/record_vector.py` — see R2)
- **R0 — the instrument must be able to fail.** Every comparison the harness gates on has a demonstrated negative: four `--poison` modes, each DETECTED, with artifacts committed.
- **R1 — the harness must not damage either store.** It seeds its own uniquely-named tenant/graph, is read-only on the query paths, and tears the tenant down (the graph copy of #13906's destructive half is explicitly out of scope).
- **R2 — no production behaviour changes; ONE production file is touched, and it is named here.**
  `tortoise/record_vector.py` gains `knn_statement(entity_type, scope, query_vec, limit, …)`: the kNN
  `SELECT` that `vector_search` used to build inline. The read now calls it. No predicate, bind,
  statement divisor, shortfall `count(*)` or fold-arm predicate changes — 87 pins across
  `test_4999_vector_mechanism.py`, `test_11642_vector_move.py`, `test_11691_vector_leg_budget.py`,
  `test_5412_empty_query_vector_leg_trace.py` and `test_13417_vectorless_rows.py` pass unchanged.
  ⛔ **Why it cannot be a separate PR:** the plan check must EXPLAIN the statement the LEG runs — an
  EXPLAIN of a SELECT the harness re-spelled proves something about the re-spelling, which is this
  PR's own reviewed defect one indirection out. That is only fixable from inside the read's module.
- **R3 — the CI selector must see the new pin.** `config/ci-surfaces.yml` + `tools/ci_selection.py::CORE_ALSO` — without both, a harness-only diff runs tier-1 smoke where the pin is not registered.

## Why

#13906's plan has five steps. **Steps 2 and 4 had already shipped** — I verified that before writing anything rather than redoing it:

| step | state at `28ca66878d` | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `vector(384)` column + backfill + HNSW | **shipped** (#11642 point/source/event, #13220 object/subject) | `20261109000001_record_embedding_vector.sql`, `20261117000001_record_object_subject_embedding.sql` — `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (public.record_embedding_vector(embedding)) STORED`, five `hnsw`/`vector_cosine_ops` indexes |
| dual-write while the old path serves | **structural** — a GENERATED column has no second writer to drift | same migrations |
| `#5004` verbatim rule | **honoured by construction** — the converter returns NULL for a non-384 payload, so a caller-owned 768-wide vector is stored verbatim and simply not ANN-indexed | `:66-84`; pinned by `test_11642_vector_move_live.py::test_a_non_384_embedding_is_stored_but_not_ANN_indexed` |
| flip behind a flag, OFF by default | flag `TORTOISE_RECORD_VECTOR_LEG`; default **ON since #13610**, but each label is gated on `record_vector.coverage` — the record answers only after a COUNT proves it holds every graph vector | `record_vector.py:264-334`, `:671`, `:777` |
| no graph copy removed | holds — nothing here touches `embedding` writes or props | — |

What had **no gate at all** is §6.1's load-bearing question: *for the same tenant and the same query, do the two dense legs agree on ids, order and recall@k?* Three instruments exist and none answers it — `entity_vector_parity_census.py` compares stored COPIES (#13629), `test_4997_vector_index_parity.py` compares index-vs-scan inside the graph, `test_11642_vector_move_live.py` executes the record's SQL but never against the leg it replaced.

## What

`tools/vector_parity_13906.py` seeds one corpus into **both** real stores and answers it with **four readers**:

| reader | answers |
|---|---|
| `truth_cosine` / `truth_euclidean` | an exact scan computed **in-process in numpy** over the corpus the harness itself wrote — neither store's index participates, so no store can bias the oracle |
| `record` | `record_vector.vector_search` → pgvector HNSW, cosine |
| `graph_scan` | `run_vector_query`'s brute-force fallback → **euclidean** (what production does today: the live graph has no vector index) |
| `graph_index` | the same call with an HNSW index created, **cosine** |

Diffs per query: **ids, order** (with an explicit tie policy: a permutation inside one distance bucket is `tie`, across buckets is `diverged`), **recall@k**, and **distances**.

Edge corpus: a 3-member exact tie group · a caller-owned 768-wide vector · a row with no embedding · a `retracted` and an `outdated` row whose vectors **are** the query (a broken `#689` cage ranks them first) · a second tenant with the same vectors · un-normalised vectors throughout (unit vectors hide the metric divergence this is here to measure).

Anti-drift: `tests/test_vector_parity_13906.py` pins the comparator **DB-free** — the tie policy, the three eligibility rules, the extra-id case recall alone cannot see, and every poison.

## Proof

Both stores real and local: Postgres 16 + **pgvector 0.8.7** (`pgvector/pgvector:pg16`, the image `test-record-postgres` pins, every migration applied by the tree's own `_ensure_record_schema`); FalkorDB **v4.20.6** (this lane's `tools/test_lane.py` container).

```
# clean run — every artifact committed under docs/research/2026-11-20-13906-vector-parity/
q_anchor: record recall=1.000 order=exact | graph_index recall=0.800 | graph_scan(euc) recall=1.000 | scan-vs-cosine 0.500
q_tie   : record recall=1.000 order=tie   | graph_index recall=1.000 | graph_scan(euc) recall=1.000 | scan-vs-cosine 0.500
q00     : record recall=1.000 order=exact | graph_index recall=1.000 | graph_scan(euc) recall=1.000 | scan-vs-cosine 0.200
q01     : record recall=1.000 order=tie   | graph_index recall=0.900 | graph_scan(euc) recall=1.000 | scan-vs-cosine 0.200
q02     : record recall=1.000 order=exact | graph_index recall=1.000 | graph_scan(euc) recall=1.000 | scan-vs-cosine 0.400
q03     : record recall=1.000 order=exact | graph_index recall=0.800 | graph_scan(euc) recall=1.000 | scan-vs-cosine 0.400
PARITY: all required comparisons agree          (ids, order AND distances inside 1e-4)

# falsifier — a harness that has never reported a difference is not a harness
--poison id      POISON DETECTED   record  recall=0.900  distance_delta=4.665
--poison order   POISON DETECTED   record  order=diverged distance_delta=0.896
--poison recall  POISON DETECTED   record  recall=0.900
--poison vector  POISON DETECTED   graph_scan recall=0.900 order=diverged   (real store divergence: the graph is seeded perturbed, the oracle is not)

tests/test_vector_parity_13906.py                                          79 passed
tests/test_ci_selection.py                                                527 passed, 1 skipped
tools/ci_selection.py --integrity                          all test files classified
```

Two instrument bugs the live run caught and this PR fixes, because each of them would have produced a **green report about nothing**:

- A freshly-created FalkorDB HNSW index answers **zero** rows while it builds, and `run_vector_query` answers that with the `#8429` fall-through to the scan — so the "indexed" arm measured the SCAN and reported its number under the index's name. `wait_index_ready()` now blocks until `queryNodes` answers and the arm **fails loudly** if it still falls back.
- The first `--poison vector` was reported **NOT DETECTED**: negating a stored vector moved its distance 0.0 → 2.0 while every unrelated row sat 15–25 away, so ids *and* order were unchanged. `compare()` now takes distances; `_verdict` fails on a distance-only divergence; the poison pushes the row beyond the whole corpus.

## The artifact's own review rounds

Rounds 5–22 of `docs/research/2026-11-20-13906-vector-parity/README.md` §5.1 record what each review
round caught and how it was measured — including **round 20** (the plan check proved a listing, not a
plan), **round 21** (the index name came from the indexed table, so every store was refused) and
**round 22** (a dangling conninfo escape the pair parser kept and libpq dro

author: jan-kubica
body:
## Summary

`withGeneratedOutputCache` hashes a generator's inputs before and after it runs and refuses the result if they differ. The hash walked the filesystem under the input globs, so it also read git-ignored build output there. When another task wrote such files during the run, the generator failed with "Generator <name> changed its source inputs", though no source had changed.

The `mcp-apps` preparation hashes `packages/**`. A Rust test compiling into `packages/scan-engine/target/` (ignored by that package's `.gitignore`) beside it is enough to trip it. That happens whenever the Rust test misses the task cache at the same time, for example when every package version changes in one commit.

- **Class fix.** In a git checkout, the input hash skips every candidate path git ignores (`git check-ignore -z --stdin`). Ignored files are build output and local state, never sources, so no concurrent writer of them can change a generator's identity. A failing `git check-ignore` fails the generation loudly.
- **No checkout.** A source archive without `.git` keeps the explicit exclusions it had (`dist`, build info, `node_modules`, other generators' outputs).
- Fewer files are hashed, so each generator's cache identity changes once.

## Tests

`packages/scripts/src/generated-output-cache.test.ts`: in a git repository, a generation during which ignored build output under `target/` is rewritten and added succeeds and caches. A non-ignored source changing during generation is still refused. The new test fails on the previous implementation.

body:
## Summary

Closes #267. Debug builds asserted "multiple heroes that share the same tag" (`<SnackBar Hero tag - _AuthToast>`) on sign-out and account switch.

Cause: `ScaffoldMessenger` shows a SnackBar in every root Scaffold, and the shell keeps each visited tab's navigator alive in an `IndexedStack`. Flutter's hero flight counts the top route of every nested navigator, hidden tabs included, so a toast during a route change (shell → Masuk) put two Heroes with the same tag into one flight.

Fix: the shell uses `StatefulShellRoute` with `ShellBranches` (`lib/routing/router.dart`), the same `IndexedStack` + `Offstage` + `TickerMode` as `.indexedStack`, plus `HeroMode(enabled: false)` on hidden tabs. This also keeps hidden tabs' own heroes out of flights.

## Evidence

- Before: `test/routing/shell_branches_test.dart` with heroes on in every tab fails with `multiple heroes had the following tag: <SnackBar Hero tag - Text("Udah keluar")>`.
  After: passes.
- Reproduced on the iOS simulator (Luma Dev, env dev) before the fix: Akun → Keluar → Keluar.
- `make check` (l10n, format, analyze, 1517 tests), `make docs-check`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** tab shell

Every tab screen renders through `ShellBranches`; visible behavior (kept state, hidden tabs offstage, tickers paused) matches `.indexedStack`.

author: ahze
body:
A man page for the FreeBSD pf firewall driver, alongside netavark-firewalld(7):
the pf.conf tables and anchor hooks the host must provide,
`net.pf.filter_local`, what each anchor holds, isolation, reloading pf, and
limitations. docs/Makefile picks it up with the other `*.7.md` pages.

Every behavioral claim was checked in the jailed pf rig:

- plain `pfctl -f` (`service pf reload`) keeps the anchor rules and table
  entries; `pfctl -F all` (`service pf restart`) drops them until
  `netavark firewall-reload`
- without the hooks in pf.conf, container packets leave un-NATed and
  published ports do not answer
- a default-deny ruleset needs both `pass from <netavark-subnets>` and
  `pass to <netavark-subnets>`; with them, published ports work from outside
  and via 127.0.0.1, and NAT out works

## 운영 수정(#1523 후속): OCR 할 쪽을 300 dpi 로 먼저 그린다

#1523 배포 뒤 첫 text run(20261119T224659Z, 상한 2564m, Tesseract 그림 4000 px 묶음)에서 처음 30 개 중 **5 개가 또 메모리 상한에 끊겼다**. #1523 의 표지는 작동했다(`memory cap: ocrmypdf exit -9`, 다시 빚짐). 커널 기록으로는 ocrmypdf 프로세스 자신이 2.1–2.5 GB 였다.

**원인**(그 5 개를 읽기 키로 받아 노트북에서 잼): 쪽이 1,134–1,200 dpi 스캔(8977×12284 px, 쪽당 110–125 Mpx)이다. OCRmyPDF 16.7.0 은 쪽을 그 쪽의 가장 촘촘한 그림 해상도로 **상한 없이** 그린다 — `pdfinfo/info.py` 의 `take_max`, `_pipeline.get_canvas_square_dpi`; 300 dpi 로 묶는 것은 `rasterize_preview` 뿐. Tesseract 그림 묶음은 그 그림이 다 그려진 뒤에 작동한다. #1523 의 표본 10 개에는 그런 쪽이 없었다.

**고침**
| 무엇 | 어디 |
| --- | --- |
| OCR 할 쪽만 Ghostscript(이미 이미지에 있다) `-sDEVICE=pdfimage24 -r300 -sPageList=…` 로 그림 PDF 를 만들고 ocrmypdf 는 그것을 읽는다; OCR 쪽 수가 보낸 쪽 수와 다르면 그 문서의 failed | `jobs/document_text/document_text/extract.py` |
| `ocr_raster_dpi` 300, `raster_timeout_seconds_per_page` 30 | 계약 |
| `memory_kill.attempts` 3 → 6: 이 고침 전에 횟수를 다 쓴 문서도 다시 빚진다(ADR-0593 §2 가 정한 길). 추출기 판은 올리지 않는다(1.6 만 개 전체 재처리 없음) | 계약 |
| 컨테이너 상한 2564m → **1280m** = (759 측정, LibreOffice 777 중 큰 것 + 75) × 1.5 | 계약 |
| Dockerfile 에 ghostscript 를 직접 적는다(전에는 ocrmypdf 의 의존으로만 왔다) | Dockerfile |

**측정**(운영과 같은 trixie 패키지 ocrmypdf 16.7.0·Tesseract 5.5.0·Ghostscript 10.05.1, `--cpus 4`, 모든 쪽 OCR):
| 문서 | 전 | 300 dpi 로 먼저 그림 (상한 2564m) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 운영에서 끊긴 5 개(13–56 쪽) | 2.1–2.5 GB 에서 죽음 | **598–709 MiB**, 모두 끝까지 |
| #1523 표본 중 큰 3 개(31–42 쪽) | 1407–1634 MiB(4000 px) | **641–759 MiB**, 글자 −4 %..+1.4 % |

실제 코드 경로(`extract_isolated`)를 **1280m 상한**에서 두 문서(1,200 dpi 13 쪽, 띠 그림 54 쪽)로 돌림: 둘 다 끝까지(ocr 13/13 쪽 9,006 자; partial_ocr), `oom_kill 0`.

**로컬 확인**: `tests/test_document_text.py` 24 개(쪽 순서 대응·OCR 쪽 수 불일치·gs 와 ocrmypdf 인자), `every-container-has-a-memory-cap` 61.82g / 62.00g, ADR 색인. ruff 는 main 과 같은 E741 셋(기준선)뿐.

ADR-0593 에 2026-11-20 개정 절을 덧붙인다(결정 본문은 그대로).

**landed 확인**: 배포 뒤 첫 text run 의 `memory_killed`(0 이어야), `memory_kill_exhausted`, `peak_memory_mib.largest_child` vs 1280m, 결과 행.

author: stumcc8
body:
Adds the agent signup operations to the specification, so an agent can sign itself up from the public description alone.

- `GET /v1/signup/availability?name=`: checks a requested name (format and reserved names).
- `POST /v1/signup/start`: the agent asks for a `.viz` name for its own Ed25519 key. It returns `201` with `signup_id`, `user_code`, `approval_url`, `expires_at_ms` and `poll_interval_ms`; the same request again returns `200` with the same receipt.
- `GET /v1/signup/{signup_id}`: the signup's state: `pending`, `live` (with `domain`, `incarnation`, `subject_agent_id`, `public_key`), `expired`, `rejected` or `cancelled`.
- `POST /v1/signup/{signup_id}/cancel`: the agent withdraws its pending signup with a signed, single-use request.

**The signed proof format** is spelled out in the schemas and the README:
- The signature covers the domain string (`ZipViz signup-start v1` or `ZipViz signup-cancel v1`), one zero byte, then the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the object without `signature`.
- `key_id` is `sha256:` plus the hex SHA-256 of the raw public key.
- `bound_digest` covers `introduced_by`, the normalized `owner_email` and `runtime`.
- `audience` is `api.zipviz.ai`, with 5-minute freshness.
- The request body must be canonical JSON.

Every error status lists its codes, and all errors share the `{error, code}` body. 429 responses carry `Retry-After: 60`.

**Tested:**
- `openapi-spec-validator` reports `openapi.json: OK`, and the test-vector check still passes.
- I built a start and a cancel request from the README and schema text alone, with a generated key, and ran them through the API's own request parsing and signature verification. Both were accepted, and the computed `bound_digest` matched.
- A pretty-printed body is refused with `E_SIGNUP_SHAPE` and a wrong audience with `E_SIGNUP_AUD`, as documented.

author: magicy565-web
body:
## Why this sits between PR #8 and PR #9

PR #8 introduced a concept-only IssueSpec and Astro spread renderer. This PR adds the source adapter and extends the renderer to consume real enterprise edition assets. PR #9 is now stacked on this PR and wires the existing enterprise build to emit `magazine-issue.json`.

## Included

- Private-review IssueSpec support for the existing media pipeline's `licensed-photo`, `ai-generated`, and `abstract-fallback` kinds; PR #8's bundled Chongker concept remains compatible.
- Deterministic mapping of compiled enterprise articles, evidence, outline and media plan/report into a complete issue.
- Exact source, outline, media-plan, media-report and image-byte bindings.
- Immutable source article/evidence/media descriptors across agent editing handoff.
- Astro resolves source media through the existing Content Collection image metadata, never a model-supplied image URL.
- Source notebook, buyer questions, product captions and original-source links.
- Private issue route loaded from `BUYERSITE_BUILD_ROOT`, noindex by default.
- Full magazine route included in desktop/mobile visual review and Playwright browser coverage.

## Stack

`PR #8 → PR #10 (this source adapter) → PR #9 (enterprise outline + build integration)`

PR #9 now calls `compileMagazineIssueFromEnterprise`, verifies normalized media bytes and writes the private `magazine-issue.json` into the same edition pack.

## Verification status

Draft only. Tests are authored but have **not** been executed in this environment; GitHub Actions previously failed before runner allocation (runner_id=0). No complete Astro build, Chromium browser review, live enterprise input, current real media grant, paid model call or public deployment is claimed.

The adapter creates a private draft only. Existing media rights checks, AI image review, full-page visual review, RFQ backend and publication gates remain mandatory.

author: hamb3r
body:
### Motivation

In `vktSubgroupsBuiltinVarTests.cpp`, every compute, mesh, and task shader writes `uvec4 result[]` (16 bytes per element) and all four compute/mesh validation callbacks (`checkComputeSubgroupSize`, `checkComputeSubgroupInvocationID`, `checkComputeNumSubgroups`, `checkComputeSubgroupID`) read `data[offset * 4 + {0..3}]`.

In all four `switch (caseDef.testType)` branches inside `test()`, the `requiredSubgroupSize == false` path correctly passes `VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32A32_UINT` to `makeComputeTest` / `makeMeshTest`, whereas the `requiredSubgroupSize == true` loop right below passed `VK_FORMAT_R32_UINT` (4 bytes per element). This did not trigger out-of-bounds writes today only because `makeComputeOrMeshTestRequiredSubgroupSize` currently overallocates the result buffer to `maxSubgroupSize^3 * elementSize`, which masks the 4x element-size mismatch.

### Changes

1. **`vktSubgroupsBuiltinVarTests.cpp`**: Pass `VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32A32_UINT` instead of `VK_FORMAT_R32_UINT` to `subgroups::makeComputeTest` and `subgroups::makeMeshTest` in all four `requiredSubgroupSize == true` branches (`TEST_TYPE_SUBGROUP_SIZE`, `TEST_TYPE_SUBGROUP_INVOCATION_ID`, `TEST_TYPE_SUBGROUP_NUM_SUBGROUPS`, `TEST_TYPE_SUBGROUP_NUM_SUBGROUP_ID`), matching the shader output type (`uvec4`), host check functions, and `requiredSubgroupSize == false` paths.

### Results

Verified clean builds of `deqp-vk` and `deqp-vksc` (`-DCTS_USES_VULKANSC`), zero `scripts/src_util` issues, and `dEQP-VK.subgroups.builtin_var.*` runs with `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`:

| Test Group | Mesa `dzn` (`NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080` / `AMD Radeon RDNA2, Ryzen 7 7700`) | Native Windows Drivers (`NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080` / `AMD Radeon RDNA2, Ryzen 7 7700`) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| `dEQP-VK.subgroups.builtin_var.compute.*_requiredsubgroupsize` (4 cases) | 4/4 Pass / 4/4 Pass (0 VUID) | 4/4 Pass / 4/4 Pass |
| `dEQP-VK.subgroups.builtin_var.compute.*` (all 8 cases) | 8/8 Pass / 8/8 Pass (0 VUID) | 8/8 Pass / 8/8 Pass |
| `dEQP-VK.subgroups.builtin_var.mesh.*_requiredsubgroupsize` (8 cases) | N/A (`NotSupported`) / N/A (`NotSupported`) | 8/8 Pass / N/A (`NotSupported`) |
| `dEQP-VK.subgroups.builtin_var.mesh.*` (all 16 cases) | N/A (`NotSupported`) / N/A (`NotSupported`) | 16/16 Pass / N/A (`NotSupported`) |
| **Total `dEQP-VK.subgroups.builtin_var.*` (36 cases)** | **14/14 supported Pass (RTX) / 8/8 compute Pass (AMD, 4 pre-existing geometry/graphics fails)** | **36/36 Pass (RTX) / 20/20 supported Pass (AMD)** |

author: toranek
body:
### What
`std::_Getloctxt` returned -2 ("no candidate") immediately for any table whose first character is NUL: `GetLocaleText` had `if (sep == TChar{}) return -2;`. That is the table Dinkumware's `num_get::do_get(bool&)` builds to read a `boolalpha` value: a NUL mark, the false name, a NUL mark, the true name, passed with a field count of 2 (`"\0false\0true"`). So a title's `stream >> std::boolalpha >> flag` could not match either name through this export.

For a table with a visible mark, the function counts the marks, adds them to the count argument and takes each mark as the start of a field. The reading of firmware 13.42's module in [#22452](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/22452#issuecomment-6971241155) describes the same routine without a special case for NUL: every occurrence of the first character is counted up to the terminator (none, when the mark is NUL, so the count is the argument alone), and the field walk "stops at the NUL" and then reads the character at that position plus the column. With a NUL mark that walk lands on each NUL in turn, which is where each field starts.

This PR does that: for a NUL-marked table the field count comes from the argument and each field starts at the next NUL. The matching (ASCII case folded on both sides, longest field wins, -1 when the input ends inside a longer field) is the existing code, unchanged, and tables with a visible mark take the same path as before. An empty table with a count of 0 still returns -2.

Not run against the module: #22452 ran only `:`- and `,`-marked tables natively. The new debt entry says so and what closes it.

### Tested
Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 2024 (10.0.26100), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`.

- 16 cases added to `CheckGroup6Getloctxt` in `core/libs/tests/GuestLibcInternalTimeGetFields.cpp`, each checking the result and the first unread character: `false`, `true`, `TRUE`, `False`, `truex`, `false 1`, the incomplete `tru` and `f` (-1), `trux` (-1, `x` left), `yes` (-2, nothing consumed), the table with a count of 0 and of 1, and a table whose first field is empty (`"\0\0on"`).
- Red: with the new test file on the parent commit (#23988), `guest_libc_internal_time_get_fields` fails at `_Getloctxt NUL-marked table result`.
- Green: with the fix, `ctest -R "^guest_libc_internal_(time|locale|facet|num|ctype|collate|messages|money)"` passes 13 of 13 after a full rebuild.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` and `python tools/debt_fold.py --check` pass.
- `python tools/pr_overlap.py --branch fix/libscelibcinternal-getloctxt-nul-marked-tables` (2018 open) reports only the two textual neighbours of the parent commit, #22462 and #23809 (see #23988); neither touches the field table this PR changes.
- This branch is stacked on #23988, so until that one merges the diff here shows both commits.

### Checklist
- [x] Based on current `main`; no other open PR implements the same functions
- [x] One topic per PR; follow-ups go in a new PR
- [x] No comments in code except [technical debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md) and the licence notice of code adapted from upstream (see AGENTS.md)
- [x] Unimplemented paths throw (`NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`); silent stubs are listed under Silent stubs in their library's [technical debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/tree/main/docs/dev/debt) file
- [x] No notes, investigation `.md` files or images added to the repository (attach them to this PR)
- [x] New third-party code is a submodule built from source
- [x] Generic behaviour, not specific to one title
- [x] Depends on: #23988
- [x] Fixes: none
- [x] Unblocks: none
- [x] GPUs tested: n/a
- [x] AI-assisted: yes

author: harisgenjac
body:
Second of two PRs that rebuild the restaurant home page to `design/restaurant-home/home.dc.html` (the first was #136). This one covers parts 6–10.

## What changes
- **"Naruči sada po nižoj cijeni":** new `GET /api/products/home` (RESTAURANT) loads all rows in one request.
  - Up to 3 stores with offers right now: the restaurant's favourites first, then the nearest stores. "Nearest" uses the two map pins, or the cities when either pin is missing. A store with no offers is never shown.
  - Each row: logo, name, "city · pin distance" (only the city without both pins), the "dio <company>" chip for a branch, and "Sve (N) →" to the store page.
  - Each row shows the store's 4 offers that expire soonest. "+" opens the existing `AddToCartModal`; the card itself opens the product page. Cards are 4, 2 or 1 per row depending on the width.
- **"Od police do vaše kuhinje":** the light green card with the three green illustrations. The highlighted phrases use i18n `Trans` tags.
- **Donation band:** the warm full-width band with the Barlow Condensed heading, "Doniraj obrok" → `/donate-food` and "Budi sponzor" → `/sponsor`.
- **New footer, on every page of every role (login pages too):**
  - Arch, background drawings, logo, info links, social icons, legal bar and "© <year>".
  - The links are kept in one config list with a TODO. They render as links that don't navigate for now.
  - The footer now comes after `<main>`, not inside it, so screen readers treat it as the page footer. On the home page the arch overlaps the donation band.
- **Removed:**
  - The old footer, `GET /api/stats/impact` (only the old footer's counter used it) and the `__APP_VERSION__` define.
- **Docs:** frontend, backend, product and the development plan updated. The plan's footer item now lists all the placeholder pages and accounts.

## Tests
- Server: new `homeOffers.test.ts` (favourites first, fill-up with nearest by pins then city, no store without offers, 4 soonest-expiring offers, N count, chain chip and logo, roles). `stats.test.ts` and `companies.test.ts` updated.
- Client: dashboards (rows, distance or city only, chip, "Sve (N)", expiry colours and texts, prices, "+" opening the dialog, hidden when empty or on error, how it works, donation band), Footer, login page footer.
- E2E, run locally in Chromium and WebKit: `restaurant-home.spec.ts` (all sections in order, "+" opens the quantity dialog, a card opens the product, the footer on `/my-orders`), the whole `mobile-layout.spec.ts` (375 px: rows, steps and footer stack, no sideways scroll), `contrast.spec.ts` (axe AA on the home page) and `first-login.spec.ts`.

author: zkochan
body:
<!-- A maintainer will only start reviewing once CodeRabbit has approved and
CI is green. Please wait for those to pass before expecting human review. -->

## Summary

Closes zkochan/pnpm-tasks#151.

Fixes two cache-scoping and grant-invalidation bugs in `pnpr`'s resolver (`0.1.0-alpha.21`) that allowed unauthorized callers without `read` grants to verify and resolve private hosted or proxied packages:

1. **`VerdictCache` (`lockfile-verdicts.sqlite`) ignored caller private-route `Footprint`:**
   - Previously, `POST /-/pnpr/v0/verify-lockfile` and `POST /-/pnpr/v0/resolve` (when verifying an input lockfile, including `frozenLockfile: true`) keyed `VerdictCache` solely on `(hash_lockfile(&lockfile), merged_policy)` without recording or checking the private-route `Footprint` (`PrivateAccessDescriptor`). Once an authorized caller (`alice`) verified a lockfile referencing a private hosted package, `past_verdict_trusted` short-circuited `verify_input_lockfile` to `Ok(None)` before any route check ran, returning `200 OK` (`type: "done"`, including the full routed lockfile on frozen `resolve`) to unauthorized callers (`bob`).
   - Consolidated `lockfile_verdicts` in place to `(hash, footprint_key, footprint, policy, epoch, verified_at_ms)` with `PRIMARY KEY (hash, epoch, footprint_key)` (allowing distinct private upstream alias footprints for the same lockfile hash to coexist up to `MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_HASH = 8` without cross-epoch overwrites or evictions).
   - Every lookup filters by `(hash, epoch)`, validates the row's HMAC `footprint_key`, and enforces `footprint.allows(route_context, identity)` before consulting `can_trust_past_check`.
   - On a `VerdictCache` hit during `POST /-/pnpr/v0/resolve`, the request's `Footprint` is extended with the matched cached `Footprint` so warm non-frozen resolves still record private footprints into `ResolverCache`.

2. **Revoking public `read` grants left stale public resolutions, verdicts, and mirror fallbacks active:**
   - Previously, when a hosted or upstream registry had `$all` or `$anonymous` `read`, `ResolverCache` and `VerdictCache` stored entries with `footprint.is_public() == true` and `pnpm-resolving-npm-resolver` wrote packuments to the unscoped public on-disk mirror. Revoking public `read` via `PUT`/`DELETE /-/pnpr/v0/admin/grants/{name}` or `pnpr grants import` updated `PackageRules` in place without invalidating `ResolverCache` or `VerdictCache`, and `RouteHook::metadata_scope` still classified denied own-origin packages as `MetadataCacheScope::Public` (enabling exact-version disk shortcuts and `disk_fallback` after `404`).
   - Updated `reload_grants` to wrap rule application, grant publication, and `ResolverShared::forget_results()` in an atomic transition sequence on `GrantState` (`stable_generation`), clearing `ResolverCache::entries`, clearing `VerdictCache`, advancing `ResolverCache::generation`, and bypassing cached verdicts across the reload window.
   - Bound `VerdictCache` rows to `(graph_generation, grants_generation)` so offline `pnpr grants import` or `pnpr registries import` invalidates persisted SQLite verdicts across server restarts.
   - Updated `RouteHook::metadata_scope` (`RouteContext::is_denied_own_package`) to isolate denied own-origin package routes into a caller-specific private scope rather than `MetadataCacheScope::Public`.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Fix two cache-scoping and grant-invalidation bugs in `pnpr`'s resolver:

1. Scope `VerdictCache` (`lockfile-verdicts.sqlite`) by private-route
   `Footprint` and `(graph, grants)` epoch:
   - Consolidate `lockfile_verdicts` to `(hash, footprint_key,
     footprint, policy, epoch, verified_at_ms)` with primary key
     `(hash, epoch, footprint_key)`.
   - Filter lookups by `(hash, epoch)`, verify the row's HMAC
     `footprint_key`, and require `Footprint::allows` for the caller's
     identity before trusting the stored policy snapshot.
   - Extend the request's `Footprint` with the matched cached verdict's
     `Footprint` on `VerdictCache` hits during `POST /-/pnpr/v0/resolve`
     so warm non-frozen resolves still record private footprints into
     `ResolverCache`.
   - Gate `LocalRegistry::verdict_epoch` with an atomic transition
     sequence on `GrantState` so concurrent verifications bypass cached
     verdicts and skip recording while `reload_grants` is in progress.

2. Invalidate cached resolutions, verdicts, and public mirror fallback
   when grants change:
   - Update `reload_grants` to call `ResolverShared::forget_results()`,
     clearing `ResolverCache::entries`, clearing `VerdictCache`, and
     advancing `ResolverCache::generation` (pinned up front before
     fetches so pre-revocation resolves in flight cannot populate
     post-revocation keys).
   - Bind `VerdictCache` rows to `(graph_generation, grants_generation)`
     so offline `pnpr grants import` or `pnpr registries import`
     invalidates persisted verdicts across server restarts.
   - Isolate denied own-origin package routes from
     `MetadataCacheScope::Public` in `RouteHook::metadata_scope` so
     unauthorized callers cannot hit exact-version shortcuts or
     `disk_fallback` against packuments cached while `$all` or
     `$anonymous` read was active.

Closes zkochan/pnpm-tasks#151.
```

body:
## What it does Fixed Pest failures around midnight UTC in the customer segmentation and Dashboard Visitors API tests. The failures occurred in SQLite with PHP 8.6 and PostgreSQL 15 with PHP 8.5. The patch changes only tests. ## How it works The order and registration datasets share their date cutoffs with their assertions. The birthday cases read the expected month and day from the customer created for the case. This keeps the expected value aligned with the fixture if Pest discovers the test before midnight and runs it after midnight. The dashboard test records the UTC date of its two visits. Its summary and trend assertions use the dates observed before and after the request. A visit created a minute before the test starts can belong to the previous UTC day and still appear in the other visitor metrics. The [segmentation failures](https://github.com/MahoCommerce/maho/actions/runs/44642065959) and the [visitor failure](https://github.com/MahoCommerce/maho/actions/runs/44640391651/job/135969823500) came from files shared with `main`. With a controlled clock, the original tests reject the date boundaries and the candidate accepts the matching fixtures. The five affected segmentation cases also completed with 117 passing assertions on an isolated SQLite store under PHP 8.6.0. ## Good to know The local Pest process exited with code 1 after writing JUnit because the browser plugin could not open a socket in the network-denied sandbox. The dashboard date check used a controlled clock and a response double. CI covers the installed API. ## Release notes Nothing to note. > [!NOTE] > **Developed with the help of AI.**

author: handfooled
body:
## Why
After the Gemini/Antigravity A/B test, the next Always UI improvement is **numeric consistency**. Borrow the constrained-scale approach from publicly available Refactoring UI Skill implementations while retaining Always UI's product-first, anti-template positioning.

## Changes
- **New `references/value-presets.md`** with seven grouped table sections:
  A. spacing and fixed geometry; B. typography (size/weight/line-height/measure); C. borders, radii, icons, control heights, z-layers; D. opacity/color stops; E. optional 5-level elevation/shadows; F. motion durations; G. responsive breakpoints.
- `SKILL.md`: in **design mode**, choose fixed values from these category tables rather than inventing `17px` padding, `23px` gaps, one-off shadows, or arbitrary Tailwind `[...]` values. Put choices in reusable named design tokens.
- `references/design-archetypes.md`: add numeric decisions to layout handoff.
- `references/check-catalog.md`: detect numeric drift relative to the project's system, without mislabeling coherent pre-existing tokens as errors.
- `README.md` and `README.zh-CN.md`: one compact reference link to the new tables, retaining the Owner-approved copy.
- `tests/evaluation-cases.md`: nine regression cases (P01–P09) for proper fallback use, existing-token precedence, accessibility, image geometry, and no invented numbers.
- `scripts/validate.py`: verify the new reference, seven categories, representative allowed values, and test cases.

## Value priority (important)
1. **Existing project tokens / component library / platform rules win** even if their numbers differ.
2. Where absent, choose from Always UI's categorized preset tables.
3. Nonpreset numbers require a justified external/asset, accessibility, user-specified, intrinsic/content-driven or platform constraint. Document exceptions as intentional tokens, not ad-hoc literals.
4. Do not force a color palette, generic radius aesthetic, extra shadows, or fixed widths in intrinsically fluid layouts.

## Provenance
Numerical scale *concepts* and common spacing/type examples were cross-checked against [s0xDk/refactoring-ui-skill](https://github.com/s0xDk/refactoring-ui-skill/blob/main/SKILL.md); existing-token precedence aligns with the approach described in [edisonmbli/refactoring-ui-skill](https://github.com/edisonmbli/refactoring-ui-skill/blob/main/skills/refactoring-ui/SKILL.md). Always UI's radii, controls, motion and breakpoint lists are curated choices, not claims that those sources mandate them. No dependency on Refactoring UI Skill is added.

## Validation
Branch file tree and categories checked; GitHub Actions validator must pass. Agent behavioral A/B tests remain **unexecuted**.

Owner review/merge only; do not auto-merge.

body:
## Weapon aim and mobility

Implements A7 and A8 on the PR #10 attack foundation. The Action FSM owns the swing direction. A gold pointer shows it independently of the center facing marker. F3 shows the current aim state and ordinary speed multiplier. M2 Option B keeps every attack phase interruptible by a successful dodge.

| Weapon | Direction | Wind-up | Active | Recovery |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Dagger | Tracks, corrects at up to 180 degrees/s during Active, holds in Recovery | 0.90x | 0.85x | 0.95x |
| One-handed sword | Locks when Active begins | 0.80x | 0.65x | 0.85x |
| Greatsword | Locks at 75% of Wind-up (240 ms) | 0.60x | 0.40x | 0.70x |

All values are provisional. Ordinary movement uses time spent in each phase when a tick crosses boundaries. The movement FSM retains velocity and collision ownership.

## Static validation

Reviewed the diff against merged PR #10, including phase timing, one aim sample per tick, signed shortest-path correction, repeat initialization, buffer expiry, switch eligibility, and successful and failed dodge paths. Resource paths, script UID continuity and documentation links checked. Both working and staged whitespace checks passed. Index and working-tree metadata checks each reported zero errors and zero informational findings. Godot execution and owner acceptance are pending independent diff review.

## Owner runtime acceptance

- [ ] Dagger tracks mouse aim through Wind-up.
- [ ] Dagger corrects direction gradually during Active, including across the angle wrap.
- [ ] Sword locks at Active start and holds through Recovery.
- [ ] Greatsword locks during late Wind-up and holds through Recovery.
- [ ] The facing marker follows the mouse after attack aim locks and retains its heading in the four-pixel dead zone.
- [ ] The gold pointer reflects Action FSM direction and disappears in Ready.
- [ ] Dagger remains relatively mobile during attacks.
- [ ] Sword has moderate movement penalties.
- [ ] Greatsword has the strongest movement penalties.
- [ ] Ordinary movement returns to full speed after attacks.
- [ ] A successful dodge interrupts each weapon in every phase, clears pending input and releases aim.
- [ ] Dodge speed, trajectory, collision and early invulnerability match PR #10.
- [ ] A failed dodge preserves the attack, its aim and valid input.
- [ ] Holding repeats with fresh aim, and a valid late buffered tap starts one more swing.
- [ ] Switching succeeds while Ready and is blocked during attacks and dodge movement.
- [ ] F3 shows the actual aim state and phase movement multiplier.
- [ ] Repeating, releasing and interrupting attacks leave no stuck state or movement penalty.

body:
Published copy of the kine-pod change (viewer/gait_viewer_12.html). Merging publishes it at https://nabilrashidd.github.io/kine-viewer/.

Adds a second live pod to the main viewer: both feet in 3D, with dead reckoning, plots, metrics, checks and recording for each pod.

**How to use:** connect one pod as before, then press **Add Kine-Left** (or Kine-Right). The picker only offers the other side's pod. Stand still with the feet parallel and press **Zero / level**; it zeroes both pods.

**Per pod**
- **3D shoe:** left is blue, right is orange, and the view is from behind so left is on the left. Without dead reckoning each shoe sits on a fixed point 18 cm apart. With dead reckoning each shoe moves by its own pod's position and leaves its own trail, and the camera follows the point between them.
- **Plots:** acceleration and gyro x/y/z side by side on one y-scale.
- **Step metrics:** each cell shows left / right (cadence, contact, flight, stride, steps, peak |a|, toe-off rate).
- **Trust checks:** packets, gravity, stance anchor, stride length, cadence, microphone, mic vs IMU contact, landings confirmed. The not-tracked / coasting badge names the shoe.
- **Recording:** every button acts on both pods: record to this device, record on the pods, sync, mark, the session list with Download per pod, and erase after a second tap. File names carry the side (`kine_…_left_…` / `…_right_…`).
- **Commands to both pods:** Zero, Recalibrate, Reset position, Auto / Gait / In hand.
- **LED ring:** commands go to whichever pod is the right one, the one with the ring.

**Still first pod only:** fatigue watch, last-step panel, gait timeline, angle bars, |a| / sagittal strips.

**Layout:** the view buttons and the per-foot readout sit at the bottom of the 3D view, and the scene is centred above them. The Pose-from-a-photo and LED ring panels are at the bottom of the side panel.

**Limits:**
- Each pod counts yaw, and so the direction its position runs in, from its own Zero. The two shoes agree only after a joint Zero, and they drift apart over time.
- With one pod, the page behaves as before apart from the new button and the moved controls.
- The previous file is kept as `viewer/gait_viewer_12_one_pod.html` (published as `index_one_pod.html`).

**Also fixed:** after connecting, the plots and the trail kept up to 6 s of synthetic-runner samples (21 g spikes).

**Testing:** done in headless Chrome only, at wide, tablet and phone sizes. A fake Web Bluetooth served two pods with the firmware's packet layouts (motion, status, live, odom, acoustic, stride, record, NUS), and a stand-in relay was used. Checked: the picker filter and side detection; both shoes moving with dead reckoning; both plot columns; left / right metrics; second-pod checks; Zero / Reset to both; record to this device producing two files; the list and CRC-checked downloads from both pods; erase on both; LED routing with either pod connected first; reconnecting (no doubled packets); a failed connect; the follower screen; 60 fps.

author: iainchesworth
body:
## Summary

Adds the licence library, `adl::licence` (`libs/licence`): the signed licence file, the states a licence is in, and the checks a program asks. It is slice 2 of the licensing plan. No program links it, nothing a program does depends on a licence, and it is not exported by the installed `adl` package. The library is built on desktop systems only.

- The signed envelope (Ed25519 over the format name, the purpose and the payload, so a signature made for one kind of file never passes as another), the payload with a signed `product` field, the eight states (`none`, `valid`, `expiring`, `grace`, `expired`, `not_yet_valid`, `clock_suspect`, `invalid`) each with a reason, `check(feature)`, the version window, computer names, the clock check, revocation lists and the plain words for them. It reads no file and no clock: the caller passes them in, so every state is tested.
- A strict JSON reader of its own. It refuses a repeated key, a comment, a trailing comma, bytes that are not UTF-8, a lone surrogate and nesting deeper than eight.
- `adl_licence_sign` and `adl_licence_test_keys`: signing, and the published RFC 8032 test key, for the tests and for the owner's tool later. No program links them.
- The trust list is empty. ARINC Data Loader has no signing key yet, so every licence is refused until the owner adds the public keys.
- `third_party/monocypher`: Monocypher 4.0.2, unmodified, for Ed25519. Its four files match the hashes Virtual Serial Studio records for the same files (they were not compared with the upstream archive again). It is C, so C is enabled for desktop builds and `third_party/` is left out of the count of preprocessor lines (decision 7). Its notice is written (`notices/fragments/monocypher.txt`) and is added to what the programs show in the change that first links the library.
- `.github/ci/plan.json` sorts `third_party/` as a build path (the gate did not know the directory). This is a change to the gate's own files, so this pull request makes the gate plan "machinery" and run every job.
- `docs/testing.md` has a row for each file of `tests/licence`.

## Terms

The library's own files (headers, sources, the strict JSON reader, the Ed25519 wrapper, the build files, the fuzz harness and its seeds, `tests/licence`, and the golden data) carry `SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later OR BSD-2-Clause`: they are offered under either licence, so that software kept outside this repository can use the same code at a pinned commit.

- Monocypher keeps its own terms (BSD-2-Clause or CC0-1.0). `REUSE.toml` now gives its four sources that and nothing else; before, the catch-all entry added the GPL to a report on them.
- The Wycheproof test vectors are Apache-2.0, unchanged.
- Nothing outside the library changes its terms.
- The library includes nothing from this repository: only the C++ standard library, Monocypher and its own headers (no `adl::platform`). The tests took one GPL-only helper, `tests/support/bytes.hpp`, for a hexadecimal decoder; they now have a decoder of their own. A directory holding only `libs/licence`, `third_party/monocypher`, `tests/licence` and `tests/golden/golden_licence.hpp` builds with plain `g++` and passes the tests (see below).
- `docs/licensing.md` says all of this.

## Format choices that freeze at the first real licence

These are in the code and not in the plan. The Virtual Serial Studio side has to take the same ones before it issues anything.

1. The signed message begins `ICL-SIGNED-FILE-1`, then a zero byte, the purpose, a zero byte and the payload.
2. Every licence carries a signed `product` field (`adl` here). A licence for another product is refused with the reason `wrong_product`.
3. A feature name may contain `_` (`data_packs` needs it). Virtual Serial Studio's own rule does not allow it.
4. The reader takes any licence number of upper-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 64 characters, and does not check its shape. `licence_id_prefix` (`ADL-`) is in `product.hpp` for the owner's tool, which is what writes `ADL-<year>-<six digits>`. The library is shared between products and the signed `product` field is what ties a licence to one of them, so a shape rule in the reader would freeze for no gain. A test holds this.

## Test plan

Checked on this branch (`develop` 22b52e4 merged in with no conflicts; `develop` merged again at 255d501, with one conflict in `CMakeLists.txt` where both sides added a block, which are both kept; and at 97c8b3e, no conflict). The local runs below were made at the first merge, and the stand-alone build and the Windows run of `adl_licence_tests` again after the last change (a test that the reader takes any licence number, and the `docs/testing.md` rows):

- Windows, MSVC (Visual Studio 2026), `windows-msvc-debug`, libraries only (`-DADL_BUILD_APP=OFF`): **617 of 617** tests pass, at the merge of `develop` and again at the tip. The library's own tests are 54 Catch2 cases in `adl_licence_tests`, label `unit` (53 when these runs were made; the 54th is the licence number test, which passes on Windows and in the stand-alone build). The applications were built and all their tests run (688 of 688) on the branch for slice 3, which contains this one; nothing in the applications uses the library.
- A directory that holds only `libs/licence`, `third_party/monocypher`, `tests/licence` and `tests/golden/golden_licence.hpp`, built with plain `g++` 14.2 (`-std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wshadow -Werror`), the fuzz harness compiled as an object: all 54 cases pass (1699 assertions). This is the check that the library stands alone, and the set of files that a repository taking the library at a pinned commit needs.
- `tests/golden/make_golden_licence.py` writes `golden_licence.hpp` again byte for byte.
- `python3 tools/ci/precheck.py`: branch name, commit text, files text, preprocessor count, action pinning, `reuse lint` and `clang-format` (23.1.5, the pinned one) pass. The changelog check fails until the `no-changelog` label is on the pull request.
- WSL Debian, GCC 14.2, built under `/mnt/e`, libraries only (`-DADL_BUILD_APP=OFF`; there is no Qt 6.12 for GCC there): `linux-debug` and `linux-asan-ubsan`, on the merge of `develop` before the two-licence commit: 613 of 614 each, no warnings, no sanitizer report. The one failure is the conformance test "a datagram arrives whole with the address it came from" (an 8196-byte datagram over the loopback, WSL): it failed three times out of three when rerun alone, earlier runs of other branches record it too, and the licence library has no network code. Run again at the tip of this branch (1fe1930): the same, 613 of 614 on each, with the same single failure.
- The previous author measured coverage of `libs/licence` in WSL with the CI's gcovr switches: 97.6% of lines and 91.1% of branches. The gate is 90% and 80% over all the portable libraries together. Not measured again here.

The pull request's own checks, on the merge of `develop` 255d501 (all pass except CodeQL): Linux (GCC, Release), Linux (Clang, ASan and UBSan), Windows (MSVC, Release), macOS (AppleClang, Release), Coverage (Linux, GCC) with its gate, Fuzz regression (Linux, Clang) (`fuzz.regress.licence` passes: the harness builds with libFuzzer and its 11 seeds replay) and ClusterFuzzLite (address), the SBOM, the docs build, `clang-format`, `platform-isolation` and Policy.

CodeQL: the analysis passes, and its check fails with 4 alerts (`cpp/integer-multiplication-cast-to-long`) on `third_party/monocypher/monocypher.c` lines 338 to 341, in Monocypher's Poly1305 code, which this project does not call (only Ed25519 is used) and which is unmodified. CodeQL is not a required check, and the alerts are for the owner to triage in Security > Code scanning.

Not tested here:

- Monocypher against the upstream archive (the four files match the hash table of Virtual Serial Studio, and the table in `third_party/monocypher/README.md`).

body:
## Summary

Full support for color GenICam cameras, starting with the Chameleon3 CM3-U3-31S4C, on Spinnaker, Aravis and GenTL. Track: `conductor/tracks/color-cameras_20261119/`.

```diff
 GenICamCamera
   pixel_format choices
     Mono8, Mono16, RGB8, Bayer 8/16, Mono10g40IDS
+    Mono12Packed, Mono12p, Bayer{RG,GB,GR,BG}12Packed / 12p   -> uint16, low 12 bits
+    YCbCr8_CbYCr (H, W, 3), YCbCr422_8_CbYCrY (H, W, 2)        -> camera's bytes
+  settings (where the camera has them in its current format)
+    BalanceWhiteAuto            Off | Continuous
+    balance_ratio_red/blue      via BalanceRatioSelector, selector restored
+  color_filter                  "BayerRG" ... or None
   frame.metadata
+    color_filter, BalanceWhiteAuto, balance_ratio_red, balance_ratio_blue
     full_scale
+      CM3-U3-31S4C Mono16 -> 65504
```

```text
_PySpinBuffer.pixels
  fmt = pfnc_name(GetTLPixelFormat())   # GetPixelFormatName() says "YUV422Packed"
  if fmt is packed 12-bit or YCbCr422   # GetNDArray() refuses these (-1003)
    shaped_pixels(GetData())
  else
    GetNDArray().copy()
```

- `_PFNC` maps both the YCbCr codes and the older `YUV*` codes the camera actually sends.
- Ratios kept while `BalanceWhiteAuto` is `Off`: recording them costs ~1 ms per capture instead of ~5.
- `SimulatedCamera(color=True)` gains BayerRG8/16 (mosaicked), `color_filter`, and white balance.
- `el-devices preview`: `f` and `F` step through the camera's pixel formats while previewing (checked on the CM3-U3-31S4C: 0.15–0.21 s to the first new frame, region kept). YCbCr shows as its Y channel.
- Fakes: a CM3-U3-31S4C on every backend; fake Aravis now follows `pIsAvailable`.
- Docs: `spinnaker.md` (Pixel formats, Color), `usb3-vision.md`, `guide.md`, and `preview.md`, which recommends previewing color cameras in `RGB8` or YCbCr. `PreviewFrame` is unchanged.
- Follow-ups: #42 (processing controls), #43 (YCbCr411), #44 (`link_recoveries`).

## Evidence

- **Before:** the CM3-U3-31S4C offered 5 of its 10 formats; Mono12 and YCbCr were not choices, and frames said nothing about the mosaic or white balance.
  **After** (2026-11-19, static scene, all three backends):
  - Every format but YCbCr411 captures 60/60 through `el-devices spinnaker` and `el-devices genicam --backend aravis|gentl`.
  - `pytest -m hardware`: Spinnaker 39 passed, 1 skipped; Aravis and GenTL 38 passed, 1 skipped.
  - Mono12Packed / Mono12p vs `Mono16 >> 4`: correlation 0.997–0.999 (wrong layout: ~0.55).
  - White balance ratio 2 / 4 scales its channel ×2.01 / ×4.09 above the black-level pedestal.
  - RGB8 matches OpenCV's `COLOR_BayerBG2RGB` of BayerRG8 within noise while on-camera processing is at identity.
- **Fakes:** `pytest` 3359 passed. `tests/test_color_cameras.py` runs formats, `color_filter`, white balance, and the frame camera contract on the fake CM3 through all four backends. The 3 failing tests (`test_fake_pyspin.py` real-PySpin name checks, skipped in CI) fail identically on `main`.
- Ruff clean; mypy's 4 errors are the same as on `main`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive: new formats, settings and metadata keys. Reverting removes them.

**Blast Radius:** consumers

- Color cameras now list `BalanceWhiteAuto` and the two ratios; apps that render every setting (e.g. `pgs-scan`) will show them.
- `Mono12Packed` is now a choice where a camera has it, and a camera opened in it stays in it instead of being switched.
- The Spinnaker backend names a buffer's format by its PFNC code; a format outside `_PFNC` would now fail at capture, though the core only selects formats it maps.
- `GenICamHardwareTests.restore` now restores `pixel_format` first and skips settings the format lacks.

author: daniel-white
body:
## Problem

Two issues in the 0.3.0 release PR:

1. The model's `{"markdown": ...}` wrapper was committed verbatim into both `release-notes/0.3.0.md` and the generated artifact.
2. The model rewrote the notes from scratch and dropped user-facing changelog entries (Skill Signal, the About page feature) while promoting release plumbing (checksums, release jobs, build metadata) into the notes.

## Fix

- The release-please changelog is now the source of truth. Every user-facing item is numbered and sent to the model for rewording only; the markdown is rebuilt from the draft, so items cannot be added, dropped, or reordered.
- Empty, internal, or unsafe rewrites fall back to the original changelog text.
- JSON wrappers and code fences are unwrapped/rejected before anything is written, and `assertCleanMarkdown()` fails the job if artifacts survive.
- Internal commit scopes such as `**release-notes:**` are filtered; user-facing scopes like `**about:**` are stripped from the text.
- Internal-work filtering covers release jobs, checksums, signing, registries, and similar plumbing.

A regression test checks the real 0.3.0 changelog shape, and the pipeline keeps all three 0.3.0 features.

Merging this PR triggers `release-please.yml`, which rebases PR #17 onto the fixed `main` and regenerates its notes. Hold off on merging PR #17 until that regeneration lands.

## Testing

`./scripts/check.sh` passes (13 release-note tests, full gate).

author: webchang
body:
## Summary

On a KVM host with egress credentials on, the host agent built every self-serve template without `--egress-ca`, so the snapshot never trusted the host's TLS-interception CA and `install-host.sh` refused its worker ("does not trust this host's egress CA"). Self-serve templates could not use egress credentials. Closes #923.

## What changes

- `deploy/sbx/host-agent.sh`: when the host's credentials drop-in exists (`moca-egress.service.d/sbx-credentials.conf`, the same test `install-host.sh`'s `check_snapshot_ca` uses) and the claimed spec has `egress: true`, the build gets `--egress-ca <SBX_ENV_DIR>/egress/ca.crt`. A spec without egress is built as before (`template-build.sh` refuses `--egress-ca` there). With credentials on and no CA file, the claimed build is reported failed (`step: egress`) instead of being built into a snapshot the worker install would refuse.
- `SBX_UNIT_DIR` (default `/etc/systemd/system`, `install-host.sh`'s own setting and default) locates the drop-in; the paths mirror `install-host.sh`'s `egress_dropin` and `EGRESS_CRED_DIR`, with a comment naming them.
- Docs: the runbook's "The template host agent" says so, and the credential-injection procedure notes that a self-serve build claimed before `--egress` is built without the CA and needs a rebuild.

The CA is part of a build's identity: `egress_ca_sha256` is inside the version-2 manifest hash. So a build made with the CA is a new build, and self-serve egress templates a host already holds need a rebuild once credentials are turned on (or the CA rotated).

## Tests

`deploy/sbx/tests/host-agent.test.sh`, new section 3b, plus a check that the agent's drop-in and CA paths render the same strings as `install-host.sh`'s for the same `SBX_UNIT_DIR` and `SBX_ENV_DIR`:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| credentials on, spec `egress: true` | built without `--egress-ca` (FAIL) | built with `--egress-ca <host CA>` |
| credentials off | no `--egress-ca` | no `--egress-ca` |
| credentials on, spec `egress: false` | no `--egress-ca` | no `--egress-ca` |
| credentials on, no CA file | built (FAIL) | reported failed, `step: egress` |

The other `deploy/sbx` suites pass. On a slow machine, the existing start-time assertion in `host-agent.test.sh` (`"startSeconds":4[0-2]`) can read 43-44 and fail; that's the same on main and unrelated to this change.

Credentials count as on when the drop-in exists: the same predicate `check_snapshot_ca` uses at worker install, so the build and the install never disagree. Two things follow:

- **A window on a fresh host, closed by procedure.** The documented order creates the CA first and installs the drop-in last, so a self-serve build claimed in between lacks the CA and is refused at worker install. The runbook's credential procedure now says to stop `sbx-host-agent` (or let no build be queued) from creating the CA until the drop-in is in; such a build is rebuilt.
- **A known limit (follow-up).** The CA is inside the manifest hash, so a build made on one host is refused on a host with a different CA: egress builds are per host. That's the placement question #923 raised (should placement match a build only to hosts with its CA?), left for a follow-up.
- **Every egress build trusts the host's CA.** On a credentials host, every `egress: true` build now trusts that host's interception CA, including templates whose owners never store a credential. That's the intended trade: the CA's key stays on the host, and the proxy intercepts only a host:port the sandbox's owner has a credential for; everything else stays an opaque tunnel.

## 왜
병원 웹이 너무 복잡하다는 피드백을 받았습니다. 응급실은 종일 자기 시스템(EMR 현황판)을 보고 있으므로, 새 화면을 하나 더 주는 대신 **쓰던 화면 옆에 좁게 띄우는 채팅형 패널**을 추가합니다.

## 무엇이 바뀌나
- `hospital-ui/panel.html` (+ `panel.css`, `panel.mjs`, `panel-state.mjs`) 새 페이지입니다. 기존 `index.html`은 수정하지 않았습니다.
- 환자 한 명이 대화 하나입니다. 요약 카드 한 장과 버튼 세 개(수용 가능 · 확인 중 · 수용 불가)로 회신하고, 수용 불가는 사유 칩을 골라야 보내집니다.
- 확정 전에는 추가 질문과 구급대 답변을 말풍선으로 보여 줍니다. 확정 뒤에는 같은 대화에서 이송 대화, 수용 유지 · 수용 취소 요청, 환자 도착 확인을 처리합니다.
- 답해야 하는 건수를 탭 제목에 표시하고, 설정에서 브라우저 알림과 알림음을 켤 수 있습니다. iframe으로 넣은 화면에는 건수만 `postMessage`로 알립니다(환자 정보는 보내지 않음).
- 자원, 수용 제한, 운영 도구는 넣지 않았고 전체 병원 웹으로 가는 링크만 둡니다.
- 서버 API는 그대로입니다. 화면 서버(`team_chat_ui.py`)는 패널 파일 4개를 허용 목록에 넣고, 기존 병원 웹과 같은 메모리 저장소 어댑터를 붙입니다.

주소: `/hospital/panel.html?hid=H01`

## 검증
- `node --test quick119-pwa/tests/test_chat_intake.mjs tests/browser/test_hospital_*.mjs` 178건 통과 (패널 상태 계산 10건 추가)
- `test_app` · `test_team_chat` · `test_intake_chat` · `test_intake_commands` 80건 통과 (main 리베이스 전 실행). 리베이스 뒤에는 Node 전체와 패널 관련 실서버 테스트 3건을 다시 돌려 통과했습니다.
- 새 실서버 브라우저 테스트: 388px 창에서 추가 질문 → 답변 표시 → 수용 가능 → 확정 → 양방향 대화 → 도착 확인 → 다른 환자 수용 불가(사유)까지 누르고, 가로 넘침과 버튼 크기(44px 이상)를 확인합니다.

- 보고 있지 않은 환자 대화에 새 메시지가 와도 표시가 없습니다.

author: spd13
body:
Over Bluetooth, the plunger axis doesn't behave like it does over USB: it never settles at rest, and the quick release and its
delay don't apply. On a Linux host (SteamOS) the plunger at rest sent a value that wandered between about -33 % and -6 % of the axis,
with noise up to 9 % of the axis, so the plunger in the game kept twitching. Over USB the same plunger sends exactly 0 at rest.

### Cause

`BleController::processGamepadMode()` reads `plunger.getAdjustedValue()`, the reading mapped to the axis range. USB gets the value
`Plunger::plungerRead()` puts on its axis (`updateGamepadAxis()`), after the processing:

- 0 at rest, once the reading has stayed within `plungerMid` ± `plungerRestingDeadZone` for `restingStateMax`
  (with `disablePlungerWhenNotInUse`);
- 0 and the launch button after a quick release;
- the quick release delay (`getDelayedPlungerValue()`).

At rest the adjusted value is also a single ADC sample: the averaging (`plungerAverageRead`) only runs while the plunger moves, since USB
sends 0 then. Bluetooth sent that unaveraged sample.

### Fix

**BLE: report the same plunger value as the USB axis.** `Plunger` keeps the value it last put on the USB axis
(`getReportedValue()`), and the Bluetooth gamepad report sends it. The values are now the USB ones; only the timing differs (USB is
polled every 1 ms, Bluetooth sends a change at most every 8 ms, as before).

**BLE: send a full gamepad report when the host subscribes.** The first commit exposed an older issue. Gamepad reports only go out
when an input changes, and the previous values start at 0. With the plunger at exactly 0 at rest, the nudge centered and no button
pressed, a host that subscribes never gets a first report: it keeps the characteristic's empty value, which the heartbeat re-sends,
and reads the sticks as fully deflected until something moves. The noisy plunger used to hide this by changing on every pass.
`update()` now resets the remembered axes when the subscription starts, so the next pass sends every axis.

No report map change: hosts don't need to pair again.

### Testing

On a PinOne Mini in Bluetooth Xbox mode, connected to a Steam Frame (SteamOS, BlueZ), with these two commits on top of the pairing fix
of #9 (needed for Linux hosts) and of a Bluetooth DOF output report we haven't proposed yet (it doesn't touch the plunger or the
gamepad report):

- before: the plunger at rest sent a moving, noisy value on every report;
- with the first commit only: after connecting, the host only got empty 1-byte reports (the heartbeat) and the sticks read fully
  deflected, which the second commit fixes;
- with both: after connecting, full reports with every stick centered; plunger untouched for 30 s, the axis stays at exactly the
  center (400 raw reports in 10 s, all at 32768).

The branch also builds on its own on `main` (arduino-cli, esp32 core 3.3.6). Not tested yet: the own (non-Xbox) Bluetooth profile,
Windows, and the quick release over Bluetooth.

author: skandagatla-newrelic
body:
## Summary

Adds the `AZUREAPPSERVICEBYPRINCIPAL` candidate category, needed by beyond/azure-configuration-fetcher for NR-644487: **App Service / Function App → CONNECTS_TO → Event Hubs namespace across subscriptions**.

An app that sends to Event Hubs with a managed identity has the *Azure Event Hubs Data Sender* role on the namespace. That role assignment lives in the **namespace's** subscription, so when azure-configuration-fetcher processes the namespace it can see the assignment, but it only knows the identity's principal id, not the app's resource id. azure-configuration-fetcher tags each web and function app with its managed identities' principal ids (`azure.identity.principalId.1` … `.5`) and emits the app as a candidate with a `principalId` field; this rule resolves it.

| Setting | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `entityTypes` | `INFRA-AZUREWEBAPP`, `INFRA-AZUREFUNCTIONSAPP` | The `kind` that separates them isn't known from a role assignment |
| `attributeKeys` | `tags.azure.identity.principalId.1` … `.5` | One tag per identity (system-assigned plus user-assigned) |
| `collectorName` predicate | `tags.collector.name` | Only entities registered by auto-discovery |
| `onMultipleMatches` | `RELATE_ALL` | One user-assigned identity can be shared by several apps, and each of them can send |
| `onMiss` | `NO_OP` | A principal id is no basis for an uninstrumented entity |

Example candidate:
```json
{ "source": { "CANDIDATE": { "category": "AZUREAPPSERVICEBYPRINCIPAL",
      "fields": { "principalId": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "collectorName": "auto-discover" } } },
  "target": { "GUID": { "guid": "<event hubs namespace guid>", "type": "AZUREEVENTHUBNAMESPACE" } },
  "type": "CONNECTS_TO" }
```

A new, dedicated category (rather than a lookup added to `AZUREAPPSERVICE.yml`), so a `principalId`-only candidate never reaches another rule's resource-id lookup — the same approach as #3375.

## Impact
- **No live candidates affected.** Nothing emits this category until the azure-configuration-fetcher PR deploys.
- **Release order:** release this before that PR is deployed. Until then its candidates have no rule and are dropped: no edges, no placeholders.
- **Data:** the matched tags hold managed-identity principal ids (object ids of service principals). They aren't credentials, but they are identity metadata on entities.

## Validation
`npm run check` (validator) passes locally via `docker compose run --rm --build validate-definitions`.

## Rollback
Revert this PR. Without the rule, the candidates simply don't match.

## Summary

Warm solve of effects stage allocates less and hashes keys faster. Facts stay identical.

```diff
 trace / beneath / deep / escaping
-  contents(flow, origin)            # new vector per walked object
-  get(heap, origin, Dict())         # empty default table per miss
+  foreach_content(visit, flow, origin)
+  slot(flow, origin, step)          # nothing on miss
 map_nodes
-  map_node(Fresh) -> new table per node per call
+  site.fresh -> one table per call site
-  caller_doubt per target
+  caller_doubt once per node
 beneath(flow, objects)
+  no fresh origin -> return objects (no copy)
 hash(Step / Root / Place / Origin / Node)
-  Moshi derived: generic array hash, module by object id
+  variant tag, then each field; steps in a loop
```

- **Facts:** sorted facts dumps identical before and after on Distances, DataStructures and JSON (methods, spots, bang lines).

|---|---|---|

author: wesm
body:
Embedded PostgreSQL vaults now have a numbered upgrade history. Version 1 captures the catalog used for fresh initialization and restore. The schema owner upgrades an existing vault explicitly through `SetupPostgres` after closing it. Initialization, restore, and runtime opening require an existing catalog to be current.

Each upgrade commits the schema changes and their history together. CI compares fresh and migrated catalogs and verifies that a failure in a later migration rolls back earlier changes and their history. Builds from the same commit use the same migration bytes across Git checkout settings.

Fingerprint-only development catalogs are outside the numbered history. Keep their data through a portable backup and restore into a fresh versioned catalog.

Model used: GPT-6

author: arclabs561
body:
The history writer uses `+00:00` and the CLI examples use `Z`. With the documented `Z` lower bound and an upper bound three nanoseconds past midnight, the CLI returned none of the three matching entries. The rebuilt CLI now reads the same index and returns all three in order: `d2`, `d1`, `d3`.

Parse RFC 3339 bounds and order matching entries by instant. SQLite still narrows the search using its timestamp index (or the backend/timestamp index). The exact comparison happens in Rust, where nanoseconds survive. Date-only and other legacy bounds keep their lexical behavior. Existing indexes and JSONL files need no rewrite.

The new test fails on the old implementation. All 20 history tests passed in a targeted harness. The cases cover both stores, offsets across midnight, equal instants, inclusive endpoints, backend filters, and the ends of the four-digit year range.

Closes #170.

author: trungnghia112
body:
## What this changes

`e2e/demo-visibility.spec.ts` waits until the browser's application has taken a demo page over before it reads any geometry. One file, a test; no library code.

## Why

The release run [44665604661](https://github.com/anguless-com/angulux/actions/runs/44665604661) stopped at the browser gate: `.p-colorpicker-hue-handle — goes red when .p-colorpicker-hue clips` failed on a commit that had passed it three times (the pull request, `main`, and the dry-run). Nothing was published.

The showcase is rendered on the server. A page's sections are visible before the browser's own application has started, and until it has, no component stylesheet is in the document. Recorded frame by frame over parallel loads of `/colorpicker`:

| time after navigation | hue handle | `ngh` markers | `<style>` elements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| about 80 ms | 0 by 0, `position: static` | 12 | 4 |
| about 590 ms | 21 by 10, `position: absolute` | 0 | 8 |

The spec read geometry as soon as the sections were visible, so on a busy machine a read landed in that window. Repeating the one test 60 times in parallel on `main` failed 23 times, and 32 on a second go: most with the handle at zero size, one with the planted clip gone again, which is what the release run saw.

`openModule` now also waits until no `ngh` marker is left. Angular removes each marker as it takes a server-rendered view over, so none left means the page being measured is the page a reader would use.

Nothing is loosened: the wait is one more condition on top of the existing ones, and a page that never finishes fails on it by name.

---

## Provenance attestation (required)

By submitting this pull request I confirm that:

- [ ] This contribution contains **no code, documentation, test fixtures or generated
      output derived from PrimeNG 22 or later**, from any PrimeNG LTS release, or from
      `@primeuix/*` / `primeicons` releases past the MIT boundary recorded in
      `PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] It contains **no content copied from primeng.dev or primefaces.org**. The
      documentation site is not covered by the MIT grant, even though the library code is.
- [ ] If I used an **AI coding assistant**, I reviewed its output for the above and I take
      responsibility for it as if I had written it by hand. (Assistants have post-MIT
      PrimeNG in their training data and will reproduce it without saying so — this is the
      likeliest way the rule gets broken.)

## Evidence

- The one test, `--repeat-each=60`, on `main`: 37 of 60, then 28 of 60. With this change: 60 of 60.
- The whole of `demo-visibility.spec.ts` with this change: 56 of 56, so no demo page keeps a marker forever.
- The rest of the browser gate is left to CI on this pull request.

## Release

Nothing is published by merging: a `test` commit releases nothing. The `22.6.10` release is run again after this merges.
