author: quanvu309
body:
## Summary

The landing page favicon looked too light in browser tabs because `apps/site/public/favicon-art.svg` stayed on `3.063` and `2.188` strokes after the rest of the AirDesign marks moved to `7` and `5`. On further inspection, `apps/web/public/apple-touch-icon.png` was also still rendered from the thin `3.063` and `2.188` mark, and `apps/site` lacked PNG, home-screen, and ICO fallbacks.

This change updates `apps/site/public/favicon-art.svg` to `7` and `5`, re-renders `apple-touch-icon.png` at the weighted `7` and `5` mark, shares all four icon files and `_headers` rules between `apps/site` and `apps/web`, links the PNG and touch icons in `apps/site/src/site/site-document.astro`, and pins icon parity and ink weight in tests.

```diff
 apps/site/src/site/site-document.astro
+  <link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="32x32" href="/favicon-32.png" />
+  <link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/apple-touch-icon.png" />
   <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon-art.svg" />

 apps/site/public/
   favicon-art.svg        stroke-width 3.063/2.188 -> 7/5
+  favicon-32.png         32x32 weighted PNG fallback
+  apple-touch-icon.png   180x180 weighted home-screen icon
+  favicon.ico            32x32 ICO fallback
+  _headers               image Content-Type rules

 apps/web/public/
   apple-touch-icon.png   re-rendered from 7/5 mark (6.7% -> 13.7% ink)
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Serving the built `apps/site` landing page in Chromium returned `/favicon-art.svg` with strokes `3.063` and `2.188`, producing `10.2%` ink coverage at 16px, and had no PNG, Apple touch, or ICO fallbacks. `apps/web/public/apple-touch-icon.png` had `6.7%` ink coverage from the old thin strokes. Adding the parity and ink-weight assertions failed 6 of 10 tests.
- **After:** Rebuilding and serving `apps/site` returned HTTP 200 for `/favicon-32.png` (`image/png`, 1264 bytes), `/apple-touch-icon.png` (`image/png`, 4098 bytes, `13.7%` ink coverage), `/favicon-art.svg` (`image/svg+xml`, 376 bytes, strokes `7` and `5`, `22.8%` ink coverage at 16px across light and dark tabs), and `/favicon.ico` (`image/x-icon`, 1286 bytes). Running `vitest` on `apps/web/worker/favicon.test.ts` and `apps/site/src/site/airdesign-mark.test.ts` passed all 10 tests, `pnpm --filter @airdesign/site build` finished with 0 errors, and `pnpm land --check` passed.

## Before / after

![Landing and studio favicons before and after across light tab, dark tab, and home-screen icons](https://github.com/Rickvu309/AirDesign/releases/download/proof-4/pr-972-favicons-before-after-2e024fad80.png)

| main | this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Site SVG uses `3.063` and `2.188` strokes with `10.2%` ink at 16px, no PNG or ICO fallbacks on site, and `apple-touch-icon.png` uses thin strokes at `6.7%` ink | Site and studio serve identical weighted `7` and `5` SVG, 32px PNG, 180px `apple-touch-icon.png` at `13.7%` ink, and ICO icons with matching `_headers` |

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Reverting these icon assets and `<link>` tags restores the previous favicon setup.

**Blast Radius:** Isolated. Touches only static favicon assets, `_headers`, three `<link>` tags in `site-document.astro`, and two unit tests.

author: christianagbotah
body:
## Objective
Continue the Hubtel merchant cancellation safeguards from #190 and launch blocker #134. Investigation requests currently exist, but merchant operators can lose sight of older cases once a case disappears from the most-recent-50 checkout list. Keep the review trail available without inventing provider void/expiry guarantees.

## Added
- Authenticated GET `/v1/payments/hubtel/cancellation-investigations`: strict tenant/branch scope, `OWNER/ADMIN/MANAGER/ACCOUNTANT` role gate, `private no-store`, bounded `limit/offset` and validated `ALL/PENDING/PAID/OTHER` filter.

- Merchant MoMo reconciliation page: responsive case worklist, outcome filter, previous/next pagination and original stock-cost review drill-down. Remains visible even for older cases and after independent provider payment verification.
- Integration tests for 2-case pagination, pending vs paid reclassification, branch filtering, cross-tenant/anonymous denial, invalid filters, one settled cashbook entry and no cancellation. Frontend contract tests and operations runbook.

## Invariant
**Read-only reporting.** Neither a request nor an outcome filter cancels a checkout or releases stock or money. Provider-side guaranteed void, race-safe exact-once inventory/valuation/COGS reversals, and real merchant pilot remain separate blocking acceptance criteria for live POS collections. Gate merge/deploy on CI + Visual QA.

Fixes #406.

**Cause.** The suggested file name is `custom-<os>-` plus every mod id joined with `+`. With 25 mods that is ~250 characters; `patch.save` also writes `<name>.syx.map.json`, which goes past 255. In Pyodide 314.0.7 (the site's) that fails the build with `FileNotFoundError`, and the leftovers cannot be removed, so every later build fails in `shutil.rmtree(OUT)` with `OSError: [Errno 55] Directory not empty` until the page is reloaded. Both errors reproduced exactly in Node + pyodide 314.0.7.

- `gui.suggested_name` and `model.ts` `suggestedName`: past 96 characters of ids the name is `custom-<os>-<N>-mods.syx` (also helps the desktop app on Windows).
- `web/bridge.py` `_name`: a typed name is capped at 200 bytes so its companion files fit.
- `web/bridge.py` `build`: an output folder that cannot be emptied is moved aside (`/work/out-oldN`) instead of failing every build after it; checked in pyodide 314.0.7 that the next build then works.

author: teknium1
body:
Some providers report how many tokens a reply used in an unusual spot: inside the reply's first choice instead of at the top. Hermes only looked at the top, so on those providers every turn counted as 0 tokens. The token counters, the context-usage gauge and the "compress when the context gets full" trigger all read zero. Now Hermes reads the choice copy when the top-level one is missing.

**Source:** MoonshotAI/kimi-code#5017 ("preserve choice-level OpenAI token usage"). Kimi Code has had a Kimi-only version of this since its first release ("Moonshot may place usage in `choices[0].usage`"). #5017 moved it into the shared OpenAI decoder so every OpenAI-compatible provider gets it.

## What changes

`agent/usage_pricing.py::response_usage` returns `.usage`, or else `choices[0].usage` (top-level usage always wins). `hoist_choice_usage` moves it onto `.usage` for a non-streamed response. The OpenAI SDK keeps the choice copy as an untyped extra dict, which is why every `.usage` reader saw `None`. It is wired in at all four places a chat-completions response gets read:

| Path | Where |
|---|---|
| main turn, streamed | `chat_completion_helpers` chunk loop (`usage_obj`) |
| main turn, non-streamed | `_dispatch_nonstreaming_api_request` |
| auxiliary (titles, compression, vision…), plain | `_create_with_progress_once` (both plain-call branches) |
| auxiliary, streamed | `_ChatStreamAggregate.feed` |
| Codex / Responses wire | `_CodexResponseAssembler._on_terminal`: usage sent on the `response.completed` event itself, not inside its `response` object (same class; kimi-code#4485 restored this fallback in their Responses decoder) |

**Live repro.** Real `AIAgent.run_conversation` and real auxiliary calls against a loopback provider that reports `{"prompt_tokens": 1234, "completion_tokens": 56}` only inside `choices[0]`:

| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| main turn, streamed: session in / out / gauge | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1234 / 56 / 1234 |
| main turn, non-streamed | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1234 / 56 / 1234 |
| aux plain call `.usage.prompt_tokens` | `None` | 1234 |
| aux streamed call | `None` | 1234 |
| top-level usage 7 + choice usage 999 (precedence control) | n/a | 7 |
| Responses: usage only on the `response.completed` event | `None` | `{input_tokens: 3, output_tokens: 1}` (nested copy still wins when both exist) |

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_choice_level_usage.py` (new, 1 parametrized test): a real HTTP endpoint and a real `AIAgent` turn, streamed and non-streamed, assert session tokens and the gauge read 1234/56/1234. Red on `origin/main` (2 failed), green on head. Plus a Responses-assembler case: red on base, green on head.
- Local (fake HOME): usage-pricing, turn-usage log line, partial-stream, auxiliary-client suites and every test touching the four call sites: 585 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped. Every test touching `codex_runtime`: 851 passed / 0 failed / 8 skipped. `scripts/check --only health` ok (`auxiliary_client.py` stays at its 8,234-line ratchet).

**Not covered:** no live Moonshot/Kimi request. The stored `KIMI_API_KEY` returns 401 on all three Kimi hosts, and Moonshot's current public docs show top-level usage on the trailing `choices: []` chunk. That shape Hermes already handles and this PR leaves untouched. The choice-level shape is the one Kimi Code's own client has handled since its first commit, and that kimi-code#5017 widened to every OpenAI-compatible provider. Related open PR #52022 (DeepSeek v4 usage on content-bearing chunks + `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`) touches the same chunk read but is a different shape. The two compose.

## Infographic

![usage inside choices is counted](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab32cc1/30ZCfin6H1IdSx8zKTMXv_g7CbqWdI.png)

author: automancer-factory[bot]
body: ## What a visitor gets When a page on automancer.uk hits its first script error, the site lazily downloads Sentry to report it. Production served **all** of `@sentry/browser` for that: 423,059 B raw, 141.8 KB on the wire, including session replay, the feedback widget, the IndexedDB offline transport and sessionStorage-linked traces. None of these is enabled. The cause was `import('@sentry/browser').then((Sentry) => Sentry.init(…))`: taking the namespace stops Rollup tree-shaking a dynamic import. Naming the seven exports in the destructuring cuts the chunk to **90,703 B (31 KB gzip)**, and it no longer references any browser-storage API. Measured on production before the merge with the new `ops/perf/first-error.mjs` (390 px phone, 4x CPU, fresh context, intercepted delivery). From the error to the report leaving: **1,014 ms** median on Slow 4G (9 rounds), **3,295 ms** at 300 ms / 400 kbps (7 rounds). After figures will be measured live once this deploys. ## Why nothing caught it, and the fix - The Vitest audit built **without** a DSN, so the bootstrap and SDK chunk were never emitted where the storage scan and page-weight budgets could see them. `deploy.yml` ran `verify` on that build, then shipped a **second** build with the DSN. On today's main that shipped build fails 4 of 208 tests, including the storage scan behind `/privacy`'s "stores nothing" claim. - The test build and the local journey now use one dummy DSN (`tests/support/build-env.ts`, `example.invalid`). As a side effect, `check` passes on the dist/ the journey leaves behind; lane notes recorded that it used to fail. - `deploy.yml` builds **once** with production settings, then runs lint, typecheck and the whole dist/ audit on the exact bytes it uploads. - `pages: write` moves off the build job, which runs `pnpm install` and third-party build code. Only `deploy` holds it, alongside `id-token`. `actions/configure-pages` is removed because nothing read its outputs. - `tests/performance.test.ts` pins the lazily loaded chunk at 90,703 B. Budgets were re-derived to include the 3,920 B bootstrap that production always carried (heaviest page 179,607 B). The storage sentinel now runs module scripts: `import.meta` becomes the script URL; a static `import` still fails closed. ## Checks - `pnpm run verify`: 209/209 (on main, the same suite against a DSN build: 4 failures). - Red first: restoring the namespace import fails the new chunk budget (423,059 B > 92,518 B) and the storage scan. - Sentinel: a module script writing `window[["session","Storage"].join("")]` is recorded; a module with a static import reports an error. - `pnpm run journey`: 24/24, including the telemetry test that drives the real SDK and inspects the envelopes. `pnpm run check` after the journey: 209/209. - `ops/test-preview-target.sh` passes. `ops/verify-production.sh --self-test` has one failure (TLS date parse); it fails the same way on unmodified main on macOS (BSD `date`) and runs on Linux in CI. Rollback: `git revert -m 1 `. The merge redeploys. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: sanikolaev
body:
## Problem

A release run can successfully upload an artifact and then fail when an immediate `download-artifact` verification cannot find it by name. The current wrapper retries the *whole upload*, which now fails with HTTP 409 because artifact names are immutable within a workflow run. This happened in [executor release CI #44666844468](https://github.com/manticoresoftware/executor/actions/runs/44666844468).

## Changes

- Upload the archive only once using `actions/upload-artifact@v6`.
- Verify the *returned artifact ID* rather than searching by name.
- Retry only `actions/download-artifact@v7` up to three times (5s/10s backoff) if visibility is delayed.
- Compare the downloaded `artifact.tar` with the original archive, and fail only if verification still fails or the contents differ.
- Add a GitHub Actions smoke test that checks the archive round trip and executable file permissions.

No changes are needed in `executor`; workflows already use this action via `@main`.

## Testing
- GitHub Actions smoke test on this PR (will run automatically).

**ADR-0016，「代價」第一點**

- **Before:** ……要收緊時，舊版 app 照樣會做出伺服器會拒絕的證明，那是看得到的失敗，不會害到持卡人。
- **After:** ……要收緊時，舊版 app 照樣會做出伺服器會拒絕的證明，那是看得到的失敗，不會害到持卡人。名冊規則不是這樣：舊版照舊規則顯示的後果，伺服器不會拒絕，所以太舊的 app 讀到最低版本後自己停（ADR-0035）。

**ADR-0016，表**

- **Before:** 七列，到「裝置不認得的平台上的帳號」。
- **After:** 多兩列：
  - 跑哪一份電路、用哪一份參數檔｜電路同時看得到憑證、公鑰和兩個簽章。伺服器給一份改過的電路，就能把憑證序號放進公開輸出，跟著證明送出去｜電路檔、驗證金鑰、參數檔的 SHA-256 寫死在裝置上，用之前核對，不同就停，在卡片簽章之前
  - 這一版 app 還能不能過卡｜名冊規則內建在 app 裡。規則改了之後，舊版顯示的後果可能和名冊實際算的不同，持卡人照錯的後果同意，公開之後收不回來。伺服器能做的只有叫裝置停，不能叫它照別的規則算｜裝置讀伺服器公布的最低版本和起算日，自己太舊就在要 PIN 之前停下來。這個值對每個人都一樣，只會讓裝置更嚴

**ADR-0031，開頭**

- **Before:** （沒有補充）
- **After:** > 補充：有手機 app 之後，生效日 D 之前新版 app 要已經在兩個商店都下載得到；改電路時商店的審查怎麼排，見 ADR-0035。

**`GLOSSARY.md`**

- **Before:** （沒有這個詞）
- **After:** **最低版本**（`minimum app version`）: 後台對每個平台的手機 app 公布的一個版本號和起算日：起算日當天起，比它舊的 app 在要 PIN 之前自己停下來（ADR-0035）。後台收證明時不看它。_Avoid_: 強制更新、支援的版本

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

只有文件。ADR-0035 裡會變成單向的是 `config` 的 `min_app` 怎麼讀：第一版 app 上架之後才改不了，現在還沒有 app。

body:
Fixes the Finance page's summary cards cutting off large amounts.

## The problem

On wide screens (`xl`, 1280px and up) the six summary cards sat in a single row, about 180px each beside the sidebar. Their amounts are large monospace text that couldn't wrap, so figures in crores ran past the card edge. **Reserve Float Held** showed `₹1,58,06,543.9`, cut off.

## The fix

All in `crm/src/app/finance/page.tsx`:

- **Layout:** three cards per row on wide screens (two rows), so each card is over 300px wide. Narrower screens are unchanged: one column, then two.
- **Safety net:**
  - an amount too long for its card now wraps instead of being cut off (`min-w-0` on the card, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the amount);
  - the amounts use tabular digits.

## Checked in the running app

Run against the disposable `biharcabs_crm_test` database, signed in as a finance user in Chrome. For each card, I measured whether the amount extends past the card or its own box.

| Width | Columns | Card width | Amounts overflowing | Reserve Float lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 390 | 1 | 86px | 0 | 4 |
| 1280 | 3 | 312px | 0 | 1 |
| 1400 | 3 | 352px | 0 | 1 |
| 1600 | 3 | 419px | 0 | 1 |
| 1920 | 3 | 419px | 0 | 1 |

I also tried keeping six columns from `2xl` (1536px) up. The page's maximum width held cards at 203px, and the reserve amount wrapped onto two lines, so three columns were kept.

`tsc` and `next build` pass.

## Not in this PR

- **Phones (390px):** the sidebar doesn't collapse, leaving the content area, and so each card, only 86px wide. That's a layout problem across the whole CRM; amounts wrap rather than being cut off.
- **"Statutory 18% GST" label:** it may not match what the card totals now that ride GST is 5%. This needs checking separately.

author: aiongg
body:
A chip whose caption follows a value took the width of its current caption. PhotoCraft's Brush Preset chip shows the brush diameter, so during a Size drag in the canvas brush picker the chip widened each time the diameter gained a digit. That moved the options after it on the bar, and the bar's kept measure no longer matched its real run, so layout memory ran the frame a second time: 8 of 30 drag moves ran two passes.

`PresetPicker::caption_range` names the numeric range and decimal places of the caption. The field measures with `NumberCodec::widest` of that range, as a number field sizes its value area, and a face's thumbnail caption shows in tabular figures, so the widest text is the widest number whatever its digits. `BrushPresetPicker` passes 1 to its largest diameter and writes its caption with the same codec.

- Trial: `a_chip_with_a_caption_range_keeps_its_width_as_the_caption_grows` (ui-patterns `tests/it/presets/picker.rs`): captions 9, 10, 100, 1000, 4888, 7 keep the chip and the button after it in place, one pass per frame. Without the range it fails at caption 100 (two passes).
- Story: `preset_picker_chip_caption_range`.

In PhotoCraft (whole app, release without LTO): a Size drag in the canvas brush picker runs one pass per move instead of 1.3 on average; together with the PhotoCraft changes for #15859, a drag move went from 12.7 to 6.4 ms.

Part of storytold/photocraft#15476, for storytold/photocraft#15859.

author: mydoxie
body:
Part 3 of the HTTP/2 plan: the two pieces gRPC needs from the native server.

## Streamed request body

- A request with `content-type: application/grpc*` (any case) streams its body. Other requests stay buffered, as before. HTTP/1.1 never streams.
- Rust sends the request record as soon as the HEADERS come, with new flag bit 4. A request whose HEADERS end the stream has no body, so it comes as a normal record without bit 4.
- New records to Dart: `BODY_PART` (kind 7, the bytes) and `BODY_END` (kind 8, status 0 for a clean end, 1 for a reset or a dead connection).
- New response kind from Dart: `BODY_ACK` (kind 10, u64 bytes consumed).
- The stream window goes back to the client only after `BODY_ACK`, in batches of half the window (512 KiB). So a slow handler holds the client back, and at most 1 MiB per stream waits for Dart.
- The connection window still goes back as bytes arrive. So one stream that nobody reads can not block the other streams.
- Padding goes back at once (Dart never sees it).
- No size limit and no body timeout for a streamed body. The per-connection body cap does not count it.
- Client trailers: checked and dropped, then `BODY_END 0`.
- Client RST, a dead connection, or a client that closes its side: `BODY_END 1`, exactly once. `REQUEST_GONE` still comes when the request has no answer.
- When Dart answers before the request body ended, Rust sends `RST_STREAM NO_ERROR` after the answer, so the client stops sending (RFC 9113 8.1).

## Response trailers

- The header lines of a kind 8 record are trailers (HTTP/2 only). After the last DATA (with no END_STREAM), a HEADERS frame with the trailers and END_STREAM ends the stream.
- Names are made lowercase. Connection-specific headers and lines with no name (eg. a pseudo header) are dropped.
- Kind 6 with no parts, then kind 8 with trailers: HEADERS, then the trailers HEADERS with END_STREAM.
- HTTP/1.1 drops trailers (`ponytail:` comment).

## Dart

- `NativeRequest.isStreamed`. The body stream gets the parts. A part is acked once the listener took it, so a paused listener (or none) acks nothing. A reset ends the stream with `HttpException('stream reset')`. A cancelled listener drops and acks the rest, so the client is not stuck.
- `NativeResponse.trailers`. A response with trailers that is not streamed goes out as kind 6 + kind 8.

## Tests

- Rust: the trigger, part order, no WINDOW_UPDATE before the ack, the window bound, ack batching and clamping, padding, client RST, clean ends and trailers, no body timeout and no limits, an early answer, trailers after DATA, trailers with no parts, a chatty stream vs the flood limits, HTTP/1.1 drops trailers, acks and connection death over a real socket.
- The `h2_conn` fuzz target now adds gRPC requests (odd seed byte), acks each part, and answers with trailers. 60 s run: no crash.
- Dart (`package:http2` client): a slow reader with pause/resume, a body nobody reads (the client blocks at the window), trailers, trailers-only, a client RST mid-body, and a bidi echo.

No version or ABI bump (at release only).

author: ross-w
body:
## Summary

If multiple sessions are found, some of which include a 5 hour window and some which do not, ccu will fail to update. This PR changes behaviour to only read the latest session used.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Security fix

## Changes Made

- `internal/statusline`: replace the per-window `pick()` with `freshest()`, which picks one session and takes both windows from it, so sessions on different accounts are never mixed
  - The ordering rules are the same as before, applied to whole sessions: a session counts as being as recent as its last confirmed response or the start of either of its windows, whichever is later; ties go to higher weekly usage, then higher 5-hour usage, then session ID
  - `FetchedAt` is that session's last confirmed response, so "updated X ago" reflects the account in use
  - When the chosen session has no 5-hour window (Ultra), the result is weekly-only via the existing nil `FiveHour` / `HasSessionLimit()` handling
- Tests: `TestPick` replaced by `TestFreshest` (12 ordering cases, each one checked to fail if its rule is broken); new `TestLoadFollowsLatestAccount` regression test for the two-account case; shared `weeklyJSON` payload helper, also used by `TestLoadWeeklyOnly`
- Docs: CLAUDE.md status line notes, README status line limitations, CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → Fixed

## Testing

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] Tests pass (`make test`)
- [x] Code lints successfully (`make lint`)
- [x] Build completes without errors (`make build`)
- [x] The changes never log to stdout/stderr when the server runs in stdio mode

## Documentation

- [x] I have updated relevant documentation

## Additional Notes

- Known gap (unchanged by this PR): a session that changes account mid-session (e.g. `/login`) can still keep the old account's 5-hour window, because `record()` keeps a session's previous copy of a window when a new payload omits it.

author: danny-avila
body:
## Summary

#18555 moved a thread row's wait on the progressive mount window from context to a subscription, and in the flat list it put that wait in a wrapper around each row. The list renders again on every frame of a streaming reply, and the wrapper rendered with it for every row of the thread, calling its hooks each time, where the memoized row beneath it would have been skipped. In a CPU profile of a reply streaming into a 984-row thread the wrapper is 71 ms of 7.0 s of main-thread work. It is the one cost that change added to a thread that has finished mounting.

The row now waits on the window itself. It is memoized on its row object, which the thread index reuses for every message that did not change, so a frame of a reply looks at the one row that grew. In the same profile after the change the row component is 4 ms and the wrapper is gone.

Related to #18555.

## How it works

```diff
 // List.tsx
-<RowGate key={row.depth} depth={row.depth}>
-  <Row row={row} currentEditId={currentEditId} setCurrentEditId={setCurrentEditId} />
-</RowGate>
+<Row key={row.depth} row={row} currentEditId={currentEditId} setCurrentEditId={setCurrentEditId} />

 // Row.tsx
 function Row({ row, currentEditId, setCurrentEditId }: RowProps): ReactElement | null {
   const { renderActivity } = useMessagesHost();
+  const mounted = useRowMounted(row.depth);
   ...
+  if (!mounted) {
+    return null;
+  }
```

## Type of change

- [x] Performance improvement

## Testing

**Tested environments/configuration:**

- Chromium via Playwright, mock e2e lane (in-memory MongoDB, fake model), built client. The profile is one streamed reply (`E2E_SLOW_REPLY`) in the 984-row thread, before and after, CPU unthrottled.

**Automated tests:**

- New `packages/chat/src/components/messages/thread/__tests__/List.spec.tsx`: when a reply grows, exactly one row waits on the window, the one that changed; rows outside the window are held back and mount as it widens. The first fails with the wrapper in place.
- `packages/chat`: `npx jest src/components/messages src/react/messages`, `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- Mock e2e: `long-conversation-mount`, `offscreen-rows`, `thread-renderers`, `message-tree`, `streaming`, `branch-history`: 28 scenarios.

author: mrz1836
body:
## What Changed

The review sheet now shows and edits who a pull request is assigned to, the way it already manages reviewers. The issue sheet's older assignee picker, which searched GitHub on every pause in typing, moves onto the same shared section and picker.

**How candidates are found and cached**
- **`internal/people`** (migration `0108_people_assignable`) adds two tables:
  - `people_assignable`: per repository and person, when GitHub last *listed* them as assignable, and when the app last *saw them assigned* (on any read of either sheet, or the user's own edit).
  - `people_assignable_reads`: each read of the list, keyed by its words (`''` is the whole list), with `total` and `listed`.
- **One row per person across every repository.** `people` was already global by login, so what the app learns in one repository serves every other. `OrgRanked` ranks the people who work on the owner's other repositories ("In acme-org").
- **Search coverage** (`Covers`), so typing reaches GitHub only when nothing kept answers it:
  - a whole list that named everyone (`listed >= total`) answers every search;
  - a complete search for `p`, under 7 days old, answers every longer query that starts with `p`;
  - any search answers the same words for 10 minutes.
- **Kept long, bounded, pruned in the writing transaction:**
  - a year of rows, 100,000 in all;
  - a week of searches, and a year of whole-list reads;
  - `PruneUnseenPeople` now also keeps whoever `people_assignable` names, so the cascade can't wipe the new rows.
- **`Summary` and `Forget`** back a new Settings row. `Forget` empties every table in one transaction.

**`internal/assignees`** (a new leaf package, shared by both sheets)
- `Finder` offers people through a `Directory` interface (core adapts the people service) and a `Read` that each sheet hands it. It never imports a GitHub client, a service, or either sheet; a new repoguard boundary enforces this.
- Core builds **one** `Finder` for both sheets. Its single-flight group is keyed by repository and query, so a repository is read at most once at a time, whichever sheet asks.
- `rank` is pure. It orders people as: you, the author, participants, those assigned before, those who work here, those just found, the rest of the listed set, then the org (only while the list is cut short). Once the whole list named everyone, a directory-only person not on it is left out. Bots are excluded, each person appears once, and the list is capped at 300, enough for a full page of 100 beside the item's own people.

**`internal/github`**
- `FetchAssignable(kind, id, query)` reads `assignableUsers(first: 100)` with `totalCount` through `... on RepositoryNode`, for an issue or a pull request. `itemRepoRead` returns a gone error by kind.
- `RemoveAssignees` takes everyone off in one DELETE. It shares one sender (`assigneesEdit`) with `AddAssignees` and the existing Unassign me (`RemoveAssignee`), which keeps its "kept you assigned" wording.
- `Edited.Assignees` carries GitHub's answer. New constants: `AssignableMax` and `MaxAssignees`.
- The pull request read asks for `assignees(first: 10)`, which is all of them, since GitHub assigns at most 10.

**`internal/review`**
- The cached context keeps the assignees (`pullContext.Assignees`). In a cache an older build wrote, it is nil, so editing stays off ("Reload the pull request") until the next read.
- `EditAssignees` sends `-` then `+`, at most two REST requests, through the inbox Actor. Steps are never re-sent across the token retry.
  - Removing first lets a swap work at GitHub's cap of 10.
  - It refuses taking the user off (that stays Unassign me) and anything that would leave more than 10 assigned.
- After each step it patches the cache with GitHub's answer (`setAssignees`: `GetDiff` + `SetDiffContext`, keeping `context_at`), so the window rebuilds with **no read**. If the patch fails, it expires the cache instead.
- New bound methods: `AssigneeCandidates`, `LearnAssignees`, `SearchAssignees`, `PeopleSummary`, `ForgetPeople`.

**`internal/issues`**
- The per-search memo and `Assignable` are gone. The sheet uses the same `Finder` through `AssigneeCandidates` / `LearnAssignees` / `SearchAssignees`.
- `Edit` now unassigns everyone in one request **before** it assigns, refuses more than 10, and records whom it assigned.

**Frontend**
- `Assignees.tsx` (`AssigneesSection`) serves both sheets, in a `summary` or `details` look:
  - each assignee's avatar and login, with "(you)" on the user's row;
  - × on hover for everyone but the user, with the row fading while its edit runs and an inline alert if it fails;
  - with no one assigned, **Assign yourself**, the author, and one more as one-click chips, plus More….
- `AssigneePicker.tsx` (on `PickerDialog`):
  - sections: Assigned (the user's row locked), Suggested, Works on, Can be assigned in, In the owner, Found on GitHub;
  - it learns once when stale;
  - it searches 300 ms after typing stops, only while the list is cut short;
  - the Apply button is named for the edit ("Assign 2 · Unassign 1").
- `PeopleParts.tsx`: `RowAction`, the suggestion chips, and `personLabel` move out of the reviewers' code, which now uses them unchanged.
- Settings → Reviewing → **People** shows "N people across M repositories" and a **Forget…** button behind a confirmation.
- Settings → **Account**: the note at the bottom now names the `repo` and `read:org` scopes the token needs (team review requests are among what `read:org` shows), which `gh auth login` grants, and the command that adds them (`gh auth refresh -s repo,read:org`). Before, the section mentioned only the optional `read:project`. Setup and the inbox already require both scopes; this only makes them visible where people check their sign-in.

**Docs**: `docs/architecture.md` (a new `internal/assignees` section, plus the github, review, issues, people, core, test-support, and frontend sections), `docs/desktop.md`, `docs/performance.md`, the README, and the project guide's Layout.

## Why It Was Necessary

The review sheet showed no assignees at all: the pull request read never asked for them, and the card only knew "assigned to me". The issue sheet's assignee picker spent a GraphQL point on every pause in typing, with no sections, avatars, or inline ×. This change gives both sheets the same experience as the reviewer picker. It learns from reads the app makes anyway, and shares what it learns across repositories and owners.

| Operation | GitHub requests |
|---|---|
| Opening the picker, showing the chips | 0 (local), or 1 GraphQL point for the whole list, at most weekly per repository, whichever sheet asks |
| Typing | 0 while the whole list named everyone, or a stored search covers the words; otherwise 1 point, 300 ms after typing stops |
| An edit (any number of people) | at most 2 REST (one DELETE, then one POST) |
| After a pull request edit | 0 (the cache is patched from GitHub's answer) |
| The pull request read | unchanged: 1 point (measured) |

## Testing Performed

- **Gate**: `magex db:generate`, `magex app:bindings`, `magex format:fix`, `magex lint`, `magex test:race`, `go-pre-commit run --all-files`, `magex frontend:gate` (4,783 tests), `magex db:check`, and `magex app:check` all pass, and a final `/fix-all` run is clean.
- **Costs measured** with GitHub's own dry run (`rateLimit(dryRun: true)`) on a real pull request, read-only:
  - the pull request read is 1 point both with and without the new assignees connection (2,722 nodes against 2,712);
  - the assignable read is 1 point (100 nodes).
- **`internal/people`**:
  - a complete list unlists whom it no longer names, and a list cut short unlists no one;
  - coverage of longer searches, the 7-day expiry, a search cut off at 100 covering nothing, and the 10-minute repeat;
  - staleness and the back-off after a failure;
  - pruning keeps the people the assignable rows name, plus the size bounds;
  - the org's people come from the owner's other repositories;
  - Summary and F

body:
On a Region Server whose grid computer is off, every sign-in waited 100 seconds before the page said "Your world's sign-in service isn't running yet". The launcher's client for Robust's account, sign-in and grid services (`GridGate.Robust`) was never configured, so it kept HttpClient's default timeout. I found it on the test VM: its grid computer doesn't answer, and a sign-in took exactly 100.0 s.

- The client now allows **5 s to connect** (`SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectTimeout`) and **30 s for a whole call**. Robust runs on the same computer or on the grid's own, and every call is a short XML lookup.
- Nothing else uses this client. Assets keep their own 2-minute client.
- The existing `RobustFailure.IsUnreachable` rule already treats the faster failure as "isn't running", so the page shows the same message, just sooner.

**Test:** `RobustClientTimeoutTests` makes a connection that never completes on the registered client. Before the fix it failed after 1 m 40 s; now it fails as unreachable in about 5 s.

author: angatv
body:
## Problem

On 2026-11-20 Steam replaced H1Z1.exe (depot 433851, manifest 9048628616520611413, nothing else changed). The new exe is 1.0.331.451183: a recompiled build with a much larger protector section (4 MB to 69 MB), new integrity guards and anti-debug checks. Our patch addresses, byte guards and attestation roots are all for 1.0.326.439939, so the launcher refuses it.

Installed clients are fine, since they run from their own copy. New installs and repairs from an updated Steam folder are refused, and the error tells players to verify their files in Steam, which only fetches the new exe again.

## Fix

- The installer copies everything from Steam except H1Z1.exe. If Steam's exe is not a supported build, it takes the supported one from Steam's `download_depot` folder (`steamapps\content\app_433850\depot_433851`), after checking its size and SHA-256. Adoption swaps the exe the same way.
- The setup checks the exe as soon as an H1Z1 folder is selected, before any copy. When Steam's exe is not the supported build, it adds a **Patch** step between Location and Install. Install only moves to that step; nothing opens on its own. The step explains what Steam will show, and an **Open Steam** button opens the Steam console with this command already copied (also shown with a small copy link):
  `download_depot 433850 433851 1929288548044868931 <installed manifest>`
  With the installed manifest as delta, Steam downloads only H1Z1.exe (58 MB). The launcher checks the depot folders every 3 s; once the exe is there the step is done and the install starts on its own.
- If the exe changes between the check and the copy (Steam updates meanwhile), the copy is refused and the setup goes back to the Patch step. The settings repair shows the command in its error, with how to open the console.
- `locateSteamDepot` lists the depot folder of each Steam library and reads the installed manifest from the app manifest.
- EN/ZH translations for the new message; the old "verify in Steam" string is gone.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck` OK, `npx vitest run`: 812 passed, 4 skipped. `build:electron` and `build:renderer` OK.
- New cases in client-build, installer-flow (refusal with the delta command, install with the depot exe, repair never copies Steam's exe, depot lookup used by the watch, patch status before the copy), setup-flow (Patch step in the list), steam-locator (acf parsing, depot folders) and i18n.
- Checked by hand with the real exes: the 1.0.331 exe is refused with the right command, and with the 1.0.326 exe in a depot folder the install ends as `h1z1-1.0.326.439939` with the right hash.
- Run end to end on the staff PC with an updated Steam (source launcher, elevated, isolated user data): the Patch step showed after Location, Open Steam opened the console with the command copied, Steam downloaded H1Z1.exe, and the install started on its own with the 1.0.326 exe.
- On an updated Steam, `download_depot 433850 433851 1929288548044868931 9048628616520611413` downloaded 1 file (58 MB). The folder held only H1Z1.exe with the supported hash, and `locateSteamDepot` found it with the installed manifest.

## Not in this PR

- Not run from a packaged build or the installer.
- The detection and the 3 s watch live in main.ts, which no test runs; the functions they call are tested. The refused-copy case (back to Patch) was only checked in the renderer preview.
- `vivoxproxy/voice_rank_patch.h` has no build check, unlike the other proxies. On the new exe it would write into the wrong function. The launcher's exe check prevents that today.

author: benevi
body:
PR 4b del plan (`docs/plan-v2.md`, PR #18; decisiones D14 = Vercel Blob privado cifrado en el móvil, D15 = una frase por persona): copias automáticas de los dos móviles en un mismo sitio.

## Cómo funciona
- **Cifrado en el móvil** antes de salir (formato v2): `AES-GCM-256(gzip(exportar()))` con la cabecera (versión, KDF, iteraciones, sal, IV) como AAD; dentro van también persona, fecha, nº de sesiones y última sesión, que se comprueban al restaurar. Clave con PBKDF2-SHA-256 (600 000 iteraciones) a partir de la **frase de recuperación**, que no se guarda: el móvil conserva una `CryptoKey` no exportable en IndexedDB. La app propone una frase de 6 palabras al azar (~66 bits) y rechaza frases débiles.
- **El servidor (`api/copia.js`) solo ve bytes cifrados**, el tamaño y la fecha de subida; los metadatos del nombre van cifrados. Mismo código de acceso que el entrenador, persona validada, cuerpo ≤ 4 MiB, rechaza todo lo que no sea una copia cifrada, registro sin datos ni mensajes crudos. **Sin almacén Blob responde 503** y la app lo dice sin romper nada.
- **Automáticas:** al terminar una sesión, tras cambios de perfil/lesiones/medidas (1 min) y al abrir si la última tiene > 24 h; solo con red; nunca en el rescate ni dos a la vez. **No sube sola una copia con menos sesiones o más atrasada** que la última: pregunta.
- **Retención:** 14 días (como mucho la última de cada hora y 10 por día), una por semana 3 meses, una por mes 2 años; la más nueva nunca se borra; 30 subidas al día por persona.
- **Perfil → Copias:** activar (frase dos veces), última copia, lista completa marcando cuáles abre tu frase (sirven frases antiguas), restaurar siempre por `importar()` (con vuelta atrás), cambiar frase. **Rescate:** «Recuperar de la nube». Avisos persistentes si pasan > 3 días sin copia, si la nube no está activada o si el móvil perdió la clave.

## Revisión
Revisión criptográfica independiente: construcción correcta y confidencialidad intacta; encontró problemas de integridad y disponibilidad (copia vacía que quedaba la primera, recuperación bloqueada por la copia más nueva, copias reetiquetables, metadatos en claro, frases débiles…). Todo corregido con pruebas.

## Pruebas
`npm test`: 525 pruebas, 471 pasan, 0 fallos, 54 `todo`. e2e 19/19 (terminar sesión → subida → navegador limpio → restaurar con la frase). `npm audit` 0 (con `overrides` de `zod`).

## Para activarlo en Vercel
1. Proyecto `el-plan` → Storage → Create → **Blob**, acceso **Private** (p. ej. `pipos-copias`).
2. **Connect Project** marcando **Production y Preview** (las vistas previas escriben en el mismo almacén).
3. Redesplegar. 4. En cada móvil: Perfil → Copias → «Activar copias en la nube» y guardar la frase en un gestor de contraseñas: **sin la frase, las copias de la nube no se pueden abrir**.

**Sin verificar:** `@vercel/blob` privado (beta pública) en Vercel real y WebCrypto/IndexedDB en Safari de iPhone.

author: unique-divine
body:
# ci(mori): Add a draft release workflow for mori/v* tags

Adds `.github/workflows/mori-release.yml`, which builds Mori's C binary
`codebase-memory-mcp` as static Linux x64 and arm64 archives and, for a
`mori/v*` tag, creates a draft GitHub release that is not marked latest. This
is Impl 6 (Release Workflow) of the Jiyuu Mori epic, in
`epics/boku/26-11-19-jiyuu-mori/04-jiyuu-ingestion.md` in boku. No tag is
pushed here. Mori 0.13.0 is released when Unique tags it.

## Rationale

Jiyuu had no tag-triggered release, and upstream's release workflow depends
on secrets, VirusTotal, MCPB bundles and six platforms that Mori does not
ship. The dotfiles Herdr release (`herdr-ud/*`) is the model here: check
that the tag matches a version in the repo, build a matrix, write
`checksums.txt` and `release-metadata.json`, and publish as a draft that is
not marked latest. Impl 7 (install with mise on the laptop and homebox)
needs these assets.

Upstream's packaging boundary in `scripts/package-release.sh` stays: the
caller passes a binary and its sha256, every container is checked against
that hash, and the binary-composition gate still runs. MCPB bundles are
still built only for darwin, windows and `linux/*-portable`, which Mori's
workflow never requests.

## Key Changes

1. `.github/workflows/mori-release.yml`: jobs `validate` → `build` (matrix
   `ubuntu-latest` x64, `ubuntu-24.04-arm` arm64) → `prepare` → `publish`.
   Triggered by `mori/v*` tag pushes and by `workflow_dispatch` with
   `dry_run` (default true). All actions are pinned by SHA. The workflow
   uses only `github.token` and OIDC, no secrets.
1. `mori/VERSION` (`0.13.0`) is the version the tag must match. The build
   passes it to `scripts/build.sh --version`, which already defines
   `CBM_VERSION`, so `codebase-memory-mcp --version` prints
   `codebase-memory-mcp 0.13.0`. Builds without `--version` still print
   `dev`. The C sources and `Makefile.cbm` are unchanged.
1. `mori/scripts/release.ts` (Bun, tested in `release.test.ts`): checks the
   tag, builds asset names, writes checksums, metadata and notes, and
   creates the draft. It refills an existing draft and refuses to touch a
   published release.
1. `mori/scripts/package-release.sh`: no installer in archives, `NOTICE`
   added, and a new `--archive-name` option for versioned names.
1. `mori/README.md`: new "Release" section covering the tag steps, asset
   layout, a mise example and publishing the draft by hand.

## 1 - Release Flow

```text
tag push mori/vX.Y.Z ─┐
dispatch dry_run=true ┴─> validate: tag == mori/v + mori/VERSION
                                   (branch dispatch: VERSION only, publish=false)
  build x64 | arm64:  grammars-fetch (actions/cache on the lock hash)
                      build.sh --version X.Y.Z STATIC=1  (gcc -static)
                      strip --strip-all, check static linking
                      smoke: --version == "codebase-memory-mcp X.Y.Z"
                             cli index_repository + trace_path greet→helper
                             (HOME, CBM_CACHE_DIR, CBM_RUNTIME_DIR in scratch)
                      package-release.sh → exact four-member archive check
                      upload artifact mori-linux-<arch>
  prepare:            checksums.txt, release-metadata.json, release-notes.md
                      upload artifact mori-<version>-<sha>
  publish (tag only): attest-build-provenance (archives + checksums.txt)
                      gh release create --draft --latest=false --verify-tag
```

`dispatch dry_run=false` publishes only on a `mori/v*` tag ref. On a branch
it fails. Publishing stays a manual step:
`gh release edit mori/vX.Y.Z --draft=false --latest=false`. The API sets
`make_latest` to true by default when a draft is published, so the flag is
needed to keep Jiyuu's latest release unchanged.

## 2 - Installer Decision

Archives no longer carry an installer. Upstream's `install.sh` and
`install.ps1` download DeusData's releases, and the import already removed
them (`mori/IMPORT.md`), so `package-release.sh` stopped at
`cp LICENSE "$INSTALLER"`. Mori is installed from the release assets with
mise's `github:` backend, which picks the archive by the
`linux-x64`/`linux-arm64` in its name. The archive name is
`codebase-memory-mcp-<version>-linux-<x64|arm64>.tar.gz`, and the archive
holds `codebase-memory-mcp`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`
(generated from `THIRD_PARTY.md`, the grammar manifest and every vendored
license). Scripts and contracts that still expect an installer
(`smoke-local.sh`, `setup.sh`, the four installer contracts in
IMPORT.md's Known Test Gaps) are left for the contracts lane.

## 3 - Static Build

`STATIC=1` is upstream's portable Linux leg (`gcc -static` on Ubuntu 24.04),
so one binary runs on any glibc or musl distro. Both legs built and passed
the composition gate. The stripped binary is about 316 MB because the
Tree-sitter parse tables are compiled in. Each archive is about 42 MB.

## 4 - Dry Run Evidence

`workflow_dispatch` can only start a workflow that exists on the default
branch, so this branch's dry run used a temporary `push: branches` trigger.
That trigger is removed in the final commit, which differs from the tested
commit `822e7a7` only by that line. Run
https://github.com/Unique-Divine/jiyuu/actions/runs/44667427444: validate,
both builds and prepare passed, and publish was skipped. In the downloaded
arm64 archive, `--version` prints `codebase-memory-mcp 0.13.0` and its
sha256 matches `checksums.txt`.

After merge, run
`gh workflow run mori-release.yml --ref main -f dry_run=true` once to check
the dispatch path itself.

author: thihodev
body:
The code is downloaded as an archive, without `.git`. vetcode could not tell that an action from the repository's own owner is the project's own code. It reported it as third-party, as on openyard-cloud/aolangai: `openyard-cloud/vetcode@main` was listed as a medium finding.

`scripts/vet.mjs` now passes `--repo owner/name`. The option arrives with vetcode 0.8.12 (openyard-cloud/vetcode#77). An older vetcode ignores it, so the order of the merges does not matter.

The same vetcode release also counts private packages and loose code in "What the code can do". Before it, a monorepo whose packages are all private read as able to do nothing. Nothing changes here for that: the summary already merges every profile.

author: songarajatin225-a11y
body:
## Summary
Platform fixes from the `mobile-native` skill.

- **Hover:** all 64 hover rules are now inside `@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`, in place, so the cascade order is unchanged. A tap no longer leaves a control highlighted, and the `:active` press feedback still works.
- **Taps:**
  - The tap highlight is transparent.
  - Text size is no longer inflated in landscape.
  - Controls use `touch-action: manipulation`.
  - A long press no longer selects a control's label.
- **Fields:** on coarse pointers every field is 16 px, so iOS does not zoom in when one is focused. Pinch zoom still works.
- **Viewport height:** `dvh` for full-screen dialogs on phones; `svh` for the scroll story and the sticky panel. `vh` stays as the fallback.
- **Safe areas:** with `viewport-fit=cover`, `env(safe-area-inset-*)` keeps the toasts, the floating buttons and the bottoms of drawers and dialogs clear of the notch and home indicator. Body content clears a landscape notch.
- **Overscroll:** `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the drawer and dialog bodies.
- **Status bar:** one `theme-color` per scheme, matching the header and following the in-app theme switch.
- **Keyboard:** `interactive-widget=resizes-content`.
- **Service worker:** the cache is now `teal-cfg-v7`.

## Tests
- `npm test`: 219 passed, 0 failed.
- Emulated iPhone 13: fields are 16 px, there is no sideways scroll, and the tap highlight is transparent.
- Not verified: sticky hover, tap delay, safe areas and keyboard behaviour need a real device.

author: mdiloreto
body:
## Why

`hierarchical-implementation` currently ships as a Claude Code plugin only, while workflows across machines often use multiple coding CLIs (Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI `agy`, OMP `oh-my-pi`, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Pi). Maintaining separate per-CLI gates causes policy drift (different caps, exemptions and logs).

## What changed

Unified multi-CLI enforcement on top of the existing `hooks/hierarchical-implementation-gate.sh` engine with thin per-CLI adapters so every tool shares the same `decide` / `report` workflow, caps (`trivial` 3 files / 60 lines, `delegate` 60-line integration budget), `security` path checks, shell-write tokenizer, `LANE_MODE`, `HI_FREE_WORKERS=1`, and TSV logs:

- **Core gate (`hooks/hierarchical-implementation-gate.sh`)**:
  - Added `--harness <claude|agy|codex|gemini|cursor|opencode|omp|pi|generic>` (or `HIERARCHICAL_GATE_HARNESS`), keeping zero-arg Claude Code behavior 100% backward compatible.
  - Added unified `patch_targets()` parser for `*** Begin Patch` payloads (Codex `apply_patch` via `.tool_input.command` and OpenCode `patch`).
  - Widened `SID_SET` to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` so session IDs with underscores (`ses_...`, etc.) work safely.
  - Expanded `SECURITY_PATHS` and `security_path()` plugin-manifest detection to cover all supported CLIs and `adapters/`.
- **OpenCode v2 (`adapters/opencode/`)**: thin `@opencode/plugin` adapter with `session.parentID` and `lane-worker` (`HI_FREE_AGENT`) bypasses, undecided gating on `worker`/`general` spawns (leaving `explore` ungated), child-session message name attribution, and Node tests.
- **Antigravity CLI `agy` (`adapters/agy/`)**: native plugin bundle (`plugin.json`, `hooks.json`, `agents/worker.md`, `skills/hierarchical-implementation`, `gate.sh`) with `{"decision":"ask"}` PreToolUse pass-through, `{"decision":"allow"}` for `decide`, and subagent bypass via `parentConversationId`, `isSubagent`, or line-1 subagent `transcriptPath` inspection.
- **OMP (`oh-my-pi`) & Pi (`adapters/omp-pi/`, `.omp-plugin/marketplace.json`, `package.json`)**: extension factory using `ctx.agent.kind !== "main"` subagent bypass, OMP hashline multi-file `paths` handling, `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`before_agent_start` hooks, and Node tests.
- **Codex, Gemini CLI & Cursor (`.codex-plugin/`, `adapters/codex/`, `adapters/gemini/`, `.cursor-plugin/`, `adapters/cursor/`)**: manifests and hook configs routing directly to the shared gate core.
- **Skill & docs**: added a concise Harness tool mapping table to `skills/hierarchical-implementation/SKILL.md`, a harness-neutral `examples/AGENTS.md`, and per-CLI install & compatibility docs in `README.md`.

## Verified

### Automated suites & validators
- [x] `bash hooks/hierarchical-implementation-gate.test.sh` — all passed (zero regressions for Claude Code)
- [x] `bash hooks/multi-cli-gate.test.sh` — 38/38 passed (AGY, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, generic, `apply_patch`, subagent bypasses, multi-CLI `security` paths, mixed-harness `report`)
- [x] `node --test adapters/opencode/gate-client.test.ts adapters/omp-pi/gate-client.test.ts` — 4/4 passed against the live gate script
- [x] `bash "$PWD/skills/hierarchical-implementation/scripts/free-models.test.sh"` — all passed
- [x] `claude plugin validate "$PWD"` — Validation passed
- [x] `agy plugin validate "$PWD/adapters/agy" --strict --json` — 0 errors, 0 warnings (`agents: 1, hooks: 1, skills: 1`)
- [x] `gemini extensions validate "$PWD/adapters/gemini"` — validated cleanly
- [x] `shellcheck -x` and `jq empty` on all new scripts and JSON manifests — clean

### Live end-to-end execution against installed binaries (isolated temp repos + temp state)
- [x] **Claude Code (`claude` 2.1.329)** — live LLM runs for both `trivial` (`deny Edit` → `decide` → `Edit` succeeds) and `delegate` (`deny Agent` → `decide delegate` → `hierarchical-implementation:worker` subagent writes ungated → `spawn` logged → driver integrates).
- [x] **OpenCode (`opencode` 2.3.2)** — live LLM runs:
  - `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` driver + `HI_FREE_WORKERS=1` + `free-models.sh` (`deny shell undecided` → `decide delegate` → headless `lane-worker` on `opencode-go/hy4-flash-free` writes ungated → `spawn ... free-models` logged → driver integrates `src/index.ts` → `node --test` 2/2 passed).
  - `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` driver + native `subagent` on `opencode-go/hy4-flash-free` (`deny subagent undecided` → `decide delegate` → child `general` writes ungated via `session.parentID` → `spawn ... general` logged → driver integrates `src/index.ts` → `node --test` 2/2 passed).
  - `opencode-go/claude-haiku-5-5` `trivial` run (`deny edit` → `decide` → `edit` succeeds).
- [x] **Antigravity CLI (`agy` 1.5.13)** — live LLM (`gemini-4-neon-high`) runs for both `trivial` (`deny edit_file` → auto-allowed `decide` → `edit_file` succeeds) and `delegate` (`deny invoke_subagent` → `decide delegate` → `adapters/agy/agents/worker.md` subagent writes ungated via `transcriptPath` detection → `spawn` logged → driver integrates).
- [x] **Codex CLI (`codex` 0.171.0)** — live cloud LLM run with `[features] hooks = true` + trusted `hooks.json` (`PreToolUse` blocks real `apply_patch` via `.tool_input.command` → `decide` → `apply_patch` succeeds) plus shell-write verification.
- [x] **OMP (`omp` 19.0.1)** — real binary end-to-end runs via local OpenAI-compatible stub for both `trivial` and full `delegate` (`deny bash` → `decide delegate` → `deny write no-worker` → `task` subagent writes ungated via `ctx.agent.kind === "sub"` → `spawn` logged → driver integrates).
- [x] **Pi (`pi` 1.5.2)** — real binary end-to-end run via local stub (`deny write` → `decide` → `write` succeeds).
- [x] **Gemini CLI (`gemini` 0.70.0)** — real binary end-to-end run with `BeforeTool`/`AfterTool`/`SessionStart` hooks (`BeforeTool` blocks `replace` → `run_shell_command` `decide` → `replace` succeeds).
- [ ] **Cursor (`cursor-agent` 2026.11.19)** — binary unauthenticated in this environment (`agent login` / `CURSOR_API_KEY` required); verified via `hooks/multi-cli-gate.test.sh` against Cursor's hook JSON contract.

author: ifrit99
body: ## 危なさ 高。理由: `.github/dependabot.yml`（REVIEW.md の CI と自動化）。 ## なぜ 現行の `github-actions` エントリと RFC S-6 コメントをそのまま残し、`pub`（`/`）、`npm`（`/test/firestore`）、`docker`（`/`）の週次 version updates を追加する。minor/patch は ecosystem ごとに 1 PR へまとめ、major は個別 PR。例外: pub の `firebase` グループ（`firebase_*` / `cloud_firestore`）は major も含めて 1 PR（core / auth / firestore が世代で縛り合うため。GitHub 席の指摘で設計 §3.3 の代案を採用）。`gradle` と `docker-compose` は入れない。auto-merge はしない。 ## 形 ``` dependabot.yml (v2) github-actions / weekly # 既存（キー増減なし） pub / weekly + limit 5 groups (first-match): firebase (firebase_* / cloud_firestore; update-types なし = major 含む) pub-minor-patch (*; minor, patch) npm /test/firestore + groups(minor,patch) + limit 3 docker / weekly + limit 1 # イメージは1つ。:stable のため現状 PR は出ない ``` ## テスト - 見たコミット: `65fa9e5` - `Verified: none (YAML parse + vendor.dependabot schema; Flutter 対象外)` - `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/dependabot.yml'))"` → 例外なし - `check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.dependabot .github/dependabot.yml` → `ok -- validation done` - `package-ecosystem` は `github-actions` / `pub` / `npm` / `docker` のみ - pub `groups` の順は `firebase` → `pub-minor-patch`。`firebase` は `applies-to` / `patterns` のみ（`update-types` なし = major 含む） - docker `open-pull-requests-limit: 1`（イメージは1つ、というコメント付き） - 1行目は RFC S-6 のまま。`github-actions` は 3 キーのまま - `git diff --name-only origin/master...HEAD` → `.github/dependabot.yml` のみ ## 危ないところ・やっていないこと - `test/firestore` の npm テストは CI で走らない。npm PR はマージ前に手動確認が必要 - Docker build は CI で走らない。現状 `FROM ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:stable` のため docker の更新 PR は出ない。Dockerfile を版番号タグか digest に固定するまで動かない（**後続課題。この PR では GitHub Issue を作らない**） - Dependabot が開いた PR ではリポジトリ secrets（`FIREBASE_*`、`SENTRY_DSN`）は空。Web ビルドは空の `--dart-define` でも通るので、CI 緑は Firebase 設定込みの確認ではない - `gradle` / `docker-compose` は入れていない - auto-merge しない。Dependabot alerts / security updates の GitHub UI トグルは触っていない - 製品コード・`pubspec.yaml`・`Dockerfile`・CI workflow は変更していない ## 戻し方 この PR を revert するだけ。Dependabot の追加 ecosystem の更新ジョブが止まる。 ## イフリトさんがやること - マージ（ops/CI 設定。エージェントはマージしない） - **pub の Dependabot PR は、マージ前にプレビューかローカルで画面を1回さわる**（音・Sentry・Firebase ログインなど。CI は画面の動きまで見ていない）。`master` への push で `deploy.yml` が Cloudflare Pages へ配置する - Dependabot が開いた PR ではリポジトリ secrets（`FIREBASE_*`、`SENTRY_DSN`）が渡らない。Web ビルドは空の `--dart-define` でも緑になり得る。CI 緑は Firebase 設定込みの証明ではない。必要なら Settings → Secrets → **Dependabot** に同じ名前で登録する - docker `:stable` は現状 PR を出さない。Dockerfile ピン（版番号タグまたは digest）は後続課題（Issue は作っていない） - マージ後: Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot で 4 ecosystem がエラーなし。各「Check for updates」を手動実行 - npm PR はマージ前に `cd test/firestore && npm install && npm test`

author: kb01111
body:
## **User description** ## Summary First step of the plan in `docs/plans/2026-11-20-pr-agent-feature-parity.md` (included in this PR): reach feature parity with CodeRabbit and Macroscope, with repo-specific memory and a merge-readiness score. This PR lays the foundations the later phases build on. The existing review behaviour does not change. ### GitHub App auth (`backend/github_app.py`) - Mints a short-lived installation token per repo from `GITHUB_APP_ID` plus the private key. - Tokens are cached in process memory only and never written to Redis. - Falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` when the App is not configured, not installed on the repo, or GitHub refuses a token. - `review_only` and PR triage (`fetch_facts`) now use it. - `/config/status` reports `auth_mode`, and `/config/test` live-checks the App. ### Event router (`backend/events.py`) - `/webhooks/github` now routes on `X-GitHub-Event`. The commit actions on `pull_request` (opened, reopened, synchronize, labeled) keep their existing path unchanged. - These events go into a per-PR activity log, capped at 200 entries: - reviews, review threads and PR comments - completed `check_suite`/`check_run` events and statuses - closed and merged PRs - Redeliveries of the same `X-GitHub-Delivery` are recorded once. - The events also set a `prdirty:` marker, which the Phase 4 score will use to know when to recompute. - Default-branch pushes drop the cached `.pragent.yaml`, and App `installation*` events keep the installation cache current. - Bot comments are ignored. CI results from bots are still recorded. - New endpoint: `GET /repos/{owner}/{name}/pulls/{n}/activity`. ### Data model (`backend/datamodel.py`, `store.py`) - Redis key layout and size budgets, sized for the free tier. - `Finding`, `MemoryEntry` and `ReadinessReport` shapes. - Stable finding fingerprints, so later incremental reviews never re-post the same finding. - Capped-list helpers in `store.py` for all four backends (redis-py, Upstash SDK, REST, in-memory). ### Agent config v2 - New fields: `profile`, `memory_enabled`, `merge_gate`, `score_threshold`, `path_instructions`, `tools`, `chat_enabled`, `autofix`. - Agents stored before this change read back with defaults. - A `PUT` from an older client keeps the stored v2 values instead of resetting them. ### Webhook secrets and Cloudflare worker - The backend and the worker accept `GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` alongside `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, so adding the App doesn't break existing repo webhooks. - The worker forwards the new events and drops uninteresting ones at the edge: non-PR comments, bot comments, non-completed checks and pushes to other branches. ### Desktop - New "GitHub App (recommended)" card under Integrations ([`src-tauri/src/github_app.rs`](src-tauri/src/github_app.rs)): - Runs GitHub's App-manifest flow through a loopback callback that checks a random `state`. - Writes the App id, slug, private key and webhook secret to `backend/.env`. These secrets never reach the webview. - Offers a button that opens the App's install page. ## Testing - Backend: `python -m pytest backend/tests`: **136 passed** (106 before), including new `test_events.py`, `test_github_app.py` (real RS256 JWT, token caching and refresh, PAT fallback) and `test_agent_config_v2.py`. - Worker: `node --test cloudflare-worker/worker.test.js`: **18 passed**. - Rust: `cargo test`: **42 passed**, including manifest, URL validation, request parsing and HTML-escaping tests. - **Not tested:** the App-manifest flow end to end against real GitHub. ## Notes for reviewers - New dependency: `PyJWT[crypto]`, added to `requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml`. - `npm run typecheck` already fails on `main`: `src/pages/auto-review.tsx` imports `KNOWN_MODELS`, which `src/lib/store.ts` does not export. This PR adds no new type errors, but `tauri build` stays broken until that is fixed. - Defaults chosen while the plan's open questions are unanswered: - The App is optional, with the PAT as fallback. - `merge_gate` defaults to `advisory`. - `autofix` defaults to `suggest`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by Sourcery Establish the foundations for GitHub App-based PR agent operation, event-driven activity tracking, and future repository memory and merge-readiness features. New Features: - Add GitHub App authentication with installation-token support, PAT fallback, configuration diagnostics, and desktop setup flow. - Record and expose GitHub pull-request activity for reviews, comments, threads, CI results, status updates, merges, and relevant repository events. - Introduce shared data models for findings, repository memory, readiness reports, and bounded event storage. - Expand agent configuration with review profiles, memory, merge-gate, path-instruction, tool, chat, and autofix settings while preserving compatibility with older agents and clients. Bug Fixes: - Prevent duplicate webhook deliveries from being recorded more than once and avoid bot conversation loops while retaining bot-generated CI results. - Invalidate cached repository configuration after relevant default-branch updates and preserve existing agent v2 settings during legacy updates. Enhancements: - Route GitHub webhooks by event type without changing the existing pull-request review flow. - Support capped-list storage consistently across Redis, Upstash, REST, and in-memory backends. - Accept either repository or GitHub App webhook secrets for backend and worker webhook verification. Build: - Add the PyJWT cryptography dependency required for GitHub App authentication. Deployment: - Extend the Cloudflare worker to forward relevant GitHub events and filter uninteresting deliveries at the edge. Documentation: - Document GitHub App authentication, event activity tracking, new agent settings, and related environment variables. - Add the phased PR-agent feature-parity plan. Tests: - Add backend, worker, and Rust coverage for GitHub App authentication, event routing, agent configuration migration, activity tracking, and desktop manifest-flow validation. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Add GitHub App setup and PR activity tracking** ### What Changed - Integrations now guides users through creating a GitHub App, saves its credentials to `backend/.env`, and provides a link to install it on repositories. The backend uses App credentials when available and falls back to the existing GitHub token. - Webhooks now record PR reviews, comments, review threads, CI results, and close or merge events. A new activity endpoint returns recent events and indicates when readiness data may be stale. - Agents gain settings for review profiles, memory, merge gates, path instructions, tools, and autofix. Existing agents receive defaults, and updates from older clients preserve saved settings. ### Impact `✅ Create a GitHub App from Integrations` `✅ PR reviews can use GitHub App credentials` `✅ Review and CI activity available for readiness tracking`

author: danihmorais
body:
## Rodada 7 — pesquisa auxiliar de preços no PNCP

Esta é a reapresentação da rodada PNCP diretamente sobre a `main` atual. O PR anterior (#96) foi fechado sem merge e sem diff; esta branch contém novamente os arquivos da implementação.

- Consulta por data de publicação, modalidade e UF, com período máximo de 730 dias e rate limit por IP.
- Modalidades: concorrência eletrônica, pregão eletrônico e dispensa de licitação.
- Busca itens candidatos por similaridade textual e consulta resultados de cada item.
- Classifica como **homologado** apenas o resultado com situação `Informado`; apresenta **valor estimado** em categoria separada quando não existe resultado homologado e o orçamento não é sigiloso.
- Exibe órgão, município/UF, modalidade, data, quantidade, unidade e referência da contratação no PNCP.
- Bloqueia a aplicação automática do preço quando a unidade diverge.
- Adiciona painel na etapa 1, cliente frontend e testes de API/unitários com respostas simuladas, incluindo CNPJ alfanumérico.

## Limites conhecidos

- Até 16 contratações por modalidade e primeira página de até 50 itens por contratação: a busca não é exaustiva.
- Similaridade textual não comprova equivalência técnica; unidade incompatível impede aplicação, mas unidade igual não certifica equivalência.
- Não calcula médias/estatísticas, não substitui pesquisa formal e não integra o Painel de Preços do Governo Federal.
- A URL-base pode ser configurada por `LICITA_PNCP_CONSULTA_URL`.

author: zyl71
body:
Closes #16

`.cargo/audit.toml` still ignores the advisories below, but `Cargo.lock` on `main` already holds a patched version of the crate, so the entries no longer suppress anything. This pull request removes them, together with the comments that explained them.

| Advisory | Summary | In `Cargo.lock` now | Patched in | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RUSTSEC-2026-0194 | Quadratic run time when checking a start tag for duplicate attribute names | `quick-xml` 0.41.0 | 0.41.0 | high |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0195 | Unbounded namespace-declaration allocation in `NsReader` enables … | `quick-xml` 0.41.0 | 0.41.0 | high |

**Why remove them.** An ignore entry keeps muting the advisory id for as long as it stays in the file. If the crate were later pinned back to an affected version, cargo-audit would stay silent about it.

**What was checked, and what was not.**

- Read from `main` at commit `124a226a1f2f` on 2026-11-20: each id is on an active line of the config, and no version of the affected crate in `Cargo.lock` is inside the affected range of its advisory (RustSec records).
- The change touches only `.cargo/audit.toml`. No Rust source and no lock file is changed. The edited file parses as TOML, and every other ignore entry and setting is unchanged.
- We did not run `cargo audit` locally, because we do not build or execute anything from this repository. CI is the first run of the tool on this change.

Disclosure: the check, the edit and this text were produced with automated tooling, including an LLM.

Feel free to close this if it is not useful.

## Summary

The Content page already treats `audio` as a content type (filter, cards, preview), but audio could not actually be saved or uploaded there: the `content_library.type` CHECK constraint rejected it, `saveContentLibraryEntry` stored audio files as `pdf`, `uploadToContentLibrary` refused them, and the upload picker's file dialog did not offer them. This PR closes those gaps.

## Related issue

None.

- New migration `20261119130000_content_library_allow_audio.sql`: recreates `content_library_type_check` as `('pdf', 'video', 'image', 'audio')`.

## Why

The Consistency check never raised a bench score in four controlled comparisons, made wrong edits (5 of 14, then 8 of 19), held every reply in the player's path, and rewrote the Narrator's text after it was shown. It had to go before the release that follows the rename. The Review model's text also undersold its main job: it keeps the story's record after every reply, and reviews the world only now and then. "Scribe" says that, and doesn't clash with Lore in the Glossary.

## What changed

- The Consistency check is removed: `src/consistency.ts`, its settings, the Settings fieldset, the Setup step, the Guide and README text, its tests, its case script, and the bench's `--consistency`, `--no-consistency` and `--decisions` flags and summary keys. The `revise` Turn event and the "fix cut" helpers it alone used go too.
- Settings files with the old `consistency*` fields still load. The fields are ignored and the key leaves the file on the next save, with a test.
- The Review model is the **Scribe**: a Glossary entry, the Settings fieldset (now above the limits in Settings → Text), the Setup step "The Scribe", the Guide and the README. The text leads with keeping the record (place, people, clothes and gear, what people learn, time), then reviewing the world. Stored setting names (`review*`) stay.

author: dream-team-bot[bot]
body:
Stage 2 of 5. It lands more bug fixes from yesterday's `/untangle-codebase` run (`untangle/source-2026-11-19`), covering dream-pass, cache-clock, jev-skill-suggestion, vercel-deploy-status and prompt-bouncer. Each commit is cherry-picked with `-x` onto today's main.

## What changed, per commit
- **8f7121e**: cache-clock's 300-row tail is one constant, `TAIL_ROWS`, instead of 4 copies across argv, PowerShell and lastLines. vercel-deploy-status's header counts in-flight states from `IN_FLIGHT`; it is the same set as before.
- **4d98edb**: prompt-bouncer's mode list was written out in the command description, the hint and the argument check. It is now one `MODES`.
- **e8018c6**: cache-clock: an invalid `CACHE_CLOCK_MAIN_TTL_MIN` used to set pinned=true and stop the transcript reads. Now only a valid value pins the TTL; an invalid one falls back to the default.
- **d55024e**: dream-pass: a merge whose `from` filtered to empty overwrote `into` with no change recorded and no backup. Such a merge is now dropped.
- **8e40e1b**: prompt-bouncer's `docs` setting says "paths from the project root", but `loadDocs` read from cwd(). It now reads from root(), with a cwd fallback, as secret-box does.
- **c36f824**: the jev band gives the bands below it the reduced `maxRows`, and it survives a band below that throws. Before, `next(e)` handed down the full maxRows, and a throw below killed jev's band.
- **37d7636 + c0f21c0**: prompt-bouncer: an unknown mode runs as quick, and the first valid mode wins (/bouncer, then env, then setting), so a typo in the env var no longer hides a valid setting. c0f21c0 supersedes 37d7636; the squash merge folds them.
- **0a971a3**: dream-pass: apply runs merges first, so a rewrite or remove of a merged file used to undo the merge; those edits are now dropped. Undo used to ignore runJob's exitCode, so after a failed rename the next undo restored the same backup; that is now reported.
- **64730b4 + 0c401bb**: vercel-deploy-status: one poll that throws used to end polling for the rest of the session. The loop now reschedules in `finally`, and the throw is logged instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.
- **6496da8**: dream-pass: no two parts of a plan touch the same merged file, so overlapping merges and adds can't undo each other. `startUndo` catches the unhandled rejection from the band's Undo button.

## Conflicts and fix-ups
- 0a971a3 and 6496da8 conflicted in `parsePlan`, because the source branch's comment purge (1b02d3e, not landed) had removed a comment there. Both are resolved to the new code, and the comment `// New memories only: an "added" file that already exists is ignored` is kept.
- undo's comment is back on `undo()` rather than on `startUndo`. That is what skipped fix-up 4d8e311 did, applied by hand.
- The `header()` comment that 8f7121e dropped is restored. No comment is removed in this PR; two are reworded, for TAIL_ROWS and the jev band.
- New regression test: dream-pass `parsePlan` drops a merge with no source and every other edit to a merged file. It fails on main and passes here.
- Patch version bumps: cache-clock 0.5.5, dream-pass 0.2.3, jev-skill-suggestion 0.2.3, prompt-bouncer 0.1.3, vercel-deploy-status 1.0.5.

## Checks
The repo has no GitHub workflows, so the local checks are the gate:
- `claude plugin validate` + `claude plugin test` on all 10 mods, and the 6 node suites.
- The output is identical to main. The only failures are the 3 that were already there: the cache-clock band-chain maxRows test, and the `detect.test.mts` SLOW timing checks on this box. This stage doesn't touch detect.

## Behaviour checks
- The engine-harness suites for the changed mods pass: dream-pass 20, jev 14, prompt-bouncer 9 (including the quick-rules session flow), cache-clock 14 of 15 as on main, and vercel 3 plus 58 queue checks.
- The parsePlan regression test was run against origin/main to show it catches the old bug.
- Not driven live: `claude -p` is not logged in on this box. Not covered by any test: the vercel poll reschedule, and the cache-clock invalid-TTL fallback (code read only).

## Codex review
- Round 1, one [Important]: dropping an overlapping merge left its surviving file out of the plan's index. Fixed with `keepListed()`: a memory the old index listed and the new one forgot keeps its old row.
- Round 2, one [Important]: the restored rows came from the pre-redirect index, so a row could keep a `[[link]]` to a merged-away file. Fixed: the rows come from MEMORY.md after its links are redirected.
- Both fixes are proven by a new `/dream` end-to-end test, `tests/dream-e2e.test.ts`. It runs over an in-memory folder with a stubbed fork reply. The second merge is dropped, the survivor keeps its row, and that row's `[[b]]` is redirected. The test fails on main.
- That was the second of at most two rounds, so the round-2 fix was not re-reviewed by Codex.

## Verified
Local checks green (same baseline failures as main), 2 parsePlan/keepListed unit tests + the /dream end-to-end test fail on main and pass here, both Codex findings fixed.

author: adityaaxenogit
body:
On a real phone, tapping next/prev fast (from the start, or past the end) zoomed into the arrow area and black boxes flickered around it.

**Causes**
1. **Zoom**: mobile Safari's double-tap-to-zoom. When the row reaches an end, that arrow becomes `disabled`; a disabled button ignores taps, so two quick taps on it count as a double-tap and the page zooms in.
2. **Black flicker**:
   - the default tap highlight (a dark box browsers flash over a tapped button) on every rapid tap;
   - the card arrow tile's `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)`: the cards change opacity every frame while the row moves (edge fade), and mobile Safari draws blurred layers inside such elements as flickering black rectangles, worst once zoomed.

**Fix** (CSS only)
- `.social-deck-strip-nav`: `touch-action: manipulation` — no double-tap zoom on the arrows or between them (disabled ones included); pinch-zoom of the page still works.
- `.social-deck-strip-btn`: `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent`; hover/focus/disabled styles unchanged.
- Card arrow tile: blur removed (the design specifies only white at 20%, which stays).

**Checked** on an emulated phone (375×815, touch): 12 rapid taps on next then 12 on prev run cleanly start → end → start, zoom stays 100%, no errors; layout unchanged (cards at 266.8, arrows at 713.3). Desktop unchanged. Stylelint passes.

Please confirm on a real iPhone: double-tap zoom itself can't be reproduced in emulation.
