author: xb1g
body:
## Summary

A new Discord bot module, `hackathon-ops`, so the founders can see and update the hackathon's operations from Discord. It is staff only, posts in one channel, sends no DMs and pings nobody.

- `/ops board`: shows every operation with its owner, deadline, status and steps done. Overdue ones are marked 🔴 and ones due within 48 hours 🟡.
- `/ops show`: lists one operation's steps. `/ops claim` makes you the owner. `/ops done` ticks a step (`undo:True` unticks it). `/ops status` sets the status line. The operation and step options autocomplete.
- An 08:30 Bangkok morning post to the configured channel only: what's due in the next 48 hours, what's overdue, and the board. It posts once a day, guarded by a database claim. It posts nothing if the board is empty, every step is done, or the channel can be seen by @everyone.
- Only members with the staff role, in the configured server, can use `/ops`. Replies are public only in the configured staff-only channel. Everywhere else, and for every error, replies are private.
- Storage is migration `20261120100000_hackathon_ops_board.sql`, which is additive and idempotent. The three new tables have RLS on, deny-all policies and no table grants. The new login `hackathon_ops_bot` can only execute `hackathon_ops_*` functions, the same model as `shift_voice_bot`. I applied it twice and exercised it as the bot role on a throwaway Postgres 15.
- The seed script (`bot/scripts/hackathon-ops-seed.ts`) reads the operation pages from a local folder at run time. The repo holds no operation, step, owner or date. Tests use made-up data.
- Registration only upserts `/ops` and never removes another module's commands. **projectseed's registration is now an upsert as well (it used to be a PUT).** With one bot token, the old PUT deleted every other command in `DISCORD_GUILD_ID`. If the team server is that guild, `/ops` would have been wiped the next time projectseed registered. If the module can't reach the database, it logs the problem and keeps running, so the student-facing modules in the same process keep working.

## Try it

Each step needs a person's go. Nothing was applied, registered, deployed or posted from this PR.

1. **Migration:** `supabase db push` applies `20261120100000_hackathon_ops_board.sql` to production.
2. **Login:** give `hackathon_ops_bot` a password, the same way as `shift_voice_bot` in bot/README.md (Deploying): `ALTER ROLE hackathon_ops_bot WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '<SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier>'` via `supabase db query --linked`.
3. **Seed from a local brain checkout** (the `hackathon-ops` branch of company-brain):
   ```bash
   git -C ~/dev/passionseed/company-brain fetch origin hackathon-ops
   git -C ~/dev/passionseed/company-brain worktree add ../company-brain-hackathon-ops hackathon-ops
   read -rs HACKATHON_OPS_DATABASE_URL && export HACKATHON_OPS_DATABASE_URL
   pnpm exec tsx bot/scripts/hackathon-ops-seed.ts ~/dev/passionseed/company-brain-hackathon-ops/private/hackathon-ops --dry-run
   pnpm exec tsx bot/scripts/hackathon-ops-seed.ts ~/dev/passionseed/company-brain-hackathon-ops/private/hackathon-ops
   ```
   You can re-run it safely. An owner, status or tick set in Discord is kept unless you pass `--overwrite`.
4. **Env** in `bot.env`: add `hackathon-ops` to `BOT_MODULES` and set `HACKATHON_OPS_GUILD_ID` (the team server), `HACKATHON_OPS_CHANNEL_ID` (the staff-only ai channel), `HACKATHON_OPS_STAFF_ROLE_ID` and `HACKATHON_OPS_DATABASE_URL`. `HACKATHON_OPS_BOARD` is optional. The bot must be a member of the team server and needs View Channel and Send Messages in that channel.
5. **Deploy, then register:** run `bot/deploy.sh`, then `--register-commands` (bot/README.md, Running). Deploy first, so that a projectseed registration on the team server uses the new upsert.
6. **Run:** type `/ops board` in the ai channel. The first morning post arrives at the next 08:30 Bangkok.

## Checks

- `pnpm test bot/src`: 35 suites, 1018 tests pass (58 new in `bot/src/ops`).
- `pnpm exec tsc -p bot/tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes.
- `pnpm bot:smoke` passes. It also passes with `--env` and the module set, and fails clearly when one of its variables is missing.
- Root `tsc`: the same 458 errors on `main` and on this branch, none in the changed files. The build ignores type errors.
- Locally, `pnpm build` compiles and renders every page, then stops at Next.js's own security audit of the pinned Next version. That stop has nothing to do with this branch, and CI shows the real result.

body:
## The problem `BANK` has a `term` field, and the Review flashcard's front **is** that term. 414 of 552 questions didn't have one — they repeated their own session name instead: | placeholder | questions | |---|---| | `"GDP, Prices & Growth"` | 57 | | `"Transportation"` | 50 | | `"Money & the Fed"` | 46 | | `"Jobs & Finance"` | 39 | | `"Market Failures"` | 33 | | …and 10 more session names | 189 | So a third of the review deck rendered a card whose front said `GDP, Prices & Growth` and whose eyebrow said `GDP, Prices & Growth`. The coach's copy-review list fell back to printing a resource-guide page number, and `blitzLabel()` existed solely to stop the miss list reading "Jobs & Finance Jobs & Finance". ## What this does Every one of the 414 now names the concept it actually tests. Where the bank already had a name for a concept, this reuses it rather than inventing a parallel — that mattered more than it sounds, because several of the unnamed questions are near-twins of named ones. `m12-34` ("a project passes if its IRR exceeds…") is the same question as the already-named `s12-19`, so it takes the same name, `IRR and MARR`. 74 of my first-draft names were rewritten this way after reading each session's existing vocabulary. | session | questions | distinct names | |---|---|---| | 1 Fundamentals | 27 | 15 | | 2 Demand & Supply | 35 | 19 | | 3 Equilibrium & Surplus | 32 | 15 | | 4 Elasticity | 33 | 19 | | 5 Gov't Policy | 33 | 21 | | 6 Market Structures | 33 | 20 | | 7 Market Failures | 43 | 29 | | 8 GDP, Prices & Growth | 57 | 38 | | 9 Jobs & Finance | 56 | 31 | | 10 Money & the Fed | 67 | 38 | | 11 Transportation I | 82 | 34 | | 12 Transportation II | 38 | 19 | | 13 Gains from Trade | 16 | 13 | 285 distinct names over 552 questions. Nothing but `term` changed — the validator compares `id`, `s`, `type`, `q`, `opts`, `a`, `ans`, `tol`, `dec`, `unit`, `spell`, `big`, `why` and `src` on all 552 before and after. `BOSSES` (14 spells) and `CHAIN` (7 links) are untouched. ## Calls worth your veto - **`Store of Value` appears in both session 8 and session 10.** Same concept, two chapters. Left as one name. - **Session 11's `dd5-*` questions cover session 12 material** (deregulation, the Trust Fund, NPV/IRR). They're tagged `s:11` in the bank, so they now carry session 12's names — `Deregulation`, `Project Delivery`, `IRR and MARR`. The name is right; the session tag may be the thing that's wrong. - **Frictional/structural get their own names** rather than joining the existing `Types of Unemployment`. The bank already treats `Cyclical Unemployment` as its own term, so this follows that, but it does mean `Types of Unemployment` and `Frictional Unemployment` now sit side by side. - **`Adverse Selection` for `m7-19`** even though the near-twin `s7-?` carries `Asymmetric Information` — the question says "Adverse selection in the used-car market means:", so the card front should say it back. - **A `Discount Rate` collision was removed**: session 10's Fed lending rate took the bank's existing `Discount vs Fed Funds`, leaving `Discount Rate` to mean only the benefit-cost discount rate in session 12. ## Verified - `0 of 536` taught questions now render a generic flashcard front (was `348 of 536`). - `0` coach review lines fall back to a page reference (was `348`). - `blitzLabel()` never has to fall back; it stays in as a guard for questions added later. - Longest front is 29 characters, unchanged from the longest already in the bank, and it renders in a wrapping `

` — no layout change. - `reg.js`, `blitz.js`, `qa2.js`, `qa3.js`, `verify.js` and a new flashcard check all pass against the patched bank: every mode still plays to a result, all-wrong and all-timeout runs still finish, the raid still sheds its forms, the blitz still has no duplicates and still caps its multiplier. `questions.js` and `game.js` cache tags bumped in `index.html`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: pipekelmanzon
body:
ClickUp: [Materiales: lo generado y el catálogo del colegio](https://app.clickup.com/t/1dfd3mc4bgx)

## Qué se hizo

**Backend (`api/`)**
- Tablas nuevas `materials` y `material_curricular_item`. Modelo `Material` (`BelongsToSchool`, `Auditable`) con `source` = `upload` (archivo) o `assessment` (copia de catálogo de una evaluación confirmada).
- Disco privado nuevo `materials` (`MATERIAL_DISK`, `s3` obligatorio en producción, igual que `reports`). Los archivos se abren solo con enlaces temporales de 5 minutos (regla 7). En producción con disco local se rechaza la subida (503).
- `MaterialPolicy`: Docente y Psicopedagogía suben; Dirección lee. Un material lo ven su dueño, Psicopedagogía y Dirección, y todo el colegio una vez que está en el catálogo. Solo el dueño lo propone al catálogo o lo borra. Psicopedagogía y Dirección lo sacan del catálogo.
- Endpoints `/api/v1/materials` (options, index con prefiltro obligatorio `subject_id` + `grade_id`, store, show, download, publish, `DELETE …/catalog`, destroy, curricular-items) y `POST /api/v1/assessments/{id}/material`.
- Subida (`StoreMaterialRequest`): solo para un grupo × materia que la persona dicta (Psicopedagogía: cualquiera del colegio). Los elementos del programa tienen que salir del catálogo de esa materia (`MaterialCurriculum`, misma lectura que el selector de la Unidad).
- Publicar un archivo exige `confirm_no_student_data` («Revisé que no tenga datos de alumnos»). Se guarda quién y cuándo.
- Publicar una evaluación guarda una copia limpia (`StudentMarkCleaner`): saca las claves de ajustes, alumnos y variantes, tapa los nombres de los alumnos del grupo y cambia el nombre del grupo por «el grupo». En el catálogo nunca se muestra el grupo.
- Al publicar, les llega un aviso a Psicopedagogía y a Dirección (`MaterialPublishedNotification`, pantalla 22).
- Test guardián de `group.writable`: `POST assessments/{assessment}/material` queda exento, porque solo guarda una copia fuera de los registros del grupo.

**Frontend (`web/`)**
- Pantalla nueva `/materiales` («Materiales» en el menú, para los tres roles). Tiene el prefiltro «Antes de buscar» (Materia + Nivel, sin los dos no hay resultados) y dos solapas, «Lo generado» e «Institucional».
- «Subir un recurso propio» (Docente y Psicopedagogía): archivo, grupo, materia, título con la ayuda «Ponele palabras clave…», tipo, etiquetas y un multiselect de elementos del programa. Si la materia no tiene elementos, dice «Todavía no hay elementos del programa cargados para esta materia.».
- Acciones por fila: Abrir, Proponer al catálogo (en un archivo, con la casilla obligatoria), Sacar del catálogo y Eliminar.
- Aviso nuevo en Notificaciones: «Se agregó un material al catálogo del colegio», con un enlace a la carpeta del catálogo.

## Supuestos
- El «Nivel» del prefiltro es el grado del grupo (`school_grade_id`). Los grupos sin grado caen en la carpeta «Sin grado».
- Las carpetas del catálogo son materia × grado, como pidió Eitán.
- «Usar en una clase» y «Usar en una evaluación» no están: dependen de las pantallas 14 y 16 (#209). Mientras tanto, «Abrir» abre el archivo o la evaluación como punto de partida.
- No hay estado «pendiente de aprobación»: el interruptor de Usuarios y permisos › Aprobaciones (pantalla 25) no existe todavía.
- Un archivo subido no pasa por IA (PA-109). Las clases confirmadas se suman cuando exista Nueva clase.

## Documento vivo
- Consultado: pantalla 19 (P19-GEN-01 a 03, P19-INS-01 y 02, P19-DEC-01 a 06, P19-DEC-61 / PA-109, P19-DEC-102 / PA-118 y la línea roja) y AI_SYNC v0.15 a v0.25.
- **Contradicción:** P19-DEC-03 y P19-GEN-03 dicen que al subir «la IA lee el archivo y propone nombre, tipo, etiquetas y elementos». Se siguió la respuesta de Eitán en ClickUp (13/11), que también recoge P19-DEC-61: por ahora sin IA, todo a mano.
- El contenido del desplegable de elementos sale del catálogo del programa de la materia. Lo dijo Eitán en la tarea de la Unidad (1dfd3mc4bga, 17/11), y eso cierra la pregunta que había quedado abierta en esta tarea.

## Fuera de alcance
CLAUDE.md no lista Materiales como fuera de alcance. Se agregaron dos entradas al glosario de `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Validación
- `api/`: `pint --test` OK. `php artisan test`: 1073 tests en verde, 12 nuevos en `MaterialsTest`. Sail/Docker no se usó: se corrió con php y composer directo.
- `web/`: `npm ci`, `npm run lint` (sin errores; solo warnings del mismo tipo que los que ya había), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test` (600 tests, 5 nuevos) y `npm run build`, todo OK.

---

body:
## What changes

The continuity benchmark gets a new design (probe design 2). Old arms, old probe text and old scores do not change.

- Position tag (start, middle, end) for each planted fact. The report shows scores by position for each arm, with counts and the same bootstrap interval.
- Two phrasings: cued and neutral. Code grades both. A self-test checks that no neutral probe holds an auto-recall cue phrase.
- Arm R: Lossless Handoff with `--auto-recall`. The runner records if the hook fired for each probe. The report shows the fire rate for cued and neutral probes.
- No-compaction condition for arms A, B and R: same session length, compaction off. The report compares the position curves.
- `run.sh estimate` and `--dry-run` print the cost of a pilot and of a full run.
- Hypotheses H1 to H5 and their thresholds are in `thresholds.json` and in the README, before any data.

## Checks

- `python3 bench/continuity/test_grader.py`: 52 tests pass.
- `python3 bench/continuity/test_litm.py`: 27 tests pass. They include hashes of old scripts and probe text, and a stored old run that gives the same report byte for byte.
- No model call and no benchmark unit ran.

## Notes

- Arm R needs `hooks/auto-recall.py` in `--lh-path`. That file comes with the auto-recall change. Until then, a run with arm R stops at once with a clear message.
- The cost numbers are estimates from Wave 1 and Wave 2. Some parts are assumptions, and the README says which.

author: moe-berri
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/db64fbf7ad5d41c8b4b63a2b7d726165
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/db64fbf7ad5d41c8b4b63a2b7d726165?variant=devin
Requested by: @moe-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Known app customers lose service when Postgres drops

How it solves it:

- Cache verified app, organization, and member records in Redis
- Keep outage spend in the existing accounting queue
- Reject unverified identities and invalidated policy

Intentional product change: with `litellm_settings.enable_redis_customer_auth_cache` and `general_settings.allow_requests_on_db_unavailable` enabled, recently verified customers can keep calling their app during a Postgres outage. The headers remain optional. Spend follows the gateway’s existing queue and is written after Postgres is reachable.

## User Flow

Before: Postgres goes down and a known customer cannot call their app.

1. Send `POST https://gateway.example/v1/chat/completions` with a valid app credential and known customer organization and member headers. Get 200.
2. Send the same request through a second gateway process after it loses access to Postgres. Get 503.

After: a second gateway with shared Redis answers the known customer's request.

1. Send `POST https://gateway.example/v1/chat/completions` with a valid app credential and known customer organization and member headers. Get 200.
2. Send the same request through a second gateway process after it loses access to Postgres. Get 200, including when the member header is omitted. An unknown app member still gets 503.
3. After Postgres recovers, the gateway includes both outage calls in app spend.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] This PR addresses only customer authentication during database outages
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each finding

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Ran two separate LiteLLM proxy processes sharing one Redis, with a scratch Postgres database and a scripted HTTP upstream. The fault relay drops the second proxy's Postgres connections while leaving the first proxy connected. A live provider is not needed to exercise this auth and accounting behavior.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the live HTTP run</summary>

Use a local Postgres admin DSN in `DATABASE_URL` and a local Redis runtime. The harness starts a separate Redis instance for the two proxies and supplies its host and port to both. From the checkout with the synced proxy and integration dependencies:

```bash
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/tests:$PWD/tests/e2e"
export REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1 REDIS_PORT=6379
export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="sk-$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
export LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-integration-salt LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True
export STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true DO_NOT_TRACK=1
export INTEGRATION_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000
export INTEGRATION_UPSTREAM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18403 INTEGRATION_MASTER_KEY="$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
python -m integration._support.upstream --port 18403 &
upstream=$!
trap 'kill "$upstream"' EXIT
python -m pytest -o addopts='' -xq --tb=short tests/integration/spend/test_app_customer_budgets.py \
  -k known_app_customer --basetemp=/tmp/customer-auth-outage-independent
find /tmp/customer-auth-outage-independent -name 'owned-proxy-*.log' -exec \
  grep -hE '"(POST /v1/chat/completions|GET /key/info|POST /budget/update) HTTP/1.[01]" [0-9]{3} ' {} +
```

The harness calls `python -m integration._support.proxy --config <config> --host 127.0.0.1 --num_workers 1 --timeout_worker_healthcheck <seconds> --use_prisma_db_push` twice on separate ports. Each process has one worker so a single process cannot mask a missing Redis read. Both use this configuration:

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  store_model_in_db: true
  allow_requests_on_db_unavailable: true
  coordination_redis:
    host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST
    port: os.environ/REDIS_PORT
litellm_settings:
  enable_redis_customer_auth_cache: true
```

The HTTP request comes from `_chat` in the test. The client sends the app's virtual key as a bearer token and uses the model and customer identities created through the management API:

```python
gateway.request(
    "POST",
    "/v1/chat/completions",
    {"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"app budget {uuid.uuid4().hex}"}], "max_tokens": 1},
    key=key,
    headers={
        "x-litellm-customer-org-alias": customer.alias,
        **({"x-litellm-customer-member-id": member or customer.member} if include_member else {}),
        **({"x-litellm-app": asserted_app} if asserted_app is not None else {}),
    },
)
```

Before the fault, the test sends `GET /key/info` with the virtual key to the second proxy. This warms only that process's normal key cache. Only the first proxy has seen the customer headers before the fault, and Redis virtual-key caching stays off.

For the before leg, copy the integration test and its database relay helper into a worktree at the merge base. Use that worktree in `PYTHONPATH` and the synced venv in `PATH`. Run the same commands with upstream port `18404` and `--basetemp=/tmp/customer-auth-outage-independent-base`. The base's production code is unchanged.

</details>

### Before (78ddb5e4de1928233e5438817732993adf0b31b6)

1. Send the known org and member request to the connected proxy. It logs `POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK`.
2. Drop the second proxy's Postgres connections and send the request there. It logs `POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 503 Service Unavailable`, with `type: no_db_connection`.

### After (5d2bec15a6021899a0fb54ad1a0e6b30c329334d)

1. Send the known org and member request to the connected proxy. It logs `POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK`.
2. Drop the second proxy's Postgres connections and send the request there. It logs `POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK`.
3. The org-only request returns 200, a mismatched app header returns 403, and a member not previously seen by the app returns 503 without an app-member row.
4. Neither outage request has a spend row while the connection is down. Restore the connection and send another request. It returns 200.
5. Send `POST /budget/update` with the app's budget ID and a lower limit to the first proxy. It returns 200. During the next fault, the second proxy logs `POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 503 Service Unavailable`.

6. Query Postgres after recovery. The two outage request IDs and the recovered request ID each have one spend row of $0.06. The persisted app total is $0.24, including the warm-up request.

On `e2e7da905d`, that same spend-log query found only the recovered request. On `8a8e7d3458`, the same budget-update regression test got `200 OK` at step 5 because the old snapshot was still valid.

`make check` and the 42 app-auth unit tests passed. The focused integration test ran locally against real services. The scheduled integration workflow runs on main rather than on every PR.

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### Medium

- App snapshots expire after at most 60 seconds
- Credential authentication still needs its normal cache or provider
- Unverifiable budgets fail closed instead of permitting outage traffic
- The existing spend queue is in memory until it flushes. It does not preserve pending entries across a proxy restart.

### Low

- With both outage settings enabled, healthy customer requests still read Postgres and populate Redis
- Live outage proof covers chat completions with virtual keys

author: shepherdjerred
body:
## Why

The local voice cascade (`scout-voice`) and the voice route (`coach/voice/turns`, #4642) existed, but nothing in Scout Desktop used them: no process owned the microphone, there were no push-to-talk or mute keys, and the window could neither show nor control voice.

## What

- **The supervisor owns the microphone; the window process never opens it.** `scout-voice` gains an engine (`engine.rs`) that runs the cascade and the input device on one thread and holds the device open only while listening or recording, and a speaker (`playback.rs`, cpal output with a linear resampler) for the answer's PCM. Conversation mode now opens at gameflow `GameStart` as well as `InProgress`, and closes at `WaitingForStats`, `EndOfGame` and every other phase.
- **A pure voice controller** (`scout-client-app/src/voice/controller.rs`) decides everything from inputs (gameflow, keys, window commands, engine events, turn events) and returns effects: consent first (persisted in `settings.json`, off until accepted, asked on first use by bringing the window forward), conversation mode, mute, push-to-talk, and the spoken turn (thinking → speaking → finish once the answer has played; push-to-talk over the answer cuts it off). The service (`voice/mod.rs`) carries effects out through ports: engine, voice route, speaker, settings file, global keys.
- **Keys.** Push-to-talk (on by default, `F8`) and mute (`Shift+F8`) via `global-hotkey`, registered on the tray's winit event loop (`hotkeys.rs`; no `scout-platform` crate exists, so this is the narrowest place). Settings offers other keys; any accelerator in `settings.json` works and is validated.
- **Player-authored turns.** A finished utterance becomes a WAV in `voice/capture.rs`, the one place that mints `PlayerAuthored<Utterance>`; `ExploreClient::start_voice_turn` now takes only that type, and `authored.rs`' workspace test pins the mint sites. The turn carries the chat's open conversation and the supervisor's allowlisted `LiveSnapshot`; the SSE stream (`transcript`, `run`, `answer`, `audio`, `error`, `done`) drives the controller, and the conversation opens in chat when the answer is done.
- **IPC protocol 10**: `voice` (state off/listening/capturing/thinking/speaking/muted/error, consent, muted, settings, detail) and `voice_turn` (heard, answer, error) supervisor → window; `voice` commands (consent, set muted, set settings) window → supervisor. No audio crosses the link; decoding stays strict.
- **Window** (gpui): the mic state beside "Scout" on every page (click to mute/unmute), a first-use consent dialog, the spoken turn above the chat transcript, and a Voice section in Settings (on/off, conversation mode, push-to-talk, push-to-talk and mute keys). The egui window ignores voice; the supervisor runs voice only with the gpui window on Windows and macOS.
- **Docs**: `desktop/README.md` gains a Voice section and the privacy table now says microphone audio leaves the device only as a finished utterance to the voice route; `scout-voice/README.md` updated.

## Verification

All tests use deterministic fakes: a scripted microphone (chunks fed by the test, silence otherwise), fake detectors, a recording speaker, an in-memory settings store, fake hotkey port, scripted gameflow, and a scripted voice route (SSE bytes through `voice_events`, and a fake `TurnRunner`). No real app, audio device or socket; every async wait has a deadline.

- `mise exec -- cargo test --manifest-path packages/scout-for-lol/packages/desktop/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features` — all pass (new: `scout-voice/tests/engine.rs` 7, playback 4, controller 16, voice service 4, capture 2, turns 2, hotkeys 3, IPC voice wire shape, voice view models 6, settings 3, `only_voice_capture_mints_a_spoken_turn`).
- `mise exec -- cargo clippy --manifest-path packages/scout-for-lol/packages/desktop/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` — clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `bunx turbo run typecheck test lint --filter=@scout-for-lol/desktop` — 3/3 successful.
- `bunx lefthook run pre-commit` — pass.
- Extended tier: `@scout-for-lol/desktop` has no `tier: "extended"` steps. `bunx turbo run test:extended --filter='...[origin/main]'` was not run: the desktop workspace has none, and the backend extended suites (PostgreSQL/Temporal) are not touched by this change.

body:
## What and why

This is the API half of step 1 of the Marketing v2 build plan (#502).

It adds the `marketing` feature flag: env `FEATURE_MARKETING_ENABLE`, PostHog key `marketing`, off until the key is created. Behind the flag it adds `GET /:workspace/marketing/overview?range=7d|30d|90d`, which needs CUSTOMER read. `range` defaults to `7d` and reuses the dashboard's analytics range.

One call returns everything the Tổng quan page shows:

- **Stages:** customers per stage now and at the start of the range, plus the Lâu không nhắn count.
- **Funnel:** split by the channel each customer first wrote from. Each step counts the customers at that stage or further along.
- **Stage moves:** moves within the range (stage then → stage now), largest first.
- **Việc nên làm:** the six counts. These always cover this week, whatever the range:
  - new this week
  - Quan tâm customers still writing
  - asked the price this week
  - 15 to 30 days after a first order
  - near the product group's repurchase cycle
  - bought, then 31 to 90 days silent

  Opted-out, paused and Khó chịu customers are counted apart, and the response includes a distinct total.
- **List health:** opt-outs within the range against the range before, and customers paused now.

The code is a new module, `apps/api/src/modules/marketing`, with a raw SQL repository like the dashboard analytics. The stage at the start of the range comes from the first STAGE event in the range. A customer with no state row reads as Mới biết.

The PR also adds `marketing: false` to the app's flags-off fallback (`apps/app/src/hooks/api/feature-flags.ts`), since the regenerated client makes the field required. The app page is ready and goes in the next PR, so each PR stays under 40 files.

Screenshots of the page on this API with 640 sample customers: https://claude.ai/artifact/4V4VKmoscDxMjNHKYw1D4D

- `pnpm --filter api test`: 424 suites and 3776 tests pass, including the new `marketing-overview.service.spec.ts` and the updated flag service spec.
- New e2e `test/e2e/marketing-overview.e2e-spec.ts` against local Postgres 16 + pgvector: 6/6 pass, including `?range=30d`.

author: marvin-bitterlich
body:
### Why?

When a call to an outside API failed the status filter, the failure reported only the status. The provider's own explanation, such as `{"error":"invalid_grant"}` or a rate-limit message, was thrown away, so it never reached application logs.

### How?

- `checkStatus` (and therefore `filterStatus`) reads an excerpt of the error body before it fails. The new `bodyExcerpt.ts` does the work:
  - It reads at most the first **2048 bytes** (`BODY_EXCERPT_BYTES`) of `response.stream`, then stops reading and releases the stream. When the body is cut, the last partial word is dropped and the excerpt ends with `…`.
  - It has a **one-second** deadline (`bodyExcerptDeadline`) on Effect's clock. If the body has not ended or reached the bound by then, or if reading it fails or someone already consumed it, the status failure is reported without an excerpt.
  - It decodes the bytes as UTF-8 and collapses runs of whitespace. A body that is empty, not valid UTF-8 or contains control bytes gets no excerpt.
  - The text then goes through `redactText` from `@shivaedev/errors/sensitive.ts` with the default sensitive keys. `http` cannot read the server's `RedactionPolicy`, because `server` depends on `http`.
  - A 2xx response is never read.
- All five status failures get an optional `bodyExcerpt` field and share one `message`: `HTTP 400: POST host/path: <excerpt>`. Before this change only `RemoteHttpError` had a message.
- `ReadClientError` with reason `status` carries `bodyExcerpt` too.
- `@shivaedev/http` now depends on the workspace package `@shivaedev/errors`. No external dependency is added.
- GitHub kit: three `releasedBodies` stories hold a 404 or 401 body open, so they now advance the one-second excerpt deadline through a named trait.
- README, AGENTS.md and the changeset are updated. The changeset is a minor bump with Added and Changed entries. Nothing is breaking: the new field is optional.

### Proof

- New stories in `failureBodies.spec.ts` drive the real fetch and node clients against the kit's fake HTTP server. They show:
  - the error text reaches both the excerpt and the message;
  - a 3000-byte body that is held open is cut at 2048 bytes without waiting for the rest;
  - a JSON `access_token` value and a `Bearer` credential are masked;
  - a binary body gets no excerpt;
  - a body that never ends fails as HTTP 400 without an excerpt once the deadline passes;
  - a reset body fails as HTTP 400 without an excerpt;
  - a body the caller already read fails as HTTP 400 without an excerpt.
- `readApis.spec.ts` gains a story for `ReadClientError` carrying the excerpt.
- `bodyExcerpt.unit.test.ts` covers the pure helper.
- These packages and specs pass: `@shivaedev/http` (209), `@shivaedev/github` (441), discord, pr-watch, agent-opencode, and server `otlpExportFailure.spec.ts`.
- `pnpm ready` passes.

Skipped edge cases (likelihood × severity): an error body that declares a non-UTF-8 charset such as Latin-1 (2×2); a secret longer than 2 KiB that straddles the cut (1×6, partly mitigated by dropping the partial word).

- With no `feature.json`, Spec Kit scripts fall back to `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`, or `/speckit-specify` writes the file again.
- No code, configuration, or documentation changes.

author: agreewithscotty
body: ## Why the row lagged Moving right was slow because every left/right press did Python work on Kodi's GUI thread before the list could finish the move. `AuroraHome.onAction` treated action ids 1 and 2 as hero updates. On each press it took the catalog lock (the same lock the background loader holds while publishing rows), read `getControl(200).getSelectedPosition()`, wrote the `Hero*` window properties, and called `setColorDiffuse` on the full-screen scrim. The scrim color never changes. `onFocus` then did that work again after the selection moved. The 0.2.2 skin was already painting the hero from `Container(200).ListItem`, so those property writes did not make the hero follow any sooner. They only held the key down. The focused card also zoomed and slid for 160ms, and the backdrop crossfaded for 80ms, so the same step felt late as well as heavy. ## What 0.2.3 does - The hero title, metadata line, and synopsis are `$INFO[Container(200).ListItem...]`. The title uses the bundled Bebas Neue face at 168px with tight leading, all caps, and room to wrap to two lines. Empty states (signed out, connecting, no results) still use window properties, because the list is empty then. - The synopsis is the full plot in a `textbox` with ``. Kodi resets that scroll when the label changes, which happens as focus moves because the label is the focused card's plot. - `onAction` ignores plain left/right. There is no `onFocus` handler. Scroll time is 0, the focus zoom and slide are gone, and the backdrop fadetime is 0. Focus is still the 4px white border and the undimmed card. Card art is requested at 720px wide and hero art at 1280px wide from Amazon's image host, so the texture cache is not storing the full master. Other image URLs are unchanged. - Selecting a card plays it through the existing `mode=PlayVideo` URL (`xbmc.Player().play`). A series plays `info['next']`, `next_episode`, `resume`, or the first entry of `info['episodes']` when that row is already a PlayVideo item. A rail card that only has a detail link opens that page. If the page contains exactly one PlayVideo row, that row starts (this is how a storefront movie, which has no ASIN on the card, starts). If it contains several, the page stays up as the episode list and nothing starts on its own. Movies and TV shortcuts do not use that one-item start. - The title window is gone. Nothing opened it after the details button was removed. Grey/charcoal, no EXPLORE filler, the non-colliding window names, and `repository.primescene` pointing at `https://agreewithscotty.github.io/ScottyWins` are unchanged. ## Verification `python3 tools/test_aurora_ui.py` — all checks passed, including no hero buttons, card click to `PlayVideo`, hero bindings on `Container(200).ListItem`, synopsis autoscroll, and no `setProperty` / `getControl` on left or right. `python3 -m unittest test_signin_transport.py` (from `source/rewrite`) — `Ran 15 tests`, `OK (skipped=1)`. `zipfile.ZipFile(...0.2.3.zip).testzip()` — `None`. `addons.xml.md5` matches the md5 of `addons.xml`. `kodi-addon-checker --branch omega` on the unpacked 0.2.3 add-on and on `packages/repository.primescene` — exit 0. Both reported `We found no problems` (warnings only, the same dependency, webp, and repository-zip warnings as 0.2.2).

author: seven332
body:
## Change

Stream Linux ordinary WRITE_FILES payloads starting at 1 MiB into the existing sealed helper input. The cutoff was 4 MiB. This removes the full decoder buffer, worker request copy and helper pipe transfer for newly eligible requests.

Move the malformed and disconnected streaming tests to 2 MiB to exercise the newly eligible range. The tests verify rejection, following-frame handling, and that a partial payload never writes its target.

## Serving observation

On Runner 0.249.69–0.249.71, 29 successful archive staging writes had 1–4 MiB of content and complete frame-write measurements in the selected 18-hour window. Staging P90 was 104 ms. A 14-file, 3.46 MB stage took 108 ms in a Blank Run with 1,021 ms API-to-spawn. The receiver cutoff uses encoded payload size.

## Local-11 comparison

Matched release x86_64-musl builds from main 9d20531a and head 44fc4199. Eight independent 2-vCPU Firecracker Guests used private NBD/COW roots and ext4 Home volumes. Four alternating boot pairs yielded 112 measured replays per arm and case. All 1,120 replays reached a following Guest exec and verified extracted bytes, mode, mtime, UID and GID.

| Staged content | Staging P90 (ms) | Write through apply and next exec P50 (ms) | P90 (ms) | P99 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.57 MB, below cutoff | 6.27 → 6.41 | 18.20 → 18.01 | 18.96 → 18.78 | 20.40 → 19.84 |
| 1.87 MB, one archive | 11.11 → 7.39 | 29.92 → 26.14 | 31.27 → 27.14 | 34.00 → 28.00 |
| 3.25 MB, 14 archives | 16.71 → 10.44 | 42.07 → 35.50 | 45.30 → 37.69 | 48.95 → 41.62 |
| 4.09 MB, near old cutoff | 19.86 → 12.42 | 53.74 → 46.35 | 57.07 → 49.27 | 62.57 → 50.39 |
| 12.98 MB, already sealed | 28.30 → 29.04 | 95.71 → 95.42 | 103.09 → 101.69 | 111.61 → 112.81 |

Each of the four boot pairs improved median replay latency on all three affected shapes. For 3.25 MB, the response wait P90 fell from 12.76 to 6.42 ms while frame-write P90 was 2.59 and 2.56 ms. The 13 MB control varied across boot pairs. This measures the staging and Guest application boundary on a prebooted VM. Production API-to-spawn remains a serving measurement.

The tradeoff is using the existing bounded, memory-backed sealed file for more requests. Full-frame preflight, single-active write admission, helper identity, and settlement still apply. The change is confined to transient Guest IPC.

## Verification

- Workspace Rust formatting check
- Locked tests for guest-control-server, guest-write-file and guest-init using the local profile. 436 passed and five existing opt-in tests were ignored.
- Locked Clippy for the same crates with all targets and features and warnings denied
- Local-11 native comparison above

Closes #49434. Related to #48246.

author: stereokkh
body:
## 작업 내용
계획은 Windows 쪽 Claude 세션, 코딩은 WSL(각자) Claude 세션에서 하는데, 세션끼리는 git 말고 공유하는 게 없습니다. **저장소(develop)를 유일한 기준**으로 삼고, develop이 움직이면 각 세션의 Claude가 알아채도록 구성합니다.

- `.claude/settings.json` (팀 공용): SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit 훅에서 `scripts/claude-sync.sh` 실행
- `scripts/claude-sync.sh`
  - `origin/develop` fetch → 현재 브랜치에 없는 커밋이 있으면 **커밋 목록 + 바뀐 공유 파일(CLAUDE.md, docs/, include/ 등) + 지시**를 Claude 컨텍스트로 출력
  - 프롬프트 훅은 15분에 한 번만 fetch, 지난번 알림 뒤로 develop이 움직였을 때만 출력 (소음 없음)
  - develop에 있고 작업 트리가 깨끗하면 fast-forward만. **작업 브랜치는 건드리지 않음**
  - 오프라인, git 저장소 아님, 최신 상태면 조용히 끝남
- `docs/decisions.md`: 날짜별 결정 기록 (오늘 결정 5건)
- CLAUDE.md "세션 간 동기화": 결정이 바뀌면 decisions.md + CLAUDE.md를 같은 PR로 / 알림 받으면 읽고 따르고, 충돌하면 사용자에게
- `.gitignore`: `.claude/settings.local.json` (개인 설정)

## 테스트 방법
WSL 임시 클론에서 6가지 상황 확인:
| 상황 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| 작업 브랜치가 develop보다 6커밋 뒤, session | 커밋 6개 + 바뀐 파일 + 지시 출력 ✅ |
| 바로 이어서 prompt (15분 안) | 출력 없음 ✅ |
| prompt, 간격 0, develop 그대로 | 출력 없음 (이미 알림) ✅ |
| develop이 뒤처지고 깨끗함 | fast-forward 후 알림 ✅ |
| 최신 상태 | 출력 없음 ✅ |
| git 저장소 아님 | 출력 없음, exit 0 ✅ |

Windows Git Bash에서도 실행 확인 (최신 상태 → 출력 없음, exit 0). `settings.json` JSON 검증.

머지 후 WSL 쪽에서 할 일: `git checkout develop && git pull` 한 번 (그다음부터는 훅이 알려 줌). 처음 세션에서 프로젝트 훅 승인이 뜰 수 있음.

## 체크리스트
- [x] Linux(WSL)에서 실행 확인
- [ ] macOS에서 확인 (POSIX sh + git만 사용)
- [x] 코드 변경 없음 (src/ 영향 없음)

body:
## What's changed

The Models page measured a model against the GPU's *free* memory only, so a 15.7 GB model on a 32 GB RTX 5090 read "Too big" and "Context that fits now: 0 of 256k" while a picture model held 19 GB. It fits the card; it just does not fit beside what is loaded.

- The GPU facts now show **Takes** (weights and buffers, before context), **Context on a free GPU** (the card less a 2 GB desktop reserve) next to **Context that fits now**, and, when the two differ, a line naming the other models in memory and how much the GPU has in use.
- A model that only the busy GPU cannot hold reads **Fits on a free GPU** instead of "Too big", on its variant row and its family row. "Too big" stays for models that do not fit the card, and a model capped by its saved GPU layers reads **Part on CPU by its settings**.
- The "Part on CPU" tooltip names the busy GPU as a cause and suggests unloading.
- Spec updated: `spec/models/server-model-browser-and-desktop-tray.md`.

Closes #3116

Fixture: a 27B Q4_K_M vision model on a 31.8 GB RTX 5090 with 12.7 GB free and SD3.5 Large in memory (hidden, off-screen Electron capture against a stub bridge).

Before:
![before](https://github.com/nekko-labs/nekko-agent/releases/download/pr-media-8/pr-3118-pr-3118-models-before.png)

After:
![after](https://github.com/nekko-labs/nekko-agent/releases/download/pr-media-8/pr-3118-pr-3118-models-after.png)

author: tubalainen
body:
Closes #30

## Bakgrund
Vid generering för 46 kameror med ett dygn bilder visade nvtop 10–20 % GPU, och htop visade en load average på 2,7 av 16 trådar med bara 3 ffmpeg åt gången. GPU-platsen omfattar hela MP4-kedjan: JPEG-avkodning, skalning och graf görs på CPU, och bara kodningen på GPU. JPEG-avkodningen i ffmpeg är i praktiken enkeltrådad per jobb, så med 3 platser stod de flesta CPU-trådarna stilla.

## Vad som ändras
- **MP4 och GIF görs parallellt i varje klipp.** GIF:en använder bara CPU och väntar inte längre på MP4:ans GPU-plats. Misslyckas den ena delen avbryts den andra, och ffmpeg-processen dödas, så att inget skriver i en borttagen temporär katalog.
- **Nya standardvärden:** 8 samtidiga jobb (förut 4) och 6 GPU-kodningar (förut 3). Hjälptexterna förklarar att GPU-platsen även omfattar avkodningen på CPU. Värden som redan är sparade i admin påverkas inte.
- **Tid per steg** (bilder, graf, MP4, GIF och totalt) visas i jobbmeddelandet, i översiktens "Senaste genereringar" och i loggen (`Clip … done in … s`). Då syns vad som tar tid på den riktiga servern.
- **Mätt och förkastat:** en processpool för grafen. Grafen tar cirka 1 s av 15 s per klipp, och arbetsprocesser skulle importera `app.main` en gång till.

Version 0.1.11. README, `.env.example` och projektminnet är uppdaterade.

## Mätning i sandlådan
Ett dygn med 1 440 bilder i 1080p, 30 s klipp, MP4 och GIF, libx264 på 4 kärnor:

| | Före | Efter |
|-|------|-------|
| 1 klipp | 17,0 s | 14,9 s |

Tid per steg efter ändringen: bilder 0,1 s, graf 1,2 s, GIF 3,3 s, MP4 13,7 s. Med NVENC är MP4-steget kortare, men avkodningen på CPU finns kvar. Därför ger fler samtidiga jobb mest på en server med 16 trådar.

## Testat
- `scripts/check-secrets.sh`, ruff och pytest: 93 passerade. Nya tester:
  - ett fel i GIF-delen avbryter MP4-delen och ger ett vanligt fel, och inget klipp sparas
  - jobbmeddelandet innehåller tiderna
  - tidsformatet
- I webbläsaren: översikten visar "tid 15,3 s (bilder 0,1 · graf 1,3 · GIF 3,4 · MP4 14,1)".

## Inte testat
- **NVENC på riktig GPU.** Pröva gärna en körning med 46 kameror och jämför den totala tiden och htop. Tiderna per steg i översikten visar om MP4-steget (avkodningen) fortfarande dominerar.

## 마이그레이션 — 이번 머지로 운영 DB에 V30~V32가 새로 적용된다

지난 릴리즈(#73)와 달리 이번엔 **실제 스키마 변경이 운영에 처음 들어간다.** #83부터 develop은 pi2(개발 DB)로만 배포되도록 분리됐기 때문이다.

| 버전 | PR | 운영 DB 상태 | 내용 |
|------|----|--------------|------|
| V26 | #72 | 이미 적용(분리 전 develop 배포) | `driving_goal`·`review.content` → TEXT |
| V27 | #77 | 이미 적용 | `member.filter_tags` → `sort_tags` 이름 변경 |
| V28 | #78 | 이미 적용 | 닉네임 공백→`_` 변환, `lower(nickname)` 유니크 인덱스 |
| V29 | #81 | 이미 적용 | `member.nickname_changed_at` 추가 |
| **V30** | #86 | **신규** | `review.difficulty`·`congestion` NOT NULL 해제, `ck_review_recommended_ratings` CHECK, `review_course_issue` 테이블·`course_issue_detail` 컬럼 추가 |
| **V31** | #88 | **신규** | `course_report`·`course_report_issue` 테이블 생성 |
| **V32** | #88 | **신규** | `review_course_issue` → `course_report` 이관 후 `review_course_issue` 테이블·`course_issue_detail` 컬럼 **삭제** |

- V30이 만든 테이블·컬럼을 V32가 바로 지우는 구조라, 운영에서는 옮길 행이 없고 결과적으로 **review NOT NULL 해제 + CHECK 추가, course_report 테이블 2개 신설**만 남는다.
- `ck_review_recommended_ratings`는 "추천 후기면 난이도·혼잡도 필수"라 기존 행(모두 둘 다 있음)과 충돌하지 않는다.
- 머지 전 확인 — 운영 DB가 V29까지 적용돼 있어야 한다:

```sql
SELECT MAX(version::numeric) FROM flyway_schema_history WHERE success;  -- 머지 전 29, 배포 후 32
```

## 이 배포가 실제로 하는 일

- 운영 앱에 후기 별로에요 문제 항목·코스 신고 API가 새로 열린다(V30~V32 적용 포함).
- V26~V29에 해당하는 기능 코드는 분리 전 develop 배포로 이미 운영에 떠 있었으므로 동작 변화 없다.
- `cd.yml`이 main 전용으로 바뀐 버전이 main에 들어온다. 이후 develop push는 운영에 배포되지 않는다(`cd-dev.yml` → pi2).
- 운영 신규 환경변수 없음(`deploy/compose.prod.yaml` 변경 없음).

## 관련 이슈

- 각 기능의 이슈(#71·#75·#80·#82·#85·#87)는 위 PR에서 이미 close 됐다. 이 PR은 배포 묶음이라 별도 이슈 없음.

## 체크리스트

- [x] `./gradlew test` 통과 (develop 기준)
- [x] 각 기능 스펙의 완료 조건 충족 (개별 PR에서 확인 완료)
- [x] 필요한 문서/스펙 갱신

## 참고

- **머지 순서 주의** — 이 PR은 develop을 추적하므로, 머지 전에 develop에 새 커밋이 들어가면 그것까지 함께 배포된다.
- V32는 테이블·컬럼을 DROP하는 비가역 마이그레이션이다(운영엔 데이터가 없어 손실은 없음). 롤백 시 이전 이미지로 되돌려도 스키마는 V32 상태로 남는다 — 이전 코드는 삭제된 객체를 쓰지 않으므로 동작에는 문제 없다.

author: kwhorne
body:
Implements [RFC 0041](docs/proposals/0041-quick-look.md). **Depends on #267 (the RFC).** Until that's merged, this PR shows its commit too.

**`WindowConfig::read_only()`**
- **Commands:** only `#[command(live)]` commands run. A call from the window runs under the live write guard (`elyra_db::live::track`), so a model-layer or backend write fails, whether the command is subscribed to or called once. Any other command is refused with `denied`, "this window only reads".
- **`can`:** says no to the abilities only commands that may write need.
- **Routes:** an allowlist of the ones that read (`security::read_only_allows`). The capabilities that change something are denied.
- **The assistant:** in that window it's offered only live tools.

**Quick Look**
- **The window:** one for the app, label `quick-look`, read-only. It's made the first time with the route as `#/…`, then hidden; a later show moves it by setting `location.hash`.
- **Placement and focus:** placed to the right, the left, or over the right part of its window (`QuickLookSpot::beside`). The window it came from is focused again.
- **Closing:** its close button hides it, and it hides when the window it was shown beside closes. It also hides when the app goes to the background: when the app's last focused window loses focus, the loop checks again 300 ms later. It doesn't keep the app running.
- **Routes:** only the app's own routes (`/…` or `#/…`), never a URL.
- **Frontend:** `quickLook.show/hide/here` and `$quickLook` in `@elyra/runtime`. In `<Table preview>`, Space previews (⌘Y / Ctrl+Y with `select`), ↓/↑ follow, Space or Esc closes, and Enter opens.
- **Rust and generation:** `Windows::show_quick_look`. `make:resource --view` writes `preview` on its lists.

**Tests**
- `tests/read_only_window.rs`: only live commands, a live command that writes refused at the write, the routes, and `can`.
- Unit tests for the route rule and the placement.
- `<Table preview>` (4) and `quickLook` (3).
- Locally: all 1328 Rust tests pass, ui has 517 and runtime 213, and lint is clean on every feature set.

**Not yet**
- Trying the window's placement and focus by hand on macOS, Windows and Linux.

author: xrfxlp
body:
## Summary

Part of #2247. Design for the metadata-collector part of #2419.

Proposes ADR-072. It moves the pod device mapper out of metadata-collector into its own module, image and DaemonSet, as the [component classification](docs/designs/070-vendor-neutral-core.md#component-classification) of ADR-070 plans. metadata-collector keeps only the NVIDIA discovery.

### Decisions

1. The mapper becomes the `pod-device-mapper` module, built with ko on the default static base. It does not import metadata-collector or NVML.
2. The mapper runs in its own DaemonSet with no vendor settings. Its node selector, `podMapper.nodeSelector`, defaults to `nvidia.com/gpu.present`, so current installs keep the mapper on their GPU nodes. To run it on nodes with other devices from ADR-071, an operator changes that selector. The mapper's metrics use `global.metricsPort`, like the other modules on the pod network. `metrics.port` stays with the discovery, so the mapper's port changes on clusters that set it.
3. metadata-collector keeps the NVIDIA discovery, its CUDA image and `gpu_metadata.json`. The discovery moves to a new ServiceAccount with no ClusterRole, and the mapper keeps the existing ServiceAccount and ClusterRole, so the old pods keep their access during the upgrade.
4. Until ADR-070 creates the NVIDIA plugin chart, the metadata-collector chart renders both DaemonSets, so every `metadata-collector` key that operators set today keeps working. The mapper keys then migrate once, with the rest of the chart.

### Out of scope

The labeler part of #2419, a chart layout for the NVIDIA plugin, a chart of its own for the mapper, MIG (#2320) and GPU sharing (#2451).

## Testing
- [ ] Tests pass locally
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [x] No breaking changes (or documented)

Checked with `helm template` (v3.19.2) on a minimal umbrella chart with two subcharts how a separate mapper chart would carry `metadata-collector.podMapper.enabled` through a dependency condition. The condition needs the subchart default removed, and Helm skips a quoted `"false"` with only a warning and starts the mapper. These results are why the ADR keeps the mapper DaemonSet in the metadata-collector chart for now.

author: cl-ghostdev
body:
**Status (2026-11-21): ready; the merge is Chii's.**
- Head is c28864d, with `main` merged in and not rebased.
- CI is green on Linux 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 and on macOS, installed from the lock.
- Merging touches nothing under `ledger/`, so it does not start `block.yml`.
- aikiri-network has no security check of its own. An independent review in another session, the CAIO's, covered security, and its findings are fixed in c28864d.
- Codex's last code review raised one P2: refuse a dangling symlink at `ledger/requests/next.json`. It moves to a separate follow-up PR and is not fixed here.

Story 1 of 3, the ledger side only. A whole course cohort's certificates are sealed as **one block**. Anyone holding one certificate can show it was in that cohort, and whether it was revoked. They can check with the CLI, or in the browser from the public files under `ledger/certs/`.

## What changed

- **New root kind `cert-cohort`** in `ROOT_KINDS`. The one-root-per-block rule (`parse_roots`) is unchanged: the root is the Merkle root of the cohort's fingerprints.
- **`aikiri_ledger/cohort.py`**
  - The Merkle Tree Hash of RFC 9162 (§2.1.1, the same as RFC 6962), with its audit path (§2.1.3).
  - Leaves and nodes take text domain prefixes, `aikiri-ledger/cert-leaf/v1\n` and `aikiri-ledger/cert-node/v1\n`.
  - Leaves are sorted and must all differ (1 to 65,536). An odd leaf is carried up, never duplicated.
  - Every proof comes from one walk of the tree, O(n log n). A full cohort builds in about a second.
  - `verify_proof` is a pure function.
- **Issuer record format.** This is the format only; every value in the repo is fake except the fixed issuer.
  - Fields: `v`, `number` (128–256 random bits, hex), `holder`, `course`, `completed` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `issuer` (exactly `Chiibitsu Labs` in v1), `instructor`, and an optional `host`.
  - Encoding: UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys, no whitespace. These are the bytes a browser's `JSON.stringify` gives for the sorted object. Strings must already be NFC; they are never normalised.
  - `fingerprint = sha256("aikiri-ledger/cert-record/v1\n" + bytes)`.
  - The payload, for `/network/cert#<payload>`, is base64url of those bytes with no padding. It must re-encode to itself, so there is one payload per record.
- **Public layout, hashes only:**
  - `ledger/certs/<fingerprint>.json` holds the proof.
  - `ledger/certs/revoked/<fingerprint>.json` holds `{v, fingerprint, block}`.
  - Both are pointers. A reader trusts only the block a file names, and a proof must sit under its own fingerprint's name.
- **CLI** `aikiri-ledger cohort …`
  - `build <file> --out <dir>`: a preview. It requests nothing, and refuses a folder inside the ledger.
  - `seal <file> [--push]`: writes the request, then writes each proof to `ledger/certs/`, naming the block the request is bound to.
    - With `--push`, it pulls first, then takes one paste, one passphrase and one approval.
    - Rerun on a cohort that is already sealed, it pushes any proof that is missing or changed.
  - `verify <proof | record.json | payload or URL>`: prints `VALID`, `REVOKED`, `NOT FOUND` or `INVALID`, plus the offline state of this ledger copy.
    - It prints the fingerprint, never the record or the input.
    - A payload of any length is read as a payload.
  - `revoke <proof> [--push]`: seals that fingerprint under the existing `revocation` kind and writes the revoked pointer.
    - It is refused unless verify would say VALID.
    - Rerun on a certificate that is already revoked, it repairs a missing or wrong pointer, or retries its push, and writes no second block.
  - Proofs and pointers are written through a fresh temporary file that never follows a link.
- **How the public files get committed:** in the same commit and push as the request. `_push_request` carries the request plus those files, and nothing else. `block.yml` is unchanged; it neither needs nor touches `ledger/certs/`.
- **`docs/certificates.md`** covers:
  - the fingerprint and record contract, and the exact canonical-bytes rules for the browser;
  - the payload;
  - the public layout and how a reader must check it;
  - the commands, the tree and the proof format;
  - plainly, what the public files reveal.
- **`ci.yml`**: the golden steps on Linux and macOS also run the golden tests in `tests/test_cohort.py`, and `cohort.py` joins the macOS path filter. No other workflow is touched.

## Proof format

```json
{"block":7,"leaf":"<fingerprint>","path":[{"sha256":"…","side":"right"}],"root":"<cohort root>","v":1}
```

- A closed schema, written canonically; no key may appear twice.
- `side` is where the sibling sits.
- `block` is `null` in a proof from `build`, which reads as NOT FOUND.

## Tests

`tests/test_cohort.py` has 165 tests.

- **Golden vectors** in `tests/vectors/cert_cohort.json`. The check page's TypeScript tests against the same file.
  - Fake records: one plain, one with a host, one with a non-ASCII NFC holder, escapes and an emoji.
  - 1-, 2- and 3-leaf cohorts with sample blocks, and one revoked fingerprint.
  - `reader_cases`: one per NOT FOUND and INVALID branch, including a proof filed under another certificate's name.
  - `revoked_file_cases`.
- **Two references for the tree:**
  - an independent RFC 9162 reference that reproduces the CT 8-entry test tree;
  - the one-walk builder, held to the per-leaf RFC path for sizes 1–33.
- **The tree itself:** odd counts, a single-leaf cohort, a leaf posing as a node, tampered proofs (14 ways), and a full 65,536-certificate cohort.
- **Bad input:**
  - a stale request, junk files, duplicate keys, planted temp-file links;
  - a quoted-JSON record file, and proof names in other letter cases.
- **The flows:**
  - revocation, pointer repair, and pointer-push retry;
  - verify by record, by short and long payload, and by URL, with errors that never echo the input;
  - `--push` carrying only the request and its files;
  - pull-before-read for both seal and revoke;
  - pushing repaired proofs.

## Review

- **Security:** aikiri-network has no security check of its own. An independent review in another session, the CAIO's, covered it with 158 tests and probes. Its findings are fixed in c28864d:
  - a long bare payload read INVALID, and the error echoed the record;
  - a quoted-JSON file was accepted as a second form of a record;
  - the proof name check was case-sensitive and skipped neutral names in `ledger/certs/`.
- **Draft stage:** two in-session reviewers, one on correctness and security, one on the brief, docs and privacy. Every confirmed finding was fixed.
- **In-session review of the pushes Codex had not seen:**
  - The record bytes were checked against Node's `JSON.stringify` on about 2,600 generated records: 0 mismatches.
  - The pointer could drift from the ledger, and a proof's name was not checked. Both fixed.
- **Codex code review, seven rounds.** Fixed:
  - pull before reading, in revoke and in seal;
  - repaired proofs are pushed;
  - a failed pointer push is retried;
  - the temporary file can't follow a link;
  - proof building is no longer quadratic.
- **Codex results by round:** round 6 found no issues. Round 7, on c28864d, raised the dangling-symlink P2 listed below.
- **Declined:** one optional P2, to start macOS on test-only edits to `tests/test_cohort.py`. It follows the existing rule for `tests/test_v2.py`.

## Not touched

`block.yml`, `deploy.yml`, the contract, and the committed `ledger/` contents. No block was written, nothing on Base was touched, and no key was used.

## Decided with the Network PM

- **Revocation:** any revocation block naming the fingerprint counts, wherever it sits. This fails closed.
- **Publication timing:** proofs are public on `main` before the GitHub approval. A cohort that is never approved leaves only unlinked hashes, which read as NOT FOUND.
- **Payload:** it carries the whole record. The holder controls who sees their link.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)

- **Dangling symlink at the request path** (Codex P2, round 7).

author: colemancda
body:
`Image(systemName:)` and `Label(_:systemImage:)` now draw 608 common SF Symbol names, and their `.fill` variants, from [Phosphor Icons](https://phosphoricons.com) (MIT), instead of Cacao's 60 or so hand-drawn symbols.

## How

- `Scripts/SymbolNames.txt` maps SF names (and aliases such as `chevron.backward`, `gearshape`) to Phosphor icons. Every name was checked against macOS's own SF Symbols.
- `Scripts/GenerateSymbols.py <phosphor checkout>` turns Phosphor's stroked regular drawings and its filled drawings into Swift path code, `Sources/Cacao/Graphics/SymbolGlyphs.swift`. Regenerating from Phosphor 2.1.1 (2b75f3ad) reproduces it exactly.
- Being code rather than resources, the symbols need nothing new from SwiftPM or the CMake build.
- Lookup: Phosphor's drawing, then Cacao's hand-drawn set, then `.circle`, `.square` and `.slash` composed around a symbol Phosphor doesn't draw that way. Unknown names stay empty, sized like a glyph.
- Strokes follow the font weight, using Phosphor's widths from thin to bold. Tinting, gradients, `renderingMode(.original)`, `imageScale` and font sizing are unchanged.

## Licence

Phosphor's MIT notice is in `ThirdPartyLicenses.md`, linked from the README, and CMake installs it with `LICENSE` to `share/doc/Cacao`.

## Trade-offs

- Symbols look like Phosphor's, not Apple's.
- One colour only: no hierarchical, palette or multicolour rendering.
- The generated code adds about 1.7 MB of machine code to a release build on arm64.
- Composed slashes have no gap beside them, because knockouts paint white rather than clearing.

## Testing

- `swift build --build-tests` and `swift test` pass on macOS. New tests cover names across categories, aliases, `.fill`, composed `.circle`, `.square` and `.slash`, mirrored symbols, stroke weight, `.original` rendering and the unknown-name fallback.
- The demo's Effects screen shows about 100 symbols, fills, weights from ultralight to black, a `Label` and `.original` rendering; checked by screenshot.
- With CMake (`-DCACAO_BUILD_HOST=OFF`), the `Cacao` target configures and builds. The full build stops at `CacaoCompositor` on the test machine because Silica isn't installed there; that is unrelated to this change.
- Not tested on Linux.

author: hassan-merhi
body:
## Cross-tab company isolation — Phases 1–6

### Phase 1: share the authenticated company among browser tabs
BroadcastChannel + storage notification, authoritative session reconciliation, serialized tab-local switches and focus/pageshow recovery.

### Phase 2: mask stale-company workspace and preserve drafts
Cover old records during verification, remount all company-owned providers and portals on a confirmed company change; retain unsaved drafts when the company is unchanged or a switch is rejected. Clear global confirmations and toast content on actual transitions.

### Phase 3: isolate caches and in-flight reads
Generation-aware React Query/network/bandwidth/hotspot/pagination/daybook/proforma/account metadata caches, fetch response fencing, no-store company-specific reads, offline fallback scope checks and stale retry suppression.

### Phase 4: centralize cross-company navigation
Supplier transaction/PO/container links and All Daybook record/comparison links await one authorized CompanyContext queue; no direct duplicate set-company POST or arbitrary delay; company-scoped Daybook filter persistence.

### Phase 5: server-side revision fence for tagged browser writes
- Rotate an opaque session companyRevision at login and on each committed set-company operation.
- Stamp both original company ID and revision on frontend mutations (raw fetch and API helpers); retain the original scope across CSRF/token delays and retries.
- Reload the persisted session at mutation ingress before checking both headers. Return 409 on a stale/malformed scope and 503 when session reload fails.
- Native/legacy untagged requests retain existing route authorization and CSRF compatibility; this is an ingress-time fence, not a universal atomic database transaction fence.
- Regression tests for wrong-company writes, same-ID switch-back, duplicate stale callbacks and refused startup session adoption.

### Phase 6: end-to-end multi-tab verification
- New **real Chrome two-tab** test: `tests/e2e/company-cross-tab-phase6.mjs`. Two pages in one browser context share a real authenticated cookie and storage, using **only** the disposable local Phase 7 fixture and ephemeral credentials.
- Assert company changes propagate without hard reload; network-delayed old-company GET results are rejected; stale voucher writes receive 409; revisions rotate when switching away and back to the same company; and voucher row counts for both companies remain unchanged after rejected writes.
- Integrated in the existing `.github/workflows/realtime-verification.yml` PR test job, after its current database-backed realtime test. Upload per-tab screenshots and JSON evidence to `artifacts/phase6-company-tabs`.
- Additional frontend regression for a refused startup switch retaining the authoritative session revision.
- Mandatory final gate: run **all** required checks against the latest commit: main CI (typecheck, lint/format, frontend/backend tests, build, audits), Realtime Verification/Phase 6 browser test, UI Quality, Security, CodeQL, Mutation Testing, Business Journeys, Database Migrations, Mobile Shell and Protection Policy. A queued/cancelled/skipped job does not constitute a pass.

**Safety:** Draft PR only, unmerged and undeployed. The browser suite refuses non-local hosts and requires `NODE_ENV=test`, `ERP_E2E_DISPOSABLE_DB=1` and database `/heliumdb`. No production database or user records have been accessed or modified. Reopen this PR for code fixes if any required check fails.

body:
## GUITAR BIOSPHERE — Phase 6

**REACTION est désormais un moteur de modulation DSP**, et non un écran de réglages inactifs.

### Moteur audio
- Huit routes indépendantes et automatisables déjà présentes dans les 97 IDs APVTS, **aucun ID ajouté/renommé**
- Sources : attaque, enveloppe, PULSE, HARMONIC LIFE, MUTATION, MEMORY, silence; EVOLUTION est délibérément muet jusqu'au développement de son DSP
- Destinations : densité granulaire, profondeur PULSE, mouvement harmonique, rappel MEMORY, résonance harmonique, mouvement granulaire, feedback MEMORY, cadence PULSE
- 6 contrôles globaux : actif, réactivité, interaction, sensibilité, réponse (30–500 ms), complexité
- Quantités positives/négatives, paramètres bornés, lissage indépendant des routes et des destinations, déconnexion progressive, changement de cible sans saut abrupt
- Déclenchement MEMORY par excitation harmonique en complément des attaques habituelles, avec cooldown et respect du gel
- Sources PULSE/HARMONIC/MUTATION/MEMORY mesurées sur les véritables sorties audio de chaque moteur ; sources des moteurs décalées d'un échantillon pour éviter les boucles algébriques
- 32 pointeurs APVTS des 8 routes résolus dans le constructeur, donc **pas de création de noms JUCE dans le callback audio**

### Preset démonstration
Le preset d'usine existant **20 - The Living Guitar** utilise trois routes : Attaque → PULSE, PULSE → mouvement harmonique, Harmonique → rappel MEMORY. Les autres routes restent éditables et désactivées dans cet exemple. Toujours 20 presets de démarrage, pas 100 inventés.

### Validation
- Nouveau test JUCE-free `Tests/ReactionRouting.cpp` : +/−, désactivation, réaffectation, huit routes, sortie bornée, audio réellement affecté et cascade
- Tests précédents : DSP, master/macros, analyse, interface zéro chevauchement et UTF-8
- Builds macOS ARM64 AU/VST3 et Windows x64 VST3 + artefacts vérifiés

Aucun changement de disposition graphique ni des polices ; interface bleu nuit/doré inchangée.
Les tests d'écoute en DAW restent nécessaires avant fusion/livraison commerciale.

author: ayostepht
body:
## What this changes and why

The database is a network hop away, and loading a build ran about 25 queries one after another. Every build page pays for that, and so does every status change, because a mutation loads the view. The builds list ran one parts query per build, and creating a build inserted its parts and plates one row at a time.

- **`loadBuildView`:**
  - One joined query reads the build, its template and the viewer's membership row. No build, no template or no membership returns `null`, exactly as before, and nothing else is read for a non-member.
  - One parallel wave of reads follows, each keyed by that build, its template or its team.
  - The time model, assembly and photos are built in memory from those rows.
- **`buildRows`:** one `inArray` query for the parts of all the listed builds, grouped in memory, with the same ordering.
- **`createBuild`:** multi-row inserts (chunked) for filaments, parts and plates, with the same values and order, in the same transaction. The quota checks and advisory locks are unchanged and still run first.
- **`applyPatches`:** updates for distinct parts go out together; patches for the same part stay in order.

Measured through a latency proxy at 40 ms per round trip, before → after:

| Request | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build page | 2.3 s | 0.6 s |
| Builds list | 3.0 s | 1.1 s |
| Team page (12 builds) | 17 s | 2.9 s |
| Create a build | 7.5 s | 1.2 s |
| Mark a plate printed | 3.3 s | 2.5 s |
| Start a demo | 58 s | 35 s |

Mutations and demo start improve less because their reads run inside a transaction on one connection. A follow-up addresses demo start separately.

## How I checked it

- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm test` (1951 passed). A new `list-rows.test.ts` compares `buildRows` with the previous per-build algorithm across two teams, a non-default variant choice, a build without part rows, a draft and an empty build.
- [x] The full end-to-end suite: 262 passed, 1 failed. The failure is the photo-viewer focus test in `assembly-handoff`, which is intermittent on `main` too and passed 5 of 5 when re-run alone; this change doesn't touch photos.
- [x] Before and after query counts, depth and wall time for each request above

## Checklist

- [x] No MakeGood files
- [x] No personal data, addresses, links, keys or access codes
- [x] No schema change; every mutation still goes through `mutateBuild`; no caching across requests
- [x] Printers untouched
- [x] No user-visible change beyond speed
- [x] Self-hosted edition: the same code exists there, but SQLite has no round-trip cost; optional to carry over.

author: drewstone
body:
## What a consumer gains in 23.0.7

- An application can install agent-eval 2.0.0 beside Knowledge without a peer conflict. The agent-eval peer range is `^1.0.0 || ^2.0.0` (#320). Nothing Knowledge uses changed in agent-eval 2.0.0.
- Retrieval tuning over the built-in index search and `FileSystemSearchProvider.asRetrievalEvalRetriever()` is no longer held for incomplete cost accounting under agent-eval 1.0.39 and later. Each local search now records a known $0 call (#320).

`CHANGELOG.md` `## 23.0.7` states both.

## What this PR changes

1. **Development pin `@tangle-network/agent-interface` 5.10.25 -> 5.10.28.** `pnpm-lock.yaml` was regenerated on the gate host. Only that package moves (the importer, the package entry, and the agent-core 1.0.3 and agent-eval 1.0.22 snapshots). Its integrity matches the registry tarball for 5.10.28.
   - Why: the publication qualifier (`qualify-publication.yml`) runs `verify:package` at every declared Eval version (1.0.0, 2.0.0, 1.0.22) and installs the Interface development pin beside each one. agent-eval 2.0.0 depends on agent-interface `^5.10.26`.
   - Effect before the fix: on `eea23e5` `verify:package` at agent-eval 2.0.0 exited 1 with `agent-eval dependency on agent-interface declares ^5.10.26, which does not admit installed 5.10.25` (gate `beelink1-be8b8fb7740104da0fa07381027b522a`). The Publish run for `v23.0.7` would have failed in `verify` the same way, as 23.0.4 did.
   - The agent-interface peer range stays `^5.2.0`.
2. **README and `docs/compatibility.md` now say Eval 1 or Eval 2.** They still said Knowledge 23 requires Eval 1, and both files ship in the package.
3. **`CHANGELOG.md` 23.0.7** now records the two items above. The version stays 23.0.7, which #320 set.

## Version

23.0.7 is a patch. In [release versioning](https://github.com/tangle-network/agent-runtime/blob/main/docs/release-versioning.md), rule 1 makes a widened peer range, a fix and a dependency move within a line patch releases, and rule 3 refuses a minor on 1.x and later. npm `latest` is 23.0.6, and 23.0.7 is neither tagged nor published.

## Proof

The gate receipt is in the first comment. On the head of this PR, in order:

- Preparation: this repository has no prepare script. `pnpm run build && pnpm run api:surface` regenerated `api-surface.json`, and the before/after diff was empty.
- The canonical local gate from `AGENTS.md`: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm run verify:package`, then the integration files #320 touched (`tests/filesystem-search-provider.test.ts`, `tests/rag-improvement-loop.test.ts`, `tests/retrieval-eval.test.ts`).
- The qualifier's per-Eval checks: `verify:package` and `verify:official-optimizers` at agent-eval 1.0.0, 2.0.0 and 1.0.22. The optimizer checks used the matching `agent-eval-rpc` Python bridge.

Not run on the gate: the full `pnpm run test`. On `eea23e5`, a docs-only head with the same source, two full-suite gates went red on lock and promotion tests that hit their 15 s timeouts. The first run, with 2 reserved cores, had 1 timeout (`beelink1-afddd368c65e76846872856568fe714e`). The second, with 1 core and host CPU pressure at 11.8, had 9 timeouts across 7 files (`beelink1-895e8b90558f493e752bbd119866124f`). The publication qualifier runs the full suite on GitHub-hosted runners before it publishes.

## After merge

Tag the merge commit `v23.0.7` and push the tag. `.github/workflows/publish.yml:3-6` starts Publish on a `v*` tag push, and it publishes only after `qualify-publication.yml` passes. agent-runtime's release PR then moves its `release/cohort.json` Knowledge ref to that merge commit.

```diff
-  type OrgReadCtx = { db; org };  type TeamPageArgs = { teamId; paginationOpts }

 convex/issues.ts
-  args: { teamId: v.id("teams"), paginationOpts: paginationOptsValidator }
+  args: teamPageArgs,  handler: … backlogPage(ctx, ctx.org._id, args)
```

**The lint rule** (`eslint.config.mjs`, `import/no-restricted-paths`, already registered by `eslint-config-next`; no new dependency):

| Zone | Target | May not import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a | `convex/lib` | a top-level Convex module (`_generated` and `schema.ts` allowed) |
| b | `app`, `components`, `lib`, `cli`, `scripts` | `convex/lib` |
| c | everything | `convex/issues.ts`, so the old re-export hub can't come back |

`AGENTS.md:14` and `docs/AGENT-API.md:44` point at the new homes.

## Evidence

- **The lint rule, red first** (`b5-probes.sh`, one probe file per zone in throwaway `git archive` exports):
  - **Before, on `main` `3141b4b`:** all 5 probes lint clean (no such rule).
  - **After, on `535c64e`:** each zone probe fails with exactly one `import/no-restricted-paths` error and its zone's message: (a) `convex/lib` → `../projects`; (b) `components` → `@/convex/lib/paging`, and `lib` → `../convex/lib/paging`; (c) `convex` → `./issues`. The allowed-imports probe (`../schema`, `../_generated/server`, `./orgRows` from `convex/lib`) stays clean.
  - The real tree has 0 violations, and `eslint-suppressions.json` is unchanged.
- **API and schema unchanged** (independent `hx-verifier`, `3141b4b` against `535c64e`): all 83 registered functions (args and returns), the 6 HTTP routes and the 16 schema tables serialise identically. Canonical JSON sha256, the same on both sides: API `e78afa6b…`, schema `dfa41d0f…`, `issues` table `a5a853dc…`. author: flacyak
body:
## SpreadsFold keeps a spread for each of the first 32 values of a column, the later ones in Other

**The hook.**
Box plot, part 2: the fold behind "how do categories' spreads compare", a box per region, channel or rep from one pass over the file.

**The problem.**
A box plot by a column needs a spread per value. Kept without a bound, a column of 50,000 customer ids would hold 50,000 spreads; the owner set the bound at 32 values of 3 figures, 4,096 buckets each, later values going to Other (2026-11-17, answer 3).

**The solution.**
`core/src/tally/spreads.ts` holds `SpreadsFold`:
- A value gets its own `SpreadFold` of `SPREAD_VALUE_AT_MOST` = 4,096 buckets while fewer than `BOX_VALUES_AT_MOST` = 32 have one and Other is empty, the rule `GroupsFold` keeps for groups, so a value's rows are all in its spread or all in Other's and every count stays exact.
- `remove` takes a row back, and a spread it empties goes, freeing its place.
- `snapshot()` sends each value's box, the highest median first, ties by value, and Other's where a row is in it.
- `SpreadFold` gains `boxed()`, its snapshot with no histogram levels, which a box plot never draws, and `rows`, every row it counts.

At its bounds the fold holds 33 spreads of 4,096 buckets, about 5 MB of heap, as the design measured. 96 lines of source.

**What was checked.**
New tests fail on #561 and pass here: over 50 seeds of 400 rows across 40 values, each of the first 32 values' box equals a `SpreadFold` of its cells alone, and Other's equals one of the rest; values stand by their medians, highest first, ties by value; and after taking back a random half, each value kept still equals its rows alone, and every other row is Other's.
`scripts/gate.sh 1` passes: check, the related tests, core's lab project, build and smoke.

**The ask.**
Nothing; a review is enough. Its save and golden hash come next.

body:
Closes FIX-19 (https://trello.com/c/hoay1QiV/285-s8-p2-fix-19-one-ai-request-pipeline-one-event-parse-shared-notification-copy)

## Summary

The four AI kinds (cv-hints, followups, interview-prep, summaries) now share one request event factory, `aiRequestedEvent(type, shape)`, and one outbox writer, `AiRepository.recordRequested`, called through `AiService` in the same transaction as `createJob`. One injectable `AiJobQueue.queueOrFail` replaces the guarded queue wiring in seven services. Capture, resumes and ping go through the shared event parse.

A refused connection or a failed token signing no longer writes an `ai_calls` row, because the request never left the api. Push now owns its prune rule in `PushSendService`, rhythm reads settings through `SettingsService`, and push and email share `notification-copy.ts`.

## How to check

- `pnpm --filter @jobflow/api exec vitest run` on the touched modules: ai, cv-hints, followups, interview-prep, summaries, capture, resumes, push, rhythm, settings.
- `git grep -n "outboxEvent.create" -- apps/api/src/modules/cv-hints apps/api/src/modules/followups apps/api/src/modules/interview-prep apps/api/src/modules/summaries` prints nothing.
- `git grep -n "без відповіді" -- apps/api/src ':!*.test.ts'` prints one line.

## Screenshots

No UI change.

## Decisions

- The factory returns `{ type, schema }`, so it drops into `subscribeParsed`. The outbox aggregate is the application when the payload has `applicationId`, else the user. Wire names and payload shapes are unchanged.
- Only a token signing failure and an ECONNREFUSED fetch error count as never reaching services/ai. A timeout or a reset still writes its row.
- Resumes keep extraction in its own try/catch, so a queue failure is settled once. The warning text for it is now "resume_parse job not queued".
- `SettingsService.find` returns null for a missing row; week close keeps a narrow `RhythmRepository.hasSettings` to stay at four providers and keep the sweep's behaviour.
- Added `NotificationScheduleService.due` for the schedule step push and email repeated.

## Known limits

- The new modules wiring (NotificationsModule and RhythmModule import SettingsModule) is proven by typecheck and unit tests locally; the integration tests run first in CI.
- The red-on-main control for the refused connection test was not run; the green side passes and the old code wrote a row for every client failure.
- The new subscriber `routeFinal` tests and the timeout and reset client cases pin existing behaviour, so they were green from the start.

## DoD

- [x] Acceptance criteria of the card met, each one checked by a command or a look
- [ ] Lint, typecheck and tests pass locally and in CI
- [x] New business logic has unit tests; a new endpoint has an integration test
- [x] Input validated by a shared zod schema (pydantic in analytics)
- [x] Errors in the common shape with `requestId`, no stack traces to the client
- [x] UI: n/a
- [x] OpenAPI updated if the API changed: n/a
- [x] No secrets in code; new env variables in `.env.example`: none
- [x] Card description updated if the implementation differs from the plan: no difference

## Design QA (section 22)

n/a

- [x] No ADR needed
