body:
## Perfil do cliente — "Recomendações do meu jeito" vem ligada (D16; sem migration)

Decisão do dono (20/11, depois de ver o Perfil do cardápio: "já deveria vir marcado"), entre as três opções apresentadas:
- a recomendada, **"Recomendações" ligada por legítimo interesse**, foi a escolhida;
- **"as três marcadas junto com os termos"** ficou de fora, porque o consentimento seria nulo (art. 8º, § 4º; Guia de Cookies da ANPD);
- a terceira era manter tudo como estava.

### O que muda
- **"Recomendações do meu jeito" deixa de ser consentimento e passa a ser legítimo interesse** (LGPD art. 7º, IX e art. 10).
  - Para quem nunca mexeu, ela vale **ligada** (`PADRAO_DA_ESCOLHA`).
  - Só um "não" gravado desliga.
  - Desligar devolve na hora ao anônimo os cliques que estavam ligados ao cliente (já era assim).
- **A entrada do cardápio:**
  - as recomendações deixam de ser caixa e viram um **aviso**, com o texto do servidor;
  - as caixas que sobram são "Lembrar como prefiro ser atendido" (que segue pedindo "18 anos ou mais") e as ofertas;
  - "Aceitar e continuar" e "Continuar sem marcar" continuam com o mesmo destaque, e "Continuar sem marcar" **não** desliga as recomendações.
- **O Perfil do cardápio:** a chave já aparece ligada e desliga ou religa sem pedir a idade.
- **O "jeito aprendido das conversas" e as ofertas continuam "sim" clicado.** O primeiro é análise de comportamento com risco alto (Res. ANPD 2/2022), e a Meta proíbe perfil feito com dados de uso do WhatsApp (4.1(a)). A caixa de ofertas do checkout segue marcada, como o dono decidiu em 19/11.
- **Onde a regra é lida:**
  - os cliques ligados ao cliente;
  - o cardápio "para você" (o "Você viu" e a ordem das categorias);
  - a ficha ("O que olha" só diz que o cliente desligou quando ele desligou).
- **Os textos** das telas e a versão dos textos gravados (`2026-11-20`).
- O plano ganhou a D16 e o resumo do **teste de legítimo interesse**: finalidade, necessidade, expectativa e salvaguardas.

### Diferença do protótipo
O protótipo mostrava as três caixas desmarcadas (D15). Agora as recomendações aparecem como aviso, e só duas caixas continuam.

### Como testei
- `privacidade-pg.spec.ts`: quem nunca mexeu lê as recomendações ligadas e recebe o aviso; o texto gravado tem a versão nova.
- `interacoes-pg.spec.ts`:
  - quem nunca mexeu tem os cliques ligados a si;
  - desligar pela gravação de verdade devolve tudo ao anônimo, e o clique novo já chega anônimo;
  - desligado, o cardápio mantém o "de sempre", mas tira o "você viu" e a ordem das categorias.
- 63 suítes de cliente, cardápio, perfil, segmentos e `app-sobe` (671 testes). `tsc`, `npm run build` e `npm test` nos dois lados.
- Roteiros `clientes-perfil` (145), `cardapio-para-voce` (434) e `saude-da-base` (181), sem falha.

author: sarahsami940
body:
What changed
Phase 1 – Production data. Money is stored as whole paisa. Each person's own time zone decides what "today" means. Every record keeps its change history, and deleting only hides it, so it can be undone. Every money action can be retried without saving it twice.
Phase 2 – Postgres and the API. A typed schema whose constraints and cross-record links are checked by the database. An API (Fastify) that runs the same money rules on every save, all or nothing. Sign-in through any standard provider (OIDC), with a development sign-in for local use. Space permissions: owner, editor, viewer.
Phase 3 – Sync and offline. An offline copy on the device with a saved outbox. Sync fetches only what changed. When two devices edit the same record, the later edit wins. A change the server refuses is undone on the device, with the reason shown.
Phase 4 – Moving browser data. Spaces saved in a browser move into the account one at a time, all or nothing, and are checked record by record after the move. It is safe to repeat. An account made on the device needs its password before its Spaces can be moved.
Phase 5 – Security and privacy. Rate limits, security headers, and logs that never hold tokens, emails, amounts or IP addresses. People can download all their data and delete their account. A nightly reconciliation checks every Space, and a restore drill checks restored backups. Docs: SECURITY.md, PRIVACY.md, LEGAL-PAKISTAN.md (questions for a lawyer, not advice).
Phase 6 – Quality and operations. Metrics and request ids. Browser tests in Playwright and accessibility scans with axe (WCAG 2.1 AA, 27 screens). A load test that checks every expense arrives exactly once. Runbooks in OPERATIONS.md.
Phase 7 – Version 1 features. CSV statement import with duplicate detection and category learning. An installable app that opens offline (manifest and service worker). Daily reminders on the device, and pushed from the server, with counts only and no amounts or names.
How it was checked
npm run check: lint, type-checks, 288 tests (domain 161, API 52, web 22, end-to-end 53) and both builds.
npm run test:browser: 9 browser tests in Edge, all passing:
the money flow, the account flow, import, offline and reminders;
accessibility scans, which found and fixed contrast, nested-control and list-structure problems.
The load test: 20 people at once, 1,440 requests, none failed, every balance matched, and reconciliation found nothing wrong.
For reviewers
CI has not run yet, because of the GitHub billing lock. It adds jobs for:
real Postgres: the load test, reconciliation, the restore drill and a log check;
the browser tests.
Still needed before launch:
choosing the sign-in provider (AUTH_MODE=oidc);
VAPID keys, for pushed reminders;
an independent penetration test;
the lawyer's answers;
35-day backup retention on the database host.
Account mode (VITE_API_URL) currently signs in with a development-only sign-in, which a staging or production API refuses.
Commit size. One large commit, because the phases were built in sequence on the same files. Reading it by package is easiest:
packages/domain
apps/api
apps/web/src/data
the screens
tests/
docs/

author: solmin6320
body:
## 기능

로그인한 멤버만 쓰는 **익명 건의함** (`/suggestions`, 헤더 `건의함` 버튼)
- 건의 작성, 공감(1인 1공감·취소), `전체`/`내 건의` 탭, `공감순`/`최신순`
- 내 건의는 본인만 삭제. 관리자 권한 없음
- **운영자도 DB·서버 설정·컨테이너로 작성자·공감자를 알 수 없음**
- 다른 기기에서 내 건의를 보려면 `복구 코드`를 옮겨야 함

## 리뷰 반영

> 운영자가 secret key, user id, 용도, 건의 id 로 대조할 수 있다

이전 `HMAC(서버 키, user_id, 건의 id)`를 없애고, 서버에 "사용자 ↔ 건의/공감"을 잇는 값이 남지 않게 했습니다.

| 문제 | 변경 |
|---|---|
| 요청에 로그인 정보가 실림 | 작성·삭제·공감·취소는 **쿠키 없이** 전송 (`credentials: 'omit'`), 핸들러에 `CurrentUser` 없음 |
| 그러면 멤버 확인 불가 | **블라인드 서명 토큰(RFC 9474)** 으로 증명. 서버는 서명할 때 토큰을 못 보므로, **개인키가 있어도** 누구 토큰인지 계산 불가 |
| 서버 키로 작성자 판별 | 판별 키는 **브라우저에만** 있음. DB 에는 그 키로 만든 값의 해시만 저장 |

- 작성 토큰: **월별 키**(이번 달·지난달 것만 유효), 하루 3개, 사이트 방문 시 미리 발급. 사용한 토큰은 `SHA-256` 만 저장해 재사용 차단. 탈퇴자·유출 토큰도 길어야 다음 달까지만 사용 가능
- 이미 쓴 토큰은 RSA 키 생성 **전에** 거름 (반복 전송으로 CPU 소모 방지)
- 공감 토큰: **건의마다 다른 RSA 키**로 서명, 사람당 1개 → 1인 1공감
- `SUGGESTION_SECRET` 제거 (**새 환경 변수 없음**)

## 리뷰 포인트

- `api/src/services/suggestions.rs`: 위협 모델 주석, 토큰 발급·검증. 익명 함수(`create`/`delete`/`vote`/`unvote`)는 사용자 정보를 인자로 받지 않음
- `frontend/src/utils/blindRsa.ts`: RFC 9474 클라이언트 (RSABSSA-SHA384-PSSZERO-Deterministic). HTTP 배포에서도 동작하도록 `@noble/hashes` 사용
- `frontend/src/utils/anonSuggestions.ts`: 브라우저 키·토큰 보관, 복구 코드, 내 건의/공감 판별
- 복구 코드 적용 시 확인 창 (기존 코드 백업·남이 준 코드 금지 안내)
- `api/src/handlers/suggestions.rs`: 익명 핸들러에 `CurrentUser` 를 넣으면 익명이 깨짐 (주석 명시)
- `Cargo.toml`: `blind-rsa-signatures = "0.19"`, debug 에서도 키 생성이 빠르도록 암호 크레이트만 `opt-level = 3`

## 남는 한계

- 운영자가 **코드를 고쳐** IP·요청을 기록하거나, 프론트 JS 를 바꾸거나, 사용자마다 다른 공개키를 내려주면(키 바꿔치기) 막을 수 없음 (웹 구조상 한계)
- 서버는 토큰 주인을 모르므로 사람별 즉시 무효화는 불가 (월별 만료로 제한). 미리 받은 공감 토큰은 그 건의에 한해 계속 유효
- 가입이 열려 있어 "멤버" = 가입자 (기존 정책)
- 공용 PC 에서는 브라우저 저장소의 키로 내 건의가 드러날 수 있음
- 트랜잭션 순서(xmin/WAL)나 토큰 발급 기록으로 **접속자가 매우 적을 때** 추정 여지 있음 (토큰 사전 발급으로 완화)
- 글 내용으로 드러나는 것은 막을 수 없음

## 확인

- `cargo test` 11개, `cargo clippy` 신규 경고 없음, `npm run lint` / `npm run build` 통과
- Rust ↔ 브라우저 블라인드 서명 상호운용 5/5, 변조 메시지 거부
- **PostgreSQL + 서버 E2E 통과**: 하루 3개 제한, 재사용·만료/위조 토큰 409 (재사용 거부 12ms vs 정상 작성 129ms → 키 생성 없이 거부), 형식 오류 400, 발급 시 키 불일치 409, 작성자만 `mine`, 1인 1공감(키 바꿔치기 차단), 복구 코드로 다른 기기 확인, 타인 삭제 403, 익명 요청 4종 쿠키 미전송, 건의·공감 테이블에 사용자·IP·시각 컬럼 없음
- 브라우저 화면 수동 확인은 안 함

> 이전 버전을 로컬에서 실행했다면 마이그레이션이 바뀌어 아래 실행 필요
> `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS suggestion_votes, suggestions; DELETE FROM _sqlx_migrations WHERE version = 20261120000000;`

author: ka87
body:
All 24 shaders lose their comments. 1066 lines down to 574.

## The reasoning did not go with them

`data/shaders/README.md` already held most of it, and it holds the rest now. Checked file by file rather than assumed -- which turned up that **five of the shaders were not in the README at all**, so what they said is new there:

- **`watersmooth.vert` / `.frag`** had no section. Its tap coordinates are worked out per corner, in the vertex stage, and that is faithfulness rather than speed: the pass being reproduced writes four coordinate sets into the quad's four vertices and interpolates between them, and its vertical offsets are nought at the top two vertices and one, two and three steps at the bottom two -- so the blur opens out towards the bottom. Per-pixel offsets would give a uniform blur, which is the obvious thing to write and the wrong one.
- **`aemotion.frag`** -- the four samples are *not* a symmetric spread about the pixel. Minus three, plus two, minus one, nothing. It leans one way and that is the effect.
- **`aezoom2.frag`** -- the transform is written as a rotation and is not one: its second row reads the first row's answer, so the determinant is cosine squared and every sample is turned *and* shrunk. Which is why a rotational smear reads as a zoom.
- **`aefade.frag`** and **`aehue.frag`**.

And three things the README did not say, each of which several shaders had a line about:

- **The matrices.** Row-vector, row-major, uploaded untransposed -- so OpenGL hands GLSL the transpose and the two cancel. That is why `uViewProj * vec4(aPos, 1.0)` in three of these is the engine's own arithmetic and not a rearrangement of it. Worth stating plainly, because transposing on upload *or* flipping the multiply would each break it alone, while doing both would work and read as though one were a mistake.
- **The frame's alpha through the after-effect chain** -- who carries it, who replaces it, and why an effect that threw it away would silently make every later one a no-op.
- `video.frag` writes the frame opaque whatever its alpha says.

The version line was also stale: it said **4.50 core** and the files are **4.10**, which is what the fallback asks for. Verified against `gl_wanted[]` rather than from memory, and `layout(location = N)` really is the only post-3.30 construct in any of the 24.

## The strip

It compares the **token stream** before and after and refuses the file if it moved, so nothing changed but whitespace, and it checks `#version` is still first.

A line that held only a comment goes rather than being left blank. The first pass left blanks and the result read wrongly -- `water.vert`'s three `uniform mat4` declarations came out separated by blank lines, which reads as deliberate grouping between things that belong together.

## Checks

- `sh tests/run.sh` green -- 59 runners and the 6 inline differentials.
- `tests/run_gloverlay.sh` loads the **real shipped files** and checks the uniform names the renderer asks for, so a uniform lost here would fail rather than produce a black world.
- `tests/run_glrender.sh` ran with a real context in this container -- **547 checks, 0 failures** -- which compiles every one of these files and reads the pixels back, every effect included. That is the check that matters: the stripped shaders compile and draw the same thing.
- No `//`, `/*` or `*/` left in any of the 24.

---

body:
## Summary

Finding q141 from the 2026-11-15 quality audit: the Media library's Upload takes every kind (image, video, audio), but it drew one placeholder per uploading file in the grid of whatever filter was shown. Uploading a WAV while the Images filter was on showed an image skeleton, which then vanished, and the audio landed in a list that wasn't on screen.

- `useFileUpload` returns `uploading`, the list of accepted files still in flight (each with its kind), instead of a count and a boolean. Callers derive what they need from it: a count, whether anything is uploading, or the files of one kind.
- `uploadingTiles` takes that list and shapes each placeholder from its file's kind.
- `MediaLibrary` draws placeholders only for the uploads of the kind it shows, and that list also decides its empty state.

## Behavior change

A file uploading in a kind other than the shown filter no longer draws a placeholder in that grid. This is pinned by `lib/upload/__tests__/use-file-upload.test.tsx`: while a WAV and a PNG upload, the hook lists them as `audio,image`, and it reports nothing once both land. The test fails on master, where the hook only returns a count.

Out of scope, a UX call: switching the filter to the uploaded kind, so the upload shows wherever it lands.

## Checks

lint, typecheck, format:check, test:run (302 files, 2405 tests) and build all pass, and knip is clean. /simplify, composition, React best-practices and web-design passes ran; the composer's duplicated count sum and the count-plus-kind `uploadingTiles` signature were folded in. - [x] `harnessd doctor` prints a dense table. It exits 1 on any `fail` or `missing`. `--json` prints the raw checks.
- [x] `harnessd run` runs the checks before the API and the loop start. On a blocking check it prints each fix and exits 1.
- [x] `GET /api/status` returns `{ "checks": [...] }` (docs/API.md). Calls at the same time share one run.
- [x] No secret value appears in any output. Sign-in checks read only exit codes and named JSON fields. A redaction pass masks env secrets in each detail and fix. Tests check this.
- [x] Tests use fake CLIs and fake HTTP. The doctor tests run real shell-script fakes on `PATH`. No test uses the network.

D-021 records one change to the issue text: `missing` blocks, the same as `fail`. A required tool that is absent stops the loop too. A check that waits on a blocking check is also `missing`, with "not checked".

## Sample `harnessd doctor` output
From this cloud container: Node 22, gh signed out, no Linear key.

## Calls made
No check spends tokens. Each command is killed at a 5 s deadline for its group. Groups run in parallel.
- Claude Code: `claude --version`, `claude auth status --json`. These come from `claude --help`. Only `loggedIn` and `authMethod` are read.
- Codex: `codex --version`, `codex login status`. Only the exit code is read, because the output can show a masked key.

- Local: `git worktree list --porcelain`, a bind on `127.0.0.1:<daemon.port>`. When the port is busy, `GET /health` on that port finds a running harnessd.

author: saieeshward
body:
## What and why

Blind judging of decks built from three real client briefs scored **evidence 3-5/10** (nothing went beyond the brief) and **take-to-pitch 3-6/10** (placeholder covers, a DRAFT banner on every slide, empty picture frames, internal reference codes on client slides). This round targets both. Stacked on #261.

**A. Evidence**
1. **Market-aware research** (`engine/agent-server/research.py evidence`). Queries are built from a sanitised gist: never the client's name, a rival's name or a figure from the brief. They go local first (the brief's national statistics office, regulator, trade bodies and local press), with an international fallback that is labelled with its market. Every finding carries market, year, metric units and a source URL. The aim is 3 local findings a run, and `short_of_local` says when a run falls short. The older web track no longer sends the client name.
2. **Evidence for the argument.** The searches come from the deck's own claims (insight, audience, proposition and reasons to believe), taken from the brief and from stage b.
3. **The deck uses the evidence** (`DECK_PITCH_READY`, on by default; 0 in the suite; `engine/deck/pitch_ready.py`).
   - `--evidence evidence.json` is read as `f_ev` facts with their sources. A prompt-only run that has them is still a prompt tier.
   - The insight, audience and proposition slides each carry 1-2 sourced figures with a short tag (source, year, market). The layout plan never moves them to the notes, and they stay under the word-budget error line.
   - "(to confirm)" comes off a figure that a cited source or the evidence verifies, and stays on anything unverified.
   - An uncited market claim on an argument slide is softened to "Our read: …". A claim that only says what the inputs lack joins "What the brief doesn't tell us". `bare_claim` agrees with both.

**B. Pitch-readiness**
4. **A real cover.** The title is the client plus the project or campaign: from the run's names, else the brief tool's `meta`, else stage a0's new `names` (kept only when the inputs state them), else the chosen territory's name. The label is the agency (when known) plus the month and year, never "Response deck". No placeholder line is printed; the presenter-and-date to-do goes to the notes.
5. **A quiet draft tag.** A small muted "Draft" now sits in the footer next to the slide number. The full list of what needs a person is in the cover's notes, in each of those slides' notes, and on a new appendix slide, "What still needs a person".
6. **Picture slots.** With no stage g subject, the image plan writes a lint-checked subject from the chosen territory (the work: its own visual hint; the idea: the thought; the cover: the mood) before falling back to the code templates. While no picture exists, the work slide draws no empty card: the role note is a narrow column and the script takes the room.
7. **Leaks.** Codes are scrubbed from every shown text: refs (`prompt:N`, `brief:x`, `req:R4`), ids (`ic_feeling`, `gap_chart`), labels (`T1`, `IC1`, `candidate B`), and slide and stage ids. The speaker notes keep them. A new check, `code_leak`, is an error in both validate and the rendered-slide QA, and is mirrored in the schemas and the app template.

## Feature record

`features/deck-look.clan`, status: building (build_log entry for this round).

- [x] The design was approved before the code (`design.approved_by`)
- [x] `build_log`, `open_questions` and `next_step` are current
- [ ] If the work drifted from the design, a decision records why (N/A)

## How verified

- Pre-push hook (`scripts/check.sh` over the pushed range): passed.
- The six phase-27 test decks (invented topics) were re-rendered from saved stages to `deck-{A,B}-evidence`, with live evidence for each topic. Pedalway and Warmhome got 9 local Irish findings each, mostly from the statistics office and the transport and energy authorities. Lumen's brief names no market, so its findings are international and labelled. Results:
  - **0 QA errors** on all six.
  - Every cover reads "Client: project" with a "November 2026" label.
  - A footer "Draft" tag on every slide, and no banner.
  - Each insight, audience and proposition slide carries a tagged figure.
  - No `code_leak` finding.
  - Validation errors went down: Lumen A and Pedalway A each lost their `bare_claim` error, and Warmhome A dropped from 3 `numbers_trace` errors to 2, which are pre-existing persona figures.
- A run with placeholder names (`--client "Brief 3"`) gets the cover "Warmhome: Who Pays, Said Plainly".
- Stage a0 was re-run on the local backend for `names` only (estimated $0.07 at list price). The evidence came from `claude -p` on the Claude Code login. $0 spent.

## Definition of done

- [x] `scripts/check.sh` passes (pre-push), CI to confirm
- [x] Tests for the new behaviour: `engine/deck/tests/test_pitch_ready.py`, `engine/agent-server/test_research_evidence.py` (invented fixtures only). No old test was weakened; `test_visual_contract` now counts 42 checks.
- [x] No paid or live model call in tests (the `claude -p` call is stubbed)
- [x] Docs: `engine/deck/README.md`, `engine/agent-server/README.md`, `docs/contracts/deck-visuals.md`
- [x] Safe to deploy: everything is behind `DECK_PITCH_READY`; the research CLI runs only by hand with `RESEARCH_WEB=claude`

## Notes for reviewers

- The deck engine still never searches the web (ADR 0023). Evidence enters only through the research agent's file.
- Picture prompts live in the plan (`<stages>/images/plan.json`). An unmade slot stays empty in `deck.json`, as before.

- **Ogni difesa ha i suoi danni.** Quando l'orda sfonda una casa, ogni tipo di zombie rovina le difese che lo fermano:
  - corridori → fossato e trappole;
  - caschi e bruti → barricate, grate e recinto;

author: martinptielemans
body:
## Problem

On the Mac, a tab shown in the system's engine runs without ilo's ad blocking (#3596). WebKit blocks only through content rule lists, so the filter lists have to be turned into them first. This PR is step 1: the converter, with nothing calling it yet. It stays a draft until the core uses it.

## Change

`app/src/ad_block/webkit.rs` adds `convert(setup, features) -> Lists`. It reads the same lists and the user's filters as `compile` does: `!#if` evaluation, the hosts-format check, response-time and pop-up filters set apart, and bare hostnames anchored.

**Reading filters**
- Each filter is read by adblock-rust's `parse_filter`, as the engine does. Types, party, exception, `$important`, `match-case`, methods, `$badfilter`, redirect, csp, removeparam and generichide all come from the parse.
- The sites (`domain=`, `from=`, `to=`, and the sites before `##`) and the pattern come from the filter's line. The parse keeps sites only as hashes. For `||*.` patterns its hostname and filter parts don't add up to the pattern, and WebKit needs the pattern as written to build its regular expression. The site and option finding reuses `responses.rs`'s uBlock Origin option finder.

**What carries over**
- Blocks and exceptions, by address, type, party and the page's site:
  - `domain=a|b` becomes `if-frame-url`;
  - `domain=~a` becomes `unless-frame-url`;
  - a single `method=` becomes `request-method`.
- `@@||site^$document` becomes an `ignore-previous-rules` with `if-domain`. It comes after the rules it undoes, so blocking and hiding are both off on that site.
- Hiding by a plain CSS selector, 100 selectors a rule. Rules for every site use `unless-domain` for `~site`, `site#@#` and `$generichide`. Rules for some sites use `if-domain`.

**Only fields the running WebKit acts on**
- `Features` says whether it acts on `unless-frame-url` and `request-method`. macOS 15's WebKit ignores `request-method`.
- A rule that needs a field WebKit doesn't act on is left out. It is never written without that field, which would block more.

**What's left out, counted by why in `Counts::left_out`**
- Anything WebKit can't hold exactly. It's left out, never broadened:
  - sites in and out at once, since a rule has one condition;
  - `site.*`;
  - regular expressions with `|`, `{n}`, class escapes, lazy repeats or non-ASCII;
  - `to=` with an address.
- Scriptlets, procedural selectors, style and remove actions, `csp=`, `removeparam=`, and `tag=`, which ilo's engine never turns on.
- Stand-ins (`redirect=`): WebKit can't answer a request with one.
- Pages, frames and pop-ups are left to the navigation check. They're asked about through ilo's engine, as `PageThrottle` does for a Chromium tab, which can show the warning page a list can't.

**Spreading the rules**
- About `LIST_RULES` (14k) rules a list, so compiling one holds the main thread under 50 ms on a hosted runner (#3596 step 0's spread16).
- Each rule is placed by an FNV-1a hash of its JSON, so the same filters make the same lists and names.
- A list doesn't see another's exceptions, so every list carries a copy of every exception, in place order: hiding, blocks, exceptions, `$important` blocks, `$important` exceptions.
- The user's filters get a list of their own. Adding a block recompiles only that list; adding an exception recompiles every list.
- Each list's name is a hash of its rules, so the store can keep a list that didn't change.

## Scope and approval

Part of #3596, as its step 1. Steps 2–4 (the core's store, the tab's controller, the held first load) come after, and this stays a draft until the core uses it. No gated file is touched.

## Surfaces

- **UI and agents:** none yet; nothing calls it.
- **Keyboard, over the page, text input, window states:** none.
- **Profiles and Spaces:** none yet. The per-site and per-profile choice is the core's, in a later step.
- **Platforms:** the code is portable and runs only where WebKit is the system's engine. `Features` is filled in by the platform layer later.
- **Hot paths:** none. Converting runs off the main thread, once a list changes, and never at launch for a profile that doesn't use the system's engine.
- **Docs:** none.
- **Reverse states:** none.

## Verification

- `cargo test --release --lib` in `app/` on Linux: 2361 passed. 12 of those are new in `ad_block/webkit/tests.rs`:
  - a table of filters and the rules they make;
  - a table of filters left out and why;
  - fields written only where WebKit acts on them;
  - `$badfilter` across lists;
  - a page exception after what it undoes;
  - hiding grouped with its exceptions;
  - 100 selectors a rule;
  - a hosts-format list;
  - every list holding every exception, with `$important` after;
  - the user's list changing alone;
  - the same filters making the same names;
  - the regular expressions WebKit reads.
- The default lists (uBlock Origin 1.75.0, as `app/ublock.ini` pins it), converted on a Linux desktop with both fields on, in 0.95 s:
  - 178,831 filters became 187,195 rules in 14 lists of 13,247–13,513 rules each;
  - 3,282 exceptions are copied into each list, 45,948 copies in all (25% of the rules), and 53.6 MB of JSON;
  - by action: 133,017 blocks, 45,948 exception copies, 8,230 hiding rules;
  - the most left out: 10,189 scriptlets, 3,519 page and frame filters, 3,108 pop-up filters and 1,390 stand-ins.
- **Compiled in WebKit.** This is the step's real check: one selector or regular expression WebKit refuses fails its whole list.
  - **How it ran:**
    - A probe branch, never to land, converted the default lists on Linux, from the release `app/ublock.ini` pins, for each macOS's fields.
    - Each list was then compiled in a fresh process, into one store as the browser would, and every list looked up twice, as a relaunch would.
    - The runs: hosted run [44718760912](https://github.com/MartinPTielemans/ilo/actions/runs/44718760912) on macOS 15 and 26, then the same harness and lists on a check VM on a real Mac.
  - **Every list compiled on every run: 42 of 42, none refused.** That includes the generic hiding rules with up to 968 sites in `unless-domain`.

| | hosted macOS 15.8.2 | hosted macOS 26.7.2 | check VM, macOS 26.6.2 (3 cores, 5 GB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| rules | 187,155 | 187,195 | 187,195 |
| exception copies a list | 3,280 | 3,282 | 3,282 |
| compile, a list | 1.19–1.97 s | 1.06–1.67 s | 0.63–0.68 s |
| **compile, all 14** | 19.8 s | 16.5 s | **9.2 s** |
| longest main-thread step a list | 40–48 ms on 11; 67.9, 69.9 and 126 ms on three | 36.5–46 ms on 13; 63.6 ms on one | **23.6–31.7 ms**, and **44 ms** on the first compile |
| peak footprint, the compiling process | 52–92 MB | 67–99 MB | 64–100 MB |
| the store | 160.8 MB | 159.5 MB | 159.4 MB |
| looking up all 14 | 3.0 ms, then 2.4 ms | 2.7 ms, then 1.5 ms | 1.8 ms, then 1.6 ms |

  - Every time here is an upper bound: the hosted runners are shared virtual machines, and the check VM is a small guest with 3 cores and 5 GB.
  - The printed summaries' header says "from a hosted runner" on the VM's run too. That's the harness's fixed text.
- **The slow first step is a cold start, from one run.**
  - On the check VM, the lists were compiled in order, then in reverse a few seconds later.
  - `ilo-140fbaf0…` took 44 ms when it was compiled first, and 26.4 ms when it was compiled last.
  - The reverse pass had no slow list, its first included (26.8 ms).
  - So the long step follows WebKit's first compile in a process, not any one list. The hosted runs' slowest steps, 126 ms and 63.6 ms, were each their run's first list too. Their two other mid-run steps over 60 ms, on macOS 15, look like the shared machine.
  - That's one run of each, not a distribution.

**For step 4's bound** (the held first load):
- A first-ever compile of all 14 lists takes about 9 s on a small real-Mac guest, and 16–20 s on a hosted runner.
- So the first system tab ever will usually reach the bound before the lists are in, and load without blocking, with the note.

author: lmmx
body:
The question: does the shipped open kernel's thin-run limit (`LIMIT = 16`, induced and queued) have a real per-block preference on Wikidata blocks, and could the kernel's run-pass counts predict it? Research only, no production change. Based on `bench/open-admission`, the branch that holds the census harness, so the diff is this measurement alone.

**The verdict: STOP. There is no exploitable per-block preference, and `LIMIT = 16` stands.** The rule was fixed in the brief before the data. Step 3, the predictor, did not run.

## Method
- **Harness:** `ab limit-sweep 40 wikidata.bz2` (feature `open-return`).
- **Blocks:** every run-route block LazyCells admits with n ≥ 65,536. That is 228 blocks, the same set as `2026-11-19-open-admission/blocks.jsonl`.
- **Arms:** limits 8, 12, 16 and 24, timed on one thread (`taskset`). There are 40 rounds, and the arms are rotated within each round.
- **Correctness:** every output matches LazyCells' byte for byte.
- **The kernel is the shipped one:** the research kernel's `construct` and `emit` are identical to master's `src/open.rs`.

## Results
| measure | 8 | 12 | 24 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| split-half r | 0.464 | 0.320 | 0.583 |
| blocks significantly faster than 16 | 0 | 8 | 17 |
| blocks significantly slower than 16 | 181 | 60 | 56 |
| fixed-L total ratio against 16 | 1.072 | 1.018 | 1.006 |

- **Significant preference:** 25 of 228 blocks (11.0%) have some limit significantly faster than 16. Under Bonferroni that drops to 14 (6.1%).
- **Honest oracle:** the limit is chosen on the odd rounds and scored on the even rounds. Its total-weighted ratio is 0.992, and 0.992 the other way round. That is above the 0.98 line. The in-sample oracle reaches only 0.990.
- **The fixed limits:** each ratio's 95% interval excludes 1. 16 is the best fixed limit.
- **The earlier i8 wins:** on the shipped queued arm, i8 never beats i16. A 2-round sign correlates only 0.24–0.38 with the same block's other 38 rounds, so the earlier "70 blocks" were noise or came from the non-queued arm.

All the details are in `docs/journal/2026-11-20-open-limit-preference.md`. Every round is in `rounds.csv`, the per-block counts are in `features.csv`, and the analysis is `analyse.py`.

Not for merging into master as it stands.

author: pkpio
body:
## Why

Settings → Billing opened on three plan cards that filled the first screen, even for someone who came to check usage, and the rest was a stack of cards each with its own heading and paragraph. Settings pages are moving to one row per setting with less text; this is Billing's turn, in all its variants (cloud Free, cloud paid, trial, plan license, self-hosted).

Layout and wording only. What is charged, every price, limit and credit amount, and what each button calls or submits are unchanged; nothing under `server/` is touched.

## What changed

- **Plan** is one row: the plan's name with a pill ("Your plan", "Trial", "Trial ended", or the license's "Lifetime" / "Tuti license"), one line under it (what Free gives, when a trial ends, or the paid plan's price and renewal), and one control: **Upgrade**, Manage plan, or the license's menu.
- On the default plan (a trial's too) **Upgrade** opens the plans in a dialog, the same picker as before. The dialog is at most the screen's height and scrolls. The page's `#plans` address still works: "Choose a plan" beside the add-on opens the plans, so does an address ending in `#plans`, and Back closes them.
- Links elsewhere that send people to Billing to upgrade (plan notices, upgrade prompts, the trial banner, limits) still go to `/settings/billing`, where Upgrade is now one click away as the page's one primary button. They are left as they are so this PR stays on one screen.
- **This month** holds the month's emails (and, on a license, the month's AI credits) as meters, with the reset day at the title's right.
- **AI credits** holds the balance as a meter, the credits by when they expire, and **Buy AI credits** as one row: the amounts as a segmented choice, the amount field when Other is picked, and Buy. The credits that last past the month stay out of "This month", so they don't read as a monthly allowance.
- **Add-ons** has the "Powered by tuti" row with a shorter line.
- **AI usage** is a card per month, a row per feature, with the month's total at the title's right; with no use, one line.
- Buy keeps the keyboard's place while Stripe's page is being opened, like the page's other buttons.

Not done from the approved design, and why:
- The design showed AI credits under "This month". Free credits, a trial's and top-ups don't reset monthly, so they have their own card; only a license's monthly credits are under "This month".
- Meters still count down ("1,000 of 1,000 left") rather than up, matching the inbox and emails that speak of what's left.
- Every month of AI use is listed, as before, instead of one month behind a chooser.

### New text

- "Plan", "AI credits", "Add-ons", "AI usage · November 2026": card titles, replacing the old headings and their paragraphs.
- "Your plan", "Trial", "Trial ended": the pill beside the plan's name, replacing the "Free plan", "Pro trial" and "Your trial has ended" headings.
- "1,000 emails a month · 2 feedback boards": what the default plan gives, in place of "Upgrade this project for more…".
- "Upgrade": the button that opens the plans. "Choose a plan": the dialog's title; under it "Plans are per project: readers are always unlimited." (moved from the page).
- "Balance": the AI credits meter's label. "AI is paused: this project owes N credits.": under it when nothing is left and credits are owed (the old heading showed a negative balance).
- "Buy AI credits", "Other", "Buy": the row's label, the last amount ("Other amount" before) and its button ("Buy credits" before). Its line loses "You pay on Stripe."; the button still says "Opening Stripe…" while it does.
- "$49 a month, on a paid plan." and "$49 a month, added to this project's plan.": the add-on's line, shortened.
- "No AI use yet.": the empty usage card, one line.

## Screenshots

| | 1440 | 390 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloud, Free | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-cloud-free-desktop.png) | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-cloud-free-phone.png) |
| Cloud, Free: Upgrade | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-cloud-free-plans-desktop.png) | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-cloud-free-plans-phone.png) |
| Cloud, Pro | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-cloud-pro-desktop.png) | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-cloud-pro-phone.png) |
| Trial | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-trial-desktop.png) | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-trial-phone.png) |
| Self-hosted | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-self-hosted-desktop.png) | ![](https://ci.tuti.so/manual/settings-billing/billing-self-hosted-phone.png) |

## How tested

- Typecheck, lint and unit tests pass.
- The Billing database test covers each plan row (default, trial, ended trial, paid, license, deactivated license, plans not for sale with and without a trial), the meters, the credits list and what's owed; the picker's cards are rendered directly, since the dialog is closed in the page's markup.
- Journeys, run against the production build: `plans`, `credits`, `trials`, `licenses`, `license`, and the ones that pass through Billing (`no-header`, `ai-tuning`, `changelog-settings`, the docs AI journey). They now assert that the plans wait behind Upgrade, that `#plans` and "Choose a plan" open them, that Escape and Back close them, that the dialog fits a phone's screen, that Buy keeps focus while its request is held, that focus moves to Upgrade after a license is unassigned, and that nothing overflows sideways at 390px on Free, Pro, trial, license and self-hosted.
- The local Claude review and security review were run before pushing and their findings fixed.

author: anish-ondc
body:
## Summary
ONDC SSO now sends each organisation's NP Portal registrations (`organisations[].configs`). This PR stores them on the user at login and returns them on the profile, so Scenario Testing can list a participant's configs without a separate API call.

## Changes
- `ondc.Organisation` reads `configs`: subscriber ID/URL, `np_type`, domain, version, use case, environment, status, request type, environment access ID. `environment_access_id` is accepted as a number or a string; missing/`null` configs become an empty list.
- `GET /auth/api/me` returns them per organisation as camelCase `configs` (never `null`). They are **not** added to the JWT.

Example (one entry):

```json
{
  "subscriberId": "newuattet22442.com",
  "subscriberUrl": "https://newuattet22442.com/",
  "npType": "BPP",
  "domain": "ONDC:RET10",
  "version": "v 1.2",
  "usecase": "Grocery",
  "environment": "Pre-Prod",
  "status": "Subscribed",
  "requestType": "Update Request",
  "environmentAccessId": "5128"
}
```

## Testing
- **Unit tests (new):** decoding a real-shaped UAT reply, missing / `null` / empty configs, number and string IDs, trimming, and the profile shape.
- **Checks:** `go build`, `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass.
- **End to end (local, real UAT SSO):**
  - 209 configs saved and returned, with 0 differences from the SSO reply.

## Deployment
- No new environment variables or secrets.
- Users see their configs after their next login.
- Merge this PR **before** the automation-frontend PR.

body:
Slice 8, the last one of the redesign: the link preview image and full page meta.

## What changes

- **`/og.png`** is the Paper card ("Link preview (OG image 1200×630)"), rendered at build time by a prerendered route with satori and resvg. Its stats come from the data (`yearsInProduction`, `projects.length`, and the new `leadYears` in `home.ts`), so the New Year rebuild moves "17 yrs" along with the rest of the site.
- **`Meta.svelte`** sets the title, description, canonical URL, Open Graph tags (title, description, url, image with type, size and alt, type, site_name) and `twitter:card = summary_large_image`. `/`, `/work`, `/devisor`, `/lab` and `/cv` use it; their titles and descriptions are unchanged. URLs are absolute on `https://tobylo.dev` (`siteUrl` and `absoluteUrl()` in `site.ts`), so a Preview's canonical and `og:url` point at production.
- **`robots.txt`** (allow all, sitemap line), a prerendered **`sitemap.xml`** with the five pages, and a **`theme-color`** per system scheme from the canvas tokens.

## Notes

- **The Worker stays the same.** The Cloudflare adapter bundles every server import and allows no externals, and resvg is a native addon. So the route loads satori and resvg by name at prerender time instead of importing them. `wrangler deploy --dry-run`: 1843.4 KiB before, 1850.8 KiB after. The difference is the two small endpoint stubs (3.8 and 0.5 KiB); no satori, resvg or yoga code is in the upload.
- **Four new devDependencies:** `satori`, `@resvg/resvg-js`, `@fontsource/inter` and `@fontsource/jetbrains-mono`. Satori needs static woff fonts, which the `@fontsource` packages ship, so no font files are committed. The avatar is a 128 px PNG (`src/lib/og/avatar.png`) because satori doesn't decode webp.
- **The name is weight 800**, as in Paper. The brief said 900.
- **It matches Paper when measured:** avatar box at 72–135 px with a 2 px border, wordmark starting at 153 px, and the yellow bar's border at 1160–1161 px. The name spans 76–801 px; Paper's text node uses `system-ui`, so its cut differs slightly from Inter.
- **`og:image` points at `tobylo.dev/og.png`**, which 404s until `redesign` reaches `main`. On this Preview, `/og.png` is served from the Preview host.
- **`theme-color`** follows the system scheme, not the manual toggle.
- **`/cv`** (from #24) uses `Meta` too, after rebasing on `redesign`.
- The "Link preview" row in Paper's build notes now describes the build-time render.

## Checks

- `bun run check`, `bun run lint` and `bun run build` pass. CodeScene gives 10 to every changed TS file.
- The built HTML for `/`, `/work`, `/devisor`, `/lab` and `/cv` has exactly one title, description and canonical, the full OG/Twitter set, and only `https://tobylo.dev` URLs.
- `og.png` from the build is 1200×630 PNG. `bun run dev` serves it too.
- The Codex bot's finding (hard-coded card colours) is fixed in 6d0ba8d: the card reads the light tokens from `app.css` at build time.
- Local adversarial review: one round of Codex lenses (security clean, failure clean, contracts had one finding, `/cv` meta, done after #24 merged), then the generic Codex review clean and CodeRabbit clean.

## Paper vs build

Built by Workers Builds and served from this Preview (`/og.png`, byte-identical to the local build):

![og.png from the Preview](https://feat-og-meta-tobylo.tobylo.workers.dev/og.png)

Paper source: [Link preview (OG image 1200×630)](https://app.paper.design/file/01M7R5C677RF9VXYNRSEDADENA/p-1-0) on the "Pages" page. The measurements above are taken from the PNG itself, against Paper's computed styles.

## Preview

https://feat-og-meta-tobylo.tobylo.workers.dev: `/`, `/work`, `/devisor`, `/lab`, `/og.png`, `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt` all return 200, and every page has the full tag set, with canonical and `og:url` on tobylo.dev. The visible pages are unchanged; this slice touches only `<head>`.

# OKF proposal: how an OATS view inside a third-party runner is built, and two lessons from building the bb plugin

## What
- `claims/decisions/a-view-inside-a-third-party-runner-reads-the-kernels-json-and-never-acts-on-its-own.md` (about workstream/provider-integration, system/oats-kernel): the plugin reads only the kernel's JSON verbs, joins by the recorded session id, shows the kernel's words, acts only through the CLI, and never acts on its own; with the alternatives rejected.
- `claims/lessons/prove-a-package-by-the-install-route-its-users-take.md` (about workstream/provider-integration): checks from a checkout hid a failing documented install.
- `claims/lessons/build-on-a-staging-branch-when-the-target-repository-does-not-exist-yet.md` (about workstream/coordination): staging branch, then a move proven by tree id.

## Why
A future instance that builds or changes a view of OATS inside another product would otherwise re-open settled choices (join by title or path, read files, retire on delete, replace the host's navigation). One that packages a plugin or a provider would test only from its tree. One whose repository is not there yet would wait, or build where nothing can be reviewed.

Observed 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20 while specifying, verifying and landing the OATS plugin for bb (bb-app 0.50.1, plugin SDK 0.6.157): two container probes, the developers' review loops, the move into oats-project/oats-bb (pull request 1). author: scottwilliamanderson
body:
With Accent from the game on, the screen stalls for a moment each time the highlight rests on a game.

`LivePut` means to recolour its brushes in place, but that never happens. WPF freezes a brush as it goes into the app's resources, so `LivePut` finds a frozen brush every time and puts a new one in its place. Replacing a resource has WPF look the key up again through the whole window. On my Ally X that took 18.6 ms for the accent and 18.2 ms for the colours that follow it, 33 to 47 ms in all for each game.

The brushes now carry an animation on their colour, which stops WPF freezing them. The animation takes no time and has no From or To, so the brush shows its own colour and no extra frames are drawn. After the first time, a new accent is a colour change on the same brush.

| Moving along a row | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Time to apply a new accent | 37.9 ms | under 1 ms |
| Stalls over 30 ms from the accent, in 30 s | 32 | 0 |

One of 10 changes from measuring why Playnite with Kippix kept my handheld's CPU and GPU busy while nothing moved. The figures are 30-second averages in percent of one CPU core, from per-thread CPU times and Windows' GPU engine counters.

Claude Code wrote this and I tested it on my ROG Xbox Ally X (Playnite 10.64, fullscreen, 1080p at 120 Hz).

author: rjskene
body:
Refs #172. PR F2 of the season simulator: the waiver bid becomes a policy an arm can name. Until now a simulated seat in a FAAB league bid by the live rule and nothing else. An arm's spec may now name a `bid` block, a small family of rules whose default member is the live rule, so a screen or a tune can ask which bidding rule finishes best. Sim first: nothing here changes what live bids, and no value of the block is chosen.

**Built on PR G (#445), the guard PR (#447) and PR E (#448), all on main.** The head `805df56` holds main `c1e1214` and was tested against it. That main is PR E squashed and its tree is the tree of PR E's head `9a0512e`, which this branch already held by merge; so main is recorded here with this branch's tree (merge strategy ours, `git diff 9a0512e c1e1214` is empty), because a plain merge of the squashed commit conflicts on every line both PRs moved. The tests below ran on this head's tree: the head and `9551192`, where they ran, have one tree, and the two commits between them are records of merges that change no file. The diff against main is 29 files, all inside `src/pickandroll/sim/`, `tests/sim/` and `docs/sim/`.

## What it does

**The arm's `bid` block.** Six keys, each with a default that is the live rule's: `week` and `season` (the weight of the move's gain on the week and on the season, the rest on the three weeks), `pace` (a spending path), `routine` (the dollar a routine claim bids, 0 or 1), `rival_cap` and `shade`. `pace` and `shade` are named whole or not at all; an unknown key, or one out of its own range, is refused by name. An arm that names no block bids through the engine's own rule, as on main; an empty block is the default member and bids the same.

**The family, in order** (`sim/bid_policy.py`, pure: no file, no generator, nothing of the world):

1. the claim's value in typicals: each horizon's gain over the seat's typical gain on it, by the block's weights. On the three weeks the typical is the live rule's (the fortnight's, the plan floor until ten moves). A week-plan step keeps the live value;
2. the pace: the value times how far the seat's dollars stand from a path over the regular season, then a straight line to nothing through the bracket;
3. the amount, by the live rule's sizing on that paced value, the routine dollar under it;
4. the rival cap: never more than the richest other team's dollars left plus one;
5. the shade: never more than a quantile of the other teams' winning bids so far plus one, once enough are seen.

**The walls.** The policy reads one record for one claim (`bid_policy.Seen`) and nothing else: the seat's own gains, typicals, dollars and sizing, the league's budget, every other team's dollars left (public in a league), the other teams' winning bids of the season (never its own, never a losing bid, never one still sealed) and the calendar. The no-peek check covers a claim decided after the changed day.

**Who reads it.** A seat on the exact or the surrogate tier in a FAAB league, and the arm's mirror rivals. Elsewhere naming it is allowed and moves nothing, and two arms apart only on a block nobody reads are one seat, refused by name. A pace at `k` 0 is no pace in that check.

**One knob gains a reader.** `playoff_weight` is read by a seat that bids on an arm whose `bid.season` is above 0, where the bracket is read: the season figure counts a bracket game that many times. **One row loses one:** a plan floor is not read as a seat's typical gain where the block gives the three weeks no weight (`policy.NO_THREE`); an arm that executes its week plan, or the queue's rule, still reads its floor.

**The counts.** A FAAB run's rows gain three keys: `dollars_at_bracket`, `weeks_at_zero` and `value_won` (the value, in typicals, of the claims the seat won). The record of a run whose arm names a block lists it under `bid`, every key with its value in force, and the reads table has the block's row.

**The screen.** Seven levers, all on the surrogate tier and read only under FAAB: `bid.week`, `bid.season`, `bid.pace.k`, `bid.pace.reserve`, `bid.routine`, `bid.rival_cap`, `bid.shade`. The surrogate tier then holds twenty-one levers and the exact tier six. A baseline that already holds a row's target meets the screen's own refusal of a nudge equal to the baseline, so a tune that has taken such a nudge leaves the row out or names another.

## Built on the guard PR and on PR E

Both edit what this PR edits, so this branch holds them by merge and each crossing has a test file.

- **The guard PR (#447).** An arm may name a block, a guard and a stake together; the seat's problem is guarded, the tier decides, and the block sizes the claims. **The bid reads the season figure with no stake** (the lead's working default): a stake moves the season term's weight inside the decision, and what a claim bids on at `bid.season` is the move's season figure as it is. The counts that part by construction between two arms are one declaration (`counts.APART_BY_CONSTRUCTION`): `value_won` joins the guard PR's count there, and this PR's own tuple in `screen.py` is gone. `tests/sim/test_sim_bid_guard.py`.
- **PR E, and a defect of the two rules together.** The bid policy told a plan's step from a set's move by its place in the queue. That is right where the queue is the set's moves and then a streaming plan's steps, as on this PR's own base. Under the queue's rule a leading plan's steps are queued and none of the set's moves, so a claim's place in the queue is not its place among the decision's moves, and a leading plan's first step was valued on the set's first move's week and season gains. Neither PR is wrong alone, and git merged the two with no conflict at that line. Found by reading the merged executor, and fixed here: the executor counts the set's moves it gathered and tells the bid policy which claim is a plan's step (`policy.bid_seen`). A step keeps the live value, its score over the three weeks' typical, so an arm that executes `queue` bids by its block's weights only on the days its set leads. `tests/sim/test_sim_bid_queue.py` holds it by hand, through the tier's own decision on a day the queue takes a plan beside a set of two, and over a season in each of PR E's FAAB league kinds; with the old inference put back, five of that file's eight tests fail.

## The decision's key holds the week's view

Found by the builder's reading at the bracket PR's refit, and closed here on the lead's decision, since this PR's block is what would have widened it.

Two variants share a team's decision on a day when they hold the same strategy in its seat (by its `repr`) and their states agree in `SimState.key()`, and the key holds no totals. On main that leaves a hole for a seat that searches the week (the exact tier on the weighted set, the queue's rule or a week's plan): two arms of one name apart only in their rivals or in `execute_plan` are one seat to the cache and could be handed each other's decision once their states agreed again on different totals. A screen names its second arm apart, a room is one variant and a pair of two names never shares a seat. A `bid` that weighs the week would have widened it to a plain pair with mirror rivals, a design the screen allows: the block puts each move's gain on the week into the decision, the two arms' mirrors are one `repr` whenever the arms are apart only in the seat's own things, and sharing a mirror's decisions is the design. What would have gone wrong is silent: the size of a mirror's claims, read from the other season's week.

Closed in the key (`run.decision_key`): a strategy that reads the value of this week (`policy.reads_week`) is keyed on its team's view of the week as well (`policy.week_view`: its opponent and both sides' totals so far, the one thing the problem builds the week's span from). That covers an arm's own exact seat that searches the week and whoever bids by a block that weighs it, a mirror rival included. Every other strategy is keyed as before, so what a run sh

author: cyberlife-coder
body: ## Description `GraphCollection::search(query, 10)` could return an **empty** result while other threads overwrote existing nodes' embeddings with `upsert_node(id, payload, Some(vec))`. Over 8 s runs, 0–15 searches out of ~20 000–30 000 came back empty. Payload-only writers never caused it. Supersedes #2866, reopened from a Git Flow branch. **Root cause.** `NativeHnsw::connect_node_with_ef` searched for neighbours **and published the links** layer by layer, from the top layer down. While that ran, a node drawn to layer ≥ 1 could already be reached at its upper layer through its back-edges, yet had no layer-0 neighbour. A concurrent search runs under the same index read guard. Its greedy descent lands on that node (for a query near its vector, the node is the best one at that layer), starts its layer-0 walk there, and returns only that node. The id mapping is written only after the insert returns, so no id maps the node yet: the search maps nothing. `search_past_unmapped` then walks again from the same dead end. Instrumented runs showed exactly this: `walked = 1`, one freshly placed slot, 0 live results. **Fix.** The searches still run top-down: each layer starts from the nearest node found at the layer above. The links are now published bottom-up, so a node becomes reachable at a layer only once every layer below already links it. The fix is local to that one function, so it covers every path that connects through it: the single insert, the parallel batch (`connect_batch_chunked`) and the async builder's `link_placed`. The quantized backends share the same inner graph, so they are covered too. Construction quality does not change: each layer's neighbour search sees the same graph as before. The new node's own links never influenced its own search at another layer. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ## How Has This Been Tested? - [x] Unit tests Two regression tests, each tried with and without the fix. Each asserts first that searches ran while the writes did (hardened method 15), then that none came back short: - `index::hnsw::native::graph::insert::tests::test_a_search_racing_an_insert_never_stops_at_the_node_being_linked`: 3 searchers query the vector being inserted. Without the fix, 6 119 searches returned fewer than k = 10 results (debug build). With it, none did. - `collection::graph_collection::overwrite_race_tests::test_a_search_racing_embedding_overwrites_never_comes_back_empty`: `GraphCollection` search racing `upsert_node` embedding overwrites. Without the fix, 2 022 short results. With it, none. The original 8 s, 2 writers / 4 searchers reproduction (release build) went from 5 empty results out of 44 007 searches to 0 out of 41 010. - `cargo test -p velesdb-core --features persistence --lib -- --test-threads=1`: 5931 passed, 0 failed. - `cargo test -p velesdb-core --features persistence test_recall -- --test-threads=1`: green, recall contracts ≥ 0.95 included. - `cargo clippy -p velesdb-core --all-targets --features persistence,update-check,internal-bench -- -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean. **Test Configuration:** - OS: Linux - Rust version: workspace toolchain ## Checklist - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes ## High-Risk Change Checklist - [x] Invariant impacted: *a node reachable at layer l has its links at every layer below l*. It now holds by construction in `connect_node_with_ef`, as documented in its "Publication order" section. - [x] No change to durability, persistence or the mappings. - [x] Concurrency tests added (see above). - [ ] Review from 2 maintainers requested. ## Additional Notes No `unsafe` code is added or changed. --- `` <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://static.devin.ai/assets/gh-devin-review-dark.svg?v=4"><img src="https://static.devin.ai/assets/gh-devin-review-light.svg?v=4" alt="Devin Review"> ``

author: richardawe
body:
Three fixes after the live front page (#83). PR only: not merged or deployed. Prices and Premium are unchanged.

## 1. Video text
- New `App\Support\VideoText` makes a summary from the description: the first sentence, plus the second if both fit in 160 characters. A long first sentence is cut at a word and ends with "…". The summary leaves out URLs, hashtags, @handles, credit lines (`Photo:`, `Music:`, `Credits:` …) and the AI disclosure paragraph (ours from `config('radio.disclosure')` or any "made/voiced with AI/Kokoro" wording).
- The homepage hero and `/reels/videos/{id}` use `SocialVideo::summary()` and never show the raw description. The page's meta description uses it too.
- Photo credits and the AI disclosure are shown only in small print at the bottom of the video page (`md-video-notes`, from `SocialVideo::smallPrint()`).
- Long words and URLs wrap with `overflow-wrap:anywhere` (hero, video page, news list). Playwright found 0 px of horizontal overflow at 390 px on the homepage and the video page.

## 2. News pictures
- `FootballNewsService` no longer reads `og:image`/`twitter:image` and never downloads source pictures. `downloadSourceImage` is removed.
- New `App\Services\NewsImages` picks a picture in this order:
  1. our match card, when the story names both clubs of a match within 4 days;
  2. the licence-checked Commons photo of an in-scope player named in full, with the credit and source link shown under the article picture;
  3. a branded 1200×675 Matchday text card (`blog-images/card-*.png`, drawn with the design tokens).
- `php artisan news:replace-source-images --dry-run` lists every article whose picture came from another site: downloaded `news-*` files, rows with `source_image_url`, or any host other than ours or Wikimedia (BBC, Getty, Reuters, AP, AFP, PA …). It shows the source host and the planned replacement and draws nothing. Without `--dry-run` it swaps the pictures, keeps the old value in `metadata.replaced_image`, and deletes a downloaded file once no article uses it. Admin uploads, Wikimedia links and our own cards are left alone.
- `news:backfill-images` now adds our own pictures instead of source ones.

## 3. No picture twice on the homepage
- `App\Support\ImageIdentity` treats two pictures as the same when our files have the same sha1, or when other links have the same address after the query string is dropped.
- `FrontPage::distinctImages` goes down the page: hero, then New on Matchday, then Latest News. When a picture was already shown, an article uses its text card and other items use a CSS fallback card. In Latest News, if both the picture and the text card were already shown higher up, a CSS card is used. The new classes avoid "-card" in their names because the cartoon look restyles every `[class*="md-"][class*="-card"]`.

## Tests
- `tests/Feature/FrontPageCleanupTest.php` (8 tests) covers the summary rules, the video page and its small print, the hero, the wrap CSS, no source picture on import, match card before Commons photo with credit, the backfill dry run then the real run, and unique pictures down the homepage (same address and same bytes).

author: keystarr
body:
## Why
Live tests had no way to stage a Start of Game card on its real engine path. The engine records Start of Game cards from the deck before the deal (`StartOfGameRules.Capture`), and a debug scenario applies after the mulligans, so a card the scenario adds to the deck never fires. The test decks that contain such cards are offered only on Sandbox saves. So the Godfrey portal fix (#264) could not be checked live on the real path.

## What
- Two new debug scenario keys: `humanStartOfGame=ID,...` and `npcStartOfGame=ID,...`, up to 3 cards each, in `plugin/Npc/DebugScenario.cs`.
  - Each card goes to the bottom of that player's deck, so the first draw and `humanDeckTop` order don't change.
  - Each card is then marked the same way the engine marks deck cards at the deal. Its effect fires in the engine's own Start of Game step, inside its own TRIGGER block.
  - The applied log says `(fires)` or `(not eligible)`.
  - A card with no Start of Game effect, an unknown id or a full deck is rejected.
- Engine: one new public method, `StartOfGameRules.Stage`, which applies Capture's rule to one deck card. Capture and Resolve are unchanged, so no golden or replay changes.
- Limits, also stated in the key's header: eligibility is checked when the scenario applies, and the staged card is not in the recorded starting deck (`DeckCards`). So Nozdormu and Mug'Zee can differ from retail. Godfrey has no condition.
- Debug scenarios are already limited to ENGINE_SOURCE lab and Deck builds. A release build ignores them.

## Tests
- native-match `DebugScenarioStartOfGame`:
  - both seats;
  - Godfrey's real effect (JAIL_509e) and the portal tag 4717;
  - the TRIGGER block sourced by the staged card;
  - bottom placement and draw order;
  - a staged NPC card stays hidden from the human until the normal Start of Game reveal;
  - eligibility, including Hamuul staying ineligible after deck changes;
  - a deterministic replay;
  - deck capacity;
  - parse rejections.
- Goldens 402/402, engine-proof green.
- native-match: main currently fails this suite at `B16MagmawProjection` and `EnchantedCopyCreatedWithItsStats`, which are #173 fallout fixed by #261. With those skipped locally (not committed), the new checks pass. **This stays a draft until #261 merges; then I rebase and run the full suite with nothing skipped.**

## Live check
On a lab test client, using physical mouse drags:
- `humanStartOfGame=JAIL_509`: the log says "fires", the human hero gets 4717=1 and JAIL_509e, and the start doesn't stall.
- `npcStartOfGame=JAIL_509`: the same on the NPC.
- `humanStartOfGame=CS2_182`: rejected with "has no Start of Game effect", and no match starts.
- With #264 merged on top, Godfrey's portal tag follows a Jaraxxus hero replacement.
- The portal animation itself could not be confirmed on screen. The tags are the evidence.

## Review
An independent review of the whole diff gave MERGE AFTER FIXES at d4c9bebc. Both fixes are in 0d943af3 (the header limits and the privacy test); the reviewer's third point was a gap in the private test tooling, fixed separately. A re-review at 0d943af3 gave MERGE. An optional follow-up: assert there is exactly one ShowEntity for the staged card before MAIN_READY.

author: errax
body:
Known issue #13: a batch of parallel native tool calls ends the whole turn.

## Why

When a model issues eight or more Cursor-native calls (Shell, Read, Grep) in parallel, the turn fails with `Cursor repeatedly requested disabled local tools (8 requests without a Pi tool result)` and nothing runs.

The provider rejects each native call and stops the run after eight rejections. The count was per call. But Cursor executes each call of a batch as it streams in, so every call of the batch is rejected before the model has read a single rejection. A batch of twelve is one mistake, not twelve ignored warnings.

## What changed

- The budget now counts **model steps** that contain a rejected native call. A parallel batch is one step. The limit stays at eight.
- A step ends at Cursor's `conversationCheckpointUpdate`, which it sends once a step's tool results are in. Rejections after that checkpoint come from a model that has already been shown the earlier ones.
- A ceiling of 64 rejected calls applies whatever the step count, so the loop stays finite if Cursor ever stops sending that checkpoint.
- The error message reports both numbers, for example `24 requests over 8 model steps`. The lifecycle log's `local_tool_rejected` and `local_tool_loop_stopped` events carry a `steps` field next to `count`.

Unchanged: text and heartbeats do not reset the budget, pending Pi calls still take priority, the counters survive transport retries, and they reset when Pi's tool results are sent.

## Why the checkpoint is the boundary

I checked the debug logs from earlier live runs (`/tmp/pi-cursor-livetest` and `~/.cache/pi-cursor`):

- Inside a parallel batch, the only messages between two native execs are `toolCallStarted`, `tokenDelta` and `toolCallCompleted`. So "the model generated something in between" cannot separate steps: `tokenDelta` arrives mid-batch.
- Between two model steps (a tool completes, then new thinking or text), a checkpoint was present in 37 of 37 cases, across Composer 2.5, Grok 4.7 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

## Verification

Live, with the prompt from the known-issues note (twelve `echo` commands, "as many in parallel as you can"), `deepseek-v41-flash-1017-max-mode`, isolated cache dir:

| build | result |
|---|---|
| `a45edc3` (`main`) | 1 of 1 failed: 8 rejections, loop stopped, 0 Pi tool calls |
| this branch | 2 of 2 passed: 12 rejections counted as 1 step, then 12 Pi `bash` calls, correct final line |

Tests:

- New: a batch of twelve is one step and the next Pi call runs; eight rejected batches in a row still stop the run; 64 calls with no checkpoint stop the run.
- The existing budget tests now put a checkpoint between rejections, so they still exercise "eight ignored rejections".
- `yarn check` passes (381 tests).

## Not covered

- The model still tries native tools first and pays for a rejected round. That is known issue #2; this change only stops the batch from being fatal.
- The limits are constants. There is no environment variable for them.

author: maxgekk
body:
The `alloc` job of `ci.yml` had never run on Arm: the preferred species is 128 bits there, and no run had shown a port's body unboxed at that width (`SKILLS.md`, "CI checks it"). This is step 1 of the plan on #37: run it once, and keep the row if every row passes. Every row passed, so the row stays.

**The reading.** The first commit added the row as a trial that could fail without failing the workflow. Its run ([job 136201242337](https://github.com/vecbricks/vfdlibm/actions/runs/44710674209/job/136201242337), on commit `820f0ff`, before the rebase) was on a runner whose probe printed `jvm: MaxVectorSize=16 UseSVE=2` and no CPU model name, as the 332 Arm jobs of `HARDWARE.md`, "What the pool gives", do. All 24 `*Preferred` rows of the five ports passed, on common and on mixed data, at 0.037 to 0.103 B/op in the worst of three iterations. The threshold is 1 B/op; a boxed body reads kilobytes. Each row's iterations, minimum, average and maximum, and JMH's table from the job's log, are committed in `bench/results/alloc-arm-2026-11-20.txt`. This is an allocation reading and no timing: the file says its ns/op are not to be quoted. It also says the job printed no kernel or load then; it does now.

One run is one run: the row has passed once, on one draw. The Arm pool read the same flags on all 332 jobs of its census, so another draw is not expected to differ, which is an expectation and not a measurement.

**What the pull request holds**, rebased on main (`ci.yml`'s `bench-scripts` job from #50 and the other jobs are kept):

- `ci.yml`: the `alloc` matrix has three rows, the two x86 rows with the command they ran before, and `Arm 128 bits`, which runs `bench/alloc-check.py --preferred-only`: the `*Preferred` rows only, since a `*256` row would run in the Java fallback at 128-bit vectors, as 512 bits does on an AVX2 host. The Arm row fails the workflow like the others. Every row first prints the machine (`bench/datapath.sh`, `lscpu`'s model lines, the check's JVM options, the kernel) and the load before the check and after it. When the check fails, `bench/alloc-check.py --why` runs and the check's JSON is kept as an artifact named for the matrix row and the run attempt.
- `bench/alloc-check.py`: `--preferred-only` derives the Arm row's regex from the one pattern the x86 rows use, so an exclusion is written once. `--why` reads the failed run's JSON and reruns the failing rows (eight at most, one of each benchmark method first, ten minutes each) under the JVM options the result records for each, with C2 compiling alone (`-XX:-TieredCompilation`, so `PrintInlining` holds C2's refusals and not C1's, with `InlineSmallCode` passed back at its tiered value), and prints each distinct `PrintIntrinsics` line with its count, then C2's refused calls that name the library, `NodeCountInliningCutoff` or a refused intrinsic, then the other refused calls into the Vector API. It says so when a rerun does not read as boxing, and prints the end of the output when a rerun measured nothing. Maven runs in a process group of its own that is killed on a timeout or a SIGTERM. The script gives Maven no stdin (exec:exec passes it to JMH). `--jvm-args` with one option needs the `=` form, which the usage and `ci.yml` use.
- `SKILLS.md`: "On Arm the check runs the preferred rows, and they pass" replaces "Arm is not checked yet", and "When the check fails, ask it why" describes `--why`. `AGENTS.md`: where CI runs the check, the `--jvm-args=` form, and the name of an Arm allocation file (`arm` is no benchmark host key).

**Checked on the laptop**, which is not the runner: `--why` on the result of the check on `ExpBenchmark.finish128` listed the two-lane `not supported` lines and `VectorSupport::compare`, `convert` and `blend` as refused intrinsics, and on `ExpBenchmark.finishPairBoxed256` listed `Lanes::hiAbove`, `hiBelow`, `intSpecies` and `Exp::expCore` refused for `NodeCountInliningCutoff` (`SKILLS.md`, "Two port bodies in one loop do not fit"); a stand-in Maven's child was gone after a timeout and after a SIGTERM. The `--why` step has not run in CI, since nothing failed there. `mvn verify` was not run locally: no Java or build file changes.

author: alastairrushworth
body:
Fixes from the site audit of 2026-11-20. One commit per fix; each has its own tests where the logic is testable.

## What changes on the site

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Pages built | 5,055 | 4,897 |
| Listed roles (home, stats, llms.txt, MCP index) | 3,568 | 3,349 |
| Duplicate pages canonicalised | 104 | 323 |
| Closed / delisted tombstones | 369 / 28 | 235 / 19 |
| City pages | 47 | 40 |
| Job titles trimmed with "…" | 1,670 | 528 |
| Meta descriptions saying the work type twice | 595 | 0 |
| JobPostings | 3,203 | 3,199 |

## The fixes

**Duplicates and dead URLs**
- **Per-city reposts fold into one listing** (`shared/indexable.ts`). Speechify had 245 roles that were one advert posted once per city. A second duplicate key folds postings with the same employer, location and description whose titles differ only by a trailing " - suffix". Speechify's 27 per-country adverts stay separate, because their pay bands differ. 219 postings fold today (217 Speechify, 1 Coupa, 1 Anyone AI).
- **Closing an aged-out role no longer revives its URL** (`site/src/lib/tombstone.ts`). The tombstone window now runs from the day the role left the board, whichever exit came first. 138 pages that had already been 404 stop coming back.

**Landing pages**
- **City pages need three employers** (`lib/landings.ts`), with the same hysteresis as the role count. Seven pages go: Basking Ridge, Hawthorne, Irving, Jersey City, McLean, Milpitas, Pleasanton. Bristol and Foster City are retained on recent evidence.
- **Clearing a filter on page 2+ restores that page's roles** (`JobFilters.astro`). It used to show page 1's roles under a pager that said page 2.

**Search snippets and markup**
- **Job titles drop the " — frontierroles.com" suffix** and give those 20 characters to the role. Total length is unchanged.
- **Work type is no longer repeated** in meta descriptions and feed summaries ("Remote, Remote").
- **No JobPosting without the employer's description** (two HSBC roles had a placeholder sentence). Shared with the engine so the Indexing API delta agrees.
- **Daily feed drops picks that have since become duplicates** (three items).

**Smaller things**
- `/companies/` lists the 190 single-role employers, each linked to its one role. Five roles had no link from any indexable page.
- A real space between names and counts ("London201"), and between two pairs of sentences that ran together.
- 404 copy covers roles that aged out, and links Locations and Companies.

**Engine**
- **A multi-site location takes its country from the site its city came from** (`pipeline/location.ts`). "London & San Francisco" was stored as London, US. `relocate` is NULL-only for country, so `relocateRow` gains one narrow case to correct rows the engine itself misread. Simulated against today's snapshot it corrects 81 rows and changes nothing else.
- Heidelberg, Tampere and Kuwait get a country (11 rows). "Blank" is no longer a city; "Banglore" reads as Bangalore.

**Audit tooling**
- `check_dist.py` now fails on a duplicate requisition in a feed, a work type stated twice, and a single-employer city page. Run against `main` it reports all three.
- `SKILL.md` and `audit-conventions.md` updated: the apex is behind Cloudflare's proxy since 8 Nov, how to read Googlebot's crawl from there, and the current rules.

## Things to know before merging

- **Seven city URLs and their RSS feeds will 404.** If the social poster subscribes to any per-city feed among those seven, repoint it first.
- **The daily feed swaps three items.** The three duplicates leave and three older picks re-enter the 100-item window, dated late October. They were in the feed before, so a poster that tracks guids will not re-send them.
- **`/ai-jobs-bangalore/rss.xml` gains one item**, the role that was filed under "Banglore".
- **The country corrections land on the next nightly run**, not on merge: they are applied by `relocate`.
- `/companies/` grows from 81KB to 119KB (about 12KB compressed) and is now the largest page.

## Deliberately not changed

- **Sitemap window (30 days).** Googlebot fetches about a dozen live job pages a day whichever way it is set, so I left the decision alone and updated the comment's figures.
- **San Carlos, Cambridge, Birmingham, Markham** stay without a country. `tests/location.test.ts` pins them as ambiguous on purpose; I had added a San Carlos hint and took it back out.
- **Tap-target sizes** (26px skill badges, 38px search box). Both clear the accessibility floor and the phone filter bar is budgeted to the pixel.
- **Breakpoint differences** across components. Each is commented.
- Items the audit routed elsewhere: the "Go" skill matching the English word, three implausible salaries, classifier scope, security headers.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`: 0 errors. `npm test`: 616 passed, 2 skipped (was 582).
- Full build, then `check_dist.py`: 337,951 internal links, none broken, no hard issues.
- Baseline diff of the two builds: 158 routes removed, none added; the only feed and sitemap changes are the ones listed above.
- Headless Chrome on the new build: filter and clear on `/ai-agent-jobs/2/`, `/27/`, page 1 and the homepage restores the page's own cards; no overflow at 320–1280px on the changed pages; no script errors.
- Location parser A/B against the old one over all 1,239 distinct locations in the snapshot: 31 change — 28 multi-site locations whose city is now paired with its own country, and the three newly placed names.

author: cjber
body:
A spot on a Feralas plateau (-5338, 827) is ringed by faces past the player's slope and step limits, so no walk from any place on the landmass reaches it, in the 8 yd grid or the full-resolution mesh. The planner found no route at all.

Now, when the goal batch reaches no target, a directed flood from the targets over cluster entrances (adjacent links plus climbs, so downhill-only ground is not mistaken for reachable) finds the ground they walk to, and the goal moves to the nearest reached node. The journey restarts toward it, unless the walk from the player already reaches the goal. The reason sits beside the code in `Routing/Path.lua` (`nearestGround`).

- The plateau click moves 157 yd to (-5409.0, 967.2, 147.0). Both Camp Mojache and the valley walk there, and the walk ends exactly on that point.
- An ordinary goal never moves.
- The restart keeps the rough route already drawn until the proved route replaces it, so `journey_optimal_spec` still sees one estimate (its pair 15 is such a goal).
- Cost only in the rare case: the grounding goal batch takes about 1050 ms against 760 to 820 ms for an ordinary Feralas goal batch, and the journey about 914 frames against 546 for clicking the moved ground directly.

`tests/peak_goal_spec.lua` covers the moved point, its reachability, the walk's end, an unmoved ordinary goal, a Stormwind journey ending on the moved ground, and a walk across the plateau to the spot that keeps it. It fails on main. Screenshots render the same pixels; `scenes.sha256` is re-recorded.

Review: Codex found five issues, all fixed in 0156ba9: the goal could move while the walk from a player already on the plateau was still pending, the move outlived Search.Reset, the fallback could start with its batch looking settled, a shared search tree across yields, and a full-square ring scan. The spec now also walks across the plateau to the spot after a reset and checks it stays put (it fails on the first commit). A Codex re-review of those fixes found one more: a replan could drop the start batch's completion callback, so the move never fired; d94e95a also grounds right after attach recovers finished results. Re-review reported the other five fixes correct. Muse could not run: `API error 429: Subscription quota exhausted. Your usage window resets at 2026-11-23T00:00:00Z`.

Closes #1113
Refs #1116: the 8 yd grid cuts off ground the full-resolution mesh joins, tracked there.
