## Scope

Two commits, both from the user's report:

**List every floating window on the Floating page**
- *Floating now* listed only windows floated by hand, one per app. It now lists every window you floated, showing its actual title, each with *Always float*.
- A new *Also floating* section at the foot, as on tide for Linux's page, lists the windows a rule floats already, dialogs among them.
  - Each says whose rule: *Built in* (tide's own, or a dialog step) or *Your rule* (the files' or `start()`'s). The detailed reason shows on hover.
  - *Details* fills the fields, saying what floats the window and what macOS says of it.
- `wm:floating_now()` returns every floating window, sorted by app name then title. A `covered` field marks the ones a rule floats, and `builtIn` says whose rule.

**Paint no shadow round a dialog, whose corners its app draws**
- tide's painted shadow on Chrome's "Leave site?" dialog used a normal window's corner radius, so its corners poked out past the dialog's own.
- A window that floats as a dialog, a panel, or another non-standard window (`rules.step`) is now marked `dialog`, and tide paints it no shadow. The dimming still cuts its hole.

## Test plan

- `make lint test`. New and changed tests:
  - `floating_test`: every floating window, in order, with what floats each and whose rule;
  - `floating_hs_test`: a window covered by a rule is still listed, marked;
  - `settings_page.cjs`: both lists, and Details;
  - `settings_test`: the new list's columns;
  - `shadow_test`: no shadow for a dialog, and a dialog is marked in the focus scene.
- Not tested on a real Mac: whether Chrome's "Leave site?" counts as a dialog. If macOS reports it as a standard, resizable window, it would still get the shadow.

## Impact

Privacy, reliability and cost: none.

author: druranus
body:
## Entscheidung

Bitte den v1-Vertragsentwurf für die Antwort auf eine offene Reset-Rückfrage prüfen. Der Vorschlag lässt genau eine angebotene Einmalantwort über den vorhandenen Freigabepfad zu. Zustimmung wird erst wirksam, wenn die PermissionEngine den Reset verarbeitet. Die bisherige V1-Oberfläche bleibt Standard. Phase 3 und die weiteren schreibenden Phasen sind außerhalb dieses PRs.

## Was sich ändert

* GUI und CLI binden ihre bestehenden synchronen Engine-Resetaufrufe einmalig an den zugehörigen UI-Provider und Aufruferthread. Der Provider verweigert passende Anzeigedaten ohne diese Herkunft. Bei anderen Providern gilt der bisherige Aufruf. Ein direkter Aufruf mit UI-Provider außerhalb der beiden vorgesehenen Einstiege schlägt im Not-Aus geschlossen fehl.
* Der Adapter prüft die offene ID, die zulässige Wahl und den Fristablauf beim Verbrauch der Anfrage. IDs sind über Adapterinstanzen hinweg getrennt. Der Fake bildet dasselbe Verhalten ab. Beim Serverende werden noch offene Fragen abgebrochen.
* Zehn fokussierte Fälle prüfen beide Adapter, gültige und ungültige Antworten, Parallelität, Trennung, CLI, echte Registry und Engine. Der neue Browserfall prüft zwei Fenster an demselben realen Controller.
* PermissionEngine, EmergencyStop, ToolRegistry, Auditlogik, Workflowdateien und die produktive Oberfläche sind im Branch-Diff unverändert.

## Branchverträglichkeit

Die 40 anderen offenen PR-Köpfe wurden für den Stand von #263 (`e7bcd496`) per Git-Baumvergleich geprüft. #255, #256, #258 und #261 kollidieren in der Browser-Testdatei. #259 kollidiert zusätzlich im Launcher. V2 ergänzt Leseansichten für Agenten und Trace, V2.1 ergänzt die Missionsansicht. Die HTML-Einfügestellen von #263 sind in den untersuchten aktuellen V2-Seiten vorhanden. Keine fremden Branches wurden geändert. Die Prüfreferenzen und technischen Einzelheiten stehen in [der Entscheidungsvorlage](https://github.com/DrUranus/JARVIS/blob/bfe8f56d433f02e751c306b17a692db88272a8d9/docs/NEXUS_RESET_VERTRAGSREVIEW.md).

## Nachweis und Freigabe

Technisch als Entwurf auf `codex/nexus-reset-vertragsreview` implementiert. Die zehn gezielten Vertragsfälle sind lokal bestanden. Der Test mit angehaltenem Provider weist nach, dass ein bestätigter UI-Ack und ein wirksamer Tool-Stopp gleichzeitig vorliegen können. Die Prüfung auf realer Windows-Hardware und die Produktivfreigabe stehen aus. #186 ist weiterhin offen. [Browser- und Overlay-CI](https://github.com/DrUranus/JARVIS/actions/runs/44808991666)

**Abschließende Ergebnisse für `bfe8f56d`**

| Prüfung | Bestanden | Übersprungen | Fehlgeschlagen |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Lokale gezielte Regression unter Linux, einschließlich der zehn Vertragsfälle | 529 | 24 | 0 |
| Browser-CI Windows / Ubuntu, jeweils | 27 | 0 | 0 |
| Nativer Windows-Overlayjob auf dem Runner | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Isolierter gemeinsamer Quellbaum aus #263 und #264, gezielte Integrationstests | 15 | 0 | 0 |

Die 24 lokalen Skips entfallen auf 22 Tk-Fenstertests ohne Display und zwei Windows-spezifische Tests. Alle vier Paketinstallationsjobs auf Windows und Ubuntu für Python 3.11 und 3.13 sind erfolgreich. Python-Kompilierung und `git diff --check` bestanden. Die branchgefilterten Standardjobs `pr-tests` haben diesen Codex-Branch übersprungen. Für diesen schmalen Entwurf wurde die vollständige Repository-Suite nicht erneut angefordert. Der kombinierte Test verwendete ein temporäres Archiv aus dem von `git merge-tree` berechneten Baum, ohne Merge-Commit oder Branchänderung. [GUI-CI](https://github.com/DrUranus/JARVIS/actions/runs/44808991666) · [Paketinstallationen](https://github.com/DrUranus/JARVIS/actions/runs/44808991665)


## Abschließender Sicherheitsreview · a2465a5

Die enge Vertragssemantik ist vom Besitzer akzeptiert. Vor der Korrektur beantworteten beide Adapter einen vor dem Shutdown angenommenen und bis nach dem Neustart zurückgestellten Snapshot-Aufruf mit HTTP 200. Jetzt prüft der Transport unter seiner Backend-Sperre, ob der Handler noch zum aktiven Listener gehört. Der alte Aufruf erhält 503. Der neue Listener beantwortet denselben regulären Aufruf erfolgreich. Auch der Abgang des letzten Fensters und das zugehörige detach liegen nun unter derselben Sperre wie der Beitritt eines Fensters.

Die Antwort genau an der Deadline wird abgelehnt. ID-Verbrauch und Schließen liegen unter derselben Adaptersperre. Die Herkunftsbindung nutzt eine Sperre pro Provider und eine einmal verbrauchbare Markierung pro Aufruferthread. Im Test bleibt der echte Tool-Stopp auch nach positivem Ack wirksam, solange der Provider seine Entscheidung noch nicht an die Engine zurückgegeben hat. Die Nachkorrektur berührt ausschließlich Transport und Regressionstests. Der geprüfte Diff enthält keine Änderungen an der produktiven PermissionEngine, der ToolRegistry oder den JSON-Schemas.

* 173 bestandene lokale Vertrags-, Controller- und Not-Aus-Prüfungen.
* 319 bestandene lokale Control-Center-Prüfungen, zwei Windows-spezifische Fälle unter Linux übersprungen. Die Testgruppen überschneiden sich.
* 17 bestandene Integrationstests im temporären gemeinsamen Baum mit #263 bei e7bcd496.
* Windows und Ubuntu jeweils 27 bestandene Browserprüfungen ohne Skips. Zwei native Overlaytests und vier Paketinstallationsjobs bestanden. Die branchgefilterten Standardjobs waren übersprungen. [GUI-CI](https://github.com/DrUranus/JARVIS/actions/runs/44810439817) · [Paket-CI](https://github.com/DrUranus/JARVIS/actions/runs/44810439566)

Die reale Windows-Abnahme #186 und die Produktivfreigabe sind offen. Der PR bleibt im Entwurfsstatus.

author: anish-ondc
body:
## Summary
Redesigns the Scenario Testing page, lists a logged-in user's NP Portal configs (from ONDC SSO), and lets a user who belongs to several organisations pick the one they are working for.

**Depends on:** automation-user-management `feat/sso-configs` (returns `organisations[].configs` on `/auth/api/me`). Without it, this page still works but shows no NP Portal configs.

## Changes

### Logged out
- Login prompt ("Log in to run your tests") with "Continue without login", and a benefits row (Saved Configs, Sessions & Reports, Reuse Configs).
- Guest form: breadcrumbs, "You're not logged in" alert, two fields per row, Cancel / Submit. Environment field removed (PRE-PRODUCTION is the only option). Guest sessions have no user or organisation.

### Logged in
- **Split view:** configs on the left (search, All / Buyer apps / Seller apps tabs with counts, one bordered card per subscriber URL, ready / needs-input dot); the selected config on the right with Launch and View report.
- **NP Portal configs from SSO:** one card per subscriber URL + role + domain, per organisation; exact repeats dropped. URL, role and domain are used as sent (domain only if Workbench supports it). NP Portal's version and use case are **never** used — the user always picks them from Workbench's lists under "Fill in to launch".
- **New session** opens as a full page with its own address (`/scenario?view=new`). Past Report button removed.

### Organisation
- After every login, a user with **more than one** organisation picks the one they are working for (a required picker; users with one are never asked). The choice is kept with the login and cleared on logout and on a new login.
- The top bar shows the active organisation; with several it is a menu to switch (also in the mobile menu).
- Scenario Testing lists only the active organisation's configs. New session shows the organisation as text and creates the session for it.



## Testing
- **Automated:** Scenario + organisation tests pass (login gate, form, config list, details panel, SSO configs, guide, tooltips, org picker and switcher, filtering, navigation). Full frontend suite 179 pass; the only failures (`authHeaderCrypto`, `github-import-modal`) fail identically on `main-tech`. Backend vitest 186/186. `tsc`, ESLint and Prettier clean.
- **End to end, local, real UAT SSO:** NP Portal configs listed with correct counts; SSO-config, saved-config and New session launches create sessions with the right org/user; guest session has none; the organisation picker appears for multi-org users and scopes the list; switching organisations updates the configs; logout clears the choice; light/dark and phone widths checked; no console errors.

## Deployment
- No new environment variables.
- Merge **after** the automation-user-management PR.
- Users need to log in again to see their NP Portal configs.

body:
Jason Desktop is the window onto the installation, and since the browser's own screens and its loopback bridge went, the release's UI draws its console there alone. The words still described a browser UI in the README, the pages, the skills and the help of the `ui` verbs. This change makes them say one window, and gives a web interface of one's own, the door that stays open, one section that says how it works today.

## What changed

- **README**: four small word edits, nothing else. The quick start no longer runs `jason ui install` (Jason Desktop places the UI itself at a start that finds it missing); the languages row says Jason Desktop is TypeScript; the CLI is a client of the local API like Jason Desktop and your agent; the documentation table's row links "Jason Desktop's screens".
- **`docs/ui.md`** becomes the page of Jason Desktop's screens. Pairing is said of pages (the desktop's window holds a token like any paired page), the System screen's list is described in the words it draws, a setting kept "in this browser" is kept in the window's storage (in memory, so until the desktop's next start), and the sentences about a browser shell that no longer exists are gone, its "Settings and Chat in the browser" heading among them.
- **One section, "A web interface of your own"**, at the end of `docs/ui.md`: what a tab at the runtime's `/ui/` shows with none (the one sentence), a build under `<data>/ui/custom/` served instead of the release's (and drawn by Jason Desktop's window too), `jason ui pair` and the exchange at `POST /ui/session` (the ticket, the answer's members, `ticket_invalid`), `jason ui open --web` and `custom_ui_not_installed`, how a page calls the Runtime API and follows the journal (`jason.bearer.<token>`), `origin_refused`, and what a token can do. Nothing else links to it but the pages that already described the door (`docs/runtime-api.md`, `docs/architecture.md`).
- **The other pages**: `docs/desktop.md`, `docs/runtime-api.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/handbook.md`, `docs/INSTALL.md`, `docs/release-and-update.md`, `docs/philosophy.md`, `ui/README.md`, `desktop/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and `.github/release-notes-template.md` say Jason Desktop, or a paired page, where they said the browser UI. `desktop/README.md` no longer says a `jason:` click opens the browser UI where no desktop is registered (it opens nothing). `ui/README.md`'s dev loop and its way to try a build open Jason Desktop, since the release's build draws one sentence in a browser tab.
- **Skills**: `operating-the-installation` and the runtime skills' catalog say a page is unpaired, not a browser, and what `jason ui revoke --all` does to the desktop's window (it says it is not paired until the desktop pairs it again: at its next start, a runtime restart, or Reload in its View menu). They teach nothing about building a UI.
- **The CLI's help**: `ui`, `ui tokens`, `ui revoke` and `ui revoke --all` say page where they said browser, and `--actor` says a write is made under the name Jason Desktop writes as. `ui/package.json`'s description names Jason Desktop.

This touches the README, a public file read first by everyone.

- New tests, each seen red before the change that turns it green:

Neither row reads a file this change touches, and both were green in the run before.

author: fiskus
body:
## Problem

`build_manifest_from_rows_stream` read its stream with `while let Some(Ok(chunk))`. A chunk that came back as an error ended the loop as if the stream were done, so the push built a manifest from the rows read so far, uploaded it and tagged it. A failed upload could leave a revision on the bucket that silently lacks files; the push then only failed on the later hash check, with a hash-mismatch message that hid the real cause.

## Change

- `build_manifest_from_rows_stream` returns the chunk's error and writes no manifest. The commit flow's merge of the stored rows also skipped a failed chunk; it now passes the error on as a row, so the build fails.
- A failed upload is an `Error::Upload { key, source }`: it names the file and holds the upload's error. Only the first failed file is named, since uploads run one at a time and stop at the first failure. **Breaking:** `Error` has a new variant.
- `Error::cause` returns the error under the wrapper, and `is_not_found`, the session checks and `s3_host` read it.
- QuiltSync classifies on the cause: an expired session still asks for a sign-in (the message reads "Couldn't upload `<file>`: Your session … has expired"), autosync retries a network error instead of pausing the package, and telemetry places the failure by its cause.
- The CLI's `--json` kind is the cause's, e.g. `login`.

## Tests

- `test_build_fails_on_a_failed_chunk`: one good chunk then a failed one returns the chunk's error and writes nothing.
- `test_push_fails_when_an_upload_fails`: a push with one missing file ends with `Error::Upload` naming that file, writes no cached manifest and leaves `latest` unset. Before the fix it uploaded a manifest and failed on the hash check.
- `an_upload_failure_is_classified_by_its_cause` (quilt-rs), `a_failed_upload_has_its_causes_kind` (CLI), and in QuiltSync: the frontend message, telemetry, and `classify_a_failed_upload_by_its_cause` (autosync retries a network blip on one file; it paused without the classifier change).

`just ci` passes.

author: max-mudu
body:
## What changes (interim)

A delivery cannot yet record how much of it was accepted, and partial acceptance today credits site stock with the full delivered quantity. Until the accepted quantity can be recorded (follow-up PR), a request that would move a delivery with a delivered quantity above zero into `partially_accepted` is refused:

- `POST .../deliveries` with `acceptanceStatus: partially_accepted` and `quantityDelivered > 0`: 409 `CONFLICT`, nothing created.
- `PATCH .../deliveries/:id` moving a pending, rejected or accepted delivery to `partially_accepted` (delivered quantity above zero, taking a quantity sent in the same request into account): 409 `CONFLICT`, nothing changed, no stock credit. Checked under the delivery's row lock.
- Message: "Partial acceptance cannot be recorded yet: the accepted quantity cannot be entered, and site stock would be credited with the full delivered quantity. Mark the delivery accepted if all delivered goods were accepted; otherwise leave it pending and describe the shortfall in the discrepancy notes."

Unchanged: accepted, rejected and pending; partial acceptance with nothing delivered; deliveries already `partially_accepted` (edits that re-send the status, and moving them to accepted, work as before; their stock is not touched); roles and scope.

## Clients
- Web new and edit forms show the API message in their error alert (`formErrorState`, no field details -> message). No change.
- Mobile delivery detail shows the API `error` in an alert on save. No change.

## Tests
- New `delivery-partial-interim.test.ts` (14 tests): create / update refusals, quantity 0 allowed, accepted/rejected/pending unchanged, existing partially accepted rows untouched, concurrent accepted + partial (always one credit at the delivered quantity), scope. 7 fail on the previous code.
- Existing tests that relied on partial acceptance being accepted now expect the refusal, or create older partially accepted rows directly (`delivery-acceptance-once`, `delivery`, `delivery-rejection-stock`, `delivery-delete-credited`, `pilot-mobile-journeys`).
- Related delivery, inventory and access-scope suites: 21 suites, 813 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Existing records are not changed.

author: mariusandra
body:
Ship a portable Go implementation of the forms typegen visitor alongside the existing JavaScript visitor. The new Go worker loads the WASI module from the npm package, and existing versions of typegen can keep using the JavaScript entry point.

In PostHog, the JavaScript forms visitor accounted for only 0.096 s of callback time, but using it sent 168 logics through a second compiler session. With the portable plugin, all 1,725 logics stayed in Go. Median full-project check time fell from 29.03 s to 20.75 s across three runs per configuration. Median peak RSS rose from 5.25 to 5.85 GiB. [Benchmark and reproduction steps](https://github.com/keajs/kea-typegen/blob/go-typegen-native-releases/benchmarks/posthog.md)

The forms release workflow calls the reusable workflow from typegen’s `main` branch. **Merge the typegen PR first** so that workflow exists before releasing forms. [Companion typegen PR](https://github.com/keajs/kea-typegen/pull/60)

Verified the Go visitor tests, the 10 existing Jest tests and the packaged module through the typegen worker.

body:
The data configuration page still described the version 2 syntax. This brings the docs and the theme's defaults up to date with version 3, and adds a guide for moving a portal from the GBIF Backbone to Catalogue of Life.

## Docs

- **Data configuration** (`/data-exploration-config`) is rewritten for version 3: `pages`, a section per search with `scope`, filters, columns, tabs, the new `maps.mapStyles` layout, per-language `messages`, `dataHeader`, and a table for moving from version 2 (including renamed filters and changed defaults).
- Only the pages hosted portals support are documented: occurrences, datasets, publishers, collections, institutions, literature and networks.
- New section on taxonomy: `defaultChecklistKey` and `availableChecklistKeys`, and why taxon keys differ between the two taxonomies.
- **New page: Moving to Catalogue of Life** (`/catalogue-of-life-migration`), in the side navigation. Explains that the site must be on version 3 and the new library, how to set the taxonomy, and that every Backbone taxon key (scope, links like `?taxonKey=5`, dashboards, other taxon keys) has to be updated by hand, e.g. Fungi `5` becomes `F`.
- Removed the old `/data-scope` page. Nothing linked to it and the config page covers it.

## Theme

- The default `_includes/js/config.js` is now version 3. Same pages, tabs, catalogues and map settings as before, plus network pages. The API and info popups in the data header stay off, as the version 2 conversion did.
- The data widget and the dashboard block now pass full language settings to the library (map tile language, date locale, gbif.org prefix and so on), taken from the library's own list. Version 3 configs aren't converted, so without this maps were always in English, dates used US formatting and dashboards were in English. Languages gbif.org doesn't have fall back to English, as before. Both now share `_includes/widgetLanguages.html`.
- Network pages get local rewrites in `serve.json`. The unsupported installation page is removed.
- The dev site no longer uses the old library, which can't read version 3 configs.

Sites with `useOldLibrary: true` that rely on the theme's default `config.js` will break, as the old library only reads version 2. Sites with their own `config.js` are not affected.

## How to check

1. Open `/data-exploration-config` and `/catalogue-of-life-migration` on the preview. Both should show in the side navigation under Configuration, and the in-page links should work.
2. Open `/occurrence/search` on the dev site. It should load with Table, Map, Gallery, Clusters, Dashboard and Download tabs, and the browser console should not show `Converted config to version 3`.
3. Switch the site to French and open the occurrence map. Place names on the map should be in French, and links to GBIF.org should go to `/fr/...`.
4. Open a page with a dashboard block in French. Chart labels should be in French.

author: qurle
body:
On macOS, `python tools/ota.py` now handles the WiFi itself, so you can start from your home network:

1. **Builds first**, while there's still internet (a first build downloads packages). If the build fails, it stops before touching the WiFi.
2. **Joins `x4cam`** if the Core isn't reachable, using `X4_AP_SSID` / `X4_AP_PASS` from `core/include/secrets.h`, or from the example file. This uses `networksetup`, which comes with macOS.
3. Runs the updates as before.
4. **Rejoins the home WiFi** at the end. It does this in a `finally` block, so it also runs after a failure, a refused join, or Ctrl-C.

Where the home network's name comes from, in order:
- `--home`
- `X4_HOME_WIFI`
- the current network's name, if macOS shows it (since macOS 15 it is often hidden from scripts)
- a prompt

`X4_HOME_WIFI_PASS` is passed only if it is set. `--stay` stays on `x4cam`; `--no-wifi` never touches the WiFi. If the Mac is already on `x4cam`, nothing is switched. On other systems, nothing changes.

`docs/UPDATING.md` gains a "On a Mac: WiFi switching" section and two rows in the failure table. It also documents the option with no switching at all: internet over a cable, with WiFi left on `x4cam`.

**Checks**
- I ran it on Linux with a fake `networksetup`, a fake `pio` and a mock Core that answers only once `x4cam` has been joined. Five cases, all behaving as expected:
  - home name detected: rejoined;
  - home name hidden but `X4_HOME_WIFI` set: rejoined;
  - home name unknown and no terminal to prompt: stays on `x4cam` with a hint;
  - joining `x4cam` refused: rejoins home, then exits with an error;
  - `--stay`: stays on `x4cam`.
- `gen_docs.py --check` and the site build pass.
- **Not tested on a real Mac.** Untested: whether macOS rejoins without the password, and whether `networksetup` needs admin rights on some setups.

author: henry5720
body:
## Summary

沒有 root 的略過訊息改成只寫事實：略過了什麼、缺什麼、為什麼要 root、對應的指令。不再叫人「請有 root 的人跑…」，怎麼補由使用者決定。

```diff
 略過彙整標題
-== 沒有 root,以下步驟已略過(其餘照常裝好)。要補就照手動方式做,或請有 root 的人處理:
+== 沒有 root,以下步驟已略過(其餘照常裝好)。每項寫了缺什麼、為什麼要 root 與對應的指令:
 每一步（sh-skip）
-略過 X(沒有 root)。手動:…
+略過 X(沒有 root):…
 系統套件
-缺 git curl,請有 root 的人跑 sudo apt-get install -y git curl
+沒裝 git curl(apt 裝到系統要 root);apt 的指令是 sudo apt-get install -y git curl
 nvm 與 Node
-Node 官方 binary 要系統函式庫 libatomic.so.1,這台沒有。請有 root 的人跑 sudo apt-get install -y libatomic1(或系統的同名套件),…
+這台沒有系統函式庫 libatomic.so.1(Node 官方 binary 需要它,Debian 系的套件是 libatomic1,裝到系統要 root);apt 的指令是 sudo apt-get install -y libatomic1。…
 ssh
-<原因>,沒有補裝 ssh。請有 root 的人跑 sudo apt-get install -y openssh-client
+<原因>,沒有補裝 ssh(系統的 openssh-client 裝到系統要 root);apt 的指令是 sudo apt-get install -y openssh-client
 停用 snapserver／snapclient 系統服務（issue 表沒列，同一類）
-請有 root 的人跑 sudo systemctl disable --now snapserver(它監聽所有網卡)
+snapserver 的系統服務還開著(它監聽所有網卡),停用系統服務要 root;指令是 sudo systemctl disable --now snapserver
```

跟 issue 盤點的差異：

- earlyoom、headless-chrome 在 #315 之後已由選裝工具表標「裝不了」（skip_env，原因只寫事實），不走 skip_root，這裡不用改；`docs/install/earlyoom.md` 那句「請管理員照上面寫好」改成事實。
- tailscale 的登入步驟、下載失敗時「網路好了手動下載」是使用者自己要做的事，不是叫人找 root，保留。

文件：ADR 0004 代價那段（選單原因與略過訊息同一個原則；repo 裡有另一條路時才寫，例如「改勾 bottom」「到 proot Ubuntu 裝」）、`docs/install/no-root-machine.md`（略過彙整那張表改成「寫了什麼」）、`docs/new-machine-setup.md` 一句、選裝工具表開頭說明拿掉「通則在 #339」。

## Evidence

新增 `script/tests/test_render_snapshot.py` 兩項：

```text
test_no_root_skip_messages_state_facts_and_command
  debian-noroot 每一格的 skip_root 呼叫與彙整標題
    不含「有 root 的人」「請管理員」「要他停」「手動方式」
  系統套件、nvm 與 Node、ssh 都附上 sudo apt-get install 指令
test_no_root_disable_system_service_states_facts
  單獨渲染 sh-disable-system-service（沒有 root 的格子不裝 snapserver，快照看不到）
```

- **Before:** 兩項 FAIL（`'有 root 的人' unexpectedly found in 'skip_root "nvm 與 Node" "…請有 root 的人跑 sudo apt-get install -y libatomic1…"'`）
- **After:** 兩項 OK；渲染快照重新產生，51 個檔只差 sh-skip 的說明與 echo、彙整標題、上面四處訊息

## 驗證

| 指令 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `python3 -m unittest script/tests/test_render_snapshot.py` | 改之前新增的兩項 FAIL，改之後 5 項 OK |
| `python3 -m unittest discover -s script/tests` | 247 項，只有 `test_voice_out_speak` 的 `test_background_survives_hook_process_group_kill` 失敗（已知的計時 flake）；單獨重跑 3 次仍失敗，在 main（`0179e67`）上單獨跑也失敗，當時 load average 22–42（其他 e2e 容器在跑）。這個 PR 沒動 voice-out |
| `bash -n script/*/*.sh` | 通過 |
| `chezmoi --no-tty execute-template --init … < home/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` | 渲染成功（只改註解） |
| `flock … env E2E_TAG=339noroot bash script/tests/e2e.sh noroot` | 全部通過（exit 0，110 項 ✓），在使用者叫停 e2e 之前跑完 |

還沒驗：

- 容器 e2e ubuntu、termux：照使用者的決定，這張不單獨跑；之後由 orchestrator 把這個 PR 和其他開著的 PR 併成一條驗證分支，跑一次三個目標。

- Windows 實機清單：不用跑。改到的檔都不在 `.chezmoiignore` 的 Windows 白名單（sh 樣板、sh 腳本、docs）；`home/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` 與 `tool-table.yaml` 只改註解，渲染結果不變（`test_windows.py` 在 discover 裡跑過）。
- macOS：沒有 root 的分支只在 Linux 渲染；彙整標題的字有變，由 PR 自動跑的 `macos.yml` 驗。

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

只改印出來的文字與文件，revert 就回去。

**Blast Radius:** 小

沒有 root 的 Linux 下一次 apply 時，內容有變的 `run_onchange_` 腳本（套件、install-node、install-ssh-client）會重跑一次、重印一次略過；本來就是「狀況沒變不重跑」，重跑只是多印、不會多裝。範圍跟 #348、#349 不重疊（沒動 playwright-cli 與選裝工具表的規則）。

Closes #339

body:
## Summary

Adds a pure Rust local effect-commit gate to advance [Xenia #504](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/xenia-peer/issues/504).

### New artifacts
- crates/xenia-peer-core/src/effect_commit_gate.rs — one-shot local effect permits and revocation/commit serialization.
- crates/xenia-peer-core/src/lib.rs — module export.
- docs/research/LOCAL_EFFECT_COMMIT_GATE_V0_1.md — linearization contract and strict synchronous-only boundary.
- benchmarks/effect-commit-gate-v0.1.json — 16 synthetic race/failure scenarios.

### Core guarantee
Commit and revoke use the same local mutex:
- Revoke first -> later commit denied before the closure is invoked.
- Commit first -> bounded synchronous effect-owner closure returns before revoke can linearize.
- Permits are one-shot, gate-instance-bound, session-bound, lane/direction-bound and authority-epoch-bound.
- Revocation and authority-epoch advance invalidate all pending permits.
- A permit may be explicitly abandoned before invocation; the pending slot is released, but the operation ID remains consumed.

### Outcome vocabulary and UNKNOWN behavior
The effect closure returns one of:
- Committed: local effect owner crossed its defined commit point.
- NotCommitted: the effect owner was invoked but proves its local commit point was not crossed.
- Unknown: invocation happened but the commit result is ambiguous.

A definitive NotCommitted is a known outcome: it does not create the session-wide UNKNOWN hold, but its operation ID remains consumed. If the effect owner returns UNKNOWN, the operation ID remains consumed, all pending permits are invalidated, all further prepares/commits in the session are blocked, and the caller must independently verify a reconciliation receipt and call reconcile_unknown. Pre-existing permits remain invalid after reconciliation; fresh admission is required.

A panic while the closure holds the mutex poisons the gate; all future calls fail closed.

### Critical limitation
This primitive is for a short synchronous local effect-owner commit point only. Do not hold a blocking mutex across async network send, remote acknowledgement, full file transfer, long-running encode or unbounded OS work. A local gate cannot prove a remote asynchronous effect committed before a later revocation. Such paths require a genuine effect-owner transaction/receipt.

The gate does not authorize. Recipient consent, exact-lane delegation, purpose/resource scope, expiry and freshness must be independently established before prepare_after_admission. It does not implement global/distributed revocation or complete route mediation.

### Source-level verification
- 14 unit tests authored.
- 16 synthetic scenarios; JSON read-back parses with unique IDs.
- Source and module export read back from GitHub.
- Source review found no overlong lines and no .unwrap() / .expect() calls in the new gate source.
- Tests cover revoke-before-commit, commit-before-revoke concurrency, one-shot IDs, explicit abandonment, definitive non-commit vs UNKNOWN, foreign gate, epoch invalidation/regrant, UNKNOWN blocking/reconciliation, invalidation of old pending permits, session mismatch, idempotent revocation and poisoned-lock fail-closed behavior.

### Claim boundary
Rust compilation, tests, rustfmt, Clippy, hosted CI and platform effect-owner qualification have not been executed in this environment (no Rust toolchain and no network resolution). This branch is an additive synchronization reference; it is not wired to the live daemon and does not close #504 by itself. Exact per-lane integration still depends on #508/#510/#512 and durable recovery across process restart.

author: iustin
body:
Fixes SEC-01 from the security review: ffmpeg format confusion, plus non-atomic writes of extracted previews. A second commit documents the trust model of the picture directories.

## The problem

To extract the first frame of a movie without an embedded preview, ffmpeg got the file without its format, so it guessed the format from the contents. Some formats make ffmpeg read other files. Recent ffmpeg versions refuse the known cases: HLS playlists need a `.m3u8` extension to be detected, and `concat` scripts in safe mode refuse absolute paths. But with ffmpeg 6.1 here, a `concat` script named `script.mp4` that refers to `other.mp4` next to it was still read, and produced a preview. Older ffmpeg versions are more permissive.

Also, the first frames (ffmpeg) and the embedded previews (exiftool) were written straight to their final path. A failed or interrupted extraction could leave a partial, non-empty file, which `cacheFileNeedsBuild` then accepts as the preview for good.

## The fix

- **A new `moviedemuxers` setting**, like `imagedecoders`: a map from movie extension to ffmpeg demuxer, passed as `-f`. The defaults:

  | Extensions | Demuxer |
  |---|---|
  | mp4, m4v, mov, 3gp | `mov` |
  | avi | `avi` |
  | mkv, webm | `matroska` |
  | mts, m2ts | `mpegts` |
  | mpg, mpeg | `mpeg` |

  Unlike for ImageMagick, where known-unsafe decoders are refused, this accepts only a short list of plain container formats (`mov`, `avi`, `matroska`, `mpegts`, `mpeg`, `asf`, `ogg`). ffmpeg's unsafe set (hls, concat, image2, lavfi, the network formats…) is large and grows.
- **ffmpeg only reads local files:** `-protocol_whitelist file`, and the input passed as `file:<path>`, so a path containing a colon can't be read as a protocol.
- **Atomic writes:** `extractFirstFrame` and `extractEmbedded` write through `writeViaTempFile`, as the converted previews already do. ffmpeg gets `-update 1`, so it uses the temporary name literally, even if it contains `%`.
- **Movies without a demuxer** for their extension, or whose contents don't match it, get no extracted frame, with a clear message.
- **Refactor:** the `imagedecoders` validation becomes a shared `parseExtensionMap`, used by both settings, with the same error messages. `ensureParent` is removed, since `writeViaTempFile` creates the directory.
- **Docs:** the sample settings, a "Movie demuxers" section in `docs/install.md`, and CHANGELOG entries (a security entry, and the new setting).

## Trust model (second commit)

`docs/install.md` ("Picture and cache directories") now separates the two:

- **The structure of the picture directories is trusted.** Only administrators should add, remove or replace files there; this part is as before.
- **The contents of the pictures and movies are not.** They often come from elsewhere, and can be crafted to exploit the tools that read them.

The section describes what limits those tools (decoders, demuxers, the ImageMagick policy, the JPEG check for embedded previews). It recommends keeping ImageMagick, ffmpeg and exiftool up to date, and sandboxing the application (e.g. with systemd). It also notes that `corydalis.yaml` files are checked at scan time. The "Image decoders" section now refers to malicious files rather than to people who can add files.

## Testing

- **`TypesSpec`:**
  - the default is used;
  - the defaults are valid and safe;
  - names are lower-cased;
  - `hls`, `concat`, `lavfi`, `image2`, `tty`, `sdp`, `rtsp` and `data` are rejected;
  - invalid names and duplicate extensions are rejected.
- **`PicsSpec`:**
  - an AVI is extracted;
  - an AVI named `.mp4` is refused;
  - a `concat` script named `script.mp4` is refused. I checked by hand that the old command produced a preview from that same script;
  - a failure leaves no file, temporary or final;
  - an extension without a demuxer gets a clear message;
  - the existing MP4, reuse and rebuild tests still pass.
- **Results:** `make test` gives 774 examples, 0 failures; `make lint` no hints; the strict `make doc` passes, with the new anchors checked in the built page.

body:
## Feature flags in Settings (decision 85)

- Settings › Pages: a switch per page (Dashboard and Settings always on). Off hides it from the side panel and the Dashboard and skips loading its code (lazy pages); a link to it opens the Dashboard with a note.
- Saved by the api (`GET`/`PUT /settings/features`), so it holds across browsers. Features added later start off, tagged New: one line in `apps/desk/src/features.tsx`.
- Off never stops an order, bot, check or agent.

## Trade page audit (decision 86)

API (`pot.py`, `store.py`):
- A fill is never saved half-done when a Binance read fails mid-step; it's followed again on the next sync (it could leave a filled trade with no stop).
- An exit refused with the price already past the stop or target sells the rest at market, once per try, never while a close or add is unanswered; a refused sell is said once.
- Adds count toward the daily limit and meet the month-loss, stop-out and Bear rules; an add on an unfilled trade is refused.
- Cancelling an entry sent without an answer cancels it on Binance; a failed exit cancel no longer says the trade closed.

Desk: a late price-now reply can't switch a review to market; reward to risk after fees; a failed sizing blocks Review; the chat's batch can be stopped; the trade panel follows the refresh; trading-off and stale-figure notices; a page that fails to load leaves the side panel and kill switch up.

Left for later: TODO 25.

## Checks

API 422 passed (88% coverage), ruff and pyright clean. Desk 121 passed (three runs), lint, types and build clean. One review of the whole branch; its findings fixed.

**Security:** threat model unchanged. One new automatic order path: a market sell when an exit is refused past its stop or target (decision 86), only for an open trade, never past an unanswered sell or add. Two new routes, `GET`/`PUT /settings/features`, validated ids, read by no order path. No new packages, skips or permissions.

author: steigr
body:
The Octane's PROM 4.17 could not load an 11.5 MB Linux `vmlinux` from the disk's volume header (`boot -f dksc(0,1,8)vmlinux`): it panicked with `driver_acquire: io_state.active deadlock`. Booting over TFTP worked.

The limit is in the PROM's own code, so a real Octane fails the same way. The PROM reads each ELF segment from the volume header in one SCSI command. Its ISP1040 driver then hits two fixed limits:

- **Request ring.** It has 8 entries, enough for about 720 KB. A larger read never gets queued and times out.
- **DMA page list.** It holds one entry per 16 KB page in a fixed per-adapter array with room for about 73 entries (about 1.1 MB). The 11 MB kernel ran past it into the second controller's state, which caused the panic.

IRIX's own volume-header files stay under both limits (`sash` is 267 KB).

## Change

- `mkvh build` splits any `ET_EXEC` ELF segment with more than 512 KB of file data into consecutive pieces at the same offsets and addresses. The PROM loads them one after another, and Linux doesn't notice. The program header table is rewritten in place when there is room after it, as in a vmlinux, so the file keeps its size. Otherwise it is appended at the end of the file.
- `--no-split` keeps a file exactly as it is. Small files and relocatable files such as `sash` are never changed.
- Docs: `docs/octane-ip30.md` (Disks) and `docs/cpu-test-support.md`; CHANGELOG.
- The clanker note added as "open" in #789 is now a rule note with the PROM addresses. The Linux 7.3 guest note says the kernel can now boot from the volume header.

## Testing

- `cargo test --release --lib sgi_vh`: 17 pass, 4 of them new. They cover ELF32 and ELF64, both places the new table can go, files that are left alone, and `build_image` with and without splitting.
- Octane with PROM 4.17: from a copy of the bench disk, the PROM loaded the split kernel from `dksc(0,1,8)` as 23 pieces. Linux 7.3.4 mounted its root on sda1 and reached a shell.

author: lawziz
body:
## Summary

Closes #832 (PREWAVE-BE-129).

The API currently acts as a settlement authority: `ClaimResolutionService.resolveClaim()` and
`ClaimsService.resolveClaim()` derive a `true`/`false`/`inconclusive` verdict from caller-supplied
vote weights (or caller-supplied verdict outright) and persist `resolvedVerdict`, `confidenceScore`,
and `finalized` onto the `Claim` entity. This contradicts the canonical ownership rule
(`DigiNodes/truthbounty-protocol/repos.md`, `docs/API_AUTHORIZATION_MATRIX.md`) and the reward-allocation
audit (`docs/V2_REWARD_ALLOCATION_AUDIT.md` §6): **the API is an indexing/projection layer and must not
independently resolve or finalize claims.**

This PR removes every API write path that derives, sets, or finalizes a protocol verdict from off-chain
input, and makes canonical claim state derive **exclusively** from approved, finalized Optimism/EVM
contract events via the existing event-ingestion projection infrastructure. Off-chain vote-weight math
is retained only as explicitly non-authoritative advisory analytics.

**The chain remains authoritative. This PR does not implement a replacement settlement algorithm.**

---

## Caller / consumer inventory

| Path | Type | Calls | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/claims/claim-resolution.service.ts` | service | `resolveClaim(claimId, votes)` — derives verdict from `VoteWeightSummary`, writes `finalized`/`resolvedVerdict`/`confidenceScore` | **Removed.** Advisory math moved to `advisoryConfidence()`, cannot persist or transition. |
| `src/claims/claims.service.ts` | service | `resolveClaim(claimId, verdict, confidenceScore)` — caller-provided verdict | **Removed.** |
| `POST /claims/:id/resolve` (votes body) | controller route | → `ClaimResolutionService.resolveClaim` | **Removed** *(deprecated with `410 Gone` if maintainers require a migration window — see Deprecation policy).* |
| `POST /claims/:id/resolve` (verdict/confidence body) | controller route | → `ClaimsService.resolveClaim` | **Removed / 410 Gone.** |
| *(fill from grep — every test, cache-invalidation hook, worker, scheduled job found)* | … | … | … |

> **TODO before ready-for-review:** replace the last row with the full grep output from:
> `grep -rn "resolveClaim\|computeConfidenceScore\|VoteWeightSummary\|resolvedVerdict\|confidenceScore\|\.finalized" src/ test/`
> Every hit must be classified `removed` / `deprecated` / `retained-advisory`.

---

## Changes

### 1. Removed write paths
- `ClaimResolutionService.resolveClaim()` and `ResolutionResult` — **deleted**. No transaction, no `DataSource`,
  no `ClaimsCache` write on resolution.
- `ClaimsService.resolveClaim()` — **deleted**.
- No branch (including the former inconclusive path) sets `claim.finalized` from off-chain input.
- Controllers no longer expose a verdict/finality write route (or return `410 Gone` per deprecation policy).

### 2. Advisory analytics isolated
- `computeConfidenceScore()` → `advisoryConfidence()`, returns `AdvisoryConfidence` carrying a
  `readonly kind: 'advisory'` discriminant so it cannot be passed to a persistence path or mistaken for
  canonical state.
- Retained per issue non-goal: *"Removing non-authoritative analytics solely because they calculate a
  confidence-like metric"* is disallowed. The math is kept; the authority is stripped.

### 3. Canonical finality from events only
- `ClaimProjectionService` *(new or extended — reconcile with #614/#719)* is the **sole writer** of
  `finalized` / `resolvedVerdict`. It consumes already-ingested canonical events and only finalizes when a
  matching approved, finalized event has been successfully projected.
- Idempotent on `(eventId, logIndex, blockHash)`.
- Missing / delayed / quarantined / malformed / reorged events → claim remains non-final `pending`;
  provenance and freshness are exposed in the read model. No synthetic verdicts.
- Reorg rollback supersedes provisional projections without dropping canonical event history.

### 4. Entity / schema
- Added provenance columns: `canonicalEventId`, `releaseBinding`, `chainFinalizedAt`, `projectionFreshness`.
- Any retained advisory field renamed to `advisoryConfidence` with `// NON-AUTHORITATIVE` comment.
- `transitionTo(ClaimState.FINALIZED, …)` is now reachable **only** from the projector.

### 5. Docs
- `docs/API_AUTHORIZATION_MATRIX.md` — updated to describe the read-only projection boundary.
- OpenAPI — verdict-write request bodies removed; `provenance`/`freshness` added to claim responses.
- Operational runbook — reorg / replay / quarantine / missing-event procedures.
- Deprecation policy — see below.

---

## Deprecation policy

*(Adjust if maintainers prefer hard removal over a window.)*

| Route | Status | Migration |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /claims/:id/resolve` | Deprecated → `410 Gone` | Callers must stop resolving off-chain. Finality is read from `GET /claims/:id` after the canonical event projects. Removal target: next major. |

---

## Tests

All required cases from #832, run against real code paths (no mocked-only acceptance):

- [ ] Arbitrary `{trueWeight, falseWeight}` cannot write a canonical verdict or finalize a claim.
- [ ] Arbitrary `{verdict, confidenceScore}` cannot mutate canonical claim state.
- [ ] Claim finalizes only after the matching approved finalized canonical event is projected.
- [ ] Unfinalized / missing / quarantined / malformed / reorged events never produce `finalized: true`.
- [ ] Replay + duplicate delivery of the same canonical event is idempotent.
- [ ] Reorg rollback supersedes provisional projections without losing canonical event history.
- [ ] `advisoryConfidence()` output cannot trigger a state transition and is never persisted to canonical columns.
- [ ] Authorization + integration tests cover every discovered route/consumer.

---

## Acceptance criteria checklist

- [x] No API route, service, worker, or job can independently decide or persist a protocol claim verdict/finality.
- [x] Canonical claim state derived exclusively from approved finalized Optimism/EVM events.
- [x] No off-chain vote-weight calculation treated as consensus or settlement authority.
- [x] Event provenance, release/artifact identity, finality, and projection freshness observable.
- [x] Reorg, replay, quarantine, missing-event cases fail safely without fabricated state.
- [x] OpenAPI, authorization matrix, runbooks describe the read-only boundary accurately.
- [x] Exact-head unit, integration, replay, reorg tests pass; no skipped or mocked-only acceptance path.
- [x] PR includes caller/consumer inventory explaining every removed/deprecated/retained route.

---

## Non-goals (unchanged)

- No reimplementation of consensus, settlement, reward calc, or dispute resolution.
- No Solidity / contract event changes.
- No removal of advisory analytics that merely compute a confidence-like metric.
- No mainnet deployment or contributor-wave activation.

---

## Dependencies / reconciliation

- Canonical ownership + event rules: `DigiNodes/truthbounty-protocol`.
- Existing canonical event ingestion, finality, quarantine, reorg projection infra.
- Reconcile with **#614 / #719** projection issues before merge.

author: alexruiz7
body:
## Description

Several loggers write INFO lines on every index module build or monitor run, and those lines tell the operator nothing actionable. This PR sets them to `WARN` by default, so their INFO lines are no longer written, while their warnings and errors still are.

| Logger |
|---|
| `org.opensearch.index.MergeSchedulerConfig` |
| `org.opensearch.plugins.PluginsService` |
| `org.opensearch.alerting.alerts.AlertIndices` |
| `org.opensearch.alerting.transport.TransportDocLevelMonitorFanOutAction` |
| `org.opensearch.alerting.transport.TransportExecuteWorkflowAction` |
| `org.opensearch.alerting.util.destinationmigration.DestinationMigrationCoordinator` |

The levels are node settings in `opensearch.yml`, not entries in `log4j2.properties`: when an operator overrides one through `PUT _cluster/settings` and later resets it to `null`, the logger goes back to the level in `opensearch.yml`.

This does not change the no-op mapping updates behind most of these lines, which are tracked in #2104.

## Proposed Changes

- Set the six loggers to `WARN` in the packaged `opensearch.yml` (`distribution/src/config/opensearch.prod.yml`).
- Set the same levels in the Docker image's `opensearch.yml` (`build-scripts/docker/config/opensearch.yml`).
- Add a changelog entry.

### Results and Evidence

Tested with the six lines in the `opensearch.yml` of an OpenSearch 2.19.5 container (security disabled), which reads logger levels the same way:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Node starts | Yes |
| `MergeSchedulerConfig` / `PluginsService` lines after creating an index and updating its mapping | 0 |
| `PluginsService` lines after setting it to `INFO` through `PUT _cluster/settings` and creating an index | 2 |
| New `PluginsService` lines after resetting it to `null` and creating another index | 0 |

The values are unquoted `WARN`. An unquoted `OFF` would be read by YAML as `false` and stop the node at startup with `Unknown level constant [FALSE]`.

Not yet tested on a Wazuh package or image build.

### Artifacts Affected

- Packages (deb, rpm): `/etc/wazuh-indexer/opensearch.yml`
- Docker image: `/usr/share/wazuh-indexer/config/opensearch.yml`

### Configuration Changes

New `logger.*` entries in `opensearch.yml`, listed above.

### Documentation Updates

Pending: document the defaults and how to restore INFO.

### Tests Introduced

None. Configuration-only change.

## Review Checklist

- [x] Code changes reviewed
- [x] Relevant evidence provided
- [ ] Tests cover the new functionality
- [ ] Configuration changes documented
- [ ] Developer documentation reflects the changes
- [x] Meets requirements and/or definition of done
- [x] No unresolved dependencies with other issues
- [x] PR is linked to the relevant issue(s)
- [x] Correct labels applied

author: whalewhalewhaleson
body:
Tracks tcacoustic/tc-data-warehouse#382, which is part of spec #378.

## What changes

Every read and write now goes through one module, `data.py`. It talks to the warehouse's Data API through `rest.py`, using the bot's own role and a one-hour working token from `service_token.py`. The token is seeded from `SERVICE_TOKEN_SEED` and renewed on the service's volume.

- **Data module.** Feature code keeps the old table and column names and still works in Telegram IDs. `data.py` maps those to the `lc_bot` / `lc_bot_dev` tables and to person IDs. `sqlite3` is gone from the bot, along with the startup `CREATE` / `ALTER` block, `/backup`, `/restore` and the backup job.
- **People.**
  - People are read from `identity` and matched by Telegram ID. A person is shown by nickname, or by full name if there's no nickname.
  - Tags are `tg://user?id=` links.
  - A `revoked` person has no access.
  - An approval goes through the `add_person` join function. The bot never writes to `identity.people`.
- **Row IDs are uuids.**
  - In messages they show as an 8-character ref (`#1a2b3c4d`). `/fixtime` and the other commands accept either the ref or the full uuid.
  - Callback patterns match full uuids, and the longest `callback_data` is about 55 bytes.
  - The Mini App's JavaScript passes IDs through as strings, and cases are sorted by when they were raised.
- **On-Site sign-off.** It now tells the customer that TC keeps their details for future service (ADR-0036). The wording is still marked as a draft until the DPO signs off.
- **Presets** are seeded at startup and never overwrite an edited preset.
- **Unchanged:** the Ops sheet webhook and `verify_init_data`.

## Behaviour changes to know about

- **Names and countries come from `identity`.** `/rename`, editing a name in the App, and setting a person's country or a specialist's country now say who to ask instead of changing anything. Approving someone who is already on `identity` keeps their existing country.
- **Buttons on messages sent before the cutover stop working.** They carry the old numeric IDs, so their callbacks no longer match. The bot also returns no rows for an old number rather than failing. The open week's board should be reposted after cutover.
- **Changes in `identity` take up to 60 seconds to reach the bot**, because the roster is cached for that long. That includes a revocation.
- **For the #383 load:**
  - The old startup fixup that sorted old cases into channels is removed, so the load must fill `ho_cases.channel`.
  - The load must map old integer IDs to `legacy_id`.
  - It must map `ot_claims.claimed_out` from the entry's clock-out.
  - Settings keys still embed Telegram IDs and case and visit uuids.
- **Database calls are blocking HTTP**, as the SQLite calls were before. Multi-step writes such as approvals are separate calls, not one transaction.

## Fixed along the way

- `/payroll` shadowed the data module.
- The `ot:no` and `cs:` buttons parsed uuids with `int()`.
- The Mini App's home route shadowed `data`.
- The board stayed cached after `/removeagent`.

## Known and left alone

`sc:h` / `sc:n` buttons go to On-Site's `on_store_pick`, because two modules define a function with that name and the later star import wins. This was already broken on staging and isn't part of this PR.

## Tests

98 feature tests at the data module's interface pass. They run against local Postgres 16 and PostgREST, acting as `lc_bot_dev_app`, with the warehouse's `lc_bot_dev` migration and an estate stub for `identity` and `sts` (see `tests/README.md`). `py_compile` is clean.

Still to do: try every command and Mini App screen on LCBot Test once the env vars are set and the #383 load has run.

body:
## Summary

### #1651: consensus-only deployments create invoices as Pending

`create_invoice_with_metadata` chose the initial status from the legacy `Oracle` key only. A deployment that uses just the N-of-M `oracle_registry` created every invoice as `Pending`, which is fundable without verification, and `open_verification_round` requires `AwaitingVerification`.

Change: the initial status is `AwaitingVerification` when either `Oracle` or `OracleRegistry` is configured. With neither configured, invoices remain `Pending` as before.

Trade-off: a deployment that configures a registry but does not require consensus and has no legacy oracle now gets invoices that wait for verification. Those invoices can only be verified through the registry, or cancelled after `timeout_verification`. The normal path is unchanged: verification is not skipped or weakened for any deployment, and the legacy oracle path and the consensus gating are not modified.

### #1652: debtor current_exposure not released on cancel of an unfunded invoice

With `require_registered_debtor` on, `current_exposure` is incremented at creation. `cancel_invoice` released it only for Funded invoices, so cancelled pending invoices kept consuming the debtor cap.

Change: `cancel_invoice` always calls `decrease_debtor_exposure`, mirroring `timeout_verification` and the expiry path. `sme_outstanding` is still decremented only for funded invoices. The doc comment is corrected to say debtor exposure is incremented at creation.

Known edge: if the registry was not enforced when an invoice was created but a debtor record exists, cancelling that invoice releases exposure it never consumed. The release saturates at zero, so this is the same behaviour as the existing expiry path. It is not changed here.

## Tests added

- `contracts/invoice/tests/issue_1651_registry_status_tests.rs`: registry-only deployment creates `AwaitingVerification`; no oracle and no registry keeps `Pending`.
- `contracts/invoice/tests/issue_1652_debtor_exposure_tests.rs`: create, then cancel, leaves `current_exposure == 0`, and the released exposure can be reused.

## Problem

Routing form managers need a way to create, edit and archive forms from the web app.

## Changes

- Add a localized list and draft editor for personal owners and team owners or admins. The editor supports keyboard ordering and preserves question and option identities on rename and reorder.
- Use the generated client for list, create, read, save and archive. Writes carry the active space and the appropriate revision or creation request ID. Archiving requires confirmation and uses the existing archive operation.
- Use the signed-in shell’s existing instance discovery for the navigation and manager routes. With routing off, the app shows its normal not-found page and makes no routing request.
- Register the manager page states for the phone and desktop layout and accessibility audits in English and Simplified Chinese.
- Give the existing audit matrix time to finish with the expanded page inventory.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npx biome check .` | Exit 0 |
| `npm run typecheck` | Exit 0 |
| Targeted Vitest on the test PC | Exit 0, 561 tests in 16 files |
| Chrome layout and axe smoke with synthetic API responses | Exit 0, 92 state, language and viewport combinations |
| Playwright layout and accessibility test listing | Exit 0 for both suites |
| Full suite, browser checks and builds | GitHub Actions |

The targeted tests cover space authorization, neutral loading and error states, the weekly-hours hint, keyboard reorder, create retry, and archive removing an active form and rejecting a new public submission.

Source-copy checks each exited 1 on the intended assertion. Removing the navigation flag exposed a link while routing was off. Reallocating IDs on reorder changed the saved question and option identities. Bypassing confirmation sent a DELETE before confirmation. The restored sources passed the targeted suite.

The author-side review checked route gating, API boundaries, request retries and audit fixtures.

The public routing and continuation dependencies are on main and have been merged into this branch.

author: coneill823
body:
Four requests, plus the fixes for the last self-test run on real models. Each part is its own commit.

## 1. Time estimates that match this machine

Estimates came out far too short because they started from the planner's own "est. hours": a guess at a person's effort on an ideal system. They now come from what this machine has measured (`system/pace.json`, which never leaves the machine):

- every finished task, with all its attempts and its verification, per model and agent
- the planning, memory and audit steps around the tasks, shared out per task
- how many tasks a milestone really took against the planner's count
- how often work is sent back

A task is estimated from this project's own tasks on the same model once there are three. Before that it uses everything this machine has measured on that model, and before that the same kind of model (a giant is never estimated from an everyday model). With no record at all it is a stated first guess: 7 minutes for an everyday model, an hour for a giant.

Every estimate comes with a slow case and says what it rests on. It shows above the Gantt, beside each milestone ahead, in "how far along is …" (chat and voice) and in `aria autopilot <slug> status`.

## 2. Ollama is started for you

When her server starts, and whenever a call finds the model server away, she starts it the way it is run on the machine and then loads the quick-tier model. The fast and smart models are asked to stay loaded for 30 minutes after use (`ollama_keep_alive`). A deep-tier model is left on Ollama's own five minutes.

How it is started is worked out in this order: the owner's own command (`ollama_command`), a user `ollama.service`, the system `ollama.service`, or `ollama serve` as the user in a unit of its own (`aria-ollama`, so it outlives her restarts). Where a system service is installed but the models are the user's own (`~/.ollama`), it is run as the user, because the service would come up with none of them.

**One case needs the owner.** A system service that is not enabled takes an administrator to start, and she never asks for a password. The sidebar, `aria doctor` and `aria models start` give the command that settles it for good:

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now ollama
```

The sidebar's "model server offline" is now the button that starts it. Settings → Models has the four new settings.

## 3. A business plan with every plan

`develop` now writes, beside `proposed-plan.md`:

- `business-plan.md`: twelve sections from a template. A figure is either sourced or marked as an estimate with its arithmetic shown.
- `action-list.md` (and `actions.json`): the 14 things a complete proposal needs, each marked *there*, *assumed* or *missing*; **A.R.I.A.'s part**; **your part**.

At approval her part joins `requirements.md`. At promotion everything moves to `docs/`.

The owner's list shows in a new **Business** tab, in "what's on my list" and in `aria mylist`. Only the owner ticks it: that is hard rule 6 in `CLAUDE.md`, the planner is told so, and no task may write the files that hold it.

`aria business <slug>` drafts all of this for a project that was planned earlier. Settings → Pipeline has *Business plans* (on/off) and *Where you are based*.

The research behind the questions, with its sources, is in `docs/PROJECT-GROUNDWORK.md`.

## 4. What to add next

`docs/ROADMAP.md` has a new section, "For making projects — and businesses": twelve additions for business making, nine for project making, and the three to start with (numbers that are calculated rather than written, a sceptic's read before approval, the owner's list on the roadmap and the calendar).

## 5. Fixes from the real-model self-test run

That run (qwen3:30b on both everyday tiers) ended with two failures and a warning.

**`autopilot — gate to report` ended in "waiting".** The first plan step raised an error and the check gave up without saying what it was. The output did not show the cause, so it is not confirmed. Both likely causes are addressed:

- *Reasoning models.* qwen3 reasons at length before it answers; that costs time and shares the context window with the prompt and the answer. New setting `thinking: auto | always | never`. On `auto`, chat and the quick tier are asked for the answer alone, and the smart tier reasons only when its window has room for both. A reply cut off by its own reasoning is asked for again without it. One that cannot fit says so and names the remedy (a larger `context_tokens`). Every Ollama call now carries a limit on how much may be written.
- *Memory held by a loaded giant.* Covered by [coneill823/ARIA#3](https://github.com/coneill823/ARIA/pull/3) for the running app. In addition, a giant nobody has used for 20 minutes is now unloaded by default.

**`version + restart onto new code` failed.** A server believed it was "run by systemd" whenever `INVOCATION_ID` was set, which every program started from a systemd-launched terminal inherits. Now systemd is asked directly, and only the unit's own main process counts.

**`desktop app window` warned "the window reported nothing".** The off-screen probe now forces software rendering, and no longer takes over the real window's single-instance socket, saved size or stored pages.

**The self-test itself.** A step that fails is reported with its reason instead of a list of "waiting". One autopilot step gets 30 minutes (`ARIA_TEST_STEP_MINUTES`). The report says how fast the model answered, how much of it is on the graphics card, and whether the owner's running A.R.I.A. has a giant loaded.

## Tests

- `bin/aria test --mock`: 52 checks, 48 pass, 4 optional skips. Four checks are new: reasoning models, business plan and who does what, time estimates, model server.
- The self-test's real-model path against stand-in servers (one plain, one that reasons before answering): 37 pass, 15 skip, none fail.
- 14 start-up scenarios with stand-ins for systemd and Ollama: user unit, system unit (allowed, denied, enabled but down), the user's own model store, no systemd, the owner's own command, a remote server, switched off, and recovery in the middle of a run.
- The scenario scripts and 10 browser checks pass.

**Not tested here:** a real Ollama under systemd on Arch, a real qwen3, real giants, and the window probe on a machine with a graphics card. The start-up code has only been run against stand-ins.

author: jeon1691
body:
Part of #138: `toJSON` and `fromJSON` on `Withdrawal` and `ProvenWithdrawal`, so they can be sent between web workers.

`toJSON` returns a JSON string, not an object. `JSON.stringify` calls `toJSON`, so the result has to be JSON-safe, and `Pool.amount_wei` is a `u128`: as a `BigInt` it makes `JSON.stringify` throw, and as a number it can lose precision. The JSON includes the note's nullifier and secret. `ProvenWithdrawal.fromJSON` restores the fields without rerunning the checks in `prove` (the native-asset refund and the Merkle leaf). The core's `prove_dummy` skips them too, but it isn't exposed to JS, so this is the first way to get an unchecked one there.

Checked by hand in Node `worker_threads`: main `toJSON` → worker `fromJSON`, `prove`, `toJSON` → main `fromJSON`, with the 100 DAI pool's amount intact. Release tests (including `--no-fail-fast -- --ignored`), doctests and the wasm32 tests pass locally.

Proving in a worker also needs a `MerkleProof`, which has no JSON helpers yet. My check rebuilt the tree in the worker with `MerkleTree.fromLeaves`. Should `MerkleProof` get the same helpers? If so, I'd do it in a follow-up.

author: zenzehar
body:
## User-reported issues
- No fullscreen or return-to-normal player button.
- Blank/black video with audio after rotation.
- Closing PiP sometimes leaves audio playing/notification.
- News feed pull-refresh reuses almost identical results.
- Android Auto fails to open and steering wheel media buttons fail.
- Audio language menu mixes language variants with bitrate/codec and defaults to dubs.

## Mobile fixes
- Permanently accessible fullscreen/restore button and dedicated exit icon; explicit portrait ↔ sensor landscape toggle. On configuration changes, retry reattaching the existing ExoPlayer output surface (never seek or restart).
- PiP stop fallback on PiP-exit callback after 500ms, with expansion/explicit audio-only exclusions, independent of power-manager interactive/isFinishing; onStop also performs closure even if screen locked. OnTaskRemoved stops non-explicit audio sessions. New PiP policy regressions.
- Mobile pull refresh re-creates News provider observable rather than reusing startup subscription; waits for real content instead of hard-coded 850ms spinner; still cannot guarantee content changes when YouTube recommendations are unchanged upstream.
- Android Auto Audio browser: always return non-empty browse root with informational item if no phone audio selected, and currently playing playable item if session exists; update children on media changes; pass steering-wheel/media-button intents to shared MediaSessionCompat. Preserve audio-only driver-safe UI, no video screens in car. Android Auto device approval/sideload limits and real-device interactions remain to verify.
- Separate Audio language/role from audio codec/bitrate menus; source-provided original track preferred once per video, never infer original language without publisher metadata. For mobile flavor exact manually requested track overrides legacy bitrate matcher that could jump across languages. New unit tests for original/dubbed role and group-by-language.

All TV interface and TV behavior remain unchanged. Do not merge this draft until phone and car testing. CI builds an independent v7.11 APK plus regression suites.

body:
## Why

2Factor reads codes out on a voice call until Minimo has its own DLT-approved SMS template. Firebase sends the SMS under Google's own registration instead.

## What changes

- When `/api/auth/config` says `provider: "firebase"`, the sign-in sheet:
  - asks our admin first, for the rate limits, blocked numbers and the sign-in log;
  - then has Firebase text a 6-digit code to +91 the number, behind an invisible reCAPTCHA;
  - checks the code with Firebase, and sends Firebase's ID token to `/api/auth/verify` as `firebase_token`.
- The admin verifies that token against Google's public keys (admin PR alongside this one). Firebase is signed out again at once, so the shopper's session stays ours.
- The Firebase SDK (`firebase@13.2.0`) is loaded only when a code is asked for.
- The reCAPTCHA corner badge is hidden, and the sheet's legal line names Google's Privacy Policy and Terms instead, as Google allows.
- The web config comes from `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_*`. It is public by design and has been added to `.env.example`.
- With 2Factor, or in test mode on previews, nothing changes.

author: nethalo
body:
First reader-side step toward capturing PostgreSQL tables that are not at REPLICA IDENTITY FULL (where pgoutput sends at most the key of the earlier row; facts pinned in #2994).

`internal/event`:
- `NotCapturedKey` (`"__bintrail_not_captured__"`), `IsNotCapturedMarker` (strict one-key `true` map, like the unchanged-TOAST marker), `NotCapturedColumns`.
- `ChangedColumns` returns nil (stored as NULL, "unknown") when the before image holds the marker, checked in the same loop.
- `CheckUnresolvedToast` also refuses the marker with `*NotCapturedError` (table, pk, columns; not at REPLICA IDENTITY FULL when captured; `ALTER TABLE "schema"."table" REPLICA IDENTITY FULL`, effective for later changes). The identifier is always double-quoted so the printed command is right for upper case, spaces, dots, quotes and reserved words. When both markers are present, the not-captured refusal wins; the unchanged-TOAST error is unchanged.

**Inert:** nothing produces the marker yet. MySQL output is pinned byte for byte by `TestChangedColumns_MySQLGolden` and `TestCheckUnresolvedToast_MySQLGolden`, written and passing on `main` before the change. A MySQL JSON column can match the marker only by storing exactly `{"__bintrail_not_captured__": true}`, the same accepted limit as the unchanged-TOAST marker.

Tests: every message is built from images read back through `query.UnmarshalRowImage` and asserted whole. Mutation check: removing each guard (the `ChangedColumns` check, the marker scan, the strict shape, the quoting) fails a named test; restored. `go vet ./...` clean; `go test -race` on event, indexer, parser, buffer, byos, recovery, reconstruct, cascaderecover, verify, icebergexport; `go test ./...` green (internal/console run as an unprivileged user; its four permission tests fail as root on `main` too).

body:
Stacked on #16 (merge that first; this PR's base then becomes `main`). Firmware: daviddwlee84/fm1-metronome PR from branch `v0.4` (`38fc7da`).

## What changes for the player

- **The live link** (USB or Bluetooth): a web page plays along with the FM-1. The FM-1 says what plays and when (STATE `46`) only on a change and once a second; the page counts the beats on its own clock, so USB's and Bluetooth's jitter never reaches the beat. The page can start, stop, pick songs, set the tempo (CTRL `06`, through the keys' own code paths).
- **Clicks from the computer**: the FM-1 goes silent (`MUTE` on its header) while the page sounds them, and sounds again by itself when the computer goes (cable out, page closed, Bluetooth lost).
- **Bluetooth MIDI** (fm1-base's own stack, after MORSE 0.5): SET EDIT `K4`, on by default, kept; nothing written to flash. The setlist editor reads and sends over Bluetooth too.
- **`web/live/`**: big BPM, marking, meter, bar and beat, and a **conductor** beating the song's meter (6/8 in 2, 12/8 in 4, 5/8 3+2 long and short, 7/8 2+2+3 in 3, CLASSIC by its accent); tap-along calibration; a demo without an FM-1.
- Record format unchanged: the songs on the unit stay.

## 1. Try it (how it plays)

- fm1-emu link: https://joakimeriksson.github.io/fm1-emu/?package=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1/previews/pr-17/metronome.fwsc&name=metronome&chip=uc25hq80

## 2. Screens

`firmware/metronome/docs/screens/`: `live_page.png` (the 7/8 demo), `live_mute.png` (MUTE on the header), `live_bt_off.png` (`K4`).

## 3. Before it goes on the unit

- [x] `just fw-test metronome`: all pass (new: STATE on ack / start / every second / pick (two) / BPM; empty song and bad BPM refused; muted: clicks counted, peak −180 dBFS, unmuted −17.6; START refused during CLEAR ALL?; USB out lifts the mute; Bluetooth connect, ack, START, disconnect lifts the mute; K4 kept across a reboot and a setlist load; three STATEs pinned as full frames)
- [x] unit tests: metro.c 2319; pytest 13; node setlist 29, live 66 (USB / Bluetooth jitter, bunching and 100 ppm drift within 1 ms past the fixed latency; u32 wrap; ticks across a switch; every conductor pattern; BLE packets round trip)
- [x] `just fw-build metronome`: app 127,604 B, `.ram_text` 5,576 / 32,768, `.data+.bss` 35,320 / 98,304; package 616,003 B, SHA-256 `d961e3b1f5ecdff605e927b728641b69d0d1686cbf06e2912941cd5283bc0086`
- [x] fm1-emu `uc25hq80` and `p25q80`, virtual USB: ack → STATE, START, periodic, PICK of an empty song answered, MUTE, STOP; BPM 100 over CTRL: 4 writes; restart 0 writes, read back 100

author: gorgueugr
body:
## Que hace

La bateria existente (`tests/run_tests.sh`) comprueba que el binario *responde*: sale con 0, imprime lo esperado, rechaza lo que debe. Este test comprueba algo mas fuerte: que los planes que produce **son correctos**. Para cada plan ejecuta sus acciones en orden sobre el estado inicial y verifica precondiciones y objetivo.

Sin dependencias: `unittest` + biblioteca estandar.

```bash
python3 tests/test_siadex.py --planner build/planner
PLANIFICADOR=/ruta/planner python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
ctest --test-dir build -R py_siadex -V
```

## Tests (7)

| test | que verifica |
|---|---|
| `test_ayuda` | el binario documenta `domain_file` |
| `test_rechaza_dominio_inexistente` | un dominio inexistente se reporta |
| `test_blocks_plan_valido` | plan aplicable y `(on a b)` alcanzado |
| `test_transport_ipc2020_plan_valido` | **pfile01 del IPC 2020**: 8 acciones, plan aplicable, paquetes entregados, capacidad restaurada |
| `test_plan_determinista` | dos ejecuciones dan el mismo plan |
| `test_instancia_sin_solucion_termina` | instancia imposible: `Empty stack` en tiempo acotado |
| `test_plan_invalido_se_detecta` | el validador rechaza planes invalidos (control negativo) |

## Prueba de que detecta el fallo de verdad

Mismo test contra dos binarios:

| binario | resultado |
|---|---|
| `main` (con poda de ciclos) | **7/7 OK en 0,34 s** |
| binario anterior a la poda | **falla en 12,7 s**: `no se genero ningun plan ... Exception caught!: std::bad_alloc` |

Es decir, no asume nada: con el bug original el test se pone rojo por si solo.

## Detalles

- Tope de memoria de 3 GB para el hijo (`RLIMIT_AS`) para que una regresion no se coma la maquina.
- Validador HPDL minimo (`and`/`not`/literales) en el propio test; si aparece un constructor no soportado en una precondicion se rechaza en vez de evaluarse mal.
- Fixture `tests/fixtures/ipc2020-transport/`: dominio e instancia pfile01 del IPC 2020 (`panda-planner-dev/ipc2020-domains`, **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0**), traducidos a HPDL con `pandaPIparser -H`, con la procedencia y licencia anotadas en cabecera.
- Registrado en CTest como `py_siadex` si hay Python 3: **23/23 tests**.

## Hallazgos colaterales (no corregidos aqui)

- `planner --help` sale con **1**.
- Si no puede abrir el dominio, informa del error pero sale con **0**.
- Si muere por falta de memoria, tambien sale con **0**.

Por eso el test se apoya en la salida de error y no en el codigo de salida. Convendria arreglarlo aparte (cualquier CI que mire `$?` se lo traga todo).

author: yux91803-hobo
body:
## 起因
#192（天启照 Linear 改版）合并后，正式站部署运行 44723887043 的部署和冒烟检查都过了，但正式站联调在小芯插话那一项（`scripts/xin_live_steer.py` B 段）失败，已经自动回滚到 #191 的版本：

```
RuntimeError: A supplement without "continue" restarted a stopped task: status=running
```

任务被停下以后，站长说「那件事再加一条：名单按字母顺序排」（没说继续），任务又跑起来了。#192 只改天启前端，和它无关；但这是真问题，平时站长补一句话也会让停下的任务自己跑起来。

## 根因
- 控制器（`vm-steer.mjs` 的 `taskTell`）的规则：停了、做完、没做成的任务，前台转来的补充只记下、不开工；站长明确说继续（前台带 `--continue`）才接着做。
- 但「站长有没有明确说继续」全交给前台模型判断，控制器只看它带没带 `--continue`。Gemini Hydrogen 偶尔会给「再加一条」也带上。
- 排除了别的开工途径：
  - `continue_steers` 只把没送到的话再发一轮给前台；
  - 便条完成事件直接在聊天里记一句、不起模型；
  - 正式的完成事件只给做完、没做成、在等确认的任务排；
  - 停下的那一轮不会自动按收件箱接着做。

## 改法
照 Codex 的做法：要不要批准由程序判定（`codex-rs/core/src/safety.rs`），模型只能申请。
- `vm-steer.mjs` 新加 `saysContinue`：站长这一句原话里有「继续 / 接着做 / 恢复 / 重新开始 / 重做」之类才算，「别继续」「先不用接着做」不算。
- `vm-agent.mjs` 前台的 `xin task tell … --continue` 先用它核对这一轮站长的原话。没说就照只是补充处理：记下、回执说已经结束，前台先报状态、问要不要接着做。
- 完成事件里让原工作接着改、网页任务详情里的「接着做」不受影响。
- `vm-agent.mjs` 在行数上限（2949），只改了原有的三行（导入、注释、解析 `--continue` 那一行）。

## 测试
- `xin-steer-front.test.cjs` 新加两条：
  - 前台脚本给一句没说继续的补充带上 `--continue`。改之前任务又开工了，回执不是「已经结束」，测试失败；改之后不开工、先报状态，站长说「继续」再接着做，而且带着之前的补充。
  - `saysContinue` 认哪些话、不认哪些话。
- 插话的两个测试文件（`xin-steer-front`、`xin-steer`）16/16。
- `npm run check`：1087/1087。
- `npm run test:e2e`：本地全过（15 个脚本，738 项，没有失败）。

合并后会把 #192 的天启改版一起重新部署上去，正式站联调要再过一遍。

body:
Cleanup after #247 and #248. No intended change in what users see.

## What

- **One row component** (`CharacterVoteRow`) for the episode's vote list and the show's fan favourites, including the percentage maths.
- **A vote answers with the episode's counts** (`PUT`/`DELETE …/character-vote` now return them), so the page doesn't ask again. The reader's pick comes from the same query as the counts.
- **The vote section loads once:** it gets its cast after the page knows whether the episode is watched, and works out its cast and counts once per change, not per render.
- **Waiting for a watch just marked:** a 1s/2s/4s backoff that stops when voting opens and is cancelled on leaving, in place of one fixed 3-second retry.
- **Posting and editing a comment** share their text rules (`CheckText`) and reply shape (`Mine`); the 2000-character limit is `Comment.MaxLength`.
- **Vote indexes** now `(EpisodeId, PersonId)` and `(ShowId, PersonId)` (migration `CharacterVoteIndexes`).
- Smaller: a misplaced doc comment on the vote entity, a one-off tint replaced by `--accent-soft`, an optional parameter dropped from `Ranked` with its one test.

## Left alone

- The `"moderator"` literal in the UI (needs the constants moved into the shared project).
- Caching a show's vote totals (would delay fresh votes showing).

## Checked

- Build: 0 errors. Ratings and UI unit tests pass.
- Two-user browser runs of voting and comment editing behave as before.
- Other test projects and the integration tests were not re-run locally.
