author: coder13
body:
## Why

Small board edits rebuilt unchanged cells and marks. Candidate requests could wait behind slow analysis, and late solver replies could change a paused or edited puzzle. Frequent full-game clock saves and inherited resize styles also added work during play.

Startup also briefly showed Puzzles before choosing the saved game.

## Changes

- Keep Play and Puzzles blank during initial device and account loading. Show a subtle two-pixel progress line below the header without adding layout height. Respect reduced motion.
- Open a puzzle from the initial local cache immediately. Keep its identity while sync finishes, so a newer solved revision opens that puzzle's completion screen. Wait for synced display settings before showing an uncached puzzle, and keep later background sync from hiding the page.
- Memoize cells, candidate marks, clue overlays, and annotation geometry. Preserve current event handlers and the complete Board API.
- Apply dense highlights directly. Batch fade completion and share one fallback timer across exiting marks.
- Stop mobile panel sizing variables from invalidating every cell during a drag. Preserve cancellation, keyboard resizing, outside clues, and the mode badge.
- Give candidate and singles requests a separate queue, coalesce pending refreshes, and terminate owned hint and generation workers when their work is abandoned. Keep main's single-search import verification on the same cancellable runner.
- Check the current puzzle revision and play state before applying results. Keep completed exhaustive hint pages usable after color edits; close them after note or rule changes.
- Share action classification between history and progress, and finish valid history batches before processing appended actions.
- Keep ordinary clock updates in memory, with five-second checkpoints and lifecycle flushes. Moves and undo history still save immediately. Read library sort keys once per pass.

## Validation

- Repository and harness type checks passed. The component catalog covers 194 named components.
- All 859 unit tests passed in CI.
- Full Board, normal-motion, mobile resize, and all seven solver lifecycle browser scenarios passed in CI.
- All 20 startup scenarios passed with 428 assertions across desktop and mobile. These include the original server HTML, held puzzle and settings responses, cached and offline play, remote completion, empty/error outcomes, first visits, background sync, and reduced motion.
- Header, navigation, and cached grid bounds remain stable in the browser checks.
- Offline cases apply native offline state to the committed page before releasing app scripts, then verify that the cached puzzle opens with zero API requests.
- Both the app and engine workflows passed on `f4d8546`, including WebAssembly contracts and the native feature matrix.
- The final main integration also passed 38 focused tests and a React browser timer probe covering whole-second ticks, the prior puzzle ID on cleanup, pause, pagehide, and unmount.

[Preview](https://05610144.klyn-sudoku.pages.dev/) · [App CI](https://github.com/coder13/sudoku-app/actions/runs/44827912349) · [Engine CI](https://github.com/coder13/sudoku-app/actions/runs/44827912897)

Merged `main` through `5b55ddb`. The shared timer retains memory-only ticks and five-second checkpoints, and the owned generation session supports both rectangular 8×8 layouts. Startup behavior and the board optimizations are preserved.

## Measurements

These timings were recorded on optimization commit `92f0b21`, before subsequent feature integrations and startup changes.

Three production-build rounds, 180 actions per condition, desktop Chromium with a 390×844 mobile viewport and fourfold CPU throttling:

| Action | Baseline median DOM update | Current median DOM update |
|---|---:|---:|
| Selection | 5.50 ms | 4.10 ms |
| Candidate edit | 5.50 ms | 2.65 ms |
| Number entry | 5.80 ms | 2.80 ms |
| Dense digit highlight | 10.80 ms | 9.90 ms |

Normal-motion dense highlight paint work fell by about 34% on the throttled mobile profile. Peak bulk-removal fallback timers fell from 729 to 1. Mobile drag style work fell by 51–92% in two separate normal-CPU resize rounds.

Resize release remains variable, and mass removal still has long frame gaps. DOM update timings are not paint latency or INP, and these tests do not measure a physical phone.

[Full results, limits, source hashes, and raw reports](https://github.com/coder13/sudoku-app/blob/f4d8546830748285081fc68e5b78337e0c6ab93d/docs/measurements/react-responsiveness-2026-11-20/README.md)

## Scope

This changes the production React app. It preserves the current variant rules, play controls, and layouts, with matching component catalog updates. The benchmark has separate test dependencies and adds no runtime dependency.

author: tiendc
body:
Steps S4 and S5 of docs/design/e2e.md on Windows, after #379 did them on Linux.

## S4: `crates/e2e/tests/installer.rs`
- `setup.exe /S`, run once with `/CURRENTUSER` and once with `/ALLUSERS`. In each:
  - Recording: the installed `tracewing.exe` records HTTPS. The HAR holds the body sent and the body answered.
  - Kill: it takes the system proxy and arms the scheduled task, whose command is the installed program. Then it is killed.
  - `uninstall.exe /S`, which runs `tracewing uninstall` itself: the WinINet setting is back as it was, neither root store trusts the CA, and the task is gone.
  - Removal: the folder, the uninstall key, the Start menu shortcut and the PATH entry are gone, and what was recorded stays.
- The uninstaller's `tracewing uninstall` reads the window's data folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\tracewing`). The test sets whatever is there aside first and puts it back afterwards.
- The `.zip` runs from a folder: it records HTTPS, `tracewing uninstall --data-dir` takes the CA out, and the user's PATH is unchanged.

## S5 on Windows
- Chrome, Edge and Firefox each run in Set up's own profile and through WinINet's setting, with the same checks as on Linux: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, WebSocket, SSE, the test page, and no HTTP/3.
- Firefox reads the system's roots on Windows, so the user's own profile needs nothing from tracewing.
- The browser tests now pick browsers by the names Set up lists, so `TRACEWING_E2E_BROWSERS` is `chrome firefox` in the Linux container and `chrome edge firefox` on Windows.

author: frankolien
body:
Frank: tapping a request link someone sent goes to the website first. It should open the app on paying them.

**Cause:** request links are `https://fliq.cash/pay/{name}/{code}` (production `PAY_LINK_BASE_URL`). fliq.cash's `apple-app-site-association` only lists the apps for passkeys (`webcredentials`), so iOS gives the link to Safari.

**Fix**
- **Web:** the association file adds `applinks`: `/pay/*/*` opens `YCKKUWB4WD.cash.fliq.app.mainnet`. Only the mainnet app, so an old testnet build never catches a real request. Passkeys are unchanged. The data now sits in `app/lib/apple-app-site-association.ts`, because Next route files can't export extra names.
- **iPhone:** `applinks:fliq.cash` added to the associated domains, next to `webcredentials`. `onOpenURL` and `PayLink` already handle `https://fliq.cash/pay/{name}/{code}` from #312: Pay opens on the person and fills in the amount.
- **Without the app:** the link opens the website as before.

**After merge**
- The web deploys from main.
- iPhones pick up the new association file when the app is installed or updated, so this works from build 15.
- iOS only opens a universal link in the app when it's tapped from another app (Messages, WhatsApp, Notes), not when it's typed into Safari.

**Tests**
- Web: `tests/apple-app-site-association.test.mjs` checks that passkeys stay for both apps and that only `/pay/*/*` opens the mainnet app. `tsc` and eslint are clean.
- iPhone: 291 tests, 0 failures.

## Summary

`tests/php/CrowdsecServiceTest.php` repeated `tests/php/PfbCoreServiceTest.php` almost line for line: the command-double script, `arrange()`, `rc()`, `lines()`, `livePids()`, and the lock rows. This change moves Core's rc sandbox into `tests/php/CoreRcSandboxTrait.php`, following the pattern of `tests/php/DnsProxyRcSandboxTrait.php`.

The trait is parameterised by:

- the daemon(8) tag;
- the `$pfb` keys of the child's pidfile, the supervisor's pidfile and the lock file;
- the variable that marks the locked run;
- the child's command line.

The shared lock, stop, survivor and start-confirmation rows now run for both services from the trait. Production code is unchanged (`git diff --stat origin/devel -- src` is empty).

Closes #4145

## Changes

- One double script for both services. It is Core's, plus the `ps` and `sha256` roles the bouncer's rc script uses. Each class links only the command names its own script calls, so a command with no double still fails the test.
- The running pair is always 1001/1002, and a launched pair is always 3001/3002.
- Signals are recorded in `events` without a tick. The tick of each signal is in `signal.ticks`.
- CrowdSec's `gone()`/`locks` model of daemon(8) removing its own pidfiles is gone. No row ever stopped a pair the sandbox had launched, so no test exercised it.

## Evidence: coverage did not drop

**Both suites before and after** (`vendor/bin/phpunit --filter '/(PfbCoreServiceTest|CrowdsecServiceTest)::/'`, PHP 8.5.12, dash):

| | Tests | Assertions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before (`365b9e2e7`) | 101 | 5477 |
| After (`3ae1b63a4`) | 109 | 5974 |
| After the review fixes (`21dddc436`) | 112 | 6132 |

Every replaced row has the same number of assertions or more. The counts come from the JUnit logs of both runs.

- Core: every row keeps its count, except `testStopEscalatesToKillAfterFiveSeconds` (53 to 54) and `testStopThatCannotTakeTheLockInTimeSignalsNothingAndFails` (52 to 54).
- CrowdSec: each replaced row gains 1 to 4 assertions. For example, the lock-timeout stop goes from 58 to 62 and the KILL escalation from 58 to 62.
- CrowdSec also gains rows it never had: a supervisor that has not set its title yet, another daemon whose title only starts with the tag, a binary whose name only starts with the bouncer's, and an orphan that survives KILL.

**Production mutations, run in an extracted scratch tree with the tests unchanged.** The table lists the shared rows that failed under each mutant.

| Mutant (applied to each service's generator) | Core | CrowdSec |
| --- | --- | --- |
| start runs without `lockf` | 2 rows fail | 2 rows fail |
| stop runs without `lockf` | 2 rows fail | 2 rows fail |
| no KILL to the child | 4 rows fail | 4 rows fail |
| a survivor of KILL does not fail the stop | 3 rows fail | 3 rows fail |
| the lock marker is not unset before daemon(8) | 1 row fails | 1 row fails |
| no wait for the supervisor's pidfile | 4 rows fail | 4 rows fail |

With the generators restored, both classes pass again.

N/A, test maintenance. No production behaviour changes, so there is no red run. Coverage is shown by the assertion counts and the mutations above.

author: das974
body:
## The problem

An app whose database is unreachable when it starts, or one of whose hosted services fails to start, doesn't start: the process exits. On Cloud Run that's a crash loop, and it can stay down even after the dependency is back. Building the app connected to the database and ran the bootstrap, so even a tool that only builds the app needed the database up. Ledger carries pnpm patches of `@decohere/http` and `@decohere/data-typeorm` to get around this.

## What changed

- **A failed start is retried.** When a hosted service's `start()` throws, the app logs it, starts the next service, and starts the failed one again in the background. The wait starts at 1 s and doubles up to 60 s, varied by ±20%. `/ready` answers 503 until it starts. `startRetry: { initialMs, maxMs }` tunes the backoff. `startRetry: false` keeps fail-fast for one-shot jobs, and `startTestApp` uses it so a test sees the error.
- **Start steps are retried the same way.** A failed step holds back every step and service after it, so nothing starts against a database that isn't migrated. Steps are named and timed: `hostedServicesStarted()` lists them, with `started: false` for one being retried.
- **Data sources connect when the app starts, not when it's built.** Building only checks each data source's config and registers it unconnected. Config mistakes still fail the build, since they won't fix themselves.
  - The provider's start step (`typeorm data sources` or `mikro-orm data sources`) runs the bootstrap, connects, then migrates, synchronizes and seeds. It's retried while the database is down.
  - MikroORM no longer tries to create the database itself (`ensureDatabase: false`), since the bootstrap does that.
- **A request that needs a data source that isn't connected gets a 503 problem.** Resolving its unit of work throws the new `DependencyUnavailableError` (from `@decohere/core/hosting`), and http answers 503. The reason, which can name hosts and ports, is logged and not sent.
- **The db commands open the data source themselves**, through the new `MigrationTarget.open()`, since they never start the app. `db new` skips it, because it only writes a file.
- The fail-fast path no longer swallows an error from stopping the services already started: both errors are thrown together.

## How we know it works

- `projects/data/data/tests/database-down.docker.spec.ts` covers both providers against a real Postgres behind a TCP proxy that refuses connections and then forwards them. The app starts while the database is down, `/ready` lists the data source step, and the hosted service doesn't start. Resolving the unit of work throws `DependencyUnavailableError`. Once the proxy forwards, the retry bootstraps, connects and creates the tables, the hosted service starts, and a request writes and reads a row.
- `typeorm.lifecycle.spec.ts`, which needs no Docker:
  - building doesn't connect;
  - the app starts and recovers once the database comes up;
  - `startRetry: false` fails with the connection error.
  - These failed before the change, because building called `initialize()`.
- `http.problem-details.integration.spec.ts`: `DependencyUnavailableError` is answered with a 503 problem that has no detail.
- `db-command.spec.ts`: every command opens the data source before running, except `new`.
- `app.hosted-services.spec.ts` and `start-steps.spec.ts`:
  - a flaky service or step is retried while the app serves;
  - a step holds back the services until it succeeds;
  - retries stop when the app stops;
  - the backoff doubles up to `maxMs`.
- The existing Docker tests were updated for the change: building no longer creates the database, and starting does.
- `pnpm test` (1,804 tests), `pnpm test:docker` (43), `lint:check` and `typecheck` all pass.

## Decisions

- ADR 0010 (hosted services):
  - a start that throws is retried, not fatal;
  - start steps hold back what follows them;
  - data sources connect in a retried start step, not at build.
- ADR 0011 (database bootstrap): the bootstrap runs at start, and the db commands run it through `MigrationTarget.open()`.
- Breaking for apps:
  - retry is now the default;
  - a singleton that injects a `DataSource` or MikroORM instance directly gets it unconnected until the start step has run;
  - `dataSources.prepare` is replaced by `check` (at build) and `open` (at start).

Closes #87

body:
## Summary

Adds `pd-incident-workflows`, the next item from `docs/backlog.md`:

| Subcommand | What it does | Writes? |
|---|---|---|
| `export -o DIR` | Writes one JSON file per workflow: its definition, steps (`include[]=steps,team`) and its triggers. Fields the server changes on its own (`updated_at`, `self`, `html_url`, `summary`, `created_at`) are left out. | no |
| `diff -i DIR` | Shows a unified diff of each file against the live workflow, and reports workflows missing on either side. `--fail-on-drift` makes it exit 1 for cron. | no |
| `triggers-export` | Writes a CSV of trigger-to-service links (`action, trigger_id, service_id, workflow_name, trigger_type`) that you can feed straight back into `triggers-apply`. Triggers subscribed to all services are left out. | no |
| `triggers-apply CSV` | Attaches or detaches workflow triggers on services. | **yes** |

`triggers-apply` follows the same write-safety rules as the other commands:
- **Validation:** every row is checked before any write: the action, a known trigger, a known service, no contradictory rows, and no per-service links on triggers that apply to all services.
- **Idempotent:** existing links are skipped, and a detach that returns 404 counts as done.
- **The usual guards:** `--dry-run` and `-y`. Auth errors abort the run, and other failures make it exit 1.

**Scope decision:** this command doesn't write workflow definitions (`PUT /incident_workflows/{id}`). The API's step update format can't be checked against a live account from here, and pushing back a slightly wrong export could break a live workflow. Workflows are still edited in the PagerDuty UI, and `diff` shows drift from git. The backlog row is narrowed to that follow-up.

Docs are updated (README, `docs/usage.md`, CHANGELOG, `docs/backlog.md`).

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New script or feature
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] Refactor or internal cleanup (no intended user-visible behavior change)
- [ ] Dependency update

None.

## How this was tested

- `python -m pytest tests/unit` passes and `ruff check .` is clean.
- `tests/unit/test_incident_workflows.py` covers:
  - export file names, stripping of server-managed fields, and the steps include

$ git ls-tree main third_party/llama.cpp

$ git ls-tree HEAD third_party/llama.cpp
160000 commit d79524debdb8c03c75cf8e36632da035e95c6d35   third_party/llama.cpp

$ compare 4eb3f08f95ff...d79524debdb8
status=ahead  ahead_by=3  behind_by=0        # the pinned commit is an ancestor: nothing rewritten
```

The three commits:

| commit | what it does | issue |
|---|---|---|
| `f00839e0` | flash attention over several KV streams runs on HRX (one new matcher, no new kernel) | engine#2918 |
| `1233b1e4` | the GTT reserve is a cap, not a constant, so a 16 or 32 GB machine can load a model | engine#2986 |
| `d79524de` | an unlisted dispatch architecture says so instead of silently returning nullptr | engine#679 |

**The pair stays consistent without a second bump.** `third_party/hrx-system` is unchanged at `7f4236924aad`, and at the new fork head
`ggml/src/ggml-hrx/loom-jit.cpp` still speaks that line's API — `loomc_link_index_builder_allocate` (2) and `_free` (1), no
`_create`/`_release` — so `tools/ci/loomc_pair_check.py` is satisfied by construction and engine#2916's trap (bumping hrx-system toward
`main`, which is an ancestor of the pinned HRX line) is not touched.

`registry/architectures.json` carries the new sha on its `sources` line, matching the gitlink; `registry_build.py --check` in `build` is
the gate on that file.

### Measured before opening, on this box

- `compare` above, taken from the API rather than a local cache.
- the loomc symbol census above, from `loom-jit.cpp` at `d79524debdb8`.
- nothing here was device-tested: the pin moves binaries, and `hw_gate` is the measurement.

### Not in this bump, deliberately

author: 775878805osamaha
body:
## Verified source of unnecessary UI work
`RangeTickStore.readCoveredInterval` reconstructs requested real-source BID history from SHA-256-verified SQLite windows. It previously looped from the **first tick of every cached manifest** until reaching the requested timestamp, which could read 120k+ BID events even if the chart needed only a few at the end of a window.

## Change
- Add `RangeVerifiedBidWindowSlice.appendWithinLimit`: binary lower/upper bounds on the timestamp-sorted **already SHA-verified** source window, then copy only the real BID events in the requested inclusive range.
- Preserve all same-millisecond BID events in their original sequence; never add synthetic ticks, silently deduplicate, or include future / out-of-range events.
- Check `maxTicks` BEFORE copying the slice so an oversized candidate never leaves partially appended ticks in the result.
- Integrate this helper only into `RangeTickStore.readCoveredInterval` after `readVerifiedWindow` returned real ordered, SHA-matching data. The existing cursor and manifest coverage validation still enforce no time gaps or overlaps.

## Regression tests
- New test fixture with **120,000** real-shaped, same-ms-double BID events: extract eight events near the end of the window with <=50 source indexed reads vs previously scanning almost all 120k.
- Verify inclusive same-ms multiplicity, empty/quiet periods, exact disjoint adjacent window boundaries, output atomicity on exceeded tick budget and invalid bounds.
- Run the unchanged SQLite archive integration suite, full chart/Range/Replay Flutter verification and 7 Yemen timezone checks before/after merging.

No APK, Release or changes to `main`. The count bound proves algorithmic improvement, not actual Android FPS.

author: dimasbaguspm
body:
Closes #769.

**What changed**

- New `internal/common/dotconfig`: `/noxis/config.json` (or `~/.config/noxis/config.json`), one file, `0600`, directory `0700` — enforced on every write, because `WriteFile` keeps the mode of a file that already exists. JSON, not TOML: the file is six fields and the ticket's default was JSON with no new dependency.
- `noxis auth signin <token> [--api-url] [--name]` proves the token against `whoami` **before** storing it; a refused token is never written and never printed.
- `noxis auth status` prints profile, server, caller, scopes, when it was checked and the file — re-asking the server, so a revoked token shows up here first.
- `noxis auth signout` deletes the profile and clears `current_profile`; a test asserts no token string survives in the file.
- Every command resolves **flag → stored profile → environment**, then asks `whoami` unless it asked within `constants.AuthCheckWindow` (60s). A 401 from that check says `run noxis auth signin …` instead of surfacing a bare 401 mid-rehearsal. `--token`/`API_TOKEN` still work for CI and warn once, without printing the token.
- `whoami` is annotated so the boot check does not ask the same question twice; `auth` commands are annotated so they can run with no session at all.

**Proof**

- Unit tests: file and directory modes, round trip, signout removes the token, empty file is not an error; CLI resolution: no profile says how to sign in, a fresh profile is not re-checked, a revoked token says sign in again and never echoes it, a successful check is cached, a flag beats the profile.
- Manual end-to-end against a real `noxisd`: signin → status → `target ls` → signout → `target ls` refuses with the signin instruction; `config.json` is `-rw-------`.

author: scifi316
body:
Fixes TA-18. Version 1.8.7.

Before: On a big iPhone the "All days" button in the itinerary sat cut off against the left edge of the screen. A place card could only be pulled down by a thin 22px strip at the top. Pulling it part way down and letting go could leave it stuck, and the X then ignored the first tap.

After: "All days" keeps its gap from the edge. A card can be pulled down by its whole header (title, address, status) as well as the strip, and flicked down to close. A half-finished pull always puts the card back, and the X closes it on the first tap.

## Causes
1. **All days clipped:** the day strip snaps each button to its start, but snap points were measured from the screen edge, not from inside the strip's 14px padding. When the strip scrolled back to the start (which tapping "All days" does), Safari snapped to the first button's point, 14px in, so "All days" landed flush against the edge.
2. **Hard to grab:** only the strip with the little bar started a drag.
3. **X needs two taps:** the drag followed the finger with pointer events captured to that strip. On iPhone, Safari doesn't reliably keep sending captured pointer events once the finger slides off the element (WebKit bug 220196), so a drag could end without ever seeing the finger lift. The unfinished drag kept its capture, which most likely took the next tap. This is my reading of the code, not reproduced on a device.

## How
- `app.css`: `.days` gets `scroll-padding-inline: 14px`, matching its padding.
- New `public/js/sheetdrag.js`, used by every sheet through `openSheet` in `ui.js`:
  - On touch screens the header grabs too, except its buttons, links and fields. A mouse still only grabs the strip, so the title can be selected on a computer.
  - Fingers are followed with touch events (always delivered to where the touch began); mouse and pen with window listeners. No pointer capture.
  - A cancelled touch, or a new press while a drag never finished, puts the sheet back. 6px of movement before a header press counts as a drag, so taps don't nudge it.
  - Closes at 80px as before, or on a quick flick of 24px or more.
- Sheets ease back when let go and slide away from where they were pulled. `.sheet-head` gets `touch-action: none`.
- `sw.js`: `/js/sheetdrag.js` in the offline shell. `package.json` 1.8.7, changelog entry.

## Tests
`test/sheetdrag.test.mjs` (16 tests): where a press starts a drag, close and flick thresholds, following the finger, ease-back, cancelled touch, a stale drag not swallowing the next tap, two fingers, mouse leaving the strip, the snap padding matching the strip's padding. 

## Merging
#35 (1.8.6) is merged into this branch already: kept 1.8.7, changelog lists 1.8.7 then 1.8.6. `npm test`: 98 pass.

## Phone checks
I couldn't open the ticket's screenshots or run the app on a phone from here, so these need a real device:
- [ ] iPhone 17 Pro Max, itinerary: tap a later day, then "All days". The button keeps a gap from the left edge. Scroll the strip back to the start by hand too.
- [ ] Open a place from the map: pull it down by the title. It follows and closes past about a thumb's length, or with a flick.
- [ ] Pull it part way down, stop, let go: it eases back. Tap the X once: it closes.
- [ ] Pull it down and slide your finger sideways off the card before letting go: it still settles or closes, and the X works first time.
- [ ] Tap the X, the vote buttons and the Day picker in a place card: each still works with one tap.
- [ ] Scroll the place card's content: it scrolls, it doesn't pull the card.
- [ ] Phone sideways: cards still open, close and scroll.
- [ ] Android app: the same pull and close checks.
- [ ] Computer: pull a card by the strip with the mouse. The title can still be selected.

Checking every sentence also let me measure the flags: in Chapter 11, 14.4 percent of flagged claims needed revision and so did 5.6 percent of the cleared ones; in Chapter 15, 11.8 against 1.8. Three flags would have made the book worse if I had followed them.

Video: 2m39s. Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bitXsn86byeihC62p6kjwLAUL8ovfndU?usp=drive_link

## The Check That Passed

My two-tower recommender passed its gradient check and still lost to a popularity counter. On 6,198 test users, the counter's recall@10 was 5.8 percent and my model's was 3.1.

A gradient check only confirms that the code computes the slope of its objective correctly. My objective was wrong: in-batch softmax treats popular films as wrong answers in proportion to how often they appear, so the model learned to avoid them. The logQ correction (Yi et al., 2019) subtracts each film's log sampling frequency during training. Same model, same data: 3.1 percent became 8.6.

All figures come from running the repo's training and evaluation code.

Source project: github.com/Kenny0bi/pulse-recsys. Video: 2m18s. Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1YE452Ql5N9XSulackFiN93JbQBVtfToC?usp=drive_link

All four videos are 4K, in 16:9 and 9:16.


This PR also adds weeks 8 to 12 to my folder guide and my hours for weeks 9 to 14.

author: alenengineer
body:
## Why

The owner's goal is "safe on shared files" and "one door". Nothing an extension does may reach a file its permissions don't cover, and your own edits land in the file you mean. A save to a note kept as a symlink replaced the link with a regular file, so a note linked from another folder silently became a copy (#349).

The first round made every write go through a link, and that opened a hole, because the gateway judges a path by its name. An extension with `files.write` then overwrote `.git/config`, `.obsidian/graph.json` and a canvas through a note's link. The owner of `.probe`, with no permissions, overwrote a note. A folder link (`Inbox/Dot -> ../.git`) already let an extension read, write, create and trash files in `.git` on main.

The second round closed the file messages, but `items/edit` still wrote through a link the watcher had indexed. The scan skips symlinks, and the watcher didn't. An extension with only `items.edit` ticked a "note" that was a link to `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, to a file in `.trash` and to a file outside the workspace, and each target was written. An owner with no permissions overwrote `Concepts/Lava.md` through `Inbox/Lava.chores -> ../Concepts/Lava.md`.

## Decision

The coordinator made these calls after the behaviour reviews, and they are recorded with the owner's rules.

- The extension gateway never follows a symlink, for reads and writes alike.
- The watcher skips symlinks exactly as the scan does. So no linked note or owned file is in the index, and no `items/edit` can reach one, whoever asks.
- Your own saves of a file you opened by its path (the whiteboard's canvas, the menu's tag edit of a note its tree lists, the shapes file, the bookmarks) still go through a link to the file it leads to.
- The safe write is the default (round 3). `write::replace` and `Seen::replace` never follow a link. The link-following write is named for it, `replace_through_link`, and only those user saves call it. A new write over a file read is safe without anyone remembering, and one that follows a link has to ask by name.

This matches the owner's decision of 2026-11-20 (ARCHITECTURE.md, References). A linked note is meant to be one book with two shelf marks, listed for the person only. That entry isn't built yet (#357), and #357 now says it must keep extensions out of `items/edit` too.

## What changed

- `workspace::first_link` is the one rule for a link at a path or on the way to it. Three places ask it.
  - `Workspace::refresh_path`: a path the watcher (or a frontend) reports that is a link, or is behind one, is no note. A note that a link replaced is removed.
  - `Core::owned_read`: such a file is no owned file, a canvas included.
  - `files::resolve`, the file messages' guard.
- `notify` is set to follow no symlink, so a folder linked into the workspace is not watched through the link. inotify watches a folder once, under the last path it was given. Before, a change to `Concepts/Lava.md` could arrive as `Linked/Lava.md`, and CI's red run shows exactly that.
- `write::replace` (and `Seen::replace`) writes over the path itself and never follows a link. A link found at the path is refused as `WriteError::Link` ("… is a symbolic link, which this write never follows", `refused` at the gateway), so a wrong caller is loud instead of silently turning a link into a file. A link swapped in after that check is replaced by the rename, and nothing is written through it. Every write over a file the scan or the gateway found uses it:
  - `workspace/write`, and `items/edit` on a note (`gateway::write`),
  - an owned file's edit after its owner answers (`Core::write_edit`),
  - a rename's, a merge's and a recipe's writes and their put-backs (`rename::apply`, `Written::all`, `Written::put_back`), so a recipe an extension runs (`Host::run_recipe`) included,
  - `cold-lava task toggle` and `item set`, which canonicalize the path they are given first, so a link given there still ticks the target.
- `write::replace_through_link` (`Seen::replace_through_link`) is the one write that follows a link, for the user's own save of a file opened by its path: the board's canvas, the menu's tag edit (`scan_tree` lists a note that is a link), `shapes/file.rs` and `bookmarks.rs`. `replace_entry` is gone.
- `workspace/create` goes through `write::create`, which no longer follows a link.
- A `.obsidian` that is a symlink to a folder is heard where it leads (`core::linked_obsidian`, read as the core opens). One outside the workspace is watched on its own, without recursion. One inside (`.obsidian -> _settings`) is already in the recursive watch. Either way, what is heard in that folder is also named under `.obsidian` (`core::names`), so its graph colour groups and bookmarks are heard as on main. The folder's own files keep their names too, so a note in `_settings` is still a note.
- A rename, a merge and a recipe check every file they will write for a link at its path before they move or write anything (`rename::check_unchanged` asks `write::refuse_link`, `replace`'s own refusal). A backlink swapped for a link to the same bytes used to pass that check, so a rename moved the note, updated the other links and then refused the swapped one. It is now refused whole.
- `Core::run_recipe` keeps the whole chain of the error (`{e:#}`) and the write's reason (`Reason::of`). An extension's recipe refused for a link now says it is a link, with reason `refused`, where it said only "writing X; nothing was changed" with reason `changed`.
- `files::resolve` refuses a path that is a symlink or has one on the way to it. Every file message goes through it.
  - A link at the path itself reads `Data/x.md is a symbolic link, which the gateway never follows`.
  - A folder on the way reads `Data/Dot/config: Data/Dot is a symbolic link, …`.
  - `stat` and `delete` still act on a link itself.
- `write::replace_through_link` finds where the write lands once, then compares and renames that same file. A link to nothing or to a folder is `WriteError::NotAFile`, which `Reason::of` names `refused`.
- `write::taken` is the one test of whether something is at a path. `write::create` and `files::free_name` both ask it.

## Scope

- **The race left (#366).** Every guard is a check followed by a separate system call. Two things are still followed:
  - a folder on the way swapped for a link in between,
  - a read at the path itself.

  An owned file's write after its owner answers, and a recipe's, a rename's and a merge's writes, no longer follow a link at the path (round 3).

  Closing these needs system calls relative to an open folder. This is stated at `unlinked`, `landing` and docs/extensions.md.
- **Notifications through a link.** The watcher still reports a linked file of an owner's kind as `file/changed`. Its `rev` is of the bytes the link leads to. No text is sent, and the owner can't read it through the gateway.
- **Moves and trashes (#356).** A move or a trash onto a link to nothing still replaces the link. `daily.rs` and `home.rs` still ask `exists()` before `write::create`.

## Blast radius

- **Extensions.** One that read or wrote notes kept as links now gets `refused`. An `items/edit` on a linked note finds no item, because the note isn't indexed.
- **Other callers of `files::resolve`.** These refuse a link too:
  - an extension's `note.edit`, and the image view by path,
  - a shape's `create` step,
  - the menu's restore and new folder.

  The menu's tree doesn't show a symlinked folder, so the menu doesn't reach one.
- **Notes linked in while cold-lava runs** are skipped, as at start. Their tasks no longer show twice, and no stale copy is left.
- **A `bookmarks.json` that is itself a link** (not a linked `.obsidian` folder, which is fine) is refused by a rename or a merge that would update it, whole, before anything moves, instead of written through. The bookmarks dialog's own save still follows it. Bookmarks are being removed in #373.

body:
TL;DR: Lampposts were the only light a player or a townsperson could switch on and off. This adds lanterns and candles for indoors, and a trait so a townsperson can light the ones in their house at dusk and put them out later.

## What this changes

- **Four new tiles**, drawn by `scripts/generate-lanterns.ts` (`bun run generate:lanterns`) as 3D models cast through the game's projection:
  - `lantern` / `lantern-off`: an iron-framed glass box, two units tall. It has a full dark outline and a one-pixel glint along the ridge where the frame's lit and shaded faces meet. When it is lit, the panes glow where the flame is behind them. The lit lantern cycles through four uneven frames, about 1.2 s in all: its light goes between 0.76 and 0.95 intensity at a fixed radius, with the tall flame on the bright frames. Each frame is one more cached bake per chunk the light reaches, so the cycle stays at four. Every lantern reads the same animation clock, so they all brighten and dim together.
  - `candle` / `candle-off`: a taper on a brass dish, one unit tall, so it fits on a `table` or `barrel`. The flame is only particles: one-pixel motes start just above the wick, rise about half a unit (one or two pixels on screen) and turn from amber to red as they fade. A flame drawn into the sprite came out as a blob that looked like part of the wax.
  - Each pair is joined by a `switch`, as `lamppost` / `lamppost-off` are (Light / Put out / Snuff).
- **A wall lantern is a `lantern` placed with `foot: 2`**, not a separate tile. Two units is as high as `fitsFoot` lets a two-unit tile go. The gap a foot leaves is solid, so a hung lantern takes the floor cell in front of the wall, the same as one standing on that floor. Both tiles are `walkable: false` for that reason: otherwise a lantern lifted one unit would be a step into the air.
- **`tends-lights` trait** in `data/traits.json`. During the given hours it lights the unlit lanterns and candles within 6 cells; outside them it puts the lit ones out. It handles one light at a time, nearest first. This is the lamplighter's routine written as a trait. Both triggers fire at `errand`, as `keeps-hours`'s do. So if a body calls `tends-lights` before `keeps-hours`, with hours ending at its bedtime, it puts its lights out and then goes to bed.
- **`bun run scene` accepts `foot` on a placement**, so a lifted tile can be drawn. `scripts/scenes/lanterns.json` and `scripts/scenes/candles.json` are the scenes used below. The verify skill now says that a scene picture has no particles: the page draws one frame without advancing them.
- Docs: a `docs/notes.md` section on lanterns and candles (the wall foot, the particle flame, the lantern's light cycle), a bullet for the trait next to the other townsfolk traits, and the README entry.

## UX impact

The tiles appear in the editor. No townsperson calls the trait yet and no lantern is placed in `data/map.json`, so the shipped world looks the same until somebody places lights and adds the trait to a character's brain.

Screenshots and a GIF were sent in the session; they cannot be uploaded from it. The stills are from `bun run scene scripts/scenes/lanterns.json --size 640x420` at 22:00. For the flame and the light cycle, the scene page was patched locally to advance the renderer step by step; that patch is not on this branch.

## Out of scope

- Placing lanterns in the towns' houses and giving the townsfolk the trait. That is map and character authoring.

## Risk

- Outside its hours, a body with the trait also puts out any light a player lit within 6 cells of it.
- While a body is asleep (`abed` holds at `rest`) it does not get up to put out a light. If the trait's hours run past its bedtime, the lights stay lit until it wakes.
- Each lit candle keeps about 9 particles alive at once (22 a second, about 0.45 s each). A room of candles is cheap, but a hall of a hundred would use about half of `MAX_LIVE_PARTICLES`.
- Each lit lantern gives every chunk its light reaches four cached light bakes instead of one.

## How to Test

1. `bun dev`, open `/admin/play` and place a `lantern-off` on the floor and another with its foot raised to 2 against a wall. Place a `candle-off` on a table.
2. Use Light and Put out on each one. Each should switch, and the lit tiles should light the room at night. A lit candle should show a small flickering flame above its wick, and a lit lantern's light should rise and fall.
3. In the Brain tab, add `tends-lights` (from 18, to 23) to a townsperson standing near the lanterns. Set the clock to evening: they should walk to each unlit light and light it. After 23:00 they should put the lights out.

author: m-bonanno
body:
## What

Closes #90. Every PR now runs the tests and the build on Windows as well as Ubuntu. Every merge into `develop` or `main` runs the gates again on the commit it made, and semantic-release tags that commit only when they are green. ADR 0008 records the whole pipeline the owner decided; this is the first of its four PRs.

## Why

Scia ships for Windows, and no check of a PR ran there. And nothing ran on the commit a merge makes: the required checks are not `strict`, so a PR green against an older `develop` could be squashed into a commit no check had run on, and be published as a beta. The owner decided the pipeline on 20 November 2026, as four answers to multiple-choice questions (they are recorded in the ADR's Context).

## How

- **`.github/workflows/gates.yml`** (renamed from `pr-checks.yml`): it runs on `pull_request` as before, and now also on `workflow_call`.
  - `Format, lint, types, tests, build` keeps its name, because that name is a required check of `develop` and `main`.
  - New job `Windows tests, build` on `windows-latest`: `npm test` and `npm run build`. Format, lint and types give the same answer on both systems, so they run once, on Ubuntu. Neither job downloads Electron's binary (`ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD`): no spec of these layers starts it.
  - Both checkouts use `persist-credentials: false`.
- **Concurrency**: grouped by PR number, so a new push to a PR cancels its run. A run called from a release is grouped by its own run id and is never cancelled.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`**: a new job `Gates` calls `gates.yml` on a push to `develop` or `main`, and `Semantic release` now `needs` it. When the gates are red, there is no tag and the installer job is skipped. A dispatch with `installer_tag` behaves as before: the gates and semantic-release are skipped, and the installers are built for that tag.
- **Docs**:
  - new ADR [`0008-the-delivery-pipeline.md`](docs/adr/0008-the-delivery-pipeline.md): what runs on a PR, on a beta and on a stable, and on which runner; the layers; how flaky specs are kept out; the cost; what a person still does; the order of the four PRs;
  - `testing.md`: a new section, "Where CI runs them", and the no-retry rule;
  - `review-flow.md`: "The gates" now says where CI runs them;
  - `release-flow.md`: the workflow has a new first step, the gates;
  - `roadmap.md`: the line on the repository.

## Notes

- **Advisory, in the owner's meaning.** Until its burn-in of ten green runs in a row (#93), the Windows job is not required by GitHub's branch protection — and that is all "advisory" means (the owner, 20 November 2026, #90): the team merges only with it green, and a beta's tag waits for it like any gate. One unstable Windows spec therefore holds every merge and every beta until it is mended or skipped with an issue. The burn-in and the change to the protection of `develop` and `main` are #93.
- **A beta now comes out later.** The release waits for the gates before it tags. The extra time is about the same as the Windows job's run on this PR: 1 min 24 s (see Test plan).
- **No automatic retry anywhere.** `testing.md` now says what happens to a spec that fails without a cause in the change: it gets an issue, then it is fixed or skipped until it is.

## Out of scope

- The E2E suite and its job (#91).
- The smoke test of the installer, on PRs and in releases (#92).
- The burn-in and the required checks (#93).

## References

- Closes #90
- ADR 0008 (this PR). Related: ADR 0007 (the files every release carries), #91, #92, #93.

## Test plan

- [x] The gates, all of them, run by the author on Windows on each head — `b33c3c3`, `8992db3` and `7658741`: format, lint and types clean; **716 tests passed in 68 files** each time; build green.
- [x] CI on this PR, each run read from its record:
  - run 44775889668 on `b33c3c3`: `Format, lint, types, tests, build` green in 1 min 22 s (714 passed, 2 skipped — the two specs that run on Windows only); `Windows tests, build` green in 1 min 24 s, 716 passed in 68 files.
  - run 44778334901 on `8992db3`, the first with neither job downloading Electron's binary: Ubuntu green in 1 min 11 s, 714 passed and 2 skipped; Windows green in 1 min 40 s, 716 passed in 68 files.
  - run 44779215642 on `7658741`, the head merged: Ubuntu green in 56 s, 714 passed and 2 skipped; Windows green in 1 min 26 s, 716 passed in 68 files.
- [x] `release.yml`, read against the three ways a run can start:
  - a push to `develop` with the gates green: `Gates`, then `Semantic release`, then `Installer (Windows)` when a tag was made;
  - the gates red: `Semantic release` is skipped, and `Installer (Windows)` is skipped too, since it needs the release to have succeeded;
  - a dispatch with `installer_tag`: `Gates` and `Semantic release` are skipped, and `Installer (Windows)` runs.
  - _The first beta after the merge will show the first of these for real._
- [x] Real-runtime evidence: not applicable, since no runtime code changed.

author: erikdarlingdata
body:
Claude posting for Erik Darling.

Part of #9148. Release note: `get_query_store_regressions` over a week is about 30 percent faster on a large store, with the same rows.

## Regressions over a week (part E)

### What was measured
Test store: 42 servers, 45,000 Query Store interval rows a day each, 16 days (31.5 million rows), daily totals built for every whole day, the background indexes built, the text table filled for all but 1 percent of queries. One call: `hours_back` 168, limit 50.

- The tool answers from `interval_table`. That word names the tier (the interval tables, as opposed to `raw`). It does not mean the daily totals were skipped. With every whole day built, the read takes the baseline's and the recent window's whole days from `plan_regression_daily` and reads only the edge days live. So there is no wrong skip of the daily path to fix, and the earlier finding (stale days are not the cause) holds here too.
- Each edge day read is cheap: about 45,000 live rows per arm, 0.1 s.
- The cost is CPU in two aggregates. Both arms hand about 315,000 part rows (270,000 daily rows plus 45,000 live rows) to a `GROUP BY database_name, query_id` that also holds `COUNT(DISTINCT plan_id)`. A distinct count forces a sort of every row, so each arm sorted 315,000 rows (about 1.0 s for the recent arm, 1.3 s for the baseline arm in the plan).
- The statement's own time on this store was 2.3 to 2.9 s warm (3.2 s in one cold run). The rest of the tool's statements add under 10 ms.

### The change
`baseline_performance` and `recent_performance` now sum per plan first (one hashed step, 45,000 groups) and then per query, with `COUNT(plan_id)` over the per-plan rows. The sums are the same exact numeric sums, so they add to the same totals. A NULL `plan_id` forms one group that `COUNT(plan_id)` skips, as `COUNT(DISTINCT plan_id)` skipped it. `MAX(query_text)` and `MAX(last_execution_time)` are maxima of maxima. The change is in `QueryStoreRegressionBaseline` and covers the raw, wide and recent-days forms, and the viewer's copy of the statement, since they share the text.

Result on the same store, statement alone, 6 alternating runs each (the laptop was shared, so the spread is wide):

| | min | median |
|---|---|---|
| before | 2.39 s | 2.54 s |
| after | 1.58 s | 1.80 s |

The two result sets (51 rows, every column) are byte-identical. Cold (server restarted): 2.3 and 3.0 s before, 1.6 and 2.0 s after. Buffers touched are the same, as the change is CPU only.

### Not done, and why
- The remaining 1.6 to 1.8 s is the volume of daily and edge rows (315,000 per arm) read and hashed once each. Going lower needs a coarser grain than one row per plan per day (for example a per-query daily total), which is a new table. That is a store change, so it is left here for a decision. At 45,000 plan-days a server, the daily table is the dominant read.
- The field report that a call with limit 50 was slower than limit 500 did not reproduce: on this store limit 500 was not faster.
- A plain count of distinct keys on `query_store_interval_latest` for one server that ran past 90 s on a large store was not reproduced. On the test store the two edge ranges read through the `(server_id, first_execution_time)` index in 40 to 90 ms each. If the large store lacks that background index, or has it invalid, the live arms fall to a scan. Worth checking on that store, since the index is built by a background step and not by the migration.
- Lite: `LocalDataService.QueryStoreRegressions.cs` runs in DuckDB over deduped raw rows with `COUNT(DISTINCT plan_id) FILTER (...)`. It has no daily tables, a different plan shape and a much smaller window, and nothing here measured a DuckDB cost, so it is not changed.

### Tests
- No behaviour test can fail on the old code, because the answer is identical and only the CPU changes. The existing equality tests cover the answer, including plan counts: every class matching `*Regression*` ran against a live store: 288 tests, 1 failure.
- The failure was `ViewerQueriesTests.RegressionsSql_CastsSummedExecCountToBigint_PlanCountToInteger_ConvertsUnits_HonorsDatabaseFilter`, a test that pins the spelling of the SQL (`COUNT(DISTINCT plan_id)`). Its rule is spelling, so it is deleted and not moved (#5833).
- Not run: the pre-push gate (`pre-push.sh`), the full suite, and the other classes of `ViewerQueriesTests.cs` after the deletion. CI decides those.
- No source-text or plan test was added.

### Considered, not added
- Making `deduped_recent` non-materialized: an earlier measurement in that file shows the materialized form avoids a 60 s plan on a large store, so it stays.


## Review round 1

**Finding:** `plan_count` had no hand-worked test. Every live equality test compares one form of the statement with another, and all forms share the same aggregate text, so a plan-count defect common to every form would pass.

**Test:** `ThePlanCounts_AreHandWorked_InBothArms_AcrossTheDailyAndEdgeParts_AndNullPlansAreNotCounted` in `QueryStoreRegressionsDailyBaselineLiveTests`. It seeds three queries and asserts exact executions and plan counts in the baseline and the recent arm, on the served read and on the all-live read:
- Query 60: two plans, each in several parts. Baseline plan 601 has 10, 6 and 4 executions (two built days and a live edge row), plan 602 has 5 and 3. Baseline is 28 executions and 2 plans from 5 part rows. Recent is 17 executions and 2 plans from 4 part rows.
- Query 61: one real plan and one plan stored with a NULL `plan_id`, in the daily rows, the live edge and the recent arm. Baseline is 23 executions and 1 plan. Recent is 11 executions and 1 plan.
- Query 62: one plan. Baseline is 10 executions and 1 plan. Recent is 4 executions and 1 plan.

**Fail-before proof (scratch edits, never committed, each reverted):**
- `COUNT(*)` in place of `COUNT(plan_id)` at all four sites: the test fails, a NULL-plan query reads 2 plans where 1 is expected.
- Counting part rows (the per-plan step grouped by the part's executions or last execution time, so it no longer collapses the parts): the test fails, query 60 reads 5 plans where 2 is expected.
- On the unmutated branch the test passes.

**Gate:** `pre-push.sh` ran. Both Guard suites are green (Darling 4981 tests, Lite 1242 tests, 0 failed). The gate ended in GATE STOP, because the selection is the whole suite. I ran these instead against a local PostgreSQL 18.7 with TimescaleDB 2.32.1: every class matching `*Regression*` and every class in `ViewerQueriesTests.cs` (288 tests, 0 failed, 4 skipped), plus all classes in the edited test file. Build had 0 warnings. Classes the gate selected beyond those were not run: CI decides.

_Requested by **Zak** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VDEQ9nmrEGmDf5MDd2spJd?thread=cmsg_01VDEQ9nmrEGmDf5MDd2spJdHwrUM3ZuuveRWKDdE3MJU6)_

First slice of the white glove setup (Build Board epic card 180, card 181). Design: https://claude.ai/artifact/Mas7ngAbKnqSZVhcM2XCQH

## What changes

- `/start` shows **one step at a time**. The step is `stage` in the `setup` row of `policies` (business, tools, company, first). A refresh, a tool's sign-in or Stripe Checkout comes back to the same step. Back and Next call `setupGo` (approver; the step is checked against the list).
- **Step 1** opens as one card: "Let's build your company", a box for the business, a box for the website. After the first message it becomes the conversation with Avery, with what she learned and the departments she is thinking of beside it.
- **New look** for setup: white glass over soft light that drifts as the steps change, a thin progress line, a blur-fade as each step arrives. Always light, reduced motion respected, works at phone width.
- On the cloud edition the conversation opens straight away (free setup, card 162). The Claude choice shows only when agents can't think yet.
- Setup no longer names an env var when real runs are off.
- Steps 2 to 4 keep their content inside the new shell; cards 182, 184 and 186 replace them.

## What is deleted

The four steps stacked on one scrolling page, the anchor step bar, `#step-N` links and return addresses, Skip to tools as an anchor.

## Hard rules

No change to runs, tools, the gateway or tenancy. `setupGo` checks the member's role with `asRole` first (`check:roles`), and is listed as not audited in `check:audit` (it only changes which step is on screen). No migration: `stage` is one more field in a json row that already exists; a row without it opens on the first step.

## Tests

`npm run check:setup` now covers: stage order, reading a stored step, unknown steps falling back to the first, next and back at both ends, progress, the saved state keeping its step, no anchor steps or setting names in the setup page, and `setupGo` checking role then step. `check:tools-step` and `check:ee` updated for the plain `/start` return addresses.

Ran: `npm run check`, `npm run check:all` (40 checks), `npm run build`. The look was checked on a static copy of the markup with the real stylesheet at desktop and phone widths; it has not been clicked through against a live database (card 189 does that for the whole flow).

body:
Closes #5

## Summary
- In `scanVenue`, after `get_branch`, these run together with `Promise.all`: the route lookup (`roadDistance`), `get_cores`, `get_core_types`, `get_lock_yards`, and the `get_schedule_bookings` + `get_onetime_bookings` pair for each month.

author: 3outeille
body:
# What does this PR do?

When the model is loaded with transformers' distributed loading (`from_pretrained(..., distributed_config=DistributedConfig(...))`, for tensor, expert or FSDP parallelism), each rank consumes a different amount of random numbers while loading. PEFT then initializes the LoRA adapters from a different random state on each rank, so every rank starts from different adapters. Gradients are averaged across ranks, not parameters, so the replicas never come back together.

Seen with a 4-rank tensor-parallel LoRA run: the per-rank gradient norms differed from the first step, because `lora_A` differed per rank. With the adapters made identical across ranks, they agree to rounding.

This PR adds `_broadcast_trainable_parameters`: right after `get_peft_model`, when the base model was loaded with a `distributed_config`, every trainable parameter is broadcast from rank 0. A sharded DTensor broadcasts its local shard, since shards line up across ranks. Without a process group, or with a single rank, it does nothing.

Test: `TestBroadcastTrainableParameters` spawns two CPU processes (gloo), seeds each with its rank, and checks that both end with rank 0's weights.

author: xxx91n
body: ## Summary 进程登记在 `bind()` 之前就写好了，而「监听失败」这条退出从来没写结束： ```diff postWork.start() # 进程登记：一行开着的记录 bind(REQUESTED_PORT) listen 成功 → 服务正常，收到停止信号时 stop() 写结束 - listen EADDRINUSE → exit(1) # 行永远开着，PID 随进程一起消失 + listen EADDRINUSE → failToListen() # 先 stop() 写结束，再退 1 + listen 同步抛 → failToListen() # 同上（端口 NaN / 越界） ``` `failToListen` 只做三件事：说清原因、`postWork.stop()`、退 1。不用 `process.on("exit")` 兜底——那个 handler 也会在「等收尾超时」那条退出上跑，而那条路是设计上不写任何东西的（见 `shutdown.ts`）。默认端口被占、回落临时端口那条路没动。 ## Evidence - **Before:** 起一个服务占住钉住的端口，再起第二个 → `EADDRINUSE` → `process.exit(1)`，库里多一条 `ended_at IS NULL` 的行，谁也收不了尾。新用例对着改动前的代码是红的（把源码回退跑过一遍确认）。 **After:** 同样的场景，第二个实例留下登记、但登记是结束的，唯一开着的行属于还活着的那个。 ```text $ node --import tsx --test test/post-work.test.ts --test-timeout=60000 ✔ real service: /index settles before the answer, /policy's audit behind it (1254.0594ms) ✔ real service: a start that cannot listen leaves no open process record (2923.6321ms) ℹ tests 11 ℹ pass 11 ℹ fail 0 ``` ```text $ pnpm -C apps/plugin exec tsc --noEmit （无输出，退出 0） ``` 本机只跑了上面这两条，全量测试和构建留给远端 CI。 ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way —— 只动一条失败启动路径的收尾，回退就是把 `failToListen` 拆回原来那两行。 **Blast Radius:** small —— 只碰插件服务的启动失败分支；正常启动、信号收尾、默认端口回落临时端口都没动。被无信号杀掉（`taskkill /F`、`TerminateProcess`）照样留行，那部分仍归 `prune`（#343）。 ## 已知 - 票上验收第 3 条（默认端口被占、回落临时端口成功那条路不受影响）没有用例：它要求不设 `ANS_SERVER_PORT` 且默认端口 33333 被占，做不成 hermetic 的用例；代码没动那条路。 - 票上 agent brief 有三处措辞和实现对不上（Desired 说「不残留这条实例的行」、验收说「不出现开着的登记」；「退出码 1」但进程表没有退出码列；总则没罩住「收尾超时」那条）。按维护者的口径再改票，不在本 PR 里动。 Closes #344

body:
## Problem
The gateway reaches pg-shared through PgBouncer in session mode. Each idle client connection pins one Postgres server connection. Bun SQL pools default to max 10 and never close idle connections. On 20 Nov 2026 the 6 gateway replicas held 99 of the 200 server connections. Other tenants then failed with "remaining connection slots are reserved".

- New `src/gateway/pg-pool.ts`: `pgPoolOptions()` reads `AIS_GATEWAY_PG_POOL_MAX` (default 4) and `AIS_GATEWAY_PG_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30). Invalid values fall back to the defaults.
- Store and home store pools use it.
- Refresh backend keeps max 10 (8 lock holders) and gets the idle timeout.
- Browser cluster pool runs LISTEN: max 2, no idle timeout.
- Leader advisory-lock connection is unchanged.

## Checks
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`: pass.
- Gateway pool, store, refresh, browser cluster, home store and HA tests: 25 pass, 5 skip (need a test database), 0 fail.

Ajustes al módulo de Divulgaciones tras revisarlo con el usuario: debía vivir dentro de "Comunicados y Procedimientos", el formulario debía traer ahí mismo los campos de cada colaborador y los datos que siempre son los mismos debían venir preestablecidos.

**Un solo módulo**
- Se elimina la pestaña independiente "Divulgaciones". `ComunicadosModule.tsx` reúne las dos listas (Comunicados y Divulgaciones) en la pestaña "Comunicados y Procedimientos".

**Colaboradores en el formulario de divulgación**
- Cada fila de la sección "Asistencia" tiene Nombre, Cédula, Proceso/Sección (desplegable con los 20 procesos de la empresa) y Firma (ventana `SignatureDialog` con el lienzo existente). Con "Agregar persona" se añaden filas.
- Al guardar se validan las filas (completas, sin cédulas repetidas). `createDivulgacion` crea la divulgación y todos los asistentes en una sola operación; si falla el registro de asistentes, no queda una planilla a medias. La ruta `POST /api/divulgaciones` acepta `asistentes`.

body:
# PR Description — S6.2: the webinar report

## What

A private page, `/report`, that shows the owner three numbers and one table for the current webinar campaign: visits to the sign-up page, people registered, people who showed up (typed in by the owner from Zoom), and where visitors and registrants came from, one row per tracking link. One shared password opens it. Visits are counted once per browser tab by a small first-party counter on `/conversation`; each accepted sign-up is counted once per person with a keyed code, never the address. The owner's guide, his checklist and the privacy-page proposals come with it.

## Why

Sprint: S6.2 — [`docs/sprint-prompts/S6.2-webinar-report.md`](docs/sprint-prompts/S6.2-webinar-report.md) (its status block holds the "Build notes": every decision taken while building).
The owner asked for "total visits, how many registered, how many participated and where the traffic came from.. thats all", with accurate numbers and one link per platform.

## Changes

- **`/report`** (`src/app/report/`): off / locked / open / error states; `POST /report/login` (shared password, HMAC session cookie `ur_report`, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/report; rate limit 10 per 600 s, fails closed); `POST /report/save` (session, own Origin via `isAllowedHost`, rate limit 30 per 600 s, validated boxes). Every redirect has a relative Location.
- **`POST /api/conversation/arrival`** + `ArrivalCounter` / `tab-source`: one visit per tab, under the source its link names; robots and automated browsers are not counted; its own rate limit, failing closed.
- **`POST /api/conversation`**: one awaited, never-throwing record call before each accepted answer; the answer is unchanged for every input.
- **`src/lib/webinar/`**: `sources.ts` (link contract + resolver), `test-address.ts`, `report-auth.ts`, `report-store.ts`.
- **Migration 0005** (applied to `unretire-test` only): `campaign_visits`, `campaign_people`, `campaign_report_inputs`; `record_campaign_person` and `campaign_report`; RLS on with no policy; `service_role` only. Down file included.
- **Tests**: new function-level and browser specs under `tests/e2e/webinar/`; added cases in the S6.1 specs; arrival-route abuse tests; `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` now keeps request headers out of test errors (Known issue 69, owner decision D-64) with its own regression spec.
- **Docs**: owner's guide `docs/WEBINAR-FUNNEL.md` §16 and the go-live order in §9; `docs/OWNER-ACTIONS.md` PART 10; privacy proposals in `docs/content/page-copy/privacy.md` §14 (awaiting the owner's approval); TECH-ARCHITECTURE and DESIGN rows; trackers.

## Out of scope / not changed

- `src/app/privacy/page.tsx` and `docs/FEATURE-LIST.md` change only after the owner approves the words at Gate B.
- No change to `/webinar`, `/api/webinar`, Mailchimp code, `next.config.ts`, `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/middleware.ts`, `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`, `package.json` or the lockfile (`git diff --stat origin/master -- <those paths>` prints nothing).
- `AGENTS.md` is not part of this PR (`next dev` writes a block into it — Known issue 70).
- Known issue 71 (the shared limiter's sweep) is avoided here by 600-second windows; its fix is a separate branch. The Next.js 16.4.5 update is a backlog row (D-64).

## How tested

- [x] Local checks green: `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` · `pnpm format:check` · `pnpm build` (the four new paths listed as dynamic; no `REPORT_*` name in `.next/static`).
- [x] `pnpm test:e2e`, both browser projects, against a local production build with the funnel open and the report on, and again with the report off. The only failures are the local-only "no browser errors" checks (Vercel Web Analytics' script exists only on Vercel) and machine timeouts that pass when re-run; details in the sprint record.
- [x] Dummy-data test on the local production build: visits through the real tracking links, dummy people through the database function, "Showed up" typed through the page — every row, total and card matched.
- [ ] Deployed Preview PASS: "E2E — Preview" with the report spec's signed-in half run — pending on this PR.

## Screenshots (UI changes only)

The report spec captures `/report` locked and open at 320 / 768 / 1440 in the "E2E — Preview" run's `test-results` artifact; the verdict is recorded in the sprint record.

- [x] `docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md` updated in this same branch

Migration 0005 is additive, and Production gets it by hand from the owner before the merge. A host rollback does not touch the database. `supabase/migrations/0005_campaign_report.down.sql` drops the three tables and two functions and **deletes the counted data**: export what the owner wants first (`docs/database-changes/0005-campaign-report.md`, "Rollback plan").

author: hauschel
body:
Closes #576

- New in-port `DeleteProject` and MCP tool `project_delete(project, confirm)`. The project is named explicitly by id or label, as `project_list` shows them. It is never taken from the calling anchor.
- Guardrails:
  - The caller's own project is refused (any of its anchors counts). A call without an anchor has no own project and is not refused.
  - A project that still holds model resources needs `confirm=true`. Without it the call is refused and lists how many resources of which type would be lost, e.g. `3 arkreq:FunctionalRequirement, 2 skos:Concept`. Self-description and provenance graphs do not count, which is the same split `store_overview` uses.
  - A reference that is one project's id and another project's label is refused as ambiguous.
- Order: the registry entry goes first, then the model dataset.
  - `ProjectRegistry#delete` runs through `WriteFunnel#delete`. Unlike the replace path, it also removes description, default language, maintained languages and all anchor nodes.
  - The dataset goes through a new out-port `ProjectDatasets` (`KognioRdfProjectDatasets`). This is a separate port because `DatasetInventory` stays read-only.
  - A crash in between leaves at worst an unregistered dataset, which `project_list` shows as adoptable.
- Open leases: `DatasetLifecycle#delete` refuses while a lease is open.
  - arknet only holds leases for a single query or transaction and caches no per-project handle, so the adapter retries for a short time (20 × 50 ms).
  - If the dataset is still in use after that, the registry entry is already gone and the dataset is kept. `ProjectDatasetRetainedException` tells the caller to adopt the dataset and delete it again.
  - Counting and deleting never `acquire` a missing dataset, so they cannot create an empty one.
- No tombstone for the deleted project itself. That stays with #440. The registry entry's last revision gets the funnel's usual delete invalidation, like every other `*_delete`.
- README tool table, module `CLAUDE.md` and pom description updated.

Tests: `mvn -T 1C clean install` green.
- New: `ProjectServiceDeleteTest` (13 cases), `KognioRdfProjectDatasetsTest` (7), 4 registry delete cases in `KognioRdfProjectRegistryTest`, 5 tool cases in `ProjectMcpToolsTest`.
- New end-to-end case in `ArknetMcpConfigurationTest`. Its anchor directory is removed from disk before the delete. Afterwards `project_list` shows neither the project nor its dataset, and the anchor no longer resolves.

author: dengzhiyuan-math
body:
Closes #540.

## What happened

In the production smoke on 2026-11-20 the model opened `„aufhalten` with `„` and closed it with a straight `"`. That ends the JSON string, so step 2 stopped inside the quotation and the rest of the sentence, `; bis man sie misst.`, came back as step 3. The #507 guard only drops a leftover with no letter or digit in it, so this one was kept, and the student saw a step card starting with a semicolon.

## The change

`ask_answer._rejoined` joins two adjacent texts when:
- the first stops inside an open quotation (`„` closed by `“`, `«` by `»`, `“` by `”`; `“` opens only where no `„` is open), and
- the second begins with punctuation (`,;.:!?)…`), a space or a small letter.

The pair becomes one text, with the quotation closed by its own mark.
- A leftover with words keeps its leading space (French `« … » :`). If it begins directly with a word, one space is added.
- A leftover with no letter or digit (the #507 ` , `) only closes the quotation; it keeps its `?` or `.` but not the separating `,`.

It applies in three places:
- **New answers**: all text lists (`steps`, `hints`, `similar_exercises`, `knowledge_points`, `quick_replies`) in `_without_wordless_texts`.
- **Answers stored before**: as they are read back (the `StructuredAnswer` validator). This also covers today's smoke conversation.
- **Streaming**: in `completed_steps`, a step that stops inside a quotation is held back until the next step or the end of the array is known. Steps are never shown cut, and their numbering never shifts.

A text that ends inside an open quotation but is followed by a step of its own (capital letter, `$`, digit) is left as it is.

## Tests

- `tests/test_ask_tool_use.py`:
  - today's shape, stored and streamed at 1–400 pieces;
  - the partial input holding the step back;
  - a last step ending inside a quotation;
  - each joining variant (`,`, space, small letter, French `:`, English `“”`, wordless leftover);
  - steps that must not be joined;
  - every text list.
- The #507 fixture now expects step 2 with its quotation closed (`…f(x)?“`) instead of left open.
- `tests/test_conversation_structured_answers.py`: an answer stored with a cut sentence reads back as one step.

Locally: `tests/test_ask_tool_use.py tests/test_ask_answer.py tests/test_conversation_structured_answers.py tests/test_ask_output_cap.py` all pass, 232 tests; `ruff check` is clean.

body: Linear: [WYREAI-741](https://linear.app/wyre-ai/issue/WYREAI-741) (malformed Host header or request target crashes the HTTP listener before auth). Same fix as the reference, halopsa-mcp#113 (merge bdee1a18). This PR does not close the issue; the fleet sweep continues in batches. ## What broke `src/http.ts` parsed the request target against the client-supplied `Host` header. A malformed `Host` or request target made that parse throw inside the request listener, before authentication, and nothing caught it, so one unauthenticated request could end the listener. ## What changed - `src/http.ts`: the target is parsed against a fixed base inside a guard. Only the path is used, so `Host` is no longer consulted. A target that still cannot be parsed gets a `400` JSON response and the server keeps running. No change to routes, auth order, or responses for valid requests. - `src/__tests__/malformed-request.test.ts`: raw-socket regression test against a locally started listener on an OS-allocated port. It checks a malformed `Host`, an unparseable target (`//`), and an HTTP/1.0 request with no `Host`, and that the listener keeps serving afterwards. It fails on the old code. - `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under Unreleased / Fixed. ## Tests tests run in CI only (no local package access). I also ran the new test locally against stubbed dependencies: 3 pass. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * HTTP requests are no longer affected by malformed `Host` headers. * Unparseable request targets receive a clear `400 Bad request` response, and the server continues handling subsequent requests. * HTTP/1.0 requests without a `Host` header are handled successfully.

author: lunalully
body:
A parte multipart não contava contra a cota.

## Antes
A cota por participante era conferida na abertura do upload (`beginUpload`) e na conclusão (`finishUpload`) — e **nunca nas partes**.

Um participante com cota de 1 MB podia:
1. abrir um multipart;
2. mandar 10 000 partes de 5 MiB (o máximo de numeração do protocolo);
3. **nunca concluir** → **50 GiB de disco reservados**, com a cota só olhando quando já era tarde.

O `AbortMultipartUpload` existe, mas quem abusa não o chama, e o coletor de vencidos só age depois do TTL (24 h por padrão).

Reproduzido pela rota real antes da correção: cota de 20 MiB, três partes de 6 MiB enviadas, e a quarta (24 MiB no total) recebia **`200`**.

## Agora (doc 18 §4.7)
`UploadPart` confere `usado + partes abertas da conta + esta parte` contra a cota, com o **mesmo `507` da conclusão**:

| quando | o que é conferido |
|---|---|
| parte com `Content-Length` | a conta fecha **antes** de ler — nada é gravado para depois ser recusado |
| parte sem tamanho declarado (chunks) | a conta fecha com o tamanho **medido**, antes de o temporário virar a parte |
| reenvio da mesma parte | a parte anterior sai da conta — reenviar não soma duas vezes |

Recusar uma parte **não** apaga o upload: as partes que já chegaram continuam lá (há teste).

### Dois defeitos da mesma família, fechados junto
- **O teto de objeto puxava um bloco a mais**: `receivePart` lia 64 KiB inteiros para depois recusar. Agora usa `lerNoMaximo`, como o `PUT` simples do ciclo 86.
- **A recusa saía em JSON, não em XML do S3**: o `PUT` simples traduzia `STORAGE_OWNER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` → `507 QuotaExceeded`; o `UploadPart` não, então o SDK não reconhecia o código. Virou ponto único (`noVocabularioDoS3`), para as rotas de gravação não divergirem.

## Verificação
- `S3MultipartTests` **+1** com cota de 20 MiB: três partes de 6 MiB passam, a quarta recebe `507 QuotaExceeded` e o upload continua inteiro.
- Mutações: a parte não confere a cota; a cota ignora as partes abertas; sem a tradução ao SDK — **3 de 3 derrubam**.
- Suíte completa: **4382 testes, 0 falhas, 0 erros, 3 skip** (base `92f64a7b`). 13 harnesses shell verdes.
- Sem migração nova.

> Fila: #995 mesclado. Nada aberto para `qa` antes deste PR.

Nada foi mergeado. Nada de deploy.
