author: omuhamma
body:
for head sizes 257-511

test_triton_unified_attn_prefill_head_sizes (from #5409) fails on gfx942 for BF16, head_size=320, seq_lens0: the kernel requests 131072 bytes of shared memory and the device has 65536.

Head size 320 pads to 512. On a 304-CU part this case launches too few 2D programs, so it runs the 3D split-KV kernel. kv_split "any" gives it TILE_SIZE 64, so the K and V tiles need 131072 bytes with a 16-bit KV cache. The head_size >= 512 rule that keeps the 3D kernel off for large heads does not apply, because it checks the head size before padding.

Add a kv_split entry for head sizes 257-511 with a 16-bit KV cache. It is the "any" entry with TILE_SIZE_MAX and SEGMENT_TILE_MAX set to 32. An fp8 KV cache already fits and keeps its config.

Compiled every case of the test for gfx942 (wave64, CU_NUM=304, Triton 3.8.0): on main only this case is above 65536 bytes; with this change it uses 65536 bytes and the other 47 cases do not change

author: bohnbawerick
body:
Assemblies now open, take parts, mate, save and reopen in the browser. This is the first entry of the ROADMAP phase 3 App-alongside line ("assemblies in the browser"), taken as this lane's second PR by decision C, so later assembly features can pass their app acceptance in the browser.

## What it does

- **New assembly** (start page tile and command) and **Make assembly** are on in the browser.
- **Insert component** uploads one or more part or assembly files. Part files dropped on an open assembly are inserted. **File > Open** takes an assembly together with its part files in one upload.
- The page has no folder, so it holds each file it is handed as an open document, with its bytes in the session's revision store. The assembly finds its parts there: to draw a part without a copy, to say whether it is current, for Update, and for the exact solid a mate needs.
- An assembly opened without its parts still shows them, from the copies its file keeps, and each part says its file cannot be found.
- **Save** downloads the `.dwasm` file, and the recent list keeps it.
- **Form subassembly** writes a new file beside the assembly, so it stays in the desktop app and says so in the browser.

## How

The browser has one thread. `OpenOptions::same_thread` (always on in the browser) runs every loading phase as steps that `poll` takes within its frame budget: one part's display mesh per step, then the sub-assemblies' freshness, then batches of parts' freshness. Coarse and fine levels load one per poll. `open_in_background` reads the structure the first time it is asked. The bounding volume hierarchy is built once loading is done. Before this, the loader started `std` threads, which the browser does not have.

An open document whose file cannot be read is now read from the revision store at the revision it is open at (`Lookup::current`, `Lookup::found`). On the desktop the file is read first, as before. `AssemblyDocument::save_with` saves to bytes and `open_bytes_in_background` opens from bytes. The loader's clock is `web_time`.

No geometry algorithm is new here. Exact parts are rebuilt on the page's kernel, as browser part work already is. The mate solver and kernel calls are unchanged. OpenCASCADE and SMLib have no assembly loader to compare with.

The new browser check found a fault the desktop could not show: wgpu's WebGL2 backend panics on a draw with a base vertex, and the assembly renderer drew each part from its offset in one shared vertex pool. Where the device has no indirect first instance, which is WebGL2, each mesh's indices are now written with that offset already added and drawn from vertex 0 (`viewport/assembly.rs`). The culling path on native and WebGPU is unchanged.

Shared code touched, kept small: `CommandSpec::hint` is now `pub(crate)`; `platform.rs` and `web.rs` uploads carry several files and a purpose (open or insert); `workspace.rs` routes uploads and browser drops.

## Results identical at any thread count

`tests/same_thread.rs` opens one assembly (two parts, a pattern, a sub-assembly, a part that moved on) with the loader's threads and on the caller's thread, polled with no budget so each poll takes one step. The two give the same definitions, states, freshness, meshes (every position and index), occurrence boxes and hierarchy size. Update gives the same report and result on both.

## Tests

- `soliddraft-assembly/tests/same_thread.rs`: the comparison above, levels taken a job at a time, and an assembly of parts that exist only as held bytes: inserted, saved with `save_with` (no file written), reopened from bytes, found current, built exactly, moved on by Update when a newer revision is held, and opened alone with its parts missing but shown.
- `soliddraft-app/tests/assembly_app.rs` `an_assembly_of_files_handed_over_saves_and_reopens_without_their_folder`: the app's byte paths, insert, save, reopen with the parts, reopen alone, and the `shown_assembly` JSON.
- `ci/browser-assemblies.mjs`, run by the web job (rule R2, with the later feature on top): in Chromium, New assembly from the start page, Insert component with the tray and the collar in one upload and the tray again in a second, then a mate picked in the viewport, the second tray's underside on the first tray's floor (from above, then from below). The second tray must stand 2 mm up. Then save (download), a fresh load, File > Open with the assembly and both part files: same components, same placements, mate kept, every part current. Then the file alone: same placements, every part shown and missing.

## Evidence

- Local, at the head: `cargo test -p soliddraft-assembly --lib --test same_thread --test assembly` (147, 2, 21 passed), `cargo test -p soliddraft-app --test assembly_app` (5 passed), clippy with `-D warnings` on both crates, `cargo fmt --check`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s ci`.
- `ci/browser-assemblies.mjs` on the web build of hosted run 44788478693 (this branch, before the last commit, which changes only the check), in Chromium on SwiftShader as CI runs it: passed. The frames below are from that run. The run first failed on the WebGL2 panic above, then on picks sent as slow press-release pairs, which the check now sends together.

## Follow-ups

- Browser acceptance for the Universal Joint mate (https://github.com/ZIGRAWBOHNBAWERICK/soliddraft/pull/347) comes next on this lane.
- Held files last for the session. Reopening an assembly from the browser's recent list shows its copies until its parts are uploaded again.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"J3vb"} -->

## What changed

At a place change, clients now close their connection as soon as the order arrives, and the server keeps the old session until every client it sent away has disconnected (dropped after `Net.CONNECT_TIMEOUT`). Hellos arriving meanwhile are held and replayed into the next session's handshake. A listen host follows with `change_place(place, true)`. New small node `PlaceChange` (`systems/net/place_change.gd`, child of `Net`) owns this. Protocol 28.

Also from review: a peer whose hello was accepted just before the change is sent away too; the dedicated server's empty-server reset is armed after the swap (else an empty match could run forever); `MatchEnd.check_squad` ignores calls when out of the tree or while this peer closes for a place change.

## Why

`tests/integration/test_net_deploy.gd` failed about half the time, on main too. The dedicated server swapped to the match at once while the client was still in Lantern Post sending `PoseSync`, so the server logged ~500 `Node not found: GameSession/LanternPost/<peer>/PoseSync` engine errors. A second cause: the client's old connection was never closed, so the server kicked a stale peer and later logged `Unable to send packet` errors on the way back to the hub.

Plan: none: bug fix in existing co-op place change, no new feature (docs/MULTIPLAYER.md updated).

## How it was tested

- Reproduced on main: failed on the first local run (499 engine errors).
- `test_net_deploy.gd` run 30 times in a row after the fix: 30/30 passed, no error lines in any server or client log.
- New `tests/unit/test_place_change.gd` (wait for every client, nobody to wait for, held hellos, reset, kick after deadline, late joiner, second change ignored).
- New `test_an_empty_dedicated_match_goes_back_to_the_hub` in `tests/unit/test_places.gd`.
- Full GUT suite: 2000/2002 locally; the 2 failures were my own leftover test processes holding a port and both pass on re-run. CI `test`, `soak` and `coop-soak` green.

### Ready to build
n.a. (small fix)

### Simplicity check
- Only builds what this phase needs: yes
- New autoloads, managers or base classes: `PlaceChange` node under `Net`: it owns the place change state (`_leaving`, deadline, held hellos) that moved out of `net.gd` (which was at the 350-line limit)
- New abstraction used in fewer than 3 places: none
- Anything a Godot built-in already does: none
- Dead code removed: yes (`Net._leaving`, `_drop_leaving`, `_leave_deadline`)

## Checklist

- [x] CI is green (`quality`, `test` and `soak`)

author: stasson
body:
Closes #565. Closes #573.

## Problem

A trial with opencode 2.1.4 (results in the comments on #565 and #573) found:

- opencode reads its global configuration only from `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. In the global scope upskill wrote to `$HOME/opencode.json`, which opencode ignores. So a globally installed opencode plugin or MCP server was not loaded, and `doctor --global` still reported it as installed.
- opencode 2 documents the `plugins` key. upskill wrote `plugin`. opencode 2.1.4 still reads the old key in a project file.
- A relative `instructions` path in the global configuration resolves against the project directory. So the rules glob cannot reach `~/.agents/rules/` from the global configuration.

## Change

- `opencode_config_dir(scope, root)`: the project scope uses the scope root. The global scope uses `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` when that is set and absolute, else `~/.config/opencode`. Every function that reads or writes `opencode.json` takes the scope, so `add`, `update` (including the repair), `remove`, `remove-mcp` and `doctor` all use the same file. `remove` and `doctor` take the scope from the `scope` that the lockfile records for each entry.
- Plugin URIs are written under `plugins`. `doctor` accepts `plugin` or `plugins`. `remove` deletes the entry from both keys. There is no migration, and the old `$HOME/opencode.json` is left as it is.
- The global scope no longer writes the rules `instructions` glob, so globally installed rules do not reach opencode yet. The follow-up is #581.
- `scope_to_plugin_scope` now takes the scope that `resolve_scope` returns. Before, it ignored `--project`, so `add --project` outside a git repository installed plugins in the user scope. This change made the old bug matter because it would write the opencode configuration to the wrong file. Claude Code plugins installed with `--project` outside a git repository now also go to the project scope.
- `upskill_cmd` in the test harness clears `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.

## Docs

The specification §3.4, the content-format topic (format-spec §7.3), `docs/book/commands.md`, `docs/book/support-levels.md`, ADR-0003, ADR-0008 (new section with the trial evidence and decision), ADR-0010, and `AGENTS.md`.

## Tests

- 11 integration tests in `tests/cli_opencode_plugins.rs`:
  - global file, absolute and relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`;
  - no global `instructions`;
  - project `plugins` and `instructions`;
  - global doctor and repair, `remove` and `remove-mcp`;
  - legacy `plugin` key;
  - `--project` outside a git repository.
- 7 unit tests in `src/ancillary.rs`.
- `just verify` and `just sanity` pass.

## Review

An independent review ran per task. The first pass found the `--project` scope bug, fixed in the second commit. The second pass approved both verdicts: the change meets the brief, and the code is sound.

body:
## Problem

- Every PR that edits `.github/CODEOWNERS` waits for team-security, but team-security only needs to review changes to its own entries.
- In the last six months, 4 of 38 such PRs changed a team-security line.

## Changes

- An edit to CODEOWNERS no longer waits for team-security. Nobody owns the file.
- The 17 team-security paths still need its approval through the `master` branch ruleset, which a PR cannot edit. GitHub requests the team automatically.
- The ruleset rule is already live.
- Docs now name the ruleset, not CODEOWNERS. This part is mechanical.

<details>
<summary>Ruleset patterns</summary>

A rule takes at most 15 patterns per team, so two patterns are globs. Each glob matches the same two files as the old lines.

```text
.github/workflows/ci-security.yaml
.github/actions/semgrep-ci/**
.github/workflows/codeql.yml
.github/workflows/auto-assign-*.yml
.github/scripts/assign-reviewers.js
.github/scripts/label-pr-from-title.js
.github/scripts/codeowners.js
*/api/authentication.py
```

body:
### Description
Replace `github.com/jacobsa/fuse` with `github.com/kislaykishore/fuse-pool` (`v0.0.0-20261111125536-4cc6b567a4b7`, `grpc-cpu-opt` branch) via `go.mod` `replace` to eliminate unbounded idle FUSE buffer retention after concurrency bursts and reduce per-op allocations:
- Replace `jacobsa/fuse`'s mutex-guarded `freelist.Freelist` (`[]unsafe.Pointer`) for `buffer.InMessage` (`~1.05 MiB` each) and `buffer.OutMessage` with `sync.Pool`, allowing Go's garbage collector to reclaim idle FUSE request/response buffers across two GC cycles instead of pinning peak-concurrency buffers for the lifetime of the mount.
- Replace the mutex-guarded `cancelFuncs` map on `fuse.Connection` with `sync.Map`, embed `context.Context` directly in `opState` to avoid per-op `context.WithValue` wrapper allocations, use inline `OutMessage` storage, and use stack-backed `iovec` slices (capped at `IOV_MAX`) in `writev`.
- On a mounted 100k-object workload (`orbax_checkpoints`, 128-thread `warm_mount.py`), idle `buffer.NewInMessage` heap retention drops from `134.88–139.53 MB` to `1.16 MB` (`-99.1%`), reducing whole-process Go `inuse_space` across the full optimization stack (#5217, #5250, #5218, #5212, and this PR) from `209.05 MB` to `62.34 MB` (`-70.2%`) after `ReadDir` warm-up and from `292.28 MB` to `107.34 MB` (`-63.3%`, with `-49.9%` `inuse_objects` and `-36.7%` OS `Pss_Anon` RSS) after `ReadDir` + `Stat` warm-up.

author: hello-alexmcc
body:
Stacked on #7478. This change is the one revision above it.

## Description

### Problem
A gateway under a controller's address takes every worker from that controller. Until the controller's first whole snapshot it holds none. A router then found no worker for any model and answered 404 `model_not_found`, which a client reads as final. The host's own refusal for that state stood behind the router's check and was not reached.

### Limits
| limit | what happens |
|---|---|
| The stored routes are named by path | The gate lets `/v1/conversations` and `/v1/responses/` with an id through. A new stored route is refused ahead of the first snapshot until it is named. |
| A controller that never tells a snapshot | The gateway refuses every placed request for as long. It holds no worker to send to, as before this change. |
| The public reads | `/v1/models` and the other public routes are not gated. Ahead of the first snapshot the model list is empty. |
| The cost | A gateway that follows a controller pays one clone of a shared pointer and one load of a flag a request. |

### Solution
One gate stands ahead of every router of such a gateway.

- **Where.** It is a member of the four protected route stacks, behind authentication and tenant resolution and ahead of admission.
- **The answer.** Until the first snapshot a request a router would place reads 503 `policy_controller_unavailable` with `Retry-After`.
- **Stored routes.** A stored response or conversation places nothing and passes.
- **After.** Once a fleet was told the gate is one load of a flag.
- **Elsewhere.** A gateway that follows no controller has no gate in its stacks.
- **Why here.** The gate guards the gateway's own HTTP routes. Its place in the route stacks, the paths it lets through and its answer are the gateway's.

## Changes
- `policy_controller/gate.rs`: `FleetGate` and its service.
- `policy_controller/host.rs`: `Host::fleet_told`, `awaiting_fleet`, and one name for the code.
- `policy_controller/mod.rs`, `server.rs`: the module, the gate in the four stacks, and one case.

## Test Plan
| case | what it holds |
|---|---|
| a chat request ahead of the first snapshot | 503 `policy_controller_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 1`. |
| a stored response read ahead of the first snapshot | It is answered by its handler. |
| the same chat request after the first snapshot | It reaches the routers. |

| row | result |
|---|---|
| the gateway's library less `middleware::wasm` | 4,924 passed, 0 failed, 21 ignored |
| the selection stage's two size cases and the context's size case | pass |
| clippy over every target, the formatter | clean |
| red first, the gate lets every request through | 1 case fails: the chat request reads 404 |

## Numbers
| what is read | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| a chat request ahead of the controller's first snapshot | 404 `model_not_found` | 503 `policy_controller_unavailable`, `Retry-After: 1` |
| a stored response read ahead of it | answered | answered |
| the gate in the stacks of a gateway that follows no controller | n/a | none |

## Release note
A gateway that follows a policy controller answers 503 with a retry hint until the controller's first snapshot, where it answered 404.

author: aborek
body:
WP-37 (part): a dataset's versions are its Iceberg table's snapshots, and tags and branches name them. The OS stops keeping its own version records for datasets.

## What changes for a user
- **Versions panel (Data tab) and MCP tools.** A version is an Iceberg snapshot of the dataset's own table, read as you:
  - `get_dataset_versions` lists them, with the tags and branches on each.
  - `diff_dataset_data` compares two versions (rows added and removed).
  - `rollback_dataset_version` restores one.
  - `tag_dataset_version` names one, as a tag (kept by every expiry) or a branch.
- **Plain Trino sees the same.** `select * from "<t>$refs"` and `select … for version as of '<tag>'` read them without the OS.
- **Per dataset, never per table.** A table that any other dataset maps to, archived ones included, is refused for list, restore and tag. The refusal names that dataset and sends nothing to Trino. A legacy name-only lane table is read-only.
- **Snapshot retention is configurable** (`trino.catalog.iceberg.snapshotRetention`, default 7d) and never expires a tagged version.
- **Who may restore or name a version.** OPA's write rule `agentic.authz.data_version_write` decides. A personal dataset can only be restored or tagged by its owner. A Domain or Company dataset needs a domain_admin of its domain, or an admin, the same ladder as My→Domain promotion. A builder is refused and files a request instead. The decision is asked before any query or write, and it fails closed.
- **The old version log stays readable.** The `os-versions-dataset` records are shown read-only as "Earlier definition history" (`GET …/versions?view=legacy`, `get_dataset_versions {legacy: true}`). They are read with a single `_search`; the index is never created, mapped, written or deleted.
- The Monitoring detail links to Data → Versions.
- `get_version` and `diff_versions` keep their contract: the definition history in git.

## Upstream docs used
- Trino 476 Iceberg connector: metadata tables, time travel, and `rollback_to_snapshot` / `expire_snapshots`. https://trino.io/docs/476/connector/iceberg.html
- PyIceberg snapshot management (`create_tag`, `create_branch`). https://py.iceberg.apache.org/api/#snapshot-management
- Iceberg snapshot references. https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#snapshot-references

## Tests
- `os-ui/tabs/data/lib/dataset-versions.trino.test.ts` runs on the lakehouse harness: Trino 476, Polaris 1.1.0, MinIO and OPA, plus the data-runner built from this branch. It covers:
  - listing snapshots;
  - tag and branch committed through PyIceberg to Polaris;
  - the eject read by plain Trino;
  - the `EXCEPT ALL` diff;
  - rollback;
  - expiry that keeps the tag and branch but drops an untagged snapshot;
  - a shared table with an archived sibling, refused and left unchanged.
- Negative twins: a tag that exists only in the OS does not resolve in Trino. Expiry really removed the untagged snapshot.
- Red first: commit a9d54786 failed in CI (module missing). The harness itself came up.
- Unit tests:
  - `dataset-versions.test.ts`: the resolution rule and the SQL input guards.
  - `version-migration.test.ts`.
  - `store.test.ts`: no `os-versions-*` index is written. This fails on main.
  - `images/extensions/query-tool/tests/test_execute_guard.py`: rollback shape, red then green.
  - `images/extensions/data-runner/test_refs.py`.

- Role rules: Rego tests in `authz_test.rego` include the twins (a builder, the owner of an asset, a domain_admin of another domain). On the harness with the real OPA, a builder and an admin of another domain are refused, and the table and its refs stay unchanged; the domain's own admin can restore.
- Legacy view: a read-only test asserts that only `POST …/_search` is ever sent.

## Deleted
- The write path to `os-versions-dataset`: `versionLog('dataset')` recording, `listDatasetVersions` and `restoreDatasetVersion` (about 60 lines), plus their tests (about 50 lines). The index and its records are kept and read read-only.

## Migration
- `os-ui/scripts/plan-dataset-versions.ts` is a dry-run plan over read-only exports plus `--repo <domain repo clone>`.
  - A record is `superseded-by-git` only when that repo's own log has an `OS-Object: <datasetId>` commit at or before the record and another at or after it. Otherwise it is `kept-unverified`.
  - Each dataset gets its table status: own, legacy read-only, or shared.
  - There is no apply step, and it was not run against any cluster. The index is never deleted.

## Not verified
- The UI panel was not exercised in a browser.
- No Spark eject was run; plain Trino was used.
- Promotion auto-tag `promoted-<approvalId>`, promotion by rename, `remove_orphan_files`, `optimize_manifests` and the Polaris principal split are the remaining WP-37 parts and are not in this PR.

piwero
body:
Part of #482: fixes the [dark-theme Task title comment](https://github.com/Piwero/tuk-tuk/issues/482#issuecomment-7046997207) and the same bug everywhere else.

## Summary

The dark theme only re-points semantic aliases. About 25 surfaces painted raw ramp steps (`--ink-50`, `--green-100`, `--white`, ...) instead, so they kept their light-theme colour on a dark ground. The reported case: a tapped Task row keeps `:hover`, which was near-white (`--ink-25`) under light title ink.

```diff
 /* tokens.css — each alias is the old ramp step in light, its own value in dark */
 :root {
+  --surface-tint: var(--ink-25);    --surface-soft: var(--ink-50);
+  --surface-track: var(--ink-100);  --surface-inverse: var(--ink-900);
+  --selection / --highlight / --text-disabled / --text-on-fill / --text-accent-inverse
+  --border-hover / --fill-muted / --success-border(-strong) / --heat-ink
+  --focus-border / --focus-accent-hover / --chip-ground / --chip-ink
 }
 :root[data-theme="dark"] { /* the same names, dark values */ }

 /* every other stylesheet */
-  background: var(--ink-50);
+  background: var(--surface-soft);
```

| Surface | Was | Dark now |
|---|---|---|
| Task row hover, out-of-month day | `--ink-25` | `--surface-tint` |
| Button / toggle / card hover (Calendar, Focus, Goals, Habits, Settings, forms) | `--ink-50` | `--surface-soft` |
| Check Item progress track | `--ink-100` | `--surface-track` |
| **Undo toast** | `--ink-900` bar, `--text-inverse` label: dark text on a dark bar | light bar, dark label |
| **Tag chips** | tint mixed into `--white`, label into `--ink-900` | tint into the card, label lifted |
| Habit complete cell / card borders and day number | `--green-*` | `--success-border*`, `--heat-ink` |
| Search match, text selection, disabled text, off dot | amber / blue / ink steps | aliases |

A guard (`darkThemeSurfaces.test.ts`) fails if any stylesheet outside `tokens.css` names a ramp step, or if a light alias built from one has no dark counterpart.

## Evidence

- **Before:** [phone screenshot from the issue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ef561bc-c81b-4510-b4ba-40d1a8e3dcfc): the tapped row is white and its title unreadable. The guard fails on 15 stylesheets.
  **After:** the guard passes; the full frontend suite passes (142 files, 1725 tests); lint, typecheck and the frontend pre-commit hook pass. Not yet checked on a device, so the dark values are untested by eye.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

CSS only. Reverting restores the old colours.

**Blast Radius:** cosmetic, dark theme

Light theme is unchanged, apart from one detail: a Tag chip with no colour now falls back to `--text-tertiary` for its label instead of `--ink-500`, a slightly lighter grey. Dark theme changes on every surface in the table above, so a quick look at Calendar, Habits, Focus, Settings and a toast is worth doing. Remaining hard-coded colours (shadows, the Voice button's `#fff`, the audio visualizer's brand blue) were left alone.

## Summary

The Sadran app on its own branch, `claude/Sadran`. This replaces [realShadi/Claude#2](https://github.com/realShadi/Claude/pull/2): same commits, new branch name. [realShadi/Claude#1](https://github.com/realShadi/Claude/pull/1) describes the whole app: a Hebrew, phone-first weekly shift scheduler with a shared Supabase database, many stores, legal pages and consents, and accessibility.

The latest commit adds two features.

### Hours for a whole day
- Under each day of the availability grid, a **שעות** button takes one stretch of hours for the day, for example 12:00–18:00.
- The hours fall into that day's shifts. With a 07:00–15:00 morning and a 15:00–23:00 evening, the morning is marked from 12:00 and the evening until 18:00.

- Someone available for part of a shift is now scheduled like anyone else, so that person is placed in both shifts. The roster, their own shifts screen and the export show their hours under their name.

### Order of priority per role
- Each role in the settings has a **סדר עדיפות** button, where the manager orders the people in that role.
- Automatic scheduling gives the role's positions to the highest person who is available, has the role and is under their weekly maximum, before anyone lower.
- Employees never receive the order: `sadran_load` strips it for them through `sadran.config_for_employees`, which is applied to the live project.
- The privacy policy, now page version 1.2, mentions the order.

body:
## Summary

PR 4 of 5 for the analysis sandbox (#84). Adds the opt-in `sandbox` Compose profile, so the whole chain `worker-analysis` → `sandbox-launcher` → `sandbox-proxy` → Docker runs in the dev stack. The first analyzers (PR 5 and later) can then be built against it. Production runs none of it until #92.

Refs #84

## Changes

- **ADR 0029** supersedes one consequence of ADR 0016. Dev may consume the `analysis` queue before an analyzer exists, behind an opt-in profile. Prod runs no sandbox service until #92.
- **Profile guard test** (`tests/unit/scanners/test_profiles.py`): no scan profile may select an analysis scanner. It checks every scanner a profile selects, so a new profile or check can't slip past it.
- **Empty `sandbox-images.lock`** (`{}`), copied into the dev and prod image stages. The services start but allow no image, so every `POST /runs` is a 404. Two tests load the committed file through the proxy and launcher loaders.
- **`sandbox-proxy` and `sandbox-launcher`** in `compose.yaml`, `sandbox` profile only:
  - Internal network with no route out.
  - No app secrets (no `env_file`, database, Redis or encryption key).
  - Only the proxy mounts the Docker socket.
  - The launcher sees the staging folder read-only at the host path.
- **`worker-analysis`** (`sandbox` profile) consumes the `analysis` queue and is the only app service given the launcher URL. `analysis` moves from `RESERVED_QUEUES` to `QUEUES`. Routing and exchanges are unchanged. `make down` now passes `--profile sandbox` so opt-in services stop too.
- **Docs and changelog:** `development.md`, `deployment.md`, `architecture.md`, `security.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `STATE.md`, plus the per-commit plans under `docs/plans/84-analysis-sandbox/`.

## How was this tested?

- `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run pyright` and `uv run lint-imports` pass (8 contracts kept).
- `uv run pytest` passes in the pre-push hook. Updated and new tests: `test_queue.py`, `test_makefile.py`, `test_profiles.py`, plus the lock-loading tests in `test_catalog.py` and `test_policy.py`.
- Not run: the live `sandbox` profile (`docker compose --profile sandbox up`). It has no analyzer image yet, and the lock is empty on purpose.

## Notable

- **Breaking changes:** n/a
- **Migrations:** n/a
- **New dependencies (and license):** n/a
- **Security impact** (tenancy, outbound traffic, secrets, LLM payloads):
  - The proxy has no caller authentication, and `worker-analysis` shares the `sandbox` network with it. This is accepted in dev and documented in `docs/security.md`. #92 must close it before prod.
  - `SANDBOX_ALLOW_RUNC=true` in `.env.example` is for dev only. Prod refuses runc.
  - Until #87/#101 register analysis tasks, `worker-analysis` drops `analysis.*` messages and the job rows stay `queued`.
  - Merge order: after 3d, before PR 5 (`84-sandbox-ci`: fixture image, a real lock entry, a runsc CI job).

Until now, Checkov (`fail_on_findings: false`) and Trivy (no exit code) only **reported**; neither could fail a PR. gitleaks and actionlint already blocked.

author: svenbledt
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Reported: in a city, a High-Risk player with Mercenary off could attack a player in Mercenary mode, but the Mercenary
could not attack back.

A Mercenary's client sees a same-faction High-Risk or War Mode player as friendly unless the server patches the
free-for-all PvP flag into that player's values for it (`ShowsFreeForAllTo`), which it does only outside no-PvP
areas, and capitals are no-PvP areas (the Mercenary also loses its own free-for-all flag there). The server already
accepted the counterattack (the attacker is PvP-flagged by its own attack); only the Mercenary's client refused.

Once a High-Risk or War Mode player (not itself a Mercenary) damages a Mercenary or applies a harmful aura to it, the
Mercenary is now sent that player and its pets with the hostile Mercenary faction template 1163 while the player is in
combat with it. The field is resent at that first hostile action and again when the player leaves combat, which sends
its own faction back.

## Validation and remaining limits

- New scenario `mercenary-fights-back-in-capital`: two High-Risk Orcs at the Orgrimmar gate, one takes up Mercenary
  for Hire!. Before any fight the Mercenary is not sent the other Orc's free-for-all flag. After the Orc attacks, the
  Mercenary is sent it with faction 1163, the server lets it attack back and its swings go out; after the fight it is
  sent the Orc's own faction 2 again.
- `python -B tools/verify_all.py --stages source,build,gameplay --base origin/main --scenario <all 12 mercenary-* scenarios>`:
  the 11 existing Mercenary scenarios passed; the new one failed on a setup assertion of mine (the server already allows
  the counterattack). After correcting only the scenario's setup assertions,
  `--stages source,gameplay --scenario mercenary-fights-back-in-capital` → `VERIFY ALL: PASSED`.
- `codestyle-cpp.py` passes on the changed file.
- Not checked in a real client. If the attacker is still fighting someone else when its fight with the Mercenary ends,
  the hostile view lasts until it leaves combat altogether.

AI disclosure: the changes and this description were produced with AI.
- Agent: Claude Code
- Model: claude-opus-5-5
- Subagents: none
- superpowers: used (systematic-debugging)

## Data/source dependencies

No SQL. Applied SQL is unchanged; no credentials, profiles or game archives are included.

body:
## Summary

A release bumps only the project's own version (`pyproject.toml` and the `trade-research` editable package line in `uv.lock`; e.g. f3b987500). `engine.config.describe` hashed `uv.lock`'s raw bytes into `dependency_lock_sha256`, which is part of Live's `REPLAY_CODE` (`live/runs.py`), so every release voided all Live replay evidence (`LIVE_EVIDENCE_MISSING`) and rebuilt the replay image.

User decision 2026-11-21 ("授权排除版本号"): exclude the project's own version.

- `engine/config.py`: new `dependency_lock_sha256(lock)` parses `uv.lock` with `tomllib`, drops `version` from the package whose source is `{ editable = "." }`, and hashes canonical JSON. Any dependency pin still changes the value.
- `runtime/image.py` `_require_build`: checks the image's reported lock hash against the revision's `uv.lock` with the same function (it compared raw bytes, and would otherwise refuse every new image).
- `.github/scripts/replay-changed.py`: a `uv.lock` diff that only changes the project's own version selects no replay image build (same rule as `pyproject.toml`'s version).
- `pyproject.toml`'s version is hashed nowhere (`RUNTIME_SOURCE_PATHS` holds only `engine/` files).
- `engine/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (breaking once: images built before this report the old value).

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p 'test_*.py'`: 2034 tests, 2 errors in `tests/runtime/test_source_identity.py` (fixture used a non-TOML lock); fixed, then `tests.runtime.test_source_identity` and `tests.replay.test_entry` rerun: OK.
- New `tests/engine/test_dependency_lock.py` on the real `uv.lock`: a project-version-only change hashes the same, a `nautilus-trader` pin change hashes differently. `tests/runtime/test_image.py`: a main build whose lock differs only in the project version is accepted; a pin change is refused. `tests/test_ci_gates.py`: a release selects no build; a pin change does.
- `uv run --frozen ruff check .`: passed. `uv run --frozen mypy`: no issues.
- Paired acceptance (engine/README.md), isolated `ledger temp` only; one research-draft source (`VwapReversion15m`, 15-minute signals, 1-minute execution) published, prechecked (BTCUSDT ETHUSDT, 2023-01-04..01-11, passed), fixture review, line `paired-acceptance`. Reference: `trade-runtime:main` (sha256:3e5918826f09…, rev 3dbbab973) run from an `origin/main` checkout; candidate: `trade-runtime:pr-3214` (sha256:d57a8fc699dd…) from this branch.
  - Pilot BTCUSDT ETHUSDT, 2023-01-01 warm-up, trade 2023-01-04..2023-04-01: both explores passed (audit included); `engine.compare_reports` passed.
  - Full set `--universe pool`, trade 2023-01-04..2023-02-01: both passed; `engine.compare_reports` passed (34 fills each).

author: tamnd
body:
## What this changes

Nine small corrections in Volume 43, found while writing the chapter pages of the Handbook:

- **ensemble-kalman-filter**, **covariance-localization**, **gaspari-cohn-function**: the Gaspari-Cohn taper with the distance along the 40-point Lorenz-96 ring is not positive semidefinite from $c = 11$ on (smallest eigenvalue about $-0.00016$ at $c = 11$; positive at $c = 10.5$). The EnKF pitfall said any Gaspari-Cohn weights avoid the problem, the localization entry reported the $c = 15$ run without noting its taper is invalid, and the Gaspari-Cohn entry and the localization pitfall gave the threshold as $c \ge 12$.
- **monte-carlo-criticality**: $k_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1.12006$ is the $S_{16}$, 320-cell value of k-eigenvalue-problem, not the $S_8$, 80-cell one (1.120009).
- **static-condensation**: the condensed matrix is a minimum of the energy over the interior unknowns, so it is the response of least energy, not the stiffest.
- **ausm-scheme**: the moving contact of the example moves at $u = 0.5$, not $u = 1$.
- **wall-functions**: at $y^+ = 11 < 11.06$ the two-law value is 11.00 from the linear law; 11.05 is the log law alone.
- **artificial-compressibility-method**: Chorin (1967) is in volume 2 of the Journal of Computational Physics, as the entry's own source says.
- **volume-of-fluid-method**: PLIC with Youngs' normals is first order, as piecewise-linear-interface-calculation says; second order needs normals such as ELVIRA's.

## Checks

- Eigenvalues of the ring taper recomputed for $c = 10, 10.5, 11, 12, 15$.
- Each other value checked against the worked example or source in the same entry or its sibling entry.

From a blind read of maidan.world, docs.maidan.world, try.maidan.world and the README by a reviewer who was not told what the product is:

- `book/book.toml`: the docs site's description said "the coordination layer for AI agent swarms"; it now leads with "the shared workspace for agent swarms", as the landing and the README do.
- `deploy/cloudflare/try/index.html`: Open Graph and Twitter tags and an icon (`/icon.png`, added to `TRY_PATHS`; the page's CSP allows images from itself only).
- `web/landing/index.html`: a `<noscript>` line with the three ways in (sign in or create a workspace, the live demo, the quickstart). Nothing changes for a browser that runs the page.
- `deploy/cloudflare/try/try.css`: dark `--muted` and `--primary-shadow` take the landing's values again. `try-theme.test.js` was failing on `dev` and nothing ran it.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the `lint` job runs `deploy/cloudflare`'s tests.

## Retrospective (PR-level)

- **Surprising:** a test that held the try page to the landing's tokens had been red since the landing's colours changed, and CI was green: the test ran only in the deploy workflow, on a change under `deploy/cloudflare/`.
- **Deferred:** `/favicon.ico` answers 404 and there is no sitemap; the landing's board names six agents and the README's diagram names five others. Both are noted for the maintainer.
- **Learned:** a check that runs only when its own directory changes cannot see drift that starts somewhere else.

author: redbackthomson
body:
Integration tests asserted run results by parsing human-readable output, and scripts had no stable way to consume a run's results. `--output=json` prints one JSON document describing the run, so `nix-tasks run a --output=json | jq .` works and tests can assert facts instead of text.

## User-facing changes
- New `--output=json` (never chosen automatically). When the run finishes, stdout gets exactly one document and nothing else:
  - top level: `version` (1), `targets`, `flake`, `system`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, `durationMs`, `exitCode`, `error`, `counts` (passed, failed, allowedFailures, cached, skipped, interrupted), `warnings`;
  - `tasks`, in dependency order, each with `name`, `label`, `state` (`succeeded|failed|failed_allowed|skipped|interrupted`), `cached`, `afterHook` (ran only because it is an after-hook of a task in the run), `exitCode`, `error`, `skipReason`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, `durationMs`, `log`.
  - The document holds the results of the run only; task definitions stay in the config and `nix-tasks describe`.
  - Every field is always present (`null` rather than missing); timestamps are UTC RFC 3339 with millisecond precision.
  - If the run fails before any task starts (unknown task, config error), the document is still printed with `error` set.
  - The exit code is the same as in other modes. `--output=json` with `--raw` is rejected.
- In JSON mode, each task that runs writes its full output to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/nix-tasks/runs/<run-id>/<task>.log` (fallback `~/.local/state`), referenced by `log`; the 20 newest runs are kept. Other output modes are unchanged.
- The schema is documented in `docs/json-output.md`.

## Testing
Golden test of the document with a fake clock (fails if a field is added or missing), run-log and pruning tests, and integration tests for the document, logs and exit codes. About 30 integration tests now check run results through `--output=json` instead of parsing text; tests of the human-readable output keep their text checks. Integration suite: 106 pass, with and without `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`.

author: yoona-asleep
body:
## Summary

한 GitHub Release에 앱 여러 개를 실행마다 하나씩 올리는 레포에서, 뒤에 붙는 앱이 먼저 나간 앱 APK와 **같은 versionCode**로 빌드되도록 `android-release.yml`과 `release-version`에 선택 입력 `version-code-from`을 추가합니다(android-ci v1.8.0). 릴리즈에 그 패턴의 APK가 있으면 그 번호를 쓰고, 없으면(릴리즈가 아직 없거나 그 APK가 없으면) 지금처럼 새 번호를 받습니다. 그래서 앱마다 다른 앱의 패턴을 늘 넘기면 어느 앱이 먼저 나가든 뒤에 붙는 앱이 같은 번호를 받습니다. 지금까지는 나중에 붙는 앱이 새 build number를 받아 두 앱의 versionCode가 달랐습니다. 입력이 비어 있으면 동작은 이전과 같습니다.

## Changes

- `release-version` (`code`)
  - 입력 `version-code-from`(예: `SleepHub_*.apk`): `asset-pattern`, `version-code-scheme: build-number`, release·preview 태그에서만 사용. 그 외 조합(minor-blocks, asset-pattern 없음, 같은 패턴, code 외 operation)은 API 호출 전에 거부
  - 재사용과 새 번호의 판단: 먼저 이 실행의 재사용 기록(`refs/reused-numbers/<major>/`)을 봄. 기록이 없을 때, 태그에 published 릴리즈가 없거나, 릴리즈에 패턴에 맞는 APK가 없거나, 같은 실행의 이전 시도가 자기 번호를 예약했으면 새 번호(또는 그 번호 유지). 그 외에는 재사용하거나 거부하고, 다른 번호로 바꿔 빌드하지 않음
  - 번호 출처: 릴리즈에서 패턴에 맞는 APK를 내려받아 `aapt2 dump badging`으로 읽은 versionCode. APK 이름에는 코드가 없을 수 있고, `refs/build-numbers` 태그 객체는 커밋·실행 id만 담아 같은 커밋의 QA 예약과 구분되지 않기 때문. 토큰은 API 요청에만 붙이고 파일 주소로는 넘기지 않음
  - 교차 확인: 번호가 그 major 범위이고, `refs/build-numbers/<major>/<n>`이 존재하며 태그 커밋을 가리켜야 함. 기준 APK가 여러 개면 코드가 같아야 함. ref가 태그 객체가 아니면(사람이 커밋 sha로 만든 ref, `git/tags` 404) 권한 힌트 대신 그 이유로 거부
  - 카운터는 건드리지 않음(새 번호 예약 없음). 재실행 식별을 위해 `refs/reused-numbers/<major>/<n>/app-<key>/<k>`에 실행의 태그 객체를 기록
  - 재실행은 첫 시도가 받은 것을 유지: 재사용했으면 같은 번호, 자기 번호를 예약했으면 그 번호(번호를 빌려준 실행의 재실행 포함)
  - 재사용한 실행의 재실행은 그 번호로만 빌드하거나 실패. 릴리즈의 기준 APK와 이 앱 APK를 함께 읽어 맞춰 봄. 기준 APK가 없으면(기준 앱 재게시 중 `gh release upload --clobber`가 파일을 지우고 실패한 경우) 이 실행이 그 번호로 게시한 자기 APK만으로 진행. 둘 다 없거나, 릴리즈가 없거나, 어느 쪽이든 코드가 다르거나, ref가 어긋나면 새 번호를 예약하지 않고 이유와 복구 방법과 함께 실패
    - 기준 APK가 없으면: 그 APK를 만든 실행을 재실행해 되돌린 뒤 재실행. 그동안 이 앱의 새 실행은 시작하지 말 것(빌려줄 번호가 없어 새 번호를 받음)
    - 기준 APK가 다른 번호로 다시 나갔으면: 재실행 대신 새 실행(그 번호를 재사용)
    - 이 앱 APK가 다른 번호로 나가 있으면(기준 APK가 빠진 동안 새 실행이 올린 경우): 그 APK를 만든 실행을 재실행. 이 실행으로 빌드하면 `--clobber`가 더 높은 번호의 APK를 낮은 번호로 덮어써, 높은 번호를 깐 기기가 받지 못함
  - 이 릴리즈에 이미 이 앱 APK가 있으면(같은 실행의 재실행 제외) APK를 내려받기 전에 거부
  - 한 릴리즈에 versionCode가 둘 생기는 경우가 두 가지 남음. README에 둘 다 적고 피하는 방법을 안내함
    - 자기 번호를 예약하고 게시 전에 실패한 실행을, 그 사이 다른 앱이 자기 번호로 나간 뒤 재실행할 때(같은 실행은 같은 번호 원칙). 재실행 대신 새 실행이 다른 앱의 번호를 받음
    - 기준 APK가 빠진 동안 붙일 앱의 새 실행을 시작할 때. 빌려줄 번호가 없어 새 번호를 받음(결정 3 문언대로). 기준 APK를 만든 실행을 먼저 재실행해야 함
  - 그 번호보다 높은 이 앱의 빌드(릴리즈 뒤 QA, 이후 릴리즈·preview)는 비교하지 않음. vX.Y.Z 뒤 QA는 다음 버전(X.Y.Z+1-qa.N)이라 순서가 릴리즈 X.Y.Z < QA < 릴리즈 X.Y.Z+1이고, 더 새 빌드가 깔린 기기에 옛 릴리즈를 까는 건 정상 흐름이 아니기 때문. 내려받는 APK는 그 태그 릴리즈의 번호를 빌려주는 APK와, 재사용한 실행의 재실행이면 그 릴리즈에 나가 있는 이 앱 APK뿐
  - 출력 `version-code-from`(읽은 패턴, 경로와 무관하게 출력), `version-code-reused`(`true`/`false`)
- `android-release.yml`
  - 입력 `version-code-from`을 code 스텝에 전달
  - 확인 스텝 `Check the number release-version reused`: 옛 release-version이 입력을 무시하고 새 번호를 잡은 경우 빌드 전에 중단. 재사용 여부를 로그에 출력
  - plan 제한 시간: 입력이 있을 때만 30분(APK 다운로드), 없으면 10분 그대로
- README(android-ci·release-version: 입력·출력 표, 새 절 An app added later with the same versionCode, 안전 규칙, v1.8.0 항목, ref 정리 안내), `action.yml`, `release.yml.example` 주석
- 테스트: release-version 52개(첫 앱 새 번호, 양방향 재사용, preview 태그 재사용, 더 높은 QA·다른 릴리즈·floor가 있어도 재사용, 재실행, 빌려준 실행의 재실행, 실행 순서가 엇갈린 경우, 기준 APK 유실 뒤 재실행 7가지(리뷰 재현: 30 → 유실 시 실패, 31 예약 없음 → 복구 뒤 30), 자기 APK만 남은 재실행, 유실 중 새 실행이 31을 받는 경우, 그 31을 30으로 덮어쓰려는 재실행 거부(기준 APK 복구 뒤·유실 중), `refs/reused-numbers` 생성이 ruleset 422·403으로 거부될 때, 태그 객체가 아닌 ref, 거부 조건, APK 리더), android-ci 9개(워크플로 연결, 가드 스텝 두 경로, 제한 시간, 입력 위치, 입력을 읽는 곳)
- 코드 규칙에 따라 이 PR이 더한 Python·테스트·`run:` 블록의 주석을 지우고 뜻을 함수·테스트·변수 이름(일부 타입 별칭)으로 옮김. `run:` 밖의 YAML 주석과 입력 description, docstring은 그대로 둠

## Validation

- [x] pytest release-version 428 passed, android-ci 949 passed / 1 skipped(JDK 없음, 기존)
- [x] actionlint `android-release.yml`
- [ ] 머지 후 sleephub-android에서 한 브랜드 릴리즈 → 다른 브랜드 추가: 기준 APK 다운로드·aapt2 읽기, `refs/reused-numbers` 생성(ruleset 허용 여부), 같은 versionCode 게시
- [ ] 릴리즈 없는 태그 push 시 `version-code-reused: false`로 새 번호
- [ ] 같은 실행 Re-run all jobs 시 같은 번호

머지 순서: 이 PR 머지 → `android-ci/v1.8.0` 태그(`tag-major.yml`이 `android-ci/v1` 이동) → sleephub-android develop·release/1.x PR 머지(같은 자리에서). 앱 PR의 `release.yml`이 새 입력 `version-code-from`을 넘기므로, `v1` 이동 전에 앱 PR을 머지하면 GitHub가 `release.yml` 실행을 "invalid input"으로 거부해 태그 push 포함 모든 릴리즈가 시작되지 않습니다. 앱 PR 머지 후에는 `v1`을 v1.8.0 이전으로 되돌리지 않습니다.

author: cru-self-healing-agent[bot]
body:
## Links

- Work item: none — there is no Jira ticket for this. Opened in response to Datadog monitor 312883915 ("MPDX React frustration rate by page [prod]") alerting on `/accountLists/?/hrTools/staffSavingFund/transfers`.
- Spec: n/a

## Description

- Reproduced the monitor's own query over its alert window: `a/(b+20)*100` = 5 rage/error-click actions over 7 views = **18.52%**, just over the critical threshold of 18 (warning 12). Confirmed as a real (if narrow) breach, not a false positive — driven by 2 distinct users/sessions on this one page, not a bot or single repeat-clicker.
- The RUM session trace for the dominant failing session shows the actual cause: a one-time transfer was submitted with the default "today" transfer date. SAA rejected it with `SAA Error: transacted_at cannot be in the past`. The user clicked **SUBMIT four times in 11 seconds** without ever touching the Transfer Date field — each attempt reused the identical, already-rejected input and failed identically — before finally opening the date picker, advancing the date, and succeeding on the next submit.
- `TransferModal`'s `handleSubmit` caught the mutation error, toasted the generic failure message, and reset `submitting` back to `false` — leaving the Submit button enabled on input the client-side validator still considered perfectly valid. Nothing stopped (or even hinted at) the user clicking Submit again on the exact same, doomed input.
- This fix rebases Formik's baseline onto the values that just failed (`resetForm({ values })`) in the catch block and disables Submit until the user actually changes something (`dirty`), with a short inline message explaining why it's disabled. The user's other inputs (amount, note, accounts) are preserved — nothing is cleared or lost.
- This mirrors a fix already shipped for this same monitor on a different page: commit `5c3c9761c` ("Close salary calculation submit dialog when submission fails") stopped an identical repeated-click pattern on the salary calculator by closing its confirm dialog on failure. `TransferModal` is a full multi-field form rather than a simple confirm dialog, so closing it would have discarded good input — disabling Submit until a change is made is the equivalent "stop the doomed retry" move for this shape of form.
- Checked `git log`/deploy history: no infrastructure or dependency change coincides with the breach window; the regression is this client-side gap, not a deploy-correlated regression.
- Out of scope for this PR: *why* SAA considered that particular "today" past-dated. The user's local date and the error's UTC timestamp are consistent with a client/server day-boundary mismatch (the client computes "today" from the browser's local clock; SAA may be comparing against a different reference), but confirming that needs the SAA backend, which isn't in this repo. This PR only stops the resulting doomed-retry/frustration pattern on the frontend; the date-boundary question is worth a follow-up with the SAA team if this error recurs.

## Testing

- `src/components/HrTools/SavingsFundTransfer/TransferModal/TransferModal.test.tsx` has a new test, "should disable resubmission after a failed create until something changes," that mocks `CreateTransfer` to throw the same SAA error seen in the incident, submits, asserts the inline message appears and Submit is disabled, then changes the amount and asserts Submit re-enables and the message clears.
- This container has no installed dependencies/generated GraphQL types, so I could not run the suite myself. Reviewer: run `yarn jest src/components/HrTools/SavingsFundTransfer/TransferModal/TransferModal.test.tsx` and confirm the new test passes alongside the existing ones in that file.
- Manual check in preview: open a Savings Fund Transfer "New" modal, pick the "To Account", amount, and note, submit with a transfer date that SAA will reject (or stub the mutation to fail), confirm Submit disables with the explanatory text, then change any field and confirm Submit re-enables.

## Checklist:

- [ ] I have given my PR a title with the format "MPDX-(JIRA#) (summary sentence max 80 chars)" — no Jira ticket exists for this safety-net-triggered fix; titled with the monitor id instead, following the existing convention used by this repo's other safety-net-agent PRs (e.g. #2109, #2135, #2160).
- [ ] I have applied the appropriate labels (_Add the label "Preview" to automatically create a preview environment_)
- [ ] I have run the Claude Code `/agent-review:review` command locally and fixed any relevant suggestions
- [ ] The `github-actions` bot has approved the PR (it approves once `/agent-review:review` leaves no open blockers)
- [ ] I have tested my changes in preview or in staging
- [ ] I have cleaned up my commit history

author: andrewbrooks
body:
W1 of the assessment and spec: fixes B1, B2 and B3 in the dry run's check for activity after the scope.

## Why
- **B1 (a bug in the code that shipped in PR #22).** `LookupInput.fetch` took truncation from the last page's `NextToken`. When a cap cuts partway through the service's *last* page, that page has no `NextToken`, so the check said nothing was cut off and reported itself complete. Reproduced with botocore's `Stubber`, and on a real account: `main` reports `complete: true` after reading 252 of at least 254 events.
- **B2.** With a cap the check kept the newest events and dropped the oldest, which are the ones nearest the scope's end: the question the check asks.
- **B3.** The home region was read first, so a busy home region could use the whole budget before the regions where the attacker was seen.

## What
- `fetch` uses botocore's `resume_token`, which is set exactly when events were cut off (checked on nine cases against the real paginator).
- The window is read in slices, earliest first: an hour, then two, four, eight and sixteen, then a day at a time, so a long quiet window costs a few requests a region and not one an hour. The budget is spent slice by slice. Every region is read for a slice before the next slice.
- Regions are ordered by in-scope events, home region on ties. A region that fails once is not asked again.
- `activity_check` gains `slices_total`, `slices_read` and `last_time_read`. The warning says "read N events through T of U ... activity after T was not read". A slice counts as read only when every region that could be read was read for it.
- The fake pager now behaves like botocore's, and a contract test runs both on the same cases so they cannot drift apart again.

## Things to review
- **A real limitation, stated in the docs.** A slice is still read newest first, so a cap that falls inside the *first* slice drops that slice's oldest events, the ones nearest the scope. The check then claims nothing beyond the scope (`last_time_read` equals `since`). On a real window whose first hour held more than 550 events, a cap of 450 found 29 of 32 later calls. The spec's "events nearest `period_end` are kept" holds when the cap covers the first slice. A 15-minute first slice would shrink the loss; I did not do it.
- The new `activity_check` fields are required, so a dry run from before is refused with the schema message. No `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump.
- Four existing tests encoded the old behaviour (one window, home region first, "oldest events not read") and are rewritten.

## Tests
`uv run pytest -q` 700 passed; ruff and mypy --strict clean; fixtures and demo up to date; no golden changed (only `schemas/dryrun.schema.json`). New: `Stubber` tests for the mid-last-page cut at the `fetch` level and through `check_activity`; the fake-vs-real paginator contract test; slice planning, ordering and slice-major call order; a failed region asked once. Reverting the `resume_token` fix, breaking the fake pager, or removing the slicing each fails the tests that should.

Verified live on the sandbox (no repo data): cap 252 on a 254-event window is `complete: false` on this branch and `true` on `main`; an uncapped window read two slices in full; capped runs report how far they read.

Three commits: the `resume_token` fix with the fake pager, the slicing and region order, the docs.

author: gshoe2006
body:
Adds `games/wayfield/`, a standalone browser city builder. It doesn't touch Inkline itself: no Python, packaging or CI files change.

## What it is
- **Gridless roads:** straight or curved streets, avenues and highways at any angle. Crossings split into junctions automatically, and roads over water become bridges.
- **Parcels cut to fit:** each new road cuts the land along both sides into parcels of whatever shape fits, so curves make fans and wedges. A parcel that would hit water, a road or a building is shortened or skipped.
- **Procedural buildings** generated from each parcel's shape, zone and level (1–5): houses, apartment towers, shops, stepped offices and factories.
- **Simulation:** zone demand (R/C/I/O), utilities that flow along connected roads, service coverage and land value, pollution, traffic routed by congestion, a budget with taxes, milestones that unlock buildings, and a monthly autosave to the browser.
- A tilted, rotatable 2.5D canvas view with shadows and a day/night cycle. Mouse, keyboard and touch controls.

## Files
- `parts/*` is the source. `build.sh` assembles it into `index.html` (open it directly in a browser) and `wayfield.html` (the same page without the document wrapper).

## Testing
- Drove it in headless Chromium with real mouse input: drew straight and curved roads, including one that crosses an existing road; zoned with the brush; placed a park; inspected a building; opened the budget and a data view; bulldozed a road. No console errors.
- Ran about 30,000 simulation ticks: the city grew to about 1,500 people with buildings at every level from 1 to 5. Saving and reloading restored the city.
- Checked the light and dark themes and a 390 px phone width (no horizontal overflow).

author: frankray78
body:
## Why

`/gaffer:verify` said only "not green ⇒ STOP", so each run improvised when a suite failed. One run called a race "a stable failure, not a flake" after a single re-run, and the issue was parked with the wrong diagnosis. Another re-ran the whole suite and carried on past a known flake on the operator's judgement alone.

## What changes

- A new *When a suite run is not green* section in `/gaffer:verify`, used by both suite runs (step 1b and step 3's re-run):
  - The failing tests are re-run 10 times with a new **optional single-test command**. Each is reported as `reproduced 10/10`, `intermittent, failed k of 10` or `did not reproduce, failed 0 of 10`.
  - Without the single-test command, the whole suite is re-run 3 times and the result is reported as `not determined, failed k of 3`, never as reproduced.
  - Each report says whether the branch added or changed the failing test's file. In every other case it says the link was "not determined", never "unrelated" or "known flake".
  - Verify stops if any re-run fails, and also stops if no re-run fails but the branch touched the test's file. It carries on, naming the test and its counts in the report, only when no re-run fails and the branch left the test's file alone.
  - Reports never say "stable", "deterministic" or "not a flake". A stop's verdict reason says whether the failure reproduced, e.g. `suite failed: <test> reproduced 10/10`.
- The single-test command is documented under *Build, test and format* in `defaults/CONVENTIONS.md`, with no default. It is also added to the template and the getting-started snippet.
- `docs/workflow.md` no longer says that one green run is the only bar.

## Non-obvious things a reviewer should know

- "Touched" means the branch added or changed the test's **file** (per the confirmed decisions), not the code the test exercises. That is why an untouched file is reported as "not determined" rather than "unrelated".
- `/gaffer:init` is unchanged. Its rule to copy the build, test and format commands word for word may already cover the new line.

**What breaks, and for whom:** nothing breaks. A repository without a single-test command now pays for 3 whole-suite re-runs when a suite fails, where it used to stop at once. Adding the line avoids that cost.

## Related

Closes #29

Incident: FrankRay78/NetPace#555

author: typat
body:
Closes gh-8230.

The `VirtualThreadMetrics` constructor opened a JFR `RecordingStream` without a check. On a VM without Flight Recorder this throws `IllegalStateException: Flight Recorder is not supported on this VM`. The common case is a GraalVM native image that was built without `--enable-monitoring=jfr`. With Spring Boot it stops the application at startup (spring-projects/spring-boot#52841).

Changes:

- The binder checks `FlightRecorder.isAvailable()`. When it is false, it does not open the recording stream and does not register `jvm.threads.virtual.pinned` and `jvm.threads.virtual.submit.failed`.
- The `VirtualThreadSchedulerMXBean` gauges do not need Flight Recorder and are still registered.
- `close()` does nothing when there is no recording stream.
- The class Javadoc says when the two JFR meters are absent.

Tests: a package-private constructor takes the availability flag, so the tests do not need a JVM flag or a build change. One test checks that the JFR meters are absent, and one (JDK 24 and later) checks that the scheduler gauges are still present.

I targeted `1.16.x` because it is the oldest line in OSS support. The same patch applies without conflicts to `1.17.x`. Open PR #7531 changes the same constructor on `main`, so the forward merge there may need a manual step. Tell me if you prefer a different branch.

Verification:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./gradlew :micrometer-java21:check` on `1.16.x`, JDK 25 | pass |
| same patch on `1.17.x`, `./gradlew :micrometer-java21:check`, JDK 25 | pass |
| native image without JFR, GraalVM CE 25.0.2 and 25.5: `FlightRecorder.isAvailable()` | `false`, and `new RecordingStream()` throws |
| [sample](https://github.com/typat/graalvm-native-reproducers/tree/main/boot-virtual-thread-metrics) (Spring Boot 4.1.2), native image without JFR, Micrometer 1.17.2 | fails at startup with the exception above |
| same sample with a local snapshot of patched `1.17.x` | starts |

I did not run the full build for all modules, and I did not run the tests on JDK 21.

author: strikersam
body:
## Run API: create, status, events, cancel and retry (reliability plan, phase 3)

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-11-14-enterprise-reliability-durable-execution-plan.md`, phase 3.

### New endpoints (all authenticated)
* `POST /api/runs`: queues a task and returns a `run_id` at once; an `Idempotency-Key` header returns the same run instead of creating a second one.
* `GET /api/runs`, `GET /api/runs/{run_id}`, `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events`, `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/artifacts`.
* `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/cancel`: a queued run is cancelled at once; a running run is stopped by its worker at the next lease heartbeat.
* `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/retry`: a terminal run gets a new run linked by `retry_of`.
* `GET /api/runs/capabilities`: which recovery guarantee this deployment really offers.

Another user's run answers 404, never 403. Run events are redacted on write.

### Known limits
* Tenancy is per owner (users carry no company id in this repo); admins see all runs.
* Cancelling a running run takes up to one heartbeat (`RUNS_LEASE_RENEW_SEC`, default 60 s).
* Create is not atomic across run and task: a crash between them leaves a queued run with no task.

### Evidence
Targeted tests: 212 passed. Full suite and the independent verifier verdict are in the comments.

author: sadbox
body:
**What**

`internal/eco/docker`: the docker ecosystem fetcher, `docker.New() fetch.Ecosystem`. Per changed `FROM`:

- Change set: only FROM image references may change (else refuse). Every reference must be pinned by digest (else refuse). Registries are allowlisted: Docker Official Images, `gcr.io/distroless`, `ghcr.io/<owner>`; anything else goes to a human.
- Built platforms come from the workflows (`platforms:`, matrix expansion, `--platform`, `runs-on`, `$BUILDPLATFORM` stages). The fetcher falls back to amd64+arm64 when it can't tell. It also records whether the stage is a build stage or the runtime stage.
- Its own OCI client: anonymous bearer tokens and a generic UA. Manifests, configs and layers are streamed with size limits, and each is checked against its sha256 digest. Layer diff_ids are checked against the config. Nothing touches disk and nothing from the image runs. zstd layers go to a human.
- Tag check: the pin must be current, or equivalent on the built platforms, or superseded (found in docker-library/repo-info history through a blobless shallow clone). If none of these hold, the PR is refused. If no history is available, the finding is `review`.
- No-op: when the platform manifests are identical for every built platform, `Update.NoOp` is set.
- Otherwise, per platform:
  - Config diff. Only `*_VERSION` constants and rebuild labels may change; anything else goes to a human.
  - dpkg/apk package diff. Added or removed packages, and a distro release change, go to a human.
  - File-level diff, where every changed path must be attributed to one of:
    - a changed package, with its content matching the checksum the package recorded;
    - an upstream payload tied to a moved version constant;
    - narrow build noise (shadow last-change field, package logs, ldconfig cache, build serials, apk index caches whose signature verifies against an unchanged key).
  - Anything left unexplained goes to a human, and each such path is listed.
- OSV.dev delta for the changed packages. Newly introduced vulnerabilities go to a human.
- Evidence: a trusted summary, plus an untrusted details file with the package table, config diff, unexplained files with line diffs, OSV results and the annotated Dockerfile.

Verifying package bytes against signed distro archives and upstream payloads against release artifacts is v2. Until then a `docker.archive-verification-not-run` finding keeps every non-no-op update at `review` or worse.

**Why**

Docker digest refreshes are the most frequent Dependabot PRs and the only ones a deterministic check can prove to be no-ops. The rest need a reviewer who sees exactly what changed inside the image.

**Testing**

- `go vet`, `gofmt`, `go test -race ./...` (offline with `-short`).
- Offline tests use recorded index, manifest and config fixtures from five real bumps, plus synthetic layers covering whiteouts, hard links, dpkg/apk attribution, checksum mismatches, signed and tampered APKINDEX files, config and release changes, OSV, the token flow and tampered blobs.
- `TestLive` (skipped with `-short`) downloads the full images. Routes: golang digest no-op → auto, caddy digest no-op → auto, ubuntu:26.04 refresh → human (the arm64 apt sources file isn't owned by any package), node:26-alpine refresh → human (arm64 from-source build leaves a cargo cache), golang 1.27.3→1.27.4 → review. Total about 23 s; the golang patch (490 MB) takes about 15 s.
- Not registered yet: the dispatcher (#2) is still open. Registering means one line: `model.Docker: docker.New(),`.

Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for this vanilla HTML/JavaScript portfolio website following the latest official Vercel documentation.

   - Vercel automatically serves this script from the `/_vercel/insights/` path when deployed

The project uses vanilla HTML/JavaScript (no framework), so I used the vanilla JavaScript implementation method from the documentation rather than framework-specific integrations (Next.js, React, Vue, etc.).

## Deployment Instructions

To activate Vercel Web Analytics:

1. **Enable in Vercel Dashboard**: 
   - Navigate to your project on Vercel
   - Go to Analytics section
   - Click "Enable" to activate Web Analytics

2. **Deploy the Changes**:
   - Push these changes to your repository
   - Vercel will automatically deploy the update

3. **Verify Installation**:
   - After deployment, visit your site
   - Open browser DevTools Network tab
   - Look for requests to `/_vercel/insights/view` or similar
   - This confirms analytics is working

4. **View Data**:
   - Return to Vercel Dashboard > Analytics
   - Data will appear as users visit your site

## Notes

- **No package.json required**: This is a vanilla HTML project without npm dependencies, so no package installation was needed
- **Zero configuration**: The analytics work automatically once deployed to Vercel

author: saitomarch
body:
Covers the Swift half of #164: every UniFFI operation exposed in the generated Swift API is exercised against a scripted transport, and each `FfiError` variant is verified to map to the right Swift error case. No mock server or network activity — `ScriptedTransport` returns predefined `FfiHttpResponse`/`FfiError` values and records the outgoing `FfiHttpRequest` for assertions; `BlockingTransport` simulates a hung request that ends when `FfiCancellationHandle` fires.

## Test matrix (SwiftTests/NativeOIDCTests/NativeOIDCTests.swift)

| Group | Cases | What it verifies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discovery (D) | D1–D7 | `FfiServiceConfiguration.discover` request shape (URL, `Accept: application/json`), endpoint getters, `.HttpStatus`, `.InvalidResponse` (bad JSON / issuer mismatch), `.InvalidRequest` (non-HTTPS), `.TransportFailure` (FfiError passthrough and `URLError` → `"HTTP transport failed"`) |
| Revocation (R) | R1–R7 | `revoke` form encoding (`token`, `client_id`, optional `token_type_hint`), `.InvalidRequest` (bad hint / missing endpoint, no request sent), `.AuthorizationServer` (4xx with `error`+`error_description`), `.HttpStatus` (5xx), `.TransportFailure` |
| Registration (G) | G1–G6 | `register_public_client` JSON body + `Authorization: Bearer` header from `initialAccessToken`, response `client_id`, `.ClientRegistrationServer`, `.InvalidResponse` (secret in response), `.HttpStatus`, `.InvalidRequest`, `.TransportFailure` |
| End session (E) | E1–E5 | `begin_end_session` URL (params, percent-encoding), state validation via `parseRedirect` (dynamic state from the generated URL), `.InvalidResponse` (state mismatch / redirect-URI mismatch), `.InvalidRequest` (missing endpoint / unparseable URI) |
| State JSON (S) | S1–S2 | `FfiAuthenticationState` JSON round-trip (`fromJson`/`toJson`) and `.InvalidRequest` on malformed JSON — renamed from `testAuthenticationStateJsonRoundTrip` to match the coverage IDs |
| Cancellation (C) | C1–C5 | `discover`, `revoke`, `register_public_client`, and `refresh` all complete with `.Cancelled` when the shared `FfiCancellationHandle` is cancelled during the request |

Result: 33 tests, 0 failures under `swift test` (arm64 macOS).

## Other changes

- `docs/api-coverage.md`: new "Swift UniFFI Operation and Error Coverage" section mapping each test-ID group to the operations and `FfiError` variants it covers.

## Notes for reviewers

- `FfiServiceConfiguration` does not expose getters for the registration/end-session endpoints, so D1 asserts those only through the discovery JSON, not via getters (noted inline).
- C5's local `NonResponsiveTransport` is a `class` inside the test (not `final`) because nested `final class` conformances to `NativeHttpTransport` failed to resolve during an earlier draft; it is confined to this one test.
- The Kotlin half of #164 will land in a separate PR.

## Summary
Recovery mails linked to the app deep link `uncasrugby://reset-password`. Opened on a PC, Supabase consumes the one-time token, the browser can't open the deep link, and there is no screen to set the password, so the user is stuck (real case: socio 15620, 2026-11-19). Recovery links now land on a public web page that works on any device.

- **Web**: new public page `/reset-password`. It uses its own in-memory Supabase client, so it never touches the panel session. It reads the implicit-flow fragment and shows the form only for a `type=recovery` link. The tokens are stripped from the URL right away. Rules match the app: at least 8 characters plus confirmation. body:
Closes #3.

## What
`gws_passthrough_<api>` for each API in the allowlist (directory, reports,
alerts, vault, transfer). Each takes a dotted `method` and a JSON `params`
payload; only allowlisted methods run, and anything else is rejected before a
request is made with the permitted list in the error.

Off unless `GWS_PASSTHROUGH=on`. No tool exists when it is off.

## Decisions worth reviewing
- **The tool registers as a read tool.** It carries both read and write methods,
  so dropping it in read-only mode would remove the safe half as well. Write
  methods are refused inside the call while the server is read-only, matching the
  spec scenario ("the error states that write mode is disabled").
- **`ToolResult.access` is new.** Registering the tool as read would otherwise
  make the audit log record a passthrough write as a read. The result now carries
  the access actually exercised and the wrapper prefers it.
- **The allowlist stays data.** `assertAllowlistClassified` runs when the tools
  are built, so an entry without `read`/`write` refuses to load.
- **No write method is allowlisted yet.** The write path is implemented and
  tested through an injected list. I did not add `users.patch`: it would bypass
  the curated guard that never sets `isAdmin`. Adding a write method is a data
  change that gets reviewed on its own.

## Verification
- `npm run check` clean: typecheck, biome, markdownlint, 51 tests.
- Fixtures: absent without the flag, one tool per allowlisted API, present in
  read-only mode, unclassified entry refused, unknown method with permitted
  list, read method executed, 404 mapped, write refused in read-only, write
  refused without confirm, confirmed write executed with `access: "write"`,
  allowlisted-but-not-callable method reported.

author: harshilbhuva
body:
## Summary
- Introduce a shared 10 MiB UTF-8 record ceiling for untrusted collector input.
- Enforce the ceiling in direct Suricata JSON parsing, Sysmon XML parsing, and Windows Event Log XML parsing.
- Reject oversized inputs before JSON/XML decoding or tree construction.
- Make each parser's `can_parse` reject oversized text without attempting a full parse.
- Cap Suricata's configurable source limit at the parser hard ceiling.
- Add regression tests for direct strings and raw-record objects.

## Security rationale
Suricata file ingestion already marks oversized records, but callers invoking the parser directly could bypass that source-side guard. The Sysmon and Windows Event XML parsers used defusedxml correctly against entity expansion but had no payload-size bound. A large XML/JSON record can still consume excessive CPU and memory without a size cap.

## Validation
Full backend tests, Bandit, dependency audits, PostgreSQL integration, and Docker build checks will run on this PR. No production data or deployment configuration is changed.

body:
## 무엇을 하나
4988 «폰으로 파일 내려받기»의 **웹** 조각(서버 · mobile 899 · 900이 짝). 웹은 파일 바이트를 한 번도 못 봅니다 — 셸이 봉한 조각을 열고 모으고 검사해 폰 공유 창으로 넘기고, 웹은 진행(`m/n`)과 끝 낱말만 앎.

## 동작
- 파일이 화면에 보이면 **[내려받기]**(셸이 `file_download: 1`을 말할 때만). 열기가 `too_big` · `not_text`로 막히면 그 자리에 «내려받기»를 권함(비밀 · 링크 · 숨은 이름은 권하지 않음).
- `downloadFile`: 셸이 봉인(OS 확인 **매번**, 창 요청 없음) → 요청 POST → 조각 0,1,2…을 **순서대로** 읽어 셸의 `files.download_step`에 넘김 → 진행 표시 → 끝나면 서버 요청 DELETE. 끝은 낱말 하나(`saved · refused(컴퓨터의 거절) · incomplete · save_failed · timeout · needs_update · …`).
- 시간: 조각마다 60초 · 전체 5분(실패한 읽기 길 · 늦게 돌아온 읽기 · 멈춘 읽기 포함, 늦은 조각은 셸에 안 넘김). 브리지 호출이 거절돼도 `failed`로 끝나 화면이 «받는 중»에 갇히지 않음.
- **그만두기 · 뒤로 · [돌아가기] · 화면 떠남**: 셸 열차 비움과 서버 DELETE를 **동시에 바로**(한쪽이 멈춰도 다른 쪽은 나감) · 늦게 오는 답은 아무것도 안 그림 · 한 번에 하나.
- BFF: `GET /api/desktop/computers/{id}/files/{command}/chunks/{i}`(자리 0~56만 통과, UUID 검사, no-store, 쿼리 제거) · `DELETE .../files/{command}`.
- 문구 ko · en(받는 중 · 그만두기 · 17개 낱말 각자의 문장 — «8MB 넘음 · Mac 앞에서 써 주세요» 포함). 목록/열기 거절 검증에는 다운로드 전용 낱말 `incomplete`를 넣지 않음.

## 시험
- 신규: `phone-files-download.test.ts`(길 · 모든 끝 · 시간 · 정리) 21 + 화면 시험 +14 + BFF 시험. 이웃 포함 가드 묶음 412파일 5977 통과 · tsc · eslint · i18n 검사 전부.
- 변이: 단일 앵커 47개 전부 사망(중복 방어는 삭제로 동등 변이 해소).
- 코덱스 3판: 1판 막을 것 2(셸 정리 꼬리 · 직렬 정리) + 중간 · 낮음 5 · 2판 높음 1(실패한 읽기가 시간 검사를 건너뜀) · 3판 높음 1(브리지 거절) + 중간 1 → 전부 반영, 한 건은 한계로 적음.

## 한계(문서)
- 셸에 봉인 요청이 가 있는 동안(응답 대기) 그만두면 그 요청은 셸이 자기 타이머로 비움(웹이 아직 모르는 것은 취소할 수 없음).

author: goldziher
body:
Closes #207, closes #208.

The plugin launcher downloaded releases only from a hard-coded GitHub URL, and basemind had no single list of its outbound hosts and no single switch to turn them off. `BASEMIND_RELEASE_BASE_URL` now points the launcher at a mirror, `BASEMIND_OFFLINE=1` turns every run-time download off, and `docs/network.md` lists every host.

- **Mirror:** `<base>/v<version>/` holds the platform archives and `basemind_<version>_checksums.txt`, as a GitHub release does. The archive is checked against that file before it is installed. With a mirror set the launcher asks GitHub for nothing, and a mirror missing the pinned release is named in the error with the files it needs. A non-URL value is refused.
- **Offline:** `BASEMIND_OFFLINE` stops grammar downloads, the Hugging Face model and tokenizer downloads (basemind exports `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` for itself and the daemon it starts), and the launcher's binary download. Each missing artefact is an error naming it. The launcher still runs a cached binary of the pinned minor.
- **First-use grammars:** offline mode now also refuses the download a file in a new language triggers, not only the scan bootstrap and `basemind lang install`.
- **`BASEMIND_GRAMMAR_OFFLINE=false`:** no longer means offline. Both variables read `1`, `true` and `yes` as on.
- **Egress list:** `docs/network.md` covers the launcher, the npm and pip installers, grammars, models and the tokenizer, with what triggers each, the variable that redirects it (`HF_ENDPOINT` included) and how to turn it off. lancedb's `remote` feature is listed as compiled in but unused. Linked from the README.

This touches `src/cli/env_config.rs`, which #342 (boolean parser) also changes. Whichever lands second uses #342's parser.

Tests:
- `test_mcp_launch_download.py`: a mirror serves the install and only the mirror's two URLs are requested; a bad checksum is refused and nothing is installed; a mirror without the release names the layout; a non-URL is refused; offline downloads nothing, runs a cached 9.9.0 for a 9.9.1 pin, and rejects a non-boolean value;
- `offline_grammars`: either switch makes `lang install` fail with the refusal naming both variables; false values try the download;
- `model_hub_env`: a model is requested from `HF_ENDPOINT`, and with `BASEMIND_OFFLINE` the error says offline, names the repository and sends no request;
- lib tests: truthy parsing of both variables, the `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` export, the refusal text and the offline gate.

Checked locally: clippy clean; lib `env_config lang_grammars embeddings::tests` (32 passed); `offline_grammars` (2), `model_hub_env` (1), `cli_parity` (14 passed); launcher pytest (88 passed, 1 skipped).

author: wils0ns
body:
A tool Draugr has no reader for reaches a report only through SARIF, and Draugr refuses its own result properties (package, priority, labels, reachability) from another tool's file, since an arbitrary file should not set them. Some tools, npm audit among them, write no SARIF at all.

An import now takes `format: draugr-converter`: a JSON file in a versioned contract that a converter writes in a CI step. Draugr runs nothing and reads the file, held to its commit like any other import, because running a converter at scan time would put arbitrary code execution inside the scan.

**What the descriptor grants.** The converter is declared beside the import: its name, the contract version it writes (`1`), and `sets`, which of a fixed list of properties it may set: `package`, `cwe`, `labels`, `reachable` and `raise`. Each adds evidence or raises a finding. `sets` narrows the list and never widens it. The descriptor is the reviewed file; the converter's file is rewritten on every run, so nothing in it can grant itself more.

**What no converter may set.** A file that sets a suppression, `aside`, `nonShipping`, `acceptedBy`, `origin`, a band outright, or `reachable: false` is refused with an error naming the property, whatever the descriptor says, rather than read without it. A file naming a different converter, a different contract version, or a property outside `sets` is refused the same way.

**Fragments.** A fragment may come from another team, and a converter's labels can steer routing through `labelBy` and the issue publishers, so a fragment that declares a converter or imports a converter's file is refused, naming the fragment and saying to declare it in the descriptor. A `converter` on a `source:` import is refused as a file-only key.

**Docs and an example.** `docs/reference/converter-contract.md` is the contract; `docs/guides/writing-a-converter.md` walks through one; `contrib/converters/npm-audit` is a worked converter with its own tests, README and manifest. The import's reference rows, the scanner doc and the schemas describe the new format beside `source:`.

The branch was rebased onto main after GitHub's alerts import (#2270) landed; the two sets of import keys are independent, and the docs and schemas list both. `make gate` and the sealed tier pass.

Fixes https://github.com/draugr-dev/draugr/issues/2194
