author: aytacpacal
body:
## Summary

Closes the gap described in #2617: the MPAS hydrostatic core uses the dry temperature in the hydrostatic geopotential and the pressure-gradient force, so water vapour adds no buoyancy to the dynamics. CAM uses the virtual temperature there (`geopotential.F90`, CESM2.1, lines 104–113), and our physics already does (`compute_heights_from_sigma(..., q_v)`).

- New switch `MPASPrimitiveEquationConfig.virtual_temperature` (`ExperimentConfig.mpas_virtual_temperature`, launcher flag `--mpas-virtual-temperature`), **default off**: existing runs are unchanged.
- When on: `T_v = T (1 + (R_v/R_d − 1) q_v)` from the state's `q_v` tracer (`legoesm.thermo.virtual_temperature`), and `θ_v = T_v / π` in the Arakawa–Suarez forms, replace T / θ in the geopotential and the pressure-gradient coefficient, for every vertical form: `legacy`, `as83`, `as83_logmean`, `sb81_theta`.
- Temperature transport and the compression term keep the dry T (a moist treatment of the compression term would be a follow-up).
- Refused with a clear error off the single-device MPAS core (validate_strict) and when the state has no `q_v`.

## Known difference (please review, @gentine)

With the switch on, the Arakawa–Suarez pressure gradient and its θ transport no longer use the same face θ, so the form's discrete energy conservation holds for the dry part only. The dycore energy fixer then absorbs the residual. CAM-FV avoids this by carrying θ_v; whether we should do the same, or move the compression term to T_v as well, is the main design question.

## Tests

`tests/atmosphere/hydrostatic/unit/test_mpas_virtual_temperature.py`, 12 passed on this branch (based on main 926ccef558):
- switch on: the momentum tendency equals that of the dry dynamics driven by T_v, while the temperature and surface-pressure tendencies are unchanged — for every vertical form, hybrid and sigma;
- switch off, and switch on with q_v = 0, reproduce the dry result;
- refused without `q_v`; gradient through the switch finite and non-zero;
- the flag reaches the constructed dycore from the production deck; refused off the MPAS core.

Neighbouring suites (`test_mpas_div_damp4`, `test_mpas_atmosphere`, dispatch hardening, validate_strict coverage, hardcoded constants, `test_run_amip_cli`): 6595 passed, 3 failed. The same three tests fail on the unchanged code at 86d8a4372e, so they are pre-existing and unrelated: `test_production_deck_selects_both_levers_and_no_other_deck_does`, `test_the_lever_walk_exempts_a_path_not_a_basename` (deck lever walk), `TestMPASSurfaceForcingThreading::test_no_forcing_runs_dry_default` (surface temperature missing in a dry-forcing test).

## AMIP test (2°, prescribed ERA5 land, Jan–Apr 1979, on the frozen base 86d8a4372e, legacy vertical form)

One change against the current baseline year (resolved configs differ only in this switch and the run length). Model minus ERA5 1979, cos-lat weighted, 2.5° output grid:

| | Baseline | Virtual temperature on |
|---|---|---|
| Temperature bias, global, 850 / 700 / 500 / 300 hPa (K) | −2.82 / −2.24 / −1.20 / −0.18 | −2.43 / −1.69 / −0.73 / +0.16 |
| Same, tropical sea | −2.68 / −1.39 / −0.55 / +0.10 | −2.21 / −0.59 / +0.17 / +0.65 |
| Net top-of-atmosphere, global (W/m²) | +19.5 | +17.0 |
| Reflected sunlight (W/m²) | 95.0 | 97.4 |
| Rain over tropical sea (mm/day; GPCP about 3.9) | 3.04 | 3.16 |
| 8-variable score, Jan–Apr | 1.305 | 1.298 |

Effect is clear (0.4–0.8 K through 850–300 hPa), but it does not remove the boundary-layer cold bias; the upper tropical troposphere turns slightly warm. The production `as83` form on main is not yet tested in a run.

author: roger-luo
body:
Adds adversarial edge-case tests for `@data`, `@match` and `@derive`. Behavior that already works is covered by regular tests; confirmed bugs are recorded with `@test_broken` (or `@test_skip` where running them is unsafe), so each one turns into an "Unexpected Pass" once fixed.

New files: `test/data/edge.jl`, `test/match/edge.jl`, `test/derive/edge.jl`, registered in each folder's `mod.jl`. Full suite passes: 1005 pass, 29 broken.

## Bugs recorded as broken

**`@match`**
- Literal patterns against `missing` throw `TypeError` instead of falling through (also inside vectors and for a repeated variable `(x, x)`).
- Keyword patterns on plain structs, e.g. `Point(; y)`, fail with `UndefVarError: y`: `src/match/emit/call.jl` emits `Core.getfield(value, y)` with an unquoted symbol. ADT variants are fine.
- `(a = 1)` / `(a = 1, b)` as a pattern overflow the stack: `show(::IO, ::Pattern.Type)` has no `Pattern.Kw` case and its fallback error message prints the pattern again. Tested with `@test_skip` because the overflow can hang the test process.
- Guards whose condition is not a call (`if flag end`, `if false end`) crash with `MethodError`, because `Pattern.Guard` only holds an `Expr`.
- A malformed arm (`1 -> 2`) or non-block body raises `MethodError`: `scan.jl` calls `PatternSyntaxError(msg; source=...)`, which has no keyword constructor.
- Call patterns with non-constructor heads (`1:5`, `sin(x)`, `1//2`, abstract `Shape(x)`) throw internal `TypeError`/`ArgumentError` from `fieldcount` during expansion.
- `nothing` is rejected as a literal pattern ("already defined in the module") while `true`/`false` work. Judgment call: drop this test if the rejection is intended.
- `Int128` literals are rejected as unsupported pattern expressions.

**`@data`**
- Duplicate variant names are accepted silently; `variants()` lists the name twice.
- An empty body fails with "Tuple field type cannot be Union{}" instead of a clear `ArgumentError`.
- Keyword constructors of generic named variants (`M.A(; x=1.0)`) don't infer the type parameter; positional ones do.
- A type parameter named like an existing global (`struct T end` + `@data Box{T}`) resolves to the global.

**`@derive`**
- `Hash` with a `Hash.Cache` field that is not last throws `UndefVarError: h1`/`h2`: hash variables are numbered by field index but the cache field is skipped. Plain structs are fine.
- `Eq` with a `missing` field throws `TypeError` instead of returning `missing` like tuples do (ADTs and plain structs).
- Containers of ADT values print the internal element type name `var"typeof(Tree)"`, since the wrapper type has no `show` method.

author: well-prado
body:
## What

The plan for moving Oby Artifacts from the lab into obid and the app: [docs/plans/artifacts-port.md](https://github.com/obi-ai-bot/oby/blob/claude/artifacts-port-plan/docs/plans/artifacts-port.md). It splits the backend plan's port step (§7.6) into thirteen small pull requests, each with:
- its contract's scenarios, each naming the lab scenario it comes from;
- the files it owns;
- its place in the order;
- the lab workflow that becomes its Blok proof.

No code. Each PR can become a task file (`factory/queue/tasks/B00-<n>.md`, sprint 0) once the owner approves, as #2397 did for `owner-workflows.md`.

The lab built and tested Oby Artifacts on a bench (#2682, #2689, #2709, #2713). This plan moves it into the house one piece at a time. Each piece is proven in place by the same test that proved it on the bench, now pointed at the real obid or the real app.

## Why

The orchestrator asked for the port plan before any port code (2026-11-20). Plans the owner approves live in `docs/plans/` with their tasks in `factory/queue/` (the roadmap is the task files, AGENTS.md "How we work"), so the plan goes there, not only in a PR body.

## How

| PR | Lane | Depends on | Scenarios | Blok proof (from the lab) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 Store v2 | dispatcher | none | ARTIFACTS-1 to 8 | `lab/artifacts/{design,shapes,blobs,types,rename,versions,limits}` |
| P2 Export and import | dispatcher | P1 | ARTIFACTS-9 to 11, WORDS-21 | `lab/artifacts/design` (round trip), `signed` |
| P3 The turn's artifact | dispatcher | P1 | ARTIFACTS-12 | `lab/artifacts/turn` |
| P4 Oby's runtime served | dispatcher | P1 | ARTIFACTS-13 to 15 | `lab/artifactview/render` |
| P5 Agent tools and the guide | dispatcher | P4 | AGENTMCP-8 to 10 | `lab/artifactview/check`, `lab/artifactsphere/taint` |
| P6 The artifact tab (obid) | dispatcher | the browser's ports | BROWSER-29 to 32 | `lab/artifactview/tab` |
| P7 The artifact tab (app) | dispatcher | P4, P6 | BROWSERAPP-21 to 24 | `lab/artifactview/sandbox`, as `app.*` |
| P8 Conversation, Export, Import (app) | dispatcher | P2, P3, P7 | BROWSERAPP-25 to 28 | `lab/artifacts/turn`, `design`, as `app.*` |
| P9 Sharing: format and checks | between owners | P1 | ARTSHARE-1 to 3 | the lab's `artifactsphere` core tests |
| P10 Sharing over the Sphere | between owners | P9, Dmytro's server | ARTSHARE-4 to 10, WORDS-22 | `lab/artifactsphere/{share,receive,taint,update,answer,refusals,signed,edit}` |
| P11 Public links | between owners | P10, Dmytro's pages | ARTSHARE-11, 12, WORDS-23 | `lab/artifactsphere/public` |
| P12 Share, Shared (app) | between owners | P7, P10, P11 | BROWSERAPP-29 to 32 | `share`, `answer`, `public`, as `app.*` |
| P13 Settings › Artifacts | dispatcher | P5 | ARTIFACTS-16, 17 | new, written red first |

- **Files.** No two PRs own the same file. `api.rs` (P2, P10, P11, P13) and `shared/words.ts` (P7, P8, P12) land one after another.
- **`jobs.rs`.** It may only shrink. P5 moves the writing of a Claude job's `obi-mcp.json` out of it into `jobs/owner_run.rs`, so `jobs.rs` ends shorter.
- **The phone.** A design draws only on its per-version origin (the app's `oby-artifact://<id>-v<n>/`). Through the API path it shows as its files until the phone has a per-version scheme of its own: noted in P4, not hidden.

**Decided** (recorded in the plan):
- the `age` crate, not our own writing of the format, its cost noted (68 packages, required `i18n-embed`, a future-Rust warning from a dependency);
- one origin per version;
- the Claude bridge stays the project zip.

**Open** (left open in the plan):
- **Dmytro, the blob cap:** a version may be 256 MB, and the plan capped a blob at 64 MB. Either (A) the Sphere takes 256 MB blobs, in parts anyway, or (B) obid cuts them into 64 MB parts. Both have their cost written out; **B if he doesn't answer**.
- **Sangam, the invite's words and motion, and every screen's words:** the lab's are proposals. The app PRs' scenarios name his boards, never the words.

### How we checked it

- Every file and contract it names was read on `origin/dev` at `fa19c191`. Two names were corrected in the reading: `owner_run.rs` is `jobs/owner_run.rs`, and the member's screens are `PeerThread.tsx`, `Home.tsx` and `SphereTile.tsx`.
- The next free scenario numbers were taken from the contracts: BROWSER-28, BROWSERAPP-20, AGENTMCP-7 and WORDS-20 were the last.
- `scripts/preflight.sh` (on the Azure build VM): brain, coverage, fmt and clippy passed ("preflight: clean").
- `gitleaks dir docs/plans --config .gitleaks.toml`: no leaks.

## Task and scenarios

The Oby Artifacts port plan. None of the scenarios are implemented: each is proposed until its PR lands and the owner accepts the contract.

## Surfaces

None: one plan document (`docs/plans/artifacts-port.md`).

- [ ] obid (`core/`)
- [ ] the Electron app (`apps/electron`)
- [ ] the iPhone and Watch apps, and what they decode from obid's API (add-only)
- [ ] the API docs, `docs/api/<area>.md` (index `docs/runner-api.md`)
- [ ] contracts in `docs/contracts/`
- [ ] stored job and config files on disk
- [ ] the check (`scripts/oby-check.sh`, `tools/oby-check-blok`, `factory/checks.sh`)

## Dispatcher, not harness

Each PR names its lane in the plan: dispatcher for the store, views, tools and tab; between owners for sharing and public links. Nothing is added to obid here.

## Failure modes

None: a document. The plan's own risks (Dmytro's server, Sangam's words, the phone's per-version scheme, `jobs.rs` only shrinking) are named where they bite.

## Security path

No.

## Summary
- Add a formal security specification for the Schnorr multi-signature aggregator.
- Document secp256k1 mathematical foundations and key aggregation.
- Explain rogue-key defense and participant-specific key coefficients.
- Derive the MuSig2 two-round signing protocol.
- Document nonce generation, nonce binding, and aggregate nonce calculation.
- Explain partial signature generation and verification.
- Document batch partial-signature verification and final BIP-340 signature verification.
- Add signing state machine and sequence diagrams.
- Analyze nonce reuse, rogue-key attacks, replay, side channels, and participant failures.
- Document implementation differences from BIP-327.
- Clarify that the current implementation is n-of-n aggregation, not t-of-n threshold signing.

## Testing and Verification
- SchnorrThresholdAggregator tests: 8 passed.
- Mathematical notation and Mermaid diagrams reviewed.
- No implementation or test files modified.
- git diff --check: passed.

Note: This document is a source-based security specification, not a formal cryptographic proof or independent security audit.

Closes #9183

body:
## True source-backed 3D engineering, research-only

The unchanged CC0 six-shell model has cuff-center spacing 574.71mm, outside the exact locked 500 ±36mm photographed hand-center target. This draft tests inward shifts of 0 / 10 / 20 / 30 / 37mm **per sleeve**, with a 145mm smooth vertical blend toward the actual original photographed hand-height guides.

- Runs real Blender 4.5.14 over the checksum-verified CC0 Human Base Meshes v1.4.1 source and existing actual six-panel authored cloth.
- For each bounded trial, recomputes **all 6 body/garment plus 15 garment/garment** 0.5mm world-space BVH crossing counts. Better cuff spacing is explicitly rejected for further research if even *one* contact-pair category increases.

author: sunkenintime
body:
It catches real disagreements. Each bug below was planted on its own; the default CI run failed on each and printed the command that replays it:
- **Server inserts two `pageContents` rows on `page.add`** (`convex/ops.ts`). Every sequence failed at its first page add with "the server holds this row twice". The old comparator stayed green until a later settings edit.
- **A strategy rename drops its folder** (`applyOp`). Caught at seed 1, step 41 (`strategy.patch`), because a third of the seeds now start inside a folder and folders are compared.
- **The array limit raised to 9,000 in Dart.** Caught at seed 2, step 51: an 8,001-point drawing that the server refuses with `INVALID_PAYLOAD`.
- **A server exception on text elements.** Reported as "seed 0, step 86: the server threw", with the exception text.
- **Sol's three false passes on `4630bd33`, now caught:**
  - The server storing `NaN` is caught at seed 18, step 82, with "the server holds numbers JavaScript cannot compare". Before, `NaN` compared equal to `null`.
  - `appliedRevision` off by 100 is caught at seed 0, step 2. Before, revisions in the answer were not compared.
  - Dart's array limit lowered to 7,999 is caught at seed 2, step 53, because drawings are now also generated at exactly 8,000 points.
- From the first version of this PR, also caught: `merge_invalid` answered as `field_conflict`, auto page names off by one, and a trashed page's revision bump.

Replay works across the fix: `--replay build/library_parity/seed-0-step-21.json` failed with the `pageContents` bug in place and matched once it was removed. The clean CI-size run is 24 seeds × 150 ops = 3,600 ops, about 66 s on t3os.

## What it is

- **`packages/icarus_library/tool/parity_scenarios.dart`**
  - `generate`: builds a strategy and random op sequences, and predicts each op with `applyOp`.
  - `replay`: re-predicts a recorded op list with the current code.
  - It refuses to write any number JavaScript can't hold exactly.
  - Payloads come from `tool/library_parity/samples.json`, which holds what the app's move-to-cloud encoder (`appendMovedPageOps`) writes for `test/fixtures/strategy_integrity/canvas-compatibility-v97.ica`. That covers agents (plain, view cone, circle), abilities including Paranoia v2, freehand and line drawings, text, images with a picture id, and utilities including the v3 custom circle. `test/library_parity_samples_test.dart` fails if the file goes stale.
  - It also generates an 8,001-point drawing, lineup groups from the fixture, and strategies in a root folder or a nested one.
- **`tool/library_parity/parity.test.ts`**
  - Seeds convex-test with the same rows, folders included, and sends each op through `ops:applyBatch`.
  - Compares the outcome and every row after each op using `compare.mjs`, which owns its canonical JSON and does not use the server's equality helper.
  - A row either side holds twice, a missing row, or a server exception is a difference.
- **`tool/library_parity/run.mjs`** fails on:
  - any difference;
  - a seed list or per-seed op count that isn't what was requested;
  - an outcome reached fewer times than its minimum. There are 16 minimums, including `merge_invalid` (13 hits in the CI run against a minimum of 5), offline field conflicts on elements and lineups, edits and deletes on trashed pages, and the oversized drawing. A 300-op run meets none of them.
- **On a failure** it writes the ops, the Dart version and the step count to `build/library_parity/`, which CI uploads as an artifact. It prints both `--replay <file>` and `--seed N --steps S`.
- **The server's answer** must hold exactly one result, for the op that was sent. An applied op's `appliedRevision` is compared with the revision `applyOp` gives the target row. The server's rows and answer are checked for numbers JavaScript cannot compare, and `NaN` never equals `null`.
- **Replay** sends the recorded ops byte for byte. It refuses a file whose step count doesn't match its ops, or whose ops don't read back unchanged in Dart.
- **The run fails if two seeds hold the same ops**, so a generator that repeats sequences under new labels can't meet coverage.
- **`tool/library_parity/compare.test.mjs`** holds 13 negative controls: a duplicate row on either side, a folder change, a rounded number, `NaN`, a wrong revision, an extra or misaddressed result, a dropped, short or repeated sequence, and coverage that names its required outcomes.
- **The samples also hold** a map door, a zone and a High Tide wall path, built through the app's models.

```
node tool/library_parity/run.mjs                 # what CI runs
node tool/library_parity/run.mjs --large         # 150 seeds x 200 ops
node tool/library_parity/run.mjs --replay <file> # the exact ops of a failure
node tool/library_parity/run.mjs --seed 3 --steps 80 --counts
```

## Left for the field merge agent

- Stale payloads in offline merges, where only the base is stale today.
- A stale `@sortIndex` base for lineup groups.
- Later fields surviving an older whole-payload write.
- Lost-answer replay and the refusal's `current` value, which belong with the store's cloud work.

Legacy page copies stay out because their ids differ from the server's on purpose.

## CI

It runs in the `library` lane. That lane triggers on:
- `convex/ops.ts`, `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/users.ts`, `convex/test.setup.ts`, `convex/lib/`, `package.json` and `.fvmrc`;
- the app's move-to-cloud encoder and the models and providers it serializes through;
- the fixture, the samples test, the package and the tool.

The job runs the samples test, the negative controls and the corpus, and uploads failure files. It needs no secrets.

**Not covered:** a noop's `currentRevision` is not compared yet. It belongs with the lost-answer replay work you listed.

author: egg82
body:
Removes the last two pieces of save-continuity machinery: the `saves-forward` CI job, and the journal's branch for days stored before `through` existed. Part of #401 (step 3). Stacked on #408, so review that first.

## Why
The owner has ruled out machinery that exists only to keep old saves carrying on unchanged. `saves-forward` loaded the previous commit's saves under every push, so it existed to catch continuity breaks. The journal's `through is None` branch re-sorted days stored before revision 0015 into page order every time they were read.

## How
- **CI:** the `saves-forward` job is gone from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, along with its entry in `ci-ok`'s needs and per-PR list.
- **`tools/save_corpus.py`** loses its `--load` half (the job's checker) and is renamed `tools/golden_saves.py`. I kept the writer instead of deleting it: `tests/saves/test_golden.py` requires golden saves for every readable format, so the next `FORMAT` bump needs it to write the new format's saves. That test is what keeps the upgrade chain (which stays) tested against real saves.
- **Journal:** revision 0019 backfills each `save_journal` row whose `through` is null with its day's end (a closed day) and makes the column `NOT NULL`. `journal_write.written` now reads every day as stored, and `journal_composer/order.py`, which only served that branch, is deleted. The build before this one already writes `through` on every day, and it reads a closed day as stored, so it still works on the new schema.

Worth a reviewer's look: an old save's days from before revision 0015 will now show their notes in the order they were stored, not re-sorted into page order. That is a one-time visible change to old journal pages, accepted under the owner's direction. I did not count how many production rows have a null `through`.

## Verified
- New `tests/db/test_journal_through_migrate.py`: a null-`through` day gets its day's end, a set `through` is kept, and a null insert is refused afterwards. It went red with the backfill value wrong and with the `NOT NULL` step removed.
- pytest with Postgres: `tests/db`, `tests/saves`, `tests/journal_contract` and the journal wire test pass. `mutate_suite journal_days --check` passes and `--plants` exits 0. Mutation rows 9, 10 and 15 were re-anchored on the new code, and `--run --only 9,10,15` kills all three. Row 16 was removed because the code it mutated is gone (row 6 went in #408).
- pyright over the touched files: 0 errors. The CI YAML parses.

author: shadowbrush
body:
Refs #2212 (slice A3 remainder; the umbrella stays open)

## What

`agentTasksPage` is `agentTasks` as a counted page, the `<field>Page` sibling in the A1/S1 pattern (`pageArgs`, `pageEnvelope`, `{ items, total, hasMore }`; hrn:node:hadronmemory.com:specs:cor:api:120:04). It takes exactly `agentTasks`' arguments and returns the new `AgentTaskPage`. `agentTasks` itself is unchanged, and so are caps and ceilings.

`myChatsPage`, the third A3 item, is already on main (#3225), so it is out of scope here.

## Contract

| | `agentTasks` (unchanged) | `agentTasksPage` (new) |
|---|---|---|
| Gate | `withReadableApp`: participants and the App's own key (cor:agt:050:21, #1755). A non-participant gets `APP_NOT_FOUND`, like an absent App | **the same call** |
| Filter | `agentTaskListWhere` (extracted, shared) | **the same helper, the same `where`** |
| Order | `createdAt desc, id desc` | the same |
| Size | `clampListTake` (default 20, cap 200); an `externalIds` batch with no limit reads up to 200 | `pageArgs` only (default 20; 0 is count-only; over 200 is served as 200). No `externalIds` widening: `hasMore` carries the rest of a batch |
| `total` | — | `count` over the identical `where` |

## Gate invariants

- **One gate, one filter.** The `where` construction moved verbatim into `agentTaskListWhere`. Both fields call it inside the same `withReadableApp`, so there is no per-resolver gate (CLAUDE.md "Authorization invariants"). The 20 test files that touch `agentTasks` pass, 599/599.
- **`total` never counts what the caller cannot read.** It counts the identical `where`, which starts with `appId: app.id` and excludes AT0 (#2553). A pin plants AT0 plus tasks in a second App the caller also belongs to; neither is counted.
- **The refusal is the old field's.** A non-participant and an absent App give byte-identical `APP_NOT_FOUND`, never an empty page (gate builder note 1).
- **The empty cases** (gate note 1): `limit: 0` gives `{[], N, N>0}`; a past-the-end offset gives `{[], N, false}`; a filter that matches nothing gives `{[], 0, false}`.

## Pins and mutants

`src/api/graphql/schema/resolvers.agentTasksPage2212.test.ts`: 6 tests. All were red at main `6a22634c6` (commit `a14f4a8be`), because the field did not exist. They cover:
- 25 tasks paged at 7: every task appears once, in the list's order, and `total` equals the filtered count for `tag`, `status`, `queued` and `rootsOnly`;
- an identical `createdAt` pages with no repeats;
- the refusal parity above;
- `total` confidentiality;
- count-only and past-the-end;
- a GraphQL execution of the SDL field.

The fixture fixes after the red commit are described in `d9a76abb9`.

Mutants, all killed:

| Mutant | Fails |
|---|---|
| `total` counts the whole App, not the filter | 3 |
| `total` also counts other Apps | 1 |
| Drop the AT0 exclusion | 1 |
| Drop the `id` tiebreak | 1 |
| Bypass the gate by reading as an App member | 1 |
| Turn the refusal into an empty page | 1 |

Locally:
- `tsc` is clean apart from the two known local `@prisma/client` stub errors in untouched files;
- `check-loc-scope`, `check-urn-rename-aliased`, `check:sdl-enums`, `check:sdl-hash-docs`, `check:sdl-spec-citations` and `check-graphql-sdl` are all clean;
- `admissionComplexity` and `admissionListPageCap4390` pass, 61/61.

## Admission

`Query.agentTasksPage` is registered in `PAGE_ARGS_FIELDS`, so admission charges exactly the page it reads. That is possible because the page sizes only through `pageArgs`, with no `externalIds` widening. A pin covers this: a 23-id batch with no limit pages 20 then 3, while the legacy list still returns all 23. The mutant that restores the widening fails it. The reviewed paged-field inventory in `admissionComplexity.test.ts` lists it too.

## Existing tests changed

`admissionComplexity.test.ts`: one inventory line added; `admissionComplexity.ts`: `Query.agentTasksPage` added to `PAGE_ARGS_FIELDS`. No assertion changed.

## Out of scope

- **The `hadron_task_list` more-rows hint.** The tool is wire-disabled by #3082 (`agentTaskTools.ts:290` registers through `offTeamTool`, which registers nothing), so a hint there would be unreachable. Xanthos amended the gate (#2212, comment 7049418739), and the hint moves to the CLI companion hadron-cli#2734.
- Everything else in #2212 stays at the gate.

## Downstream

- **CLI companion:** `hadron team task list` can adopt `agentTasksPage.hasMore` and print a more-rows hint. Filed as hadron-cli#2734 (Eden, team chat #125516). It waits on this PR.
- Portal list views can adopt the page.

author: mtdsvvzbff-stack
body:
One lesson line at the end of `.claude/rules/tests-and-ci.md`. Nothing else changes.

## What happened

On main's Windows shard 3/3, "Terrain digging" missed its 60 us budget for "a ray across dug ground" three times today. Linux passed every time.

| Run | Merge | Ray |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [44776306053](https://github.com/TwitchTheSniper/CallOfSlop/actions/runs/44776306053), 16:52 UTC | big ships | 60.15 us |
| [44806054094](https://github.com/TwitchTheSniper/CallOfSlop/actions/runs/44806054094), 20:00 UTC | in-wall bays, #355 | 61.71 us |
| the same job re-run, 20:22 UTC | in-wall bays, #355 | 63.16 us |

- Neither merge touched terrain code.
- I timed "Terrain digging" on Linux, alternating runs:
  - **Without the bays:** a copy of the build with #355's 105 data files taken out and its two tables reverted. The ray took 40.00, 40.59 and 42.41 us.
  - **With the bays:** 40.18, 40.70 and 43.16 us.
  - The dug ground was identical both ways: 2826 cells, 43514 faces, the same checksum.
- So the Windows runners' cost of this ray sits right at the budget. Taking the least of three rounds (added after an earlier 61.5 us miss) can't help.

## The rule recorded

- A microsecond budget judged on CI should be a ratio against a reference loop, run interleaved on the same machine (`CompareCpu` in `SelfTestCpuRatio.cs`), never wall time against a fixed number.
- Before blaming a merge for a timing miss, time the check with and without the merge's change.

## Not changed

The check itself, because destructible terrain belongs to another developer (CLAUDE.md, "Who owns what"). Until it changes, main's Windows shard 3/3 will keep missing it now and then.

## Checks

- Branch CI passed on the first commit (3 Linux shards).
- The second commit rewrites only that same line.

author: sannrox
body:
Closes #781

`rusui sync -workspace -follow SESSION_ID` keeps applying a live environment's unpublished tree onto a local checkout until the operator interrupts. Same command as the one-shot apply. Poll of the existing workspace export is enough. The environment keeps running. No write lease, no turn, no guest mutation. Operator git credentials stay on the laptop.

A new uncommitted environment file appears locally without a second invocation. Interrupt leaves the last applied tree. A dirty local checkout still refuses. Unknown, archived, and cancelled sessions end the watch with an explicit error.

## Lane

- claim branch: `feat/781`
- worktree: `.worktrees/issue-781`
- base SHA: `fefcfeae1f7f8c5eae013517ed5133f321bada18`
- published SHA: `4068be6f8b097da481d118d3f22a05692e46cf98`
- authority: Publish

## Reuse decision

- Job: keep a local git checkout matching a live environment's unpublished tree while a turn runs
- Verdict: Generalize
- Concept: #771 `rusui sync -workspace` one-shot apply, polled until the CLI exits
- Edge: operator git credentials stay on the laptop
- Searched: sync, watch, follow, workspace export, SSE `read/follow`. Rejected a new verb, a daemon, and a new plane subscription. `GET /sessions/{id}/read/follow` streams transcript/state/turn/service, not the working tree.

## Prior art

Pattern: Linux `watch` / `gh run watch` (rerun until interrupt, interval flag, leave last state). Skip gitwatch/watchexec/compose watch (local-to-remote or fsnotify). Skip SSE follow (wrong payload).

## Simplify

No new verb, SSE type, or background daemon. Follow is a poll loop on the existing export apply; later polls treat the last applied tree as not dirty. `-poll-interval` matches `rusui review`. Published-ref `rusui sync` is unchanged. Remaining growth: follow loop, last-tree apply, blackbox tests.

Production + docs ~+110 / tests +277 against the merge base.

## Verify

HEAD `4068be6f8b097da481d118d3f22a05692e46cf98`, clean tree after publish.

- `go test ./cmd/rusui -count=1 -timeout 120s -run 'TestSync'` pass (focused, published SHA)
- `make all` pass
- `make test` pass (`GOCACHE` in this worktree; `GOTMPDIR` left unset so unix sockets fit)
- `make validate`: docs, go-fix, golangci-lint, govulncheck, release, store-sql, workflow-skills pass
- `validate-shellcheck.sh` skipped: host shellcheck 0.11.0, required 0.10.0, Docker daemon not running. Host 0.11.0 on the same file set exit 0. No shell scripts in this change.
- Live Docker: skipped. Docker daemon not running. No container runtime tests added.

## Autoreview

`python3.11 autoreview --mode local --engine codex --codex-config 'model_provider="cliproxyapi"'`

scoped-clean, exit 0, no accepted/actionable P0 findings.

## validate-behavior

Skipped as a separate source-blind agent. `TestSyncWorkspaceFollowCLIBlackbox` drives the built `rusui` binary against a real plane handler and git checkouts for the operator-visible clauses: new file without a second invocation, interrupt leaves the tree, dirty refuses, unknown/archived/cancelled error.

<details>
<summary>Agent Transcript</summary>

**Goal**: Deliver a documented watch of `rusui sync -workspace` for issue 781 and publish a ready PR. Do not land.

**Key decisions**:
- Same verb, `-follow` flag. Poll the existing workspace export.
- No SSE subscription: follow stream has no working-tree events.
- After the first apply, dirt that still matches the last applied tree is ours and may be replaced. Operator dirt still refuses.
- `-poll-interval` is a production flag (default 1s), used by tests at 20ms.

**Changes made**:
- `rusui sync -workspace -follow` poll loop with interrupt leave-last-tree
- last-applied dirty exception and force checkout overlay
- docs on the local-interactive how-to and the export HTTP row

**Verification**:
- focused sync tests: pass
- make all / make test: pass
- make validate: pass except Docker shellcheck skip
- autoreview: scoped-clean

**Skipped/deferred**:
- bidirectional watch
- background daemon
- land (Publish only)

</details>

## Resumo

A suíte das fontes de auditoria passa a injetar o fetch em cada cenário, em vez de substituir o transporte global. Testes repetidos foram consolidados; os casos de DNS, RDAP, e-mail, conteúdo e PageSpeed continuam observando relatórios e mensagens públicas pela interface das fontes.

Um único caso mantém a substituição do fetch global, com restauração após o teste, para provar o caminho padrão quando as dependências são omitidas. O código de produção permanece igual.

## Evidências

`npm run check` passou com 436 testes, e `npm run build` passou. A suíte de sources passou de 29 para 24 testes após a consolidação dos cenários repetidos, com um caso adicional de erro HTTP DoH.

Clean-crap não se aplica ao diff, composto apenas por arquivo de testes. Verificação de runtime e captura visual não se aplicam porque a mudança está restrita à suíte de testes.

## Impacto e reversão

Os testes principais deixam de compartilhar o fetch global. Não há mudança de contrato, dados ou configuração externa. Reverter o commit restaura a suíte anterior.

author: zedmor
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** A red run of `CI` on main is recorded in the `Main is red:` issue even when the shared GitHub API rate limit is spent while the watcher runs: the watcher waits for a reset that is at most 20 minutes away, and a red run it still could not record is counted by the next red run, so the issue names the true first red commit and streak.

`main-red-watch.yml` made every API call once. When the installation rate limit was spent, the step ended on the first refused call and wrote nothing. On 2026-11-20 two of the three watcher runs for one break died this way (44707515602 and 44717637517: `Could not ensure the main-red label; looking up the issue by title prefix.`, then `gh: API rate limit exceeded for installation`, exit 1). #39917 was opened 41 minutes after the first red run ended, names the second red commit as "first red", and its streak stayed at 1 across three red runs.

## Why it matters

The pull request skip list (`scripts/ci_main_red_skip.py`) and the pull request notice (`main-red-pr-notice.yml`) act only once that issue exists. Between the first red run and the issue, 23 of 32 pull request `CI` runs that reached a verdict failed on the three tests that were already red on main. A busy hour is what spends the shared limit, and a red main makes the hour busier, so the watcher failed exactly when it was needed.

## Not a goal

- Changing when main counts as red: the two rules that open an issue (a test red in two failed jobs of a run; a test file red in one job of two verdict runs in a row) and the rule that closes one are unchanged, and are the rules the replay applies.
- Waiting for a reset more than 20 minutes away, or storing anything between runs (a marker for a lost run, a cache, a published state).
- Closing an issue for a green run the watcher lost. The next full green run closes it, as before.
- The rate-limit handling of other workflows (`main-red-pr-notice.yml`, `main-macos-failure-watch.yml`, `scheduled-failure-watch.yml`), of `scripts/ci_main_red_skip.py` (#40006) and of the suspected-red issue from pull request runs (#39792).
- Changing `.github/actions/gh-rate-limit`.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

**Cause.** The step runs under `set -euo pipefail`. The label call and the reads of the failed jobs were guarded (a notice, or the reading stops). These were not, and a refusal on any of them ended the step: the job list of the run (red and green path), both `gh issue list` lookups, `gh issue edit`, `comment`, `close`, and the unlabelled `gh issue create`. Both runs in the evidence died on the job list. Nothing waited, and no later run looked back.

**1. Wait, bounded.** The job installs `.github/actions/gh-rate-limit` (`max-wait: 1200`) before the step, so every `gh` call, guarded or not, waits for the reset `/rate_limit` reports and is retried, out of one 20-minute budget. `timeout-minutes` goes from 10 to 30 to hold it. #40006 could not use this wrapper (a `urllib` read in a job that gates every other job); here every call is `gh` and the job gates nothing.

**2. Replay what was lost.** A reset past the budget still fails the run, and a run that cannot call the API cannot leave a marker. So every red run that names a test reads the run list (one call) and replays the red verdict runs directly before it that no issue's record holds: back to the first green run, to the last run a record holds, or 5 runs. The record is the open issue's; with none open it is the newest among the closed watcher issues (two more reads: the labelled list and the 200 newest closed issues of any label), because an issue closed while main was red leaves no green run and its runs were recorded. Per run: one job list and one annotation read per failed job. `main_red_previous.py replay` applies the watcher's own rules in order and writes the record a watcher would have left; the run then adds itself to it as it does to an open issue.

- With a record open, a replayed run counts when it names a failing test. With none, only when a test is red in two of its jobs or its jobs share a test file with the verdict run before it. The replay opens no issue: with none open, this run opens one only by its own failures under the two existing rules, and the replayed record then names the first red run.
- A replay that cannot read a run, or the closed issues, counts none, says so in a notice and the job summary, and the run writes what it would have without it.
- A green run replays nothing: what a replay would add, the same run closes.
- It also counts a run whose watcher was dropped from the queue.

**Applied to 2026-11-20.** The second watcher replays the first run and opens the issue with a streak of 2. The fourth replays the lost third: streak 4.

**Cost.** One more read on every red run that names a test; the worst case is 5 replayed runs of 21 reads.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: the issue's title, body shape, labels and state record are unchanged, as are the rules that open, update and close it; a watcher run can now take up to 20 minutes longer when the limit is spent, and the first-red commit and streak can name runs before the one that opened the issue.

Removes nothing: no command, output or record field is removed; `previous-verdict` and `same-files` keep their arguments and output, and `previous_verdict()` keeps its signature.

## Tests

Proof: PROVEN test/test_main_red_rate_limit.py::test_a_limit_spent_from_the_first_call_is_waited_out_once_and_the_issue_is_filed[stand-in], test/test_main_red_rate_limit.py::test_a_refused_issue_lookup_is_waited_out_and_the_open_issue_is_updated[stand-in], test/test_main_red_rate_limit.py::test_a_refused_read_of_the_failed_jobs_is_waited_out_and_the_issue_is_filed[stand-in-job-list], test/test_main_red_rate_limit.py::test_a_red_run_no_watcher_recorded_is_named_first_red_by_the_next_red_run[stand-in] (head ca653b3f39d2)

The step tests run the workflow's own step script with `gh` stubbed, as before, and now run it the way the job does: the harness executes the action's install script, so the step's `gh` is the real wrapper in front of the stub. `date +%s` answers a fixed clock and `sleep` records the wait and stands in for the reset, so nothing sleeps and each wait is an exact number (`test/main_red_rate_limit_harness.py`). With the workflow and script of main under the tests of this head, 44 of the 227 tests in the two main-red step test files fail. `prove.py` produced the same verdict on the first commit and then timed out three times on this shared host (its two serial runs exceed 900 s there), so the line above comes from the same revert done by hand in a throwaway worktree, with 4 workers.

New, in `test/test_main_red_rate_limit.py`:

- The three runs of the issue. A limit spent from the first call (the label call is refused first): one 605 s wait, then a labelled issue. A refused issue lookup with an issue open: one wait, the open issue is updated, none is created. A refused job list, and a refused annotation read: one wait, the issue is filed with the full set.
- A green run waits out a refused lookup, then comments and closes.
- A reset past the budget, on a red and on a green run with an issue open: no wait, exit 1, no create, edit, comment or close.
- Replay: a red run no watcher recorded is named first red by the next red run, with a streak of 2 and the notice in the log and the summary. A red run missed while the issue was open adds to its streak and keeps its first red commit. What the replay counts opens no issue for a run red in one job on another test; the same run red on the lost run's test file opens it by the look back and names the lost run first red. A lost run red in one job on another test file changes nothing about when an issue opens, and is read once for the replay and the look back together. A green run ends the walk back. A replay read refused inside the budget is waited out; one refused past it counts no run and the run is still recorded.

author: gregpriday
body:
An answered question whose agent asks for a reply (`expects_reply: true`) goes back to Needs you, and until now nothing on the desktop could end that wait: Dismiss and Withdraw are refused for answered questions, and Clear only hides it on this computer while every phone keeps waiting.

Resolves #18030

## What changes

- **Decline to reply** sits beside **Send reply** in the follow-up composer (question view and inbox detail) for a human- or proxy-answered question whose agent's latest message still asks for a reply. A confirmation shows the agent's request and the exact words sent: "I won't reply to this, so don't wait for a reply from me."
- Confirmed, it goes as the person's own follow-up through the existing owner-signed path. Once the relay takes it, `threadAwaitsHuman` stops waiting on desktop and phones alike, the agent gets it typed into its terminal, and the answer is untouched.
- The decline is bound to the request it was confirmed for: the read before signing, and the recovery of a lost reply before any resend, refuse it ("answered or replaced") unless that same request is still outstanding. A lost decline is resent only under its own id, and its id is kept for Retry while a send of it past main's deadline could still commit.
- It never touches the draft, starts nothing while the answer's delivery is stalled (#18028) or the surface is closing, and its confirmation closes for good if the request moves, a stall arrives or the surface closes.
- A follow-up that couldn't be typed in now points at Needs attention in the Decisions inbox instead of a terminal menu that may be gone.
- New row in `docs/architecture/destructive-action-safeguards.md` for the direct-IPC confirmation.

## What the desktop can and can't settle

Protocol 0.9.0 has no record of a declined reply request (`cancel` refuses human-answered questions, a person's decline refuses anything not open, and withdrawing a proxy-answered question would cancel its answer). A person-signed message is the one record that ends the wait on every device without touching the answer, so that is what this sends. Gaps that only the protocol can close are filed as daintreehq/decisions#214:

- The message names no request. If the agent's newer request reaches the relay before the decline, the decline ends that wait too (ordinary **Send reply** has the same race).
- A request posted as the thread's 200th message can't be declined; the relay refuses it and the composer says nothing was sent.
- Phones show it as a message, not as a decline.
- A request whose terminal has gone still waits until the person declines it. The decline itself then reopens the agent's session where Daintree can, or lands under Needs attention, where **Resolve delivery** / **Mark handled** is the way out.

## Testing

- Own: `DecisionFollowUpComposer.test.tsx` (decline flow: confirm and cancel, fixed words, draft kept, request replaced or answered by a phone before the send, confirmation closing on a replaced request or a stall and never reopening on its own, the pause, lost decline resent under the same id, lost decline dropped after its request moved), `decisionFollowUpModel.test.ts`, and a new `decisionFollowUpSend.test.ts` for sends still out past the deadline. Mutations of the request guard, the confirmation reset and both deadline checks each fail a test.
- Adjacent: question view, inbox, and host dialog tests.
- Impact: 250 of 5398 test files (4.6%) through spotexec, all green (5965 tests).
- `sx typecheck` green; eslint and prettier clean on the changed files.

## Resumo

Implementa a **Etapa 3 (Onda 8)** do plano de evolução — entrega das 3 frentes de produto de alto valor:

### 1. PWA com suporte offline real
- **Service Worker versionado (`public/sw.js`)**: faz cache do shell estático com estratégia *stale-while-revalidate* e fallback de navegação para `/index.html`, sem nunca cachear respostas de `/api/*`. Servido com `Cache-Control: no-store` em `src/routes/assets.ts` para atualização imediata no navegador.
- **Modo leitura offline (`public/js/api.js`, `public/app.js`, `public/js/state.js`)**: persiste o último mês carregado em `localStorage` (limpo automaticamente em logout/401), abre em modo somente-leitura com banner discreto quando sem conexão (`editable()` bloqueia mutações offline) e reconecta automaticamente no evento `online`.

### 2. Backup e exportação CSV / JSON
- **Backend (`src/repos/export.ts`, `src/routes/export.ts`)**: `GET /api/export?format=csv|json&monthId=...` isolado por `scope.ownerId`, carregando todo o orçamento em um único `db.batch`. O CSV inclui BOM UTF-8 (`EF BB BF`), separador `;` (padrão Excel/Sheets pt-BR) e proteção contra *CSV formula injection* (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`).
- **Frontend (`public/js/account.js`, `public/js/sheets/render-account.js`)**: item **Exportar backup** no menu da conta com escolha entre **Período inteiro** ou **Somente este mês** e botões de download direto para CSV e JSON.

### 3. Busca, filtros multi-mês e Visão Anual
- **Backend (`GET /api/overview`)**: agrega evolução mensal e totais acumulados por ano ou período inteiro, e filtra lançamentos por busca textual sem acento (`q`), cartão (`card`) e tarja (`casa`, `planejado`, `imprevisto`).
- **Frontend (`public/js/views/overview.js`, `public/js/views/summary.js`, `public/styles.css`)**: acessível pelo Resumo mensal (**Busca e visão anual**) e pelo menu da conta, com campo de pesquisa debounced preservando identidade DOM/foco, filtros por tarja/cartão, salto direto ao mês do lançamento e barras proporcionais CSSOM (100% compatíveis com CSP `style-src 'self'`).

### 4. Testes e validação
- **Novo `test/export-overview.test.ts`**: valida `/api/export` (JSON, CSV com BOM UTF-8, filtro `monthId`, isolamento multi-tenant, neutralização de `=SUM(...)`), `/api/overview` (totais anuais, busca sem acento, combinação ano+cartão+tarja) e headers de `/sw.js`.
- **Extensão de `test/browser-e2e.test.ts`**: valida em Chromium real a abertura de **Busca e visão anual**, pesquisa preservando identidade DOM do input e a sheet **Exportar backup**, com zero erros e zero violações CSP.
- `npm test`: **68/68 testes passando** (~8,1s).
- `npm run check`: `wrangler types`, `tsc --noEmit`, `lint:public` (36 arquivos) e `wrangler deploy --dry-run` aprovados.

author: gavingolden
body:
## TLDR

The UI review no longer asks you to accept a "defect" caused by the app rate-limiting the screenshot run: the run makes far fewer API calls, retries once, and skips still-throttled screenshots.

## User-facing changes

- A page the app throttled during the screenshot run no longer becomes an unresolved-defect box on the PR:
  - **Before:** the PR gained `DECISION: accept this UI with 1 unresolved defect` for a page that had only failed to load its data.
  - **After:** the screenshot run rarely trips the limiter, reloads a throttled page once, and leaves any screenshot still rate-limited out of the review, so no defect is filed from it.
- The PR's UI review section now says how many screenshots were left out, and a "Clean" verdict says it covers only the judged screenshots.
- When a changed page has no usable screenshot, the PR carries the existing "UI review did not run" box naming that page and what to do next:
  - **Before:** the judge reviewed the error page and reported a defect, or another page's result read as "Clean".
  - **After:** the box names the page and says to re-run verify once the app is idle; the judge is not paid when nothing is usable.
- A page this PR broke (an endpoint answering 500, or a crashed backend answering 502/504) is judged and gates exactly as before.

## System changes

- The screenshot run stops repeating every API call per screen size:
  - **Before:** each of the four screen sizes loaded the page from scratch, so a 3-page run made about 12 full sets of API calls.
  - **After:** the desktop load's API responses are served from memory to the other screen sizes, so a run makes about 3.
- A page's desktop load answered 429 or 503 waits (the app's Retry-After, kept between 5 and 15 s) and reloads once; the other screen sizes reuse what that reload got, including a 429 that persisted, so a throttled page costs two live requests. Time spent waiting and reloading shares a 60 s budget per run, and the reuse step gives up on any response body still loading after 5 s (a streaming API can no longer stall the capture).
- The capture record now carries, per screenshot, the app requests still failing when it was taken (host and path only, status, request count).
- A fix round whose after-screenshot was rate-limited is now undone instead of kept, because that screen was never re-checked; the PR names the rate limit as the reason.
- Cost: a throttled run takes up to 60 s longer; a run with no usable screenshot now spends nothing on the judge instead of up to its $3 cap.

## Why

**Failing:** On econ-data PR 1273 the screenshot run loaded 3 pages at 4 screen sizes back to back, the app's own local rate limiter answered the page's data requests with "429 Too Many Requests", and the analysis page rendered "Couldn't load this report". The design judge filed that broken page as a defect the PR introduced, and the owner was asked to accept an unresolved defect that was never in the product.

**Root cause:** The screenshot run repeated every API call once per screen size, which exhausted the app's limiter, and never checked whether those calls succeeded, so the error states were judged as product defects.

The review exists to save the owner a manual look; a box for a capture failure costs an interruption and trust in every later review. A clean recapture of that econ-data page may still show a genuine state mismatch, because its expected "first close" state depended on the listing date.

## Key decisions

- **Fix mechanism:** cut the capture's own request burst by reusing API responses across screen sizes, recover a throttled load with one reload, and keep any screenshot still rate-limited away from the judge and from the fix-round comparison.
- Only a persisting 429 marks a screenshot degraded, not every error: a 500, 502, 504 or refused connection may be the bug this PR introduced, so those pages are judged as before. A 429 on a URL the page requested 5+ times is the app's own request storm and also still judged — the rule the existing page checks already apply.
- A changed page with no usable screenshot gets the existing "did not run" box rather than a silent pass. This departs from the request's "never a ui-review DECISION": the box never asks you to accept a defect, it says the page was not reviewed.
- Pacing between page loads was dropped in favour of response reuse, which removes the burst instead of waiting it out (request item 4 was optional).
- Bundled: all six plan tasks (degraded rule, capture reuse/reload, critique filtering, PR section, loop doc, live test) shipped without a plan-review pause because this ran as a bug fix; no candidate follow-ups were ticked.
- Bundled during implementation: the route's accessibility snapshot is also kept from the judge when its desktop screenshot was rate-limited — the econ-data defect was argued from that snapshot.
- Bundled during implementation: the PR's before/after screenshot table leaves out rate-limited screenshots, so it never shows an error page beside a "Clean" line.
- Bundled during implementation: response reuse covers POST lookups too (matched on the exact request body), since econ-data's heaviest callers are POSTs; capture contexts block service workers so a worker cannot bypass the reuse.
- The chrome-devtools fallback capture (used only without Playwright) keeps today's behaviour; tracked as a candidate follow-up.

## Deviations from plan

- The response recorder attaches before the page loads (the plan said after settle), because API responses arrive during the load.
- The capture script grew to 219 lines, past the 200-line target; the new tracking and reuse code lives in its own module (`bin/lib/ui-capture-network.ts`), and the remaining growth is the reload wiring.
- `captureDegraded` is written to the loop log only when at least one screenshot was degraded, so clean runs keep an unchanged log.

## Test Steps

> [!NOTE]
> Not exercised by this pipeline's own review: skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/ui-critique-loop.md. Run `flow feature create --skills-from <worktree>` to exercise it.

<!-- flow:authoring-rubric — for each checkbox item below, the three-question
automation test from manual-test-rubric.md is: (a) named fixture/setup,
(b) deterministic assertion(s), (c) exit condition. If all three are answerable
without subjective human judgment, it must be a runnable item. Source of truth:
skills/pipeline/flow-pr-review/references/manual-test-rubric.md. -->

- [x] Run `npx vitest run bin/flow-ui-critique.test.ts -t "rate-limited capture"` — the econ-data PR 1273 regression (429 screenshots are not judged, no defect box, the not-run box names the page) passes, 500/502-only screenshots are still judged, a capture with nothing usable skips the judge, and a throttled after-screenshot reverts the fix round.

author: cdnninja
body:
Fixes #1623, fixes #1624 (same traceback).

## Problem
Since 2026-11-19, Hyundai USA `evTripDetails` records can come back without a `distance` key. The `filled_trips` loop in `HyundaiBlueLinkApiUSA._update_vehicle_properties` reads it as `float(trip["distance"])`. That raises `KeyError` before `vehicle.data = state` runs, so the whole update fails and every kia_uvo entity goes unavailable.

## Fix
One line: read it with `float_or_none(get_child_value(trip, "distance"))`, the same safe access the daily-stats loop a few lines above already uses. A missing distance is now `None` instead of `0`, which follows the repo's rule to leave fields `None` when a block is missing, so a trip doesn't show a fake zero distance.

Only Hyundai/Genesis USA (`HyundaiBlueLinkApiUSA`) is affected. `KiaUvoApiUSA` doesn't parse this payload.

## Tests
- New regression test in `tests/test_bluelink_usa_vehicle_properties.py`. It fails with `KeyError` without the fix and passes with it.
- Full suite: 1343 passed, 141 snapshots unchanged. pre-commit (ruff, mypy --strict, etc.) passes.

No captured response without `distance` is attached to either issue, so I used a minimal inline state in that file (as its other tests do) instead of a snapshot fixture. If someone posts a debug log of the `evTripDetails` response, it can be turned into an update scenario.

## Not changed
The same loop still subscripts `trip["mileagetime"]`, `trip["duration"]`, `trip["avgspeed"]` and `trip["maxspeed"]` and wraps them in `int(...)`. Nobody has reported those missing yet, so I kept this PR to the observed failure.

author: krisztiankoos
body:
Supersedes #13243. Refs learn-ukrainian/machinery#12.

The shared Playwright launcher verifies Chrome's namespace and seccomp status and checks the browser command line over CDP before handing Chrome to a caller. It closes Chrome and rejects either failure.

- **AC-01**. Frontend runs the two real-Chrome regression cases and lists each result by name. The cases check separate failure paths and require Chrome to close.
- **AC-02**. Frontend runs the existing origin-allowlist spec against the built site. The Pages workflow builds and uploads on a branch. Deployment requires a successful build, an uncancelled run and the main ref. GitHub skipped deployment after the previous branch build and upload passed. [Predecessor Pages run](https://github.com/learn-ukrainian/learn-ukrainian.github.io/actions/runs/44802142295)
- **AC-03**. The guard checks tracked source, manifests and lockfiles for direct browser launches and browser-capable dependencies. The Astro build no longer includes Mermaid. The Git-tree search found zero Mermaid fences in 22,484 tracked files under `site/src`, `curriculum` and `wiki`.

## Checks before review

- Launch options and argv. The inherited probes covered privileged caller options, independent argument arrays, an affirmative sandbox, and one-dash switch syntax with a value. The two rejection cases require a started browser and an observed disconnect.
- Paths, metadata and environment. The inherited guard probes covered JSX in a path with spaces, a scoped optional npm alias and a nested lockfile alias, with clean controls under an isolated home and Git config.
- Selection, timing and cancellation. Playwright discovered four tests in the named spec. The file filter is anchored to the spec suffix, and the build runs before the spec. Pages checks the artifact build result and cancellation before authorizing the deploy job. The marker test still checks the exact SHA.
- The focused pytest run passed 187 tests after restoring tracked sparse-checkout fixtures. A real Chrome smoke verified the sandbox and CDP checks. Both controlled rejection cases reported that Chrome disconnected.
- The tree secret scan found zero findings across 6,390 files. Actionlint, Node syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

## Design charter

The launcher checks Chrome's own status and command line and reports the failed check. The rejection tests own their temporary directories. CI installs locked dependencies and uses the Chrome on its declared runner image. Removing Mermaid also removes its browser adapter. The Pages job condition refuses failed or skipped builds and cancelled runs.

## Review history

Critical infra review. Round 1 of the three-round lineage budget was recorded on #13243. Supplemental Neon admission was refused at that risk tier. [Round 1 verdict](https://github.com/learn-ukrainian/learn-ukrainian.github.io/pull/13243#issuecomment-7049283365)

- **F1**. The deploy job now has an explicit status function, so a skipped automatic eligibility job does not suppress successful manual builds on main.
- **F2**. The new Playwright step is scoped to browser hardening. A1 navigation, Atlas contrast and Atlas practice failures from the first full Playwright run remain with their existing owners. [Original Frontend run](https://github.com/learn-ukrainian/learn-ukrainian.github.io/actions/runs/44802347282) · [Contrast](https://github.com/learn-ukrainian/learn-ukrainian.github.io/issues/10180) · [Practice](https://github.com/learn-ukrainian/learn-ukrainian.github.io/issues/10702)
- **F3**. Malformed dependency metadata fails the guard. Round 1 classified the diagnostic quality as a non-blocking finding.

Initial implementation by the predecessor Codex task, preserved in its original commit. Continued by GPT-6.2 Sol in Codex.

## Summary

- Remove the unconditional `SmsTemporalBus` port-write history; retain only functional bus state and tests. Bump affected serialized-state versions.
- Bound the SMS machine trace buffer at 65,536 events and account for drops across machine, ingress queue and retained history.
- Introduce one `DiagnosticsConsent` capability shared by the central logger and SMS worker. Remove the worker's public boolean enable API.

author: divingwhale
body:
Builds on #2, #3 and #4: this branch merges them, so merging this PR alone lands all four. Close those three after this merges, or merge them first; either way works.

## Why the animations felt worse than the prototype
1. **Rendering:** every pixel went out over blocking SPI from one 16-line buffer, so the CPU idled during transfers. The panel now uses `esp_lcd` with DMA and two 40-line buffers, so drawing and sending overlap. LVGL refreshes every 15 ms instead of 30 ms.
2. **Motion design:** the new screen slid over the old one, which stayed visible underneath, and nothing faded. Transitions now follow the prototype's CSS: enter 40 px from the direction of travel while fading in from 20%, ease-out, 0.26–0.30 s. Edge bounce, note and ticker slides match too. See the new spec section 4.13.

## Visual parity with the prototype
- Icons are the prototype's SVG strokes, rasterized to anti-aliased alpha bitmaps (`tools/gen_icons.py`) instead of Montserrat symbols.
- Added items the spec asked for but the firmware lacked: Today header sync status, hold-overlay icons, Saved check circle and "Syncing next / Will sync when online", warning triangle and large battery for errors, MD atom, the pill toast.
- Recording shows a scrolling waveform from the live level.
- Fixed picker overlap with two-line titles.
- A swipe up that starts on the brightness bar now closes the quick panel without changing brightness.

## Known problems fixed
- `main.cpp` split into `ui_kit` (palette, primitives, motion), `tasks` (sample data and persistence behind the interface the Pi sync will fill) and shared `layout` rectangles, so each touch target is drawn and hit-tested from one definition. Screens render byte-identically before and after.
- Automatic Wi-Fi logins back off after failures (2 → 60 min).
- Sleep runs the CPU at 80 MHz.
- Deferred, with reasons in `firmware/README.md`: the ESP-IDF 5 move that would drop the supplicant patch. It needs a hardware session for USB and campus login.

## Host simulator (`firmware/sim/`)
Compiles the real `main.cpp` and font pack against LVGL on the Mac with fake hardware, then runs scripted keys and touches on a virtual clock and writes screenshots and animation films. `scenes/tour.txt` covers every screen, `interact.txt` every touch target, `motion.txt` every transition. All the UI work above was checked this way.

## Testing
- [x] `python3 firmware/tools/build.py` succeeds after every commit (RAM 49%, flash 54%).
- [x] Simulator: tour (EN/ZH), interaction and motion scenes reviewed. Refactor commits verified pixel-identical.
- [ ] **Not flashed.** On hardware: screens look right, `perf` shows >30 fps during page swipes, the panel and unlock. Also check that recording still works, USB card mounting and serial work, and Wi-Fi sessions still end by themselves (`firmware/tools/wifi_stress.py`).

author: shukrat
body:
## What

Kit Core v31: a zone can hold small buttons, and slots change size as they move between zones.

- **`small = true`** on a zone: its slots are small round buttons (22), the other zones' full slots. Each zone slot takes the size of the zone it's in and changes as it's dragged from one to another in edit mode, including while the drop is only being previewed. A slot on a bar (or being dragged onto one) is a full slot wherever its zone is, since the bars' cells are full size. Only used when a kit has a small zone, so other kits are unaffected.
  - `Kit:SetSlotSmall(btn, small)` swaps the look out of combat. The look it isn't using is hidden and kept; the one it needs is made the first time (`MakeSmallRound`, `ApplyShape`). Pin dot, glow, highlight and the edit-mode highlight change size with it, at the Button size setting.
  - `MakeSmallRound` can now be called again (its mask, ring and highlight are made once), and it keeps where the icon sat as a full slot so it can go back.
  - `Kit:SizeZoneSlots()` runs in `ApplyZones`. Before the slots are made it only sets `slot.small`, which they're built from. It runs again in `Refresh` to catch up a move that happened in combat.
- `SizeZoneSlots` reads `kit:Bars()`, which is the preview during a drag, so it sizes slots on bars correctly before `MarkBars` runs.
- **`only = { slotKey, ... }`**: just these slots can be dropped in the zone (any other is offered the other zones), and one saved there goes back to the zone it started in (`CleanZones`).
- **`track = true`** on a ring zone: its outline runs through the middle of its buttons, with its name beyond them, for a ring inside another ring.
- `VERSION` 31, the `C.NewKit` docs and README updated.

## Why

Warlock Kit's Demonic Sacrifice, Soul Link and Fel Domination can now be dragged out of their small inner ring onto the ring or under the line. There, or floated onto a bar, they should be full-size slots, and small again when dragged back. Shukrat/WarlockKit#113 uses all three options:

```lua
{ key = "inner", label = "Inner ring", ring = 2, small = true, only = { "sac", "link", "feldom" }, track = true },
```

## Testing

- Not tried in game yet.
- `KitCore.lua` compiles (`texluac -p`).
- A stub harness ran the new zone, ring and look code (extracted from this file) with Warlock Kit's `ApplyZones` on mock frames: 70 checks pass. They cover:
  - drop targets and `only`
  - sizes following zones, both before and after the slots are made
  - full size on a bar: saved, previewed mid-drag, dropped back on the kit, and at login
  - small to full and back, with parts reused, the icon mask applied once, and the icon's anchors and tex coords restored
  - the Button size setting
  - no change in combat, with the refresh catching up after
  - a kit without a small zone left alone
  - saved layouts, including a slot saved in a zone that doesn't take it

## Releasing

Once merged: tag `v31`. Bump kits will skip Warlock Kit if #113 has already merged (it moves `.pkgmeta` to v31 itself), and opens the usual PRs for the other kits.

body:
Fixes the failing **Workers Builds** check on pull requests.

For non-production branches Cloudflare runs `npx wrangler preview`, which requires a `previews` block in the Wrangler config:

```
✘ [ERROR] Your Wrangler configuration is missing a `previews` block to run this command.
```

This adds an empty `"previews": {}` to `wrangler.jsonc`. Assets and compatibility settings are inherited from the top level, so nothing else changes, and production deploys from `main` are unaffected.

**How to verify:** this pull request's own *Workers Builds* check runs `wrangler preview`. It should pass and post a preview URL.

author: kyrokohan
body:
## Problem
From the play test after #48: the turn is smooth, but it turns at one speed. Each press or repeat of Left or Right turned the aim 2 degrees, so a held key turned about 20 degrees a second (a repeat every 90 ms, the macOS default) and a half turn took over 8 seconds. A tap should nudge the aim, and a held key should start slow and speed up, so that wide turns are easy.

## Change
- A tap of Left or Right turns the aim 1 degree (`tapStep`), half of what it was.
- Held, the aim turns at 20 degrees a second (`slowTurn`) for a quarter of a second after the repeats begin. It then speeds up on an eased ramp over a second (`rampTime`) to 180 degrees a second (`fastTurn`). A half turn takes about 2.2 s of holding.
- Most terminals send no releases, only a press and then the OS's repeats. A press of the same key within 0.15 s of the one before (`repeatGap`) is the key held down. It turns the aim for the time since that press, at the speed of the ramp, so the speed held does not depend on the OS repeat rate. Any other press is a tap. The OS's first repeat comes long after the press, so it counts as a tap and the ramp is timed from it. Quick taps never speed up, and a press of the other way is always a tap.
- The turn still goes through the spring of #48, so it stays smooth. `glide` is unchanged.
- Up and Down stay fine steps of 0.1 degrees. The arrow keys still move a cue ball in hand as before.
- README: the Aim row says Left and Right turn faster when held.
- Out of scope: a ramp for Up and Down or for the cue ball in hand.
- To know: let go at full speed and the aim coasts about 19 degrees on, over about a fifth of a second. That is the spring catching up with the last repeat. Slower speeds coast less.

## Testing
- New tests, failing first: a key held as a terminal sends it (pressed, repeated after 0.4 s, then every fifth frame) turns at about 20 degrees a second as the repeats start, and at about 180 after 2.5 s. It never turns back, and no frame turns more than 1.5 times the frame before. `turnRate` is slow before the ramp, fast after, and rises in between.
- New guards, passing before and after: ten taps 0.2 s apart turn exactly ten steps; letting go stops the aim within half a second and no further than a fifth of a second at full speed; Left just after a long hold of Right asks for one step. Both guards fail when the check of which way the key goes is taken out.
- Measured: 13 degrees a second at 0.5 s, 21 at 0.7 s, 72 at 1.1 s, 159 at 1.5 s, 179 to 182 from 1.7 s on.
- `make check` and `make lint` pass. `make media` leaves `docs/media` byte-identical, as the recordings press only Down.
- The built binary in a pseudo-terminal: V, Right repeated 30 times at the OS rate, Left, charge, shoot, V, quit. No panic, and the screen was restored.
- Not done: played by hand.

## Stack
- Base `main`. No open parent.

body:
## Why

geophysix owns the Earth constants (its design decision 5), and Core libraries sit below it, so kernellib cannot import it at run time. kernellib keeps `EARTH_RADIUS_KM`, but its value must equal geophysix's mean radius, and a test must say so.

Today (bug): `EARTH_RADIUS_KM` is `6371.0088`, the IUGG mean radius R₁ = (2a + b) / 3 rounded to four decimals, and nothing checks it against geophysix's `SPHERE.semi_major`.

After this PR: `EARTH_RADIUS_KM` is exactly R₁, `6371.008771415059` km (I chose the exact value over keeping the rounded one and testing to 1e-9, so the two libraries agree to the last digit), and `tests/test_geophysix_constants.py` fails if they drift.

| Default | Today | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `EARTH_RADIUS_KM` | 6371.0088 km | 6371.008771415059 km (−2.86e-5 km = −2.9 cm, −4.5e-9 relative) |

## What stays the same

- `EARTH_RADIUS_KM` keeps its name, its km unit, and its exports from `kernellib` and `kernellib.functional`. Every `radius` argument still defaults to 1.0 (angles in radians); only callers who pass `EARTH_RADIUS_KM` see the 4.5e-9 relative change.
- geophysix is a test-only dependency: it is in the `dev` group and in `[tool.uv.sources]`, pinned to `v0.0.3`, and nothing under `src/` imports it. `tests/test_dependency_rules.py` still passes.
- The README sketch that writes `6371.0 * unit` is prose with a rounded radius, not a default, and is untouched.

## Evidence

- `6371.0088 − 6371.008771415059 = 2.8585e-5` km, a relative change of 4.49e-9.
- The new `tests/test_geophysix_constants.py` asserts `EARTH_RADIUS_KM * 1000` equals geophysix's `SPHERE.semi_major` and `WGS84.mean_radius` to 1e-12 relative, with `pytest.importorskip("geophysix")`.
- Expected numbers I updated: none. The tests that use `EARTH_RADIUS_KM` (`test_functional_geo`, `test_geo_great_circle`, `test_geo_chordal`, `test_geo_neighbors`, `test_heuristics`) take it as an argument or compare to a reference computed with it, and all pass unchanged.
- Local checks against geophysix at the `v0.0.3` tag (65b1faa): `pytest tests/test_geophysix_constants.py tests/test_functional_geo.py tests/test_geo_great_circle.py tests/test_geo_chordal.py tests/graph/test_geo_neighbors.py tests/test_heuristics.py tests/test_dependency_rules.py tests/test_capabilities.py tests/test_geo_taper.py tests/test_geo_sphere_series.py -m "not slow"` gave 154 passed (29 slow deselected); `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean; `uv lock` adds only geophysix.
- `ty check src/kernellib` reports 4 diagnostics (a missing `pynndescent` import, three argument-type notes in untouched files) in the borrowed local environment; none is in a file this PR changes.

## Outcome

Fixes the `Validate beta code` failure introduced by #618 (`fatal: Not a valid object name origin/main` during `pnpm check` → `scripts/check-comments.mjs`), and prevents the same failure in `Desktop build` when `run-checks: true` is used by `Release`.

Both `.github/workflows/beta.yml` and `.github/workflows/desktop-build.yml` check out a specific commit SHA with the default shallow `fetch-depth: 1`, producing a detached HEAD with no `origin/main` ref or parent commit, and invoke `pnpm check` without `FACTORY_COMMENT_BASE`. Both workflows now fetch `fetch-depth: 2` and set `FACTORY_COMMENT_BASE: HEAD~1` for `pnpm check`, comparing the checked-out `main` commit against its parent just as the `Quality` workflow does on pushes to `main`.

## Verification

- Reproduced a shallow `--depth=2` detached checkout without `origin/main`:
  - `node scripts/check-comments.mjs` fails with `fatal: Not a valid object name origin/main`.
  - `FACTORY_COMMENT_BASE=HEAD~1 node scripts/check-comments.mjs` passes on a clean commit and rejects a newly added comment.
- Verified `FACTORY_COMMENT_BASE` is forwarded through `pnpm check:static` (`vp run gate:static` → `lint:comments`).
- Full pre-push gate (`pnpm check`: 31/31 tasks — format, lint, fallow, typecheck, backend/desktop/frontend/script tests, and build) and Git attribution check passed on `78bd3dfb`.
- Material limit: `beta.yml` and `desktop-build.yml` run on GitHub Actions only after merge (or manual workflow dispatch on `main`), so live Beta/Release workflow execution is verified after merge.

## UI screenshots

Workflow-only change (`.github/workflows/beta.yml` and `.github/workflows/desktop-build.yml`); no UI impact.

## Scope and contracts

- **Ownership & need:** Fixed only the two CI workflow callers that run `pnpm check` on detached SHA checkouts; no changes to `scripts/check-comments.mjs`, dependencies, or contracts.

author: zastrowm
body:
## Description

On Linux, GNU make can't run any recipe in a box. With a Makefile like this:

```make
# Makefile
all: ; @echo built
```

`make` in a box on Amazon Linux 2023 (make 4.3, glibc 2.34) prints `make: echo: Operation not permitted`, even when `echo` and the shell are granted. make starts each recipe with `posix_spawn` and `POSIX_SPAWN_RESETIDS`, and glibc's spawn child then calls `setresuid(-1, getuid(), -1)` and `setresgid(-1, getgid(), -1)`. The workload filter admits only `setresuid(0, 0, 0)` and `setresgid(-1, -1, -1)`, so it answers `EPERM` and the spawn fails before `execve`. Python's `os.posix_spawn(..., resetids=True)` fails the same way.

The user namespace maps one user and one group, both `0`, so every id the workload has is `0`. This change admits `setresuid` and `setresgid` when each of their three arguments is `0` or `-1`, which is eight rules for each call. Every admitted call leaves the ids as they are. A call that names any other id still gets `EPERM` from the filter, and `setuid` and `setgid` stay refused. The evidence is in the containment `AGENTS.md` beside the `renameat2` note, and `docs/design/linux-enforcement.md` names the exception next to `copy_file_range`.

<details>
<summary>Things to know</summary>

- musl's `POSIX_SPAWN_RESETIDS` calls `setuid` and `setgid`, which stay refused, so a musl-built program that sets the flag still fails. I left that out because those calls have no "leave it" argument to scope.
- Two existing tests (`scoped_workload_permits_accept_only_approved_arguments` and `apply_delivers_every_property_it_claims`) used `setresgid(-1, 0, -1)` as their refused example. That call is now admitted, so they use id `1` instead.
- macOS is unchanged.

</details>

## Related Issues

None.

## Type of Change

Bug fix

## Testing

New test `a_workload_resets_its_own_ids_and_cannot_change_them`, in `crates/containment/tests/reset_ids_linux.rs`, runs under the real trampoline. It runs glibc's `posix_spawn` with `POSIX_SPAWN_RESETIDS`, then makes every `setresuid` and `setresgid` call with each mix of `0`, `-1`, and `1` in the three positions, and expects only the calls that name `1` to get `EPERM`. It fails on `main` (`spawn_errno: 1`), and fails again with one admitted combination dropped or with `1` admitted in the saved position.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- Linux aarch64 (Amazon Linux 2023): `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p strands-box-containment --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` (no warnings), and `cargo test -p strands-box-containment --all-features` pass.
- A box running `make` with granted `echo`, `bash`, `tr`, and `uname` ran a plain recipe, a recipe piped through `tr`, and `uname`. The same box without this change failed each recipe with `Operation not permitted`.
- `scripts/test-all.sh` had one timeout in `runtime_mcp_start.rs::two_servers_whose_commands_expand_to_one_command_are_refused_at_start`. It passes on its own, on this branch and on the fork point.
