author: teetangh
body:
Fixes #2925 "[booking][P1] An unverified expert can still get sessions: trials and 1:1 requests skip the verification check, and a moderation reject leaves bookings live".

An expert whose profile is not `VERIFIED` can no longer be booked or paid, and only they see their plans. A moderation reject moves the profile to `REJECTED` in a small transaction, ends their unpaid sales right after it commits, and keeps everything already paid. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2026-11-21-unverified-experts-cannot-be-booked.md`.

## Owner decisions

| Date | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-11-21 | Rejection: stop new sales, keep what is booked; purge the expert's cached profile |
| 2026-11-21 | New bookings: refuse at every door and hide the plans; experts may still build and publish while they wait |
| 2026-11-21 | Organisation-invited experts are verified first |
| 2026-11-21 | Unpaid pay links are expired at the rejection, in its transaction; a late capture is refunded |
| 2026-11-21 | Unpaid requests: refused at approval and declined at rejection |
| 2026-11-21 | Paid requests not yet approved are kept |
| 2026-11-21 | Learner copy is neutral, never "rejected" and never a reason |
| 2026-11-21 | Confirmed: the ending runs right after the reject commits; "If you were charged, the money is refunded automatically." for a sale with a real gateway order; paid pending requests stay placeable |
| 2026-11-21 | A failed ending is re-run by the existing moderation enforcement retry sweep until it settles |
| 2026-11-21 | By-id webinar and class plan responses are shared for at most 60 s with no stale window |
| 2026-11-21 | An uncertain gateway read inside the ending is reported once here; the payment reconciler will re-read orders closed in the last 72 h and refund any capture (separate PR, branch `fix/reconcile-closed-orders`) |

## Doors

One shared check, `assertExpertVerified` (`lib/booking/booking-rule-error.ts`), uses the existing `EXPERT_NOT_VERIFIED` refusal (409) and its copy.

| Door | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/trials` (free and paid) | never read the expert's status | refused; also refuses an archived plan, an organisation-only plan and a soft-deleted expert exactly as checkout does (`assertPlanOnSale`) |
| `POST /api/scheduling/request-for-approval` | same | same refusals |
| Pay-link price, `calculateAmount` in `lib/payments/operations/approval-payment.ts` (1:1 and trial, every mint and re-mint) | priced any expert | refused; the approval routes answer 409 with the code (`approvalMintConflict`), and the refusal is not sent to Sentry |
| Checkout's in-lock re-read, `verifyPlanExistsInsideLock` | re-read pause and booking mode only | re-reads verification for all four plan types, before any gateway order |
| Approval of an unpaid request: the 1:1 and subscription detail PATCH routes, and `updateEventStatus`, which every allocate route reaches (the organisation's too) | approved | refused by `assertUnpaidApprovalVerified` (`lib/booking/approval-verification.ts`) unless the booking is already approved or has a captured payment |

## Readers

The rule is `isPublicExpertProfile`, plus its new `where` form `publicExpertProfileWhere` (`lib/profiles/public-profile.ts`): verified and not deleted.

| Reader | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `oneOnOnePlanListWhere` (`GET /api/plans/consultations`, `GET /api/plans/subscriptions`) | listed every expert's plans | owner only |
| `buildPlanWhereClause` (webinar and class list APIs behind `/explore/programs`) and `liveConsultantWhere` in `lib/data/explore-programs.ts` | deleted owners only were dropped | unverified owners are dropped too; ownerless organisation plans stay |
| Plan pages and by-id APIs (`isPlanViewable`, `canViewPlanDetail`, the four `plan-details.ts` readers, the event waitlist) | served | 404 to everyone but the owner; the owner's facts are a required field, so every caller selects them |
| `getOrgMemberCatalog` | listed unverified experts' plans | verified experts only |
| Organisation Members page | badge from `isVerified`, labelled "Unverified" | badge from the same rule, sent as a boolean (`memberExpertOf`), labelled "Waiting for verification" |
| Moderation action route | purged only review surfaces | also calls `purgeExpertSurfaces` after the commit |

## What a rejection does

The reject transaction (`unverifyProfiles` in `lib/moderation/side-effects.ts`) only moves the profile to `REJECTED` and ends collaborations. Every sale writer (trial, request, the checkout commit on every attempt, both pay-link claims, the unpaid-approval guard) re-reads the expert's standing under a `FOR SHARE` row lock (`assertExpertStandsInTx`, `lib/booking/expert-standing.ts`), so the reject waits for a write in flight and the ending sees what it committed.

Right after the commit, `endUnverifiedExpertSales` (`lib/booking/unverified-expert-notices.ts`):

1. Asks the gateway about every open order on the expert's unpaid sales. A live payment keeps that sale for reconciliation to confirm; an order the gateway can't answer for closes nothing.
2. Ends, in one Serializable transaction (`endUnpaidSalesInTx`, `lib/booking/unverified-expert-sales.ts`), every sale whose orders were all cleared. Every write is a CAS through an existing helper with the neutral history reason `EXPERT_UNAVAILABLE`, a free-text column, so there is no schema change.
3. Reads each closed order once more; a capture found there goes through `handlePaymentSuccess`, which refunds it.
4. Stages the learner notices, and reports anything unchecked, unread or failed once per reject (`REJECT_SALES_UNSETTLED`).

| Before | After | Money | Learner reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1:1 or subscription `APPROVED_PENDING_PAYMENT`, nothing captured | `EXPIRED` through `lapseApprovedRequest`; holds released | open order expired by CAS; credit, code use and engagement returned | "<expert> isn't taking bookings right now, so your request was closed." plus the money line |
| `PENDING`, nothing captured (a request, a free request, an open checkout) | `REJECTED`; holds, seats and proposals released | same | same |
| Trial `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, not paid | `CANCELLED`; call tombstoned | same | the trial-cancelled notice |
| An unpaid seat on the expert's own webinar or class | released; the event and paid seats stay | same | the request-closed notice |
| Anything with a captured payment, or an order the gateway reports live | unchanged | unchanged; payouts follow the normal holds | nothing |

- **Money line:** "No payment was taken." only when no gateway order existed; otherwise "If you were charged, the money is refunded automatically."
- **Pay page:** "This expert isn't taking bookings right now." plus the money line, with no request-again line.
- **Retry:** if the whole ending step fails, the action records `unpaidSales: "failed"` in its `sideEffects`, and the moderation enforcement retry sweep (`retryUnpaidSalesEnding`, `scripts/cleanup/retry-moderation-enforcement.ts`) re-runs it within its shared attempt and age budget, skipping an expert verified again. No new job and no schema change.
- **Counts:** the action summary and the staff moderation page carry `payLinksClosed`, `requestsDeclined`, `trialHoldsReleased`, `seatsReleased` and `salesKept`.
- **Caches:** `purgeExpertSurfaces` runs after the commit and also purges the programs page; the by-id webinar and class plan responses are `public, s-maxage=60` with no stale window.

The free remedy rebook after an incident is left alone: it replaces a session the learner already paid for.

## Research

Summarised on the issue: https://github.com/Practitionist/familiarise_web/issues/2925#issuecomment-7050056009

- **Credential-led marketplaces** keep a provider unbookable and unlisted until a person approves them: Practo, Preply, Clarity.fm, Urban Company, and Airbnb (a listing "won't be published until you finish" verification).
- **Open listing with a badge** is the long-tail model (Topmate,

body:
The lab campaign of the v2026.11.20 pre-release (scenario 87), measured against v2026.11.19-3 the same evening with the same clients.

**Verdict: ready to promote.**

- **#680, reloads under new connections**: 40 reloads of the VRRP master under ~12,000 new connections a second straight on the VIP: **571 failed requests on v2026.11.19-3, 0 on v2026.11.20** (1.65 M requests), 40/40 reloads handed over (`-x`), one HAProxy left, `tcp_migrate_req` 0 → 1. Same at a saturating rate. HAProxy 3.0.31 and 3.2.27: 20/20 handed over, 0 errors, 0 AVC. A cluster member: 0 errors (release: 112 and 149).
- **Reloads that open new listeners** (a changed backlog): `handover: false` then `true`, 0 errors. A janusd restart reloads HAProxy itself at its start; the errors seen during a restart are the VIP leaving and coming back (keepalived is janusd's child), none in the reload's second.
- **#694**: the hang reproduced on the release (every ACME call and even a HAProxy apply cut at 10 s, the file set aside); after the upgrade note (restart, update) the boot put the file back. On the pre-release: refused in 0.03 s while `haproxy.cfg` uses the certificate, accepted in 0.06 s once it doesn't.
- node_exporter 1.13.1, the keep-alive relay still 0, cluster updated in place in 40.9 s with its tables carried, core campaign as on the release, 0 AVC / oops / OOM, CIS 33/33.

Findings, none a regression: a janusd restart reloads HAProxy (the CLI's "HAProxy keeps serving" is true but the pid changes); a cluster member's stick-table counts can dip at a reload under load on both releases, once restarting for good (worth an issue); `acme status` keeps a stale failure under a certificate valid again.

author: tommkv
body:
Closes [CTX-1453](https://linear.app/ctxpipe/issue/CTX-1453).

## What changed

- **pnpm store cache mount.** Each `pnpm install` in the backend, worker, UI, docs and codesearch Dockerfiles uses `RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm-store,target=/pnpm/store`. A lockfile change downloads only the new packages.
- **The UI copies only its backend imports.** A new `ui-imports` stage runs `scripts/checks/ui-bundled-imports.mjs`. That script holds the import closure that the check `build:image-ui` already used for its inputs (moved out of `projects.mjs`). The builder copies only those backend and shared files (12 files now). A backend change outside them does not rebuild the Vite bundle. BuildKit keys `COPY --from` on the file content, so the stage can run again and the build step stays cached.
- **Registry layer cache for each CI image.** `production-builds` reads `ci-cache:production-<name>` for each image; the chat sandbox reads `chat-sandbox-arm64`, the cache of test-shards. The `layer-cache` job on `main` also writes ui, docs and cost-telemetry. CTX-1452 adds backend and worker. The local checks of ui, docs and cost-telemetry read the same caches.

## Measured times

docker buildx, docker-container builder, linux/arm64, Colima with 16 CPUs, `--output type=cacheonly`. "cold" starts from an empty builder cache. Each other build starts from the cache of the cold build. "lockfile" adds `is-number` to `packages/cli`, which no image copies.

| Image | Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| backend | cold | 30 s | 23 s |
| backend | source | 1 s | 1 s |
| backend | lockfile | 16 s | 10 s |
| worker | cold | 221 s | 213 s |
| worker | source | 2 s | 2 s |
| worker | lockfile | 16 s | 8 s |
| ui | cold | 87 s | 86 s |
| ui | UI source | 47 s | 46 s |
| ui | backend source (`server.ts`) | 52 s | **0 s** |
| ui | lockfile | 83 s | 73 s |
| docs | cold | 27 s | 32 s |
| docs | source | 12 s | 14 s |
| docs | lockfile | 22 s | 21 s |
| codesearch (`deps` stage) | cold | 7 s | 9 s |
| codesearch (`deps` stage) | lockfile | 2 s | 2 s |

The pnpm install steps alone, after a lockfile change: backend 5.3 + 9.6 s → 3.0 + 3.6 s, worker 8.1 → 2.7 s, ui 20.6 → 7.5 s (2605 packages downloaded before, 0 after), docs 6.9 → 2.2 s. The rest of a lockfile build is the Vite or Next build, which must run again when `node_modules` changes. This host has a fast network. On a runner with a slower network, the download part is larger. I measured codesearch only to its `deps` stage, because its toolchain stages are not changed and the full image is too large for the shared disk.

## Review notes

- **Blacksmith (deploy.yaml):** its builder keeps the layers and the cache mounts on a persistent disk ("Because Blacksmith persists the whole builder disk, these mounts survive between CI jobs", docs.blacksmith.sh, Docker builds). The deploy builds get the store mount. deploy.yaml is not changed.
- **Registry cache (CI):** an exported cache holds no cache mount. When the install layer of a CI build hits, the cache mount is not used. When it misses (a lockfile change), the mount is empty on the fresh runner, so the install downloads each package again, as before this change. Only a lockfile pruned per image (`turbo prune`) could keep that layer in a registry cache. `deploy-images.mjs` already uses `turbo prune` to select which images to build, but it does not do this inside the Dockerfiles. That is a possible follow-up.
- **No `pnpm fetch` layer:** I did not use the spec's `pnpm fetch` + `--offline` design. The store is in a cache mount, so a fetch layer would hold no packages. In CI, a fetch layer from the registry cache together with an empty mount would make an `--offline` install fail. `pnpm fetch` also downloads the packages of every workspace package, not only the packages of the image. A plain install with the store mount gets the same reuse.
- **No apk or cargo mounts:** the apk steps take 1–3 s, and they run again only when the base image changes. The only cargo steps are the converter stage (CTX-1452 owns it) and the pinned debian-lsp install of codesearch, which runs again only when its revision or base image changes.
- **UI types:** the type-only imports (the RPC route types) are not needed by the Vite build, because Vite erases them. The typecheck still reads the full backend source.

author: brandonpayton
body:
## What

The "PHPUnit Tests" job log only prints progress dots and a single total line (e.g. `Tests: 6207, Assertions: 25865, Skipped: 2125.`), so there is no way to tell from a job which tests ran or which were skipped.

This PR adds `--testdox` to the existing `vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.xml` call. PHPUnit then prints every test under its class, marked as passed (✔), failed (✘) or skipped (↩):

```
Proxy End To End
 ✔ Rejects private and reserved destinations with data set "localhost"
 ...
Block Markup Merge (WordPress\Merge\Tests\BlockMarkupMerge)
 ↩ Clean merge cases with data set "internet_history_parent.html"
```

Nothing else changes: same tests, same suites, same matrix, same exit code. The run still ends with the usual totals line.

An earlier commit on this branch added a JUnit report and a custom per-component summary script; the second commit replaces that with this single flag.

## Trade-offs

- The log for this step gets long: about 9,200 lines for the Project Test Suite alone, plus Blueprints. Searching the log for ✘ or ↩ finds failures and skips quickly.
- At the end, PHPUnit prints a "Summary of non-successful tests" section that repeats each failure and every skipped test (about 2,100 in CI), before the totals line.
- Headings are test class names (e.g. "Proxy End To End"), not component names. Tests from the same component appear together because they run folder by folder.

## Testing

- Checked `--testdox` output on PHPUnit 8.5 (`php:7.2-cli`) and 9.6 (`php:7.4-cli`, and locally on PHP 8.5): same format, including ✘ for failures and ↩ for skips, and failures still produce a non-zero exit code.
- `vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.xml --testdox --testsuite "Project Test Suite"` locally: exit 0, `Tests: 5978, Assertions: 25614, Skipped: 2033.`
- Nothing in the repo parses PHPUnit's console output.
- actionlint passes on the workflow.

This PR's own CI run will be the first on GitHub's runners, including Windows.

body:
Part of maksimtech/apkradar#116.

## Why
After #99 was merged, Security Posture failed on main (f36a3f3) with two Docker Scout alerts and no exception:
- **#345, CVE-2026-84786** (OpenSSL, DANE), against the base image's openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3: the one tracked across the Radars in maksimtech/apkradar#116.
- **#346, CVE-2026-109908** (libfontenc1): #99 removed the package, and Trivy, which scans the image built from main, no longer reports it. Docker Scout scans the image published on Docker Hub, built for 2026.48 before #99, which still has it.

## What
Two entries in `SECURITY-EXCEPTIONS.toml`, both `source = "Docker Scout"`:
- **CVE-2026-84786**, review 2026-12-15 with the other OpenSSL entries. No OpenSSL advisory yet (fix in openssl/openssl#33634), no Debian fix. Not reachable: Python's ssl exposes no DANE, cookieradar reads no TLSA record, and Chromium carries its own BoringSSL. Same reasoning as maksimtech/apkradar#118 and maksimtech/mailradar#124.
- **CVE-2026-109908**, review **2026-12-08**, the day after the release that rebuilds the published image. Debian: open in every suite, bug 1154283 (`patchradar debian`). Once the new image is out, Scout stops reporting it and the entry fails the build as unused: it is meant to be deleted then. Being Scout-only, it does not excuse the finding if Trivy ever reports it on the image built from source.

CHANGELOG: two entries under [Unreleased] → Security.

## Checks
- Gate simulation on this tree against the open alerts: 0 unexplained, 0 unused (13 settled, as on main).
- `pytest`: 1069 passed, 5 skipped (skipIfs already in the suite). `ruff check cookieradar tests tools`: clean.

author: gabrielaraujo-eng
body:
Fecha #107

## Escopo
Reescreve `linguagens/ASPECTJ/` (23 arquivos, incluindo README e o relatório de auditoria abaixo).

# Relatório de correção — pasta `linguagens/ASPECTJ`

## 1. Fontes consultadas
- AspectJ Programming Guide, capítulo de semântica de pointcuts: <https://eclipse.dev/aspectj/doc/released/progguide/semantics-pointcuts.html> — confirmadas as formas `call`, `execution`, `get`, `set`, `handler`, `within`, `withincode`, `cflow`, `cflowbelow`, `this`, `target`, `args`, `if`, e a declaração nomeada `pointcut nome(Formais): expressão;`.
- Programming Guide, seções de advice, declarações inter-tipo e aspectos estáticos (mesma coleção `progguide`, referenciadas no README).
- Verificação prática da sintaxe: compilador `ajc` 1.9.22.1 (Maven Central, `org.aspectj:aspectjtools` e `org.aspectj:aspectjrt`), executado sobre Java 21 (OpenJDK 21.0.13.1). Todo comportamento descrito abaixo foi confirmado pelo compilador, não por inspeção visual.

## 2. Estado encontrado na pasta original
Os 21 arquivos existiam, mas apenas `exemplo_1.aj` era um programa AspectJ válido. Os demais eram fragmentos de Java, pointcuts soltos ou esqueletos vazios, nenhum compilável isoladamente:

| Arquivo | Problema |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | citava arquivos com extensão `.aspectj` (inexistente na pasta); lista de tópicos genérica; continha a sequência literal `\n## Nota de Auditoria\n` em vez de quebras de linha reais |
| `exemplo_2.aj` | `int x = 10;` — declaração de campo fora de qualquer tipo |
| `exemplo_3.aj` | `if (x > 5) { }` — comando solto fora de método |
| `exemplo_4.aj` | `for (int i=0; i<10; i++) { }` — laço solto |
| `exemplo_5.aj` | `public int square(int n) { ... }` — método fora de classe |
| `exemplo_6.aj` | `List<Integer> list = ...` — comando solto, sem imports |
| `exemplo_7.aj` | `after() throwing (Exception e) : call(* *(..)) { }` — advice fora de aspecto |
| `exemplo_8.aj` | `String s = "Olá" + " Mundo";` — comando solto |
| `exemplo_9.aj` | `double r = Math.sqrt(16);` — comando solto |
| `exemplo_10.aj` | `public pointcut setter() : call(void set*(..));` — pointcut fora de tipo, e `public` em arquivo com outro nome |
| `exercicio_1.aj` | `aspect MyAspect { }` — aspecto vazio, sem programa |
| `exercicio_2.aj` a `exercicio_9.aj` | comandos Java soltos (`boolean active = true;`, `while(x > 0) {}`, `int[] arr = {1};`, `try { } catch ...`, `s.length();`, `Math.abs(-5);`), sem classe, sem `main`, sem aspecto |
| `exercicio_10.aj` | `declare parents : MyClass implements Serializable;` — declaração estática fora de aspecto e referenciando tipo inexistente |

Resumo: 1 arquivo correto em 21; nenhum exercício era um programa; nenhum arquivo, exceto o primeiro, podia ser compilado.

## 3. Reescritas
Todos os 21 arquivos foram reescritos. Cada `.aj` agora é autocontido — classes Java de apoio mais o aspecto — e termina com uma classe `main` executável. Os pointcuts são sempre restritos às classes do próprio arquivo, de modo que os arquivos também possam ser compilados em conjunto sem interferência cruzada.

Exemplos: progressão de `pointcut`/`before`/`after` (1) para contexto `target`/`args` (2), `call` versus `execution` (3), `around` com `proceed` (4), `after returning`/`after throwing` (5), `thisJoinPoint` e `if(...)` (6), `within`/`cflow` com recursão (7), declaração inter-tipo (8), `declare parents`/`warning`/`error`/`precedence` (9) e estilo `@AspectJ` (10).

Exercícios: contador de chamadas, cronômetro, validação de argumento com exceção, memoização, registro de falhas, log de entrada e saída, controle de acesso por `within`, desconto via ITD, ordenação com `Comparable` injetado e monitor de desempenho anotado. Nenhum repete o tema de outro; todos têm resultado verificável na saída.

## 4. Erros encontrados na validação e correções aplicadas
A primeira rodada real de compilação reprovou 7 arquivos. Cada falha e sua correção:

1. `The public type Ex1OlaMundo must be defined in its own file` (todos os arquivos). O `ajc` 1.9.22 aplica a regra do `javac`: tipo público exige arquivo homônimo, e os arquivos se chamam `exemplo_N.aj`. **Correção:** classes e aspectos de topo passaram a ser declarados sem `public` (visibilidade de pacote); a JVM continua executando a classe `main`. Limitação registrada no README.
2. `Syntax error, parameterized types are only available if source level is 1.5 or greater` (`exemplo_9`, `exercicio_4`, `exercicio_9`). O `ajc` assume `-source 1.4` para `.aj`. **Correção:** `-source 17 -target 17` nos comandos de compilação e no `validate.sh`.
3. `Syntax error, annotations are only available if source level is 1.5 or greater` (`exercicio_10`). Mesma causa do item 2.
4. `Type mismatch: cannot convert from int to Object` em `Object resultado = proceed(...)` (`exemplo_4` em três pontos, `exercicio_2`, `exercicio_4`). `proceed(...)` devolve o tipo declarado no advice `around`, não `Object`. **Correção:** variável local passou a `int`, eliminando também conversões desnecessárias.
5. `circular advice precedence: can't determine precedence between two or more pieces of advice that apply to the same join point: method-execution(int Ex10Tarefa.somar(int, int))` (`exemplo_10`). `@Before`, `@AfterReturning` e `@Around` incidiam sobre o mesmo join point dentro de um único `@Aspect`. **Correção:** os advice foram separados em pointcuts disjuntos (`executar`, `somar`, `main`) e o motivo foi documentado no cabeçalho do arquivo e no README.

Depois das correções, a rodada final compilou e executou os 20 programas sem erro.

## 5. Validação executada (comandos e resultados reais)

```sh
-rw-r--r-- 1 ubuntu ubuntu 15177853 ... aspectjtools-1.9.22.1.jar
```

Compilação e execução de cada arquivo, em diretório de saída separado (`validate.sh`):

```sh
$ java -cp aspectjtools-1.9.22.1.jar org.aspectj.tools.ajc.Main \
    -source 17 -target 17 -cp aspectjrt-1.9.22.1.jar -d out/exemplo_7 exemplo_7.aj
$ java -cp out/exemplo_7:aspectjrt-1.9.22.1.jar Ex7Principal
```

Resultado agregado da rodada final:

```

```

author: nikotpab
body:
## Qué cambia

- **Decisión (pendiente 6 del README):** tramos de las tres políticas. En las tres, la tarifa de servicio no se devuelve.

  | Días antes de la llegada | Flexible | Moderada | Estricta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 14 o más | 100 % | 100 % | 50 % |
  | 7 a 13 | 100 % | 50 % | 0 % |
  | 5 a 6 | 100 % | 0 % | 0 % |
  | 2 a 4 | 50 % | 0 % | 0 % |
  | Menos de 2 | 0 % | 0 % | 0 % |

- **Una clase por política (Strategy):** `PoliticaModerada` y `PoliticaEstricta`, sin cambiar `PoliticaFlexible`.
  - Los tramos viven en la clase porque `politica_cancelacion` guarda un solo tramo y estas tienen hasta dos.
  - Cada una solo declara sus tramos y calcula con `PoliticaCancelacion.porTramos`, para no repetir el cálculo de la flexible. SonarQube Cloud marcaba 8 % de duplicación en la primera versión.
  - `PoliticaCancelacion.porNombre` agrega una línea por cada una.
- **Migración `V14`:** agrega Moderada y Estricta al catálogo con su descripción (RF-16). El formulario de publicación lista las políticas desde `GET /api/v1/catalogos`, así que el frontend ya las ofrece sin cambios.
- **La estimación y la cancelación funcionan con las tres.** Una política sin clase sigue respondiendo 409 con un mensaje claro (SCRUM-38).
- **README:** decisión pendiente 6 marcada como resuelta, con la tabla.

## Pruebas

- **`PoliticaModeradaTest` y `PoliticaEstrictaTest`:** los límites de cada tramo (14, 13, 7 y 6 días; llegada y después), y el redondeo de la mitad al peso.
- **`PoliticaFlexibleTest`:** las tres políticas tienen reglas. El caso "sin reglas" usa ahora un nombre inexistente ("Personalizada"); lo mismo en `ServicioCancelacionesTest`.
- **`CancelacionesIT`:**
  - Moderada a 10 días estima la mitad;
  - Estricta a 40 días estima la mitad, y a 10 días cancela sin devolución y sin llamar a la pasarela.
- **`TiposAlojamientoIT`:** el catálogo ofrece las tres.
- **`CrearPublicacionIT`:** se publica con la política Estricta.
- **`mvn -B verify` con Docker:** 106 pruebas unitarias y 351 de integración, 0 fallas. `ModulosTest` y `ArquitecturaTest` en verde.

## Orden de merge

Usa `V14`. Mergear después de SCRUM-116 (#79, `V12`) y SCRUM-115 (#80, `V13`). Este PR y #80 cambian líneas vecinas de la misma sección del README ("Decisiones pendientes"), así que el segundo que se mergee puede pedir resolver ese conflicto.

author: janezomgzomg
body: _Requested by **Jane**_ ## What changed Fixes the CodeQL alerts flagged on #454 in the song enrichment helpers and ChordsLink (alert numbers from code scanning). - **`songEnrichmentRules.ts` — alerts 28, 29, 30 (`js/redos`, the `VOCAL` regex) and 27, 36 (`js/polynomial-redos`, its two uses).** `VOCAL = /^((oh|ooh|yeah|hey|mm+|mh|hm+|la|na|whoa|uh|ah|a)\s*)+$/` had overlapping alternatives inside a repeated group (`mm+` repeated, `hm+` against `h`+`mm`), so a run of `m`s backtracked exponentially. It is replaced by `isVocalLine`, which checks each word letter by letter (a small dynamic-programming pass, linear in the line length). Same vocables, same answers: fuzzed against the old regex on 300k random strings with no mismatch. - **`enrichmentMatching.ts:5` — alert 33.** `baseTitle` stripped `/\s*\([^)]*\)/g`, which is quadratic on long runs of spaces or of `(`. It now uses a short `withoutParens` loop with `indexOf` that removes the same spans (spaces before a `(`, through the next `)`; an unclosed `(` is kept). Fuzzed against the regex with no mismatch. - **`songCard.ts` (`tagSlug`) — alert 35.** `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")` → `.replace(/^-|-$/g, "")`. The line before collapses every run of non-alphanumerics into one `-`, so there is never more than one dash in a row and the result is identical. - **`ChordsLink.tsx:19` and `:29` — alerts 22, 23 (`js/xss-through-dom`).** The chart URL a member types into ChordChartSlot flows into the link's `href`. ChordsLink now renders nothing unless the address starts with `http://` or `https://`, so a `javascript:` or `data:` URL can never become a link. The server already only accepts Ultimate Guitar http(s) links, so real charts look exactly the same. React already escapes attribute values, so markup in a URL was never rendered as elements; the new test pins that. - **`hymnary.ts:40`** — already fixed on `feat/mobile-mvp` (`trimTrailing` loop; alert 34 is closed), so nothing to change here. Not in this PR (other alerts still open, outside this task): SongEditor.tsx `js/xss-through-dom` (19, 20), `youtube.com` substring checks (13, 14, 15), `scripts/ticketing-test-env.mjs` clear-text logging (12), and the tickets checkout regex (1). ## Why CodeQL flagged these on #454. The enrichment helpers run on lyrics, titles and tag names from outside services, so a crafted value could stall a request. A chart URL is typed in by members and shown to everyone, so it must never be a `javascript:` link. ## Tests - `packages/core`: new tests pin the lyrics' first-line fallback around vocal lines (`Ooh, mm-hmm, la la la…` skipped; `Oh yeah, ohh yeah…` and `Mmh mmh…` kept), bracket stripping in Wikipedia title matching (several and nested brackets dropped, an unclosed one kept), and dash trimming in `tagSlug`. One test per fixed pattern runs a 50k-repetition adversarial string (`mm`, `mahm`, `hmm`, spaces, `(`, ` (`, `-`) and checks it finishes under 500 ms. - `apps/web`: new `ChordsLink.test.tsx`: a normal chart renders both links; `">` inside a URL comes out as escaped text with no `` element; `javascript:`, `data:` and bare markup render nothing. - Results: core vitest 584/584 passed, web vitest 956/956 passed, web and core `tsc --noEmit` clean, `node scripts/check-repo-rules.mjs` OK. - Playwright not run: ChordsLink looks the same for every link the app can store (they are all http(s)). ## Verification steps 1. Open a set with a song that has a chord chart: the Chords pill and phone icon still link to Ultimate Guitar. 2. Add a chart with the dashed Chords button: it saves and shows as before. 3. Run song enrichment on a song: first line, hook and Wikipedia matching behave as before. 4. After CI, check Security → Code scanning: alerts 22, 23, 27, 28, 29, 30, 33, 35 and 36 should be closed. ## Build check - [ ] `npm run build` not run: Jane's dev server is always running on this machine, so builds are left to CI. `tsc --noEmit` is clean for web and core. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
Explorer tables now keep the seller / model name column pinned on the left while the rest of the row scrolls sideways on narrow screens.

## Problem and resulting behavior

On phones, Explorer tables (`components/ui.tsx` `Table`) scroll horizontally. Once you scroll right, the first column (seller, model, day) disappears and the numbers lose the row they belong to.

After this PR:
- The first column of every `Table` is sticky, with an opaque background that inherits the row and header colors.
- A 1px divider and soft shadow appear only while the table is scrolled sideways, using a CSS scroll timeline. At scroll 0, and on tables that fit, the table looks as it does on `develop`. Browsers without `animation-timeline` (Firefox today) keep the sticky column but show no divider.
- Below the `md` breakpoint, model names in tables that overflow are capped at `55vw - 2rem` with an ellipsis, and the full name stays in `title`, so a pinned name can never cover the other columns. A small client wrapper (`components/table-scroll.tsx`) sets this cap only on tables that overflow. It uses a `ResizeObserver` to measure the uncapped table and sets `data-overflow` on the scroll container. Tables that fit render exactly as on `develop`, and real names (e.g. `qwen3-0.6b Q4_K_M`) are never cut.
- Full-width `colspan` empty-state cells are not sticky. Desktop is unchanged.

Explorer UI only (`app/globals.css`, `components/ui.tsx`, `components/table-scroll.tsx`, `components/usage-section.tsx`). No API, wire, storage or registry (`components/board`) changes.

author: gustavopaixao
body:
## What it does

Node.js 26 becomes the target LTS. 22.14 (the minimum, from #317), 24 and 26 are all supported, and CI runs each version only where its risk is: the ends of the range, nothing in between.

**The target moves to 26**
- **`.nvmrc`:** `26`.
- **The Docker image:** `node:26-trixie-slim`, pinned by digest.
- **The server bundles:** `NODE_MAJOR = 26`. They fetch Node.js 26 and verify it against `SHASUMS256.txt`.
- **The feed workflow `rmk` writes:** Node.js 26, with its golden files updated.
- **The Homebrew service check:** takes the target from `.nvmrc`, as `bundles.yml` and `packages.yml` now do.

**CI: one job per role, not per version**
- **`ci.yml`:**
  - "Lint, typecheck, test, build (target Node.js)" runs everything the Node 24 job ran.
  - "Runtime tests (minimum Node.js)" runs exactly `MIN_NODE`, 22.14.0, and only `pnpm install` and the new `pnpm test:runtime`.
  - Step conditions use `matrix.role`, so the next LTS changes only the numbers.
- **`server-checks.yml`:** installs and runs the packed server on 22.14.0 and 26, on Linux, macOS and Windows. That's 6 jobs instead of 9, with no Node.js 24 job (the owner's decision).
- **`pnpm test:runtime`:** every test except the component tests (`*.test.tsx`) and `repo-tools`. That's the code that runs on a person's Node.js, the SQLite database tests included.

**Guards in `repo-tools`**
- **The drift guard fails when:**
  - the Dockerfile, `NODE_MAJOR`, the feed workflow, the Homebrew check or a role matrix names a major other than `.nvmrc`'s;
  - a minimum entry isn't exactly `MIN_NODE`;
  - a published package's `engines` isn't `^MIN_NODE || >=MIN_NODE_23`.
- **The N-API guard** fails when a `.node` file in the server's runtime tree isn't N-API. Skipping 24 is safe only because every native module is one binary for every Node.js version.

**Two other changes**
- **A telemetry test now skips on 22.14.0.** It uses `module.registerHooks`, which arrived in 22.15. Pinning the minimum to 22.14.0 caught this on its first run. The target's job still runs the test, and no shipped code uses that API.
- **The docs state the 26 target and the CI split:** `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the dependency policy, MVP.md (with a §15 entry), `test-runs.md` ("Which Node.js version runs what"), `release.md` and `threat-model.md`.

**Required checks:** none of the renamed jobs is on `main`'s required checks (read on 2026-11-20), so branch protection doesn't change.

## Feature or issue

Feature 188, in `docs/features/188-node-26-target`:
- **Tasks 1 to 9 are done**, each with a state-witness pass in `WITNESS.md` and an adversarial pass where the task was risky.
- **All 13 acceptance criteria are ticked.**
- **Measured:**
  - on Node.js 26: install, lint, typecheck, test, build, `build:server`, `packages:check`, `release:smoke` and `pnpm dev`;
  - on 22.14.0: `test:runtime`;
  - the Docker image prints v26.

**This pull request is stacked on #317**, which raises the minimum to 22.14. Merge #317 first. Then:

```
git rebase --onto main bugfix/315-node-22-14-minimum feat/188-node-26-target
```

Retarget this one to `main`, then merge it.

## Checks

- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` pass (the pre-commit hook), on Node.js 26; `pnpm test:runtime` on 22.14.0
- [ ] Database code: none changed
- [ ] Screen text: none changed
- [ ] Dependencies: none added (the Docker base image moves to Node.js 26)

## Documentation

The website's home page stack line, the runtime fact and the From a clone step say Node.js 26, in en, pt and fr: ronneai/ronne-web#102, shared with #317. No in-app helper names a version.

body:
Stacked on #81. This completes the data step of `Docs/Port.md`.

## What
- `DataAssets.LoadAll<T>()` returns every data asset of a type in the content folder, skipping hidden folders and broken files. `Find<T>(Tag id)` finds a definition by its id. The file list resets when a `.fvdata` file changes.
- `DataTypes.ReadRows` / `WriteTable` are shared by the runtime and the editor.
- Tables open in the Data tab (`TableDocument`, `TableViewModel`, `TableRowViewModel`):
  - a form per row;
  - rows can be added (`Row`, `Row 2`…), renamed in place (an empty or taken name reverts) and removed;
  - edits are held unsaved like a data asset's.
- CSV export and import (`TableCsv`): a `name` column, then one column per property. Strings are written as they are, other values as JSON. Quoted cells, commas and doubled quotes are handled, and an unknown column is refused without changing the rows.
- CLAUDE.md documents it.

## Notes
- Rows are shown as one collapsible form per row, not a grid.
- Import errors only show as a tooltip on the Data tab for now.

## Tests

## Summary

dab-v1-147 (monthly ball-security dashboard) failed in 3/4 archives on deterministic anchors: the eval requires each headline number (months=7, games=82, first/last eFG and TOV/g) to appear **inside each artifact payload** — `serialize_artifact_text` flattens artifact values (skipping only `title`/`name`/`label`/`unit`-family keys) per `kind`, and series data alone cannot carry a count or a summary value.

Classification: teachable gap, not a tool gap. The schema already supports it — `chart.footnote` renders and stays in the payload, `table` rows carry summary cells — but nothing taught the analyst that headline numbers must be embedded *inside* every artifact, not only in prose.

Fixes:
- `visual-artifacts` SKILL.md gains "§4 Headline Numbers Live Inside the Payload": table → summary/denominator rows; chart/scatter/shot_chart → scope counts and endpoint values in `footnote`; compare → dedicated rows; memo → figures inside each section body.
- `runtime.ts` submit directive now says figures must appear "inside every emitted artifact payload — not solely in prose", naming the footnote/summary-row mechanism.

Scoped test (`test_artifact_headline_numbers.py`) encodes the contract: a 147-shaped chart (footnote) and table (summary rows) each recover all six anchors; a series-only chart provably cannot carry the counts.

author: arismoko
body:
> 🤖 Opened by Aria's agent swarm, Dyna, not by Aria.

A stable patch release on `release/26.3` may ship after only the daily legs its cherry-picks select have passed, instead of the full daily, once two people approve it in GitHub. It builds on #3768's stable kind (`nightly build` with `kind=stable`) and the daily evidence it already uses.

**Stacked on #3813** (the stable mod API semver check); its base is that branch. Break-glass never bypasses that check: it runs on every stable release, break-glass included, and break-glass adds a stricter surface rule on top. Break-glass skips only the full daily. The 26.3-0.1.0 release doesn't use this path: with no published stable release there is nothing to patch.

## Precondition: the release branch is the trust boundary
GitHub runs `nightly-build.yml` from the ref it is dispatched on. A stable release's workflow, its checks (`nightly.py`, `release_train.py`) and its signing script (`sign_release.sh`) are therefore `release/26.3`'s own, and no step in the workflow can make them independent of that branch.

What this PR keeps independent of the candidate's built code:
- the mod API is judged by the published parent's own `sunrise-stage`;
- signatures are checked with OpenSSL against main's `release-keys.txt`.

Before any stable release after 0.1.0, Sunrise's owners set a ruleset on `release/26.3` and every later `release/*` (`docs/release-flow.md`, "Release branches"):
- a pull request for every change;
- one approving review from someone other than the last pusher, with stale approvals dismissed on a new push;
- force pushes and deletion blocked;
- no bypass actors.

Code-owner review is added once `.github/CODEOWNERS` names a sunrise-org team. Today it names another organisation's team, so requiring it would request nobody.

## Every stable release, not only break-glass
This PR also closes #3813's review findings 1–4 for ordinary stable releases. #3813's own fixes (findings 5–9) are merged forward from `moddist-semver-gate`.
- **No candidate code judges the candidate.** For every same-line stable release, `stable-mod-api` builds the published parent's own `sunrise-stage` from the parent's tree alone, then uses it to export both trees and diff them. Its export of the parent must equal the parent's signed `surface.json`, and a tree it cannot read is refused.
- **Isolation.** No `cargo` run in these checks inherits `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, the Actions tokens, a target folder or a compiler wrapper.
- **Before signing.** `stable-mod-api` runs in `pick` for every stable release, before any approval, build or signature. It runs again in `publish` before the tag.
- **Parent tag.** The parent's tag must name the commit its own signed `sunrise-release.json` names.
- **Version step.** The first release is 0.1.0; a patch keeps the major and minor; a minor is `X.N.0`; a major is `N.0.0`. This is checked at the pick, in `stable-mod-api` and in `reserve-stable-tag`, which also re-checks the parent for every stable release.

- **Release signatures without the checkout's code.** `nightly.py verify-sums` checks a release folder as launchers do, using the runner's OpenSSL and main's `release-keys.txt`. It replaces `cargo run sunrise-release-sign` in `pick`, `publish` and `musl-attach`, so no release job runs cargo in the candidate's checkout. The only build left is the parent's `sunrise-stage`, built from the parent's own tree. No cargo or built tool run here inherits the job's tokens or its `GITHUB_ENV`, `GITHUB_PATH`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `GITHUB_STATE` or `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` files.
- **Content declarations (#3813 finding 7).** Until #3817 exports content declarations, the stable gate refuses patches and minors that change a guarded manifest or content reader (`CONTENT_SCHEMA_PATHS`), even if the SDK's `content_api` is unchanged. The refusal lists every changed path, so legitimate fixes in those files also have to wait for a major.
- **The real differ (#3813 finding 8).** A daily integration test drives the stable gate with the real `sunrise-stage surface-diff` on schema-3 fixtures. It checks the patch and minor policy for all four verdicts, and shows that a valid change note cannot waive a refusal.

## One parent for every check
`nightly.stable_parent` resolves the newest published stable release on the target (not draft, not pre-release) before the release being made. The path diff, the leg evidence, the parent's daily and `stable-mod-api`'s surface comparison all use it.
- A `26.3-*` tag above it with no published release refuses. That covers an aborted run's tag or one pushed by hand. It applies to every stable release, at the pick before anything is built (a dry run warns), so #3813's ordinary check and the notes' "Since" section use the same parent.
- `pick` outputs the parent's tag and commit and shows them, with the selected legs, in the run summary before either environment asks for approval. `reserve-stable-tag` resolves the parent again and refuses if its tag or commit changed.

## The four review points

**1. Two approvals, enforced by GitHub.**
- `nightly-build.yml` binds one job to each of two environments. `release_train.BREAK_GLASS_APPROVERS` names each environment's approver by GitHub user id: UMCEKO for `break-glass-umceko`, arismoko for `break-glass-aria`. GitHub lets any one reviewer of an environment approve, so two people need two environments.
- The `break-glass` job reads every page of the run's recorded approvals. It refuses unless:
  - each environment was approved once, by its own approver, who is a user (not a bot or app);
  - no environment has a rejection or a second review.
- Only the run's first attempt counts, because the approvals record carries no attempt. `pick` refuses a re-run before anyone is asked, and the approval jobs, `break-glass`, `exporters`, `build`, `musl-build`, `sign`, `publish` and `musl-attach` run a break-glass release only in attempt 1, so a re-run of failed jobs never re-enters an approval, a build or a signing. A new dispatch asks both people again.
- `exporters`, `sign` and `publish` each wait for a successful `break-glass` job. `reserve-stable-tag` checks the approvals again right before the tag.
- `break_glass` is only the reason text. No input or variable stands in for an approval.
- **Settings to configure** (both environments): the one required reviewer; deployment branches limited to `release/26.3`; admin bypass off. With *Prevent self-review* on, the person who dispatches the release can't approve their own environment.

**2. Changed paths select the daily legs, fail-closed.**
- `release_train.break_glass_legs` maps each path that differs between the parent and the release commit through `BREAK_GLASS_LEGS`; the first matching row wins. Paths are read with `git -c core.quotePath=false diff -z --raw --no-renames`.
  - `docs/modding/` and `tools/book_quickstart.py` select `book-quickstart`. Other `docs/` paths select nothing extra.
  - The code that judges a release needs the full daily: `sunrise-mod-api-gen`, `sunrise-mod-surface`, `sunrise-mod-package` and `sunrise-release-sign`, and every local crate they build from (`release_train.judge_graph`: path dependencies of every target, those through `[workspace.dependencies]`, and every crate the root's `[patch]` or `[replace]` points to). So does any change to `[patch]` or `[replace]`, to a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry those crates take, or to the `Cargo.lock` entries they build from (their crates.io versions included).
  - Other `crates/`, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` select every leg that tests the game: `cargo-sunrise-mod`, `parity`, the ignored-test `shards` and `windows-runtime-leases`.
  - A folder row also matches the folder replaced by a file or link.
  - The SDK legs sdk-publish waits for (`sdk`, `machine-sample`, `fn-replace-check`) always run, because a release ships only after its `sdk-<sha>`.
- The full daily is needed for any unmapped path, a symbolic link, a submodule, or a name holding a line

author: schnie
body:
When `astro local check` provisions a venv to parse a project's Dags, it caches the venv under a key built from Airflow, Python, the requirements and the constraints. The project's index pages (`[tool.uv.sources]` routes, passed to the install as `--find-links`) were left out of the key.

So two projects with the same requirements but different indexes, each with its own build of an internal package, shared one cached venv. The second project's check then ran against the first project's packages.

## Change

`uvProvisioner.key` now hashes `spec.FindLinks` as its own delimited section. It does so only when there are any, as it already does for constraints, so a spec without find-links keeps its existing key and its cached venv. A project that does route packages gets a new key and rebuilds its venv once; the existing sweep removes the old one.

## Tests

`TestProvisionerKeyIsStableAndSpecific` gains two cases:
- the same spec with find-links added gets a different key;
- two projects with the same requirements and different index pages for `internal-lib` don't share a key.

Both fail without the change.

## Checks

- `make test`
- golangci-lint on `cmd/local`
- `GOOS=windows go vet`
- `make deadcode`

## 관련 이슈

closes #1337

## 구현 내용

앱 설치 안내 배너를 첫 방문일에는 띄우지 않고, 다음 방문일부터 띄운다. 첫 방문일에는 배너가 DOM에 들어오지 않고, 배너용 입력 감지와 `beforeinstallprompt` 처리도 등록하지 않는다.

판단은 이미 브라우저에 저장하던 방문 기록(`siglens:visit-history:v1`)의 첫 방문일을 읽어서 한다. 한국 날짜 기준이며 기기 시간대와 무관하다. 서버로 더 보내는 정보는 없다.

기록을 읽을 수 없거나(차단, 비공개 모드) 값이 깨졌거나 첫 방문일이 미래면 배너를 띄우지 않는다.

개인정보처리방침 v15(ko, en, ja, zh)의 방문 기록 항목에 이 용도를 한 문장으로 추가했고, 가드 테스트가 네 언어에서 두 구절("앱 설치 안내"에 쓴다는 것, 서버로 더 전송되는 정보가 없다는 것)을 확인한다.

## 변경 파일 목록

[수정]
- `src/entities/visitor/lib/visitHistory.ts`: `isReturnVisitDay`
- `src/features/visitor-ping/lib/visitHistoryStorage.ts`: `readIsReturnVisitDay`
- `src/features/pwa-install/hooks/usePwaInstall.ts`: 재방문일일 때만 배너와 트리거 활성화
- `e2e/support/pwaBanner.ts`(`seedReturnVisit`), `e2e/specs/pwa-install.spec.ts`, `e2e/specs/symbol-overlays.spec.ts`
- `docs/conventions/TESTING.md`: TE-66(e2e 부재 단언은 대상 코드가 이미 실행됐다는 증거가 필요), 약속 문장 가드 보강
- `db/seeds/terms/privacy/v15.{md,en.md,ja.md,zh.md}`: 방문 기록 항목 용도 문장 추가
- `src/features/CLAUDE.md`
- 테스트: `visitHistory.test.ts`, `visitHistoryStorage.test.ts`, `usePwaInstall.test.ts`, `visitHistoryPrivacy.test.ts`

## 검증

- 로컬: typecheck, lint, format:check, i18n:extract(변화 없음), 범위 테스트 126 파일 2061건 통과
- 브라우저(로컬 e2e 스택, webkit iPhone 14와 Chromium 모바일): 첫 방문일에는 배너 없음, 재방문일에는 첫 입력 뒤 배너 표시와 닫기 유지, 내일 날짜/깨진 값/저장소 예외는 배너 없음, 기기 시간대를 바꿔도 같은 결과, 첫 방문과 재방문의 네트워크 요청 집합 동일

## 알려진 한계

- Safari는 7일간 방문이 없으면 스크립트가 쓴 저장소를 비운다. 그 브라우저는 다시 첫 방문으로 계산되어 다음 방문일까지 배너가 없다.

## Summary

Moves `drizzle-orm` (in `@wfgraph/core`) and `drizzle-kit` (root) from 1.0.0-rc.5 to 1.0.0-rc.6, after reading the [rc.6 release notes](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/releases/tag/v1.0.0-rc.6).

### Changes that rc.6 required

- **SQLite integer decoding.** rc.6 removed cast codecs and now asks `node:sqlite` (`effect-sqlite-node`) for integers as `bigint` per statement. An integer `sql` expression with no `.mapWith()` therefore arrives as a `bigint`. Five fields in the native SQLite backend broke four conformance cases: `new Date(bigint)` threw, `isCurrent === 1` never matched, and the superseded count came back as `2n`. The five fields are two `count(*)`, `min(started_at)` and two `coalesce` flags. Each now has `.mapWith(Number)`, and the nullable `min` keeps its `| null` type.
- **drizzle-kit snapshot format 10.** drizzle-kit rc.6 refuses to generate against format 9 snapshots. `drizzle-kit up` rewrote the 38 committed PostgreSQL snapshots. The only edits are the `version` field and the removed `"concurrently": false` index key. No `migration.sql` changed, so `assertJournalHashesAreOurs` still holds. `db:generate` and `db:generate:sqlite` both report no schema changes.
- **pnpm release age.** rc.6 was published the day this PR was opened, so pnpm added both versions to `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`.
- **Changeset.** A patch changeset for `@wfgraph/core`.
- **Intent review.** The maintainer review is recorded in `.intent/review-state.json`. No published skill needed an edit.

### ADR-0005 amendment: Drizzle's own Effect driver

rc.6 also ships `drizzle-orm/postgres/effect`, an Effect driver on Drizzle's own PostgreSQL client. I evaluated it against a local PostgreSQL 16 and the installed type declarations as a replacement for postgres.js, and the Postgres backend stays on postgres.js. The dated amendment to ADR-0005 records why:

- The client can't `LISTEN`, and `postgres-run-wakes.ts` relies on `LISTEN` for the cross-process run wake.
- It discards server notices.
- Its Effect layer config has no field for startup `options`.
- Its `ssl` option has no `allow` or `prefer`.

The amendment also lists three behaviours a future migration must handle that no type error reports, and four conditions for reopening the decision.

### rc.6 breaking changes that don't affect this repo

The repo uses none of these: the query cache, the `up-migrations` helpers, `.concurrently()` on pg indexes, `withCastCodecs`, or `postgresJsCodecs` / `minipg`. The `postgres-js` raw `execute` calls in `cancel-order.ts` read only a boolean (`locked`), so removing the transparent decoders doesn't change their results. Type-check also passes with rc.6's new `| null` typing on subquery fields.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run type-check`
- [x] `pnpm run lint`
- [x] `pnpm run test` (6661 passed)
- [x] `pnpm run test:postgres` with `WFGRAPH_REQUIRE_POSTGRES=1` against a local PostgreSQL 16 (365 passed)
- [x] `pnpm run build`
- [x] `pnpm run knip`
- [x] `pnpm run skills:validate`
- [x] `pnpm run package:smoke`
- [x] `pnpm run fix` leaves the tree clean
- [x] `pnpm exec intent maintainer check`

All of these ran on Node 22.23 in the session container. The repo's `engines` floor is Node 24, so CI is the Node 24 run.

author: annabigihed
body:
## What changed

- `POST /api/v1/sessions/refresh` (anonymous, 30/min per address, 1 KB body): single-use refresh tokens; reuse of a rotated token revokes the whole family and the revocation is saved before the 401 (reloaded and retried once if that save fails; a database error still ends in the generic 401); sliding 30-day and absolute 90-day expiry; two concurrent refreshes of one token give exactly one successor.
- Access tokens carry `sid` (the family); `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/current` revokes the caller's own family (idempotent; a foreign or unknown `sid` changes nothing).
- `DELETE /api/v1/me`: deletes the account and its sessions and upserts the subject hash into `erasure_log` in one transaction (rolled back if the log write fails); idempotent, also for concurrent calls; afterwards the old access token gets 401 on `/me` and a new sign-in creates a new account.
- `deploy/server/pt-erasure-reapply` + `deploy/sql/erasure-reapply.sql`: export the live erasure log before a restore, re-apply it after (dry run by default, validated private copy of the input, only accounts created on or before the erasure day, purge rows older than six months); installed by `provision.sh`, ShellChecked in CI.
- Domain `UserAccount.EndFamily`, Backend.Application commands `RefreshSession`, `EndSession`, `EraseAccount`, `IErasureLog`; Contracts `RefreshSessionRequest`; OpenAPI operations and examples.
- Test infrastructure: the test PostGIS container starts with `max_connections=500` (each E2E test migrates its own database with its own pool).

## Why it changed

Stage S5, PR 6 of the plan (ADR-0014, ADR-0015, architecture 6.1): the rest of the session lifecycle and the GDPR erasure endpoint, so the app (PR 7) can sign in, stay signed in through the foreground service, sign out and delete the account.

There is no issue tracker entry, so the branch is `feature/s5-…` as in the earlier S5 pull requests.

## How it was tested

- `verify.py`: build OK; Api.E2E 127, Backend.Application 47, Persistence.EntityFrameworkCore 34, Domain 492, all other projects passing; 10 live-source tests skipped as usual.
- Deploy tests: `test_pt_deploy.sh` 76 passed (stub docker proves dry run → ROLLBACK, `--commit` → COMMIT, psql failure → exit 1, invalid files never reach docker); Python 38 OK.
- Independent security review: one P2 (re-apply would delete an account re-created after the erasure) and several P3s, all fixed; recheck clean. Standards review: no blocking finding; notes applied.

## What to review carefully

- `RefreshSessionCommandHandler` (reuse path and retry), `EraseAccountCommandHandler`, `erasure-reapply.sql`.
- The same-day erase-and-sign-up limitation of the re-apply, documented in the runbook.

## Migration or deployment notes

No migration and no new secret: merging deploys as usual. ShellCheck of the new script runs only in CI (not available locally).

### Author self-review

- [x] I read the diff end-to-end after my last commit
- [x] CHANGELOG: Added entry under [Unreleased]
- [x] No secret, credential, or PII committed
- [ ] CI is fully green on the latest commit (running)

## Summary

This PR adds `.github/workflows/check-heading-siblings.yml`, a caller of gha's `check-heading-siblings.yml@v3` ([Morrison-Lab/gha#2171](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/2171)).

On pull requests, it fails two kinds of heading:

- a heading the PR adds to a group of more than seven siblings;
- a lone numbered subheading (a 1.1 with no 1.2) that the PR adds or changes. This is Ezra's rule from [psw#692](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/pull/692).

A manual run scans the whole tree.

A whole-tree run on main finds 22 groups. The check is diff-scoped, so it reports one only when a PR touches it.

**What changed**

author: levismadar80-ship-it
body:
## Summary

The LCP sweep on staging (20/11; Pixel 5, slow 4G, CPU ×4) found two pages whose first content waited for hydration.

- **`/he/map`: LCP 6.40s.** The LCP element is the cookie banner's text. `CookieBanner` started hidden and appeared only after its effect read localStorage. Every first visit on every page paid for this; on /map it was the largest element.
- **`/he/login` (and `/he/favorites` for a guest): LCP 5.50s / 7.04s.** `LoginClient` wrapped its whole body in a `Suspense` that called `useSearchParams`, so the static HTML held only «loading». It also gated the form on `authLoading`.

**Fix (industry pattern: put the consent banner and auth form in the server HTML, and use a pre-paint flag for state that lives only in storage):**
- `lib/prehydration-flags-inline.js` is a 1-line inline script, placed first in `<head>` next to the existing MEH-3164 script. CSP already allows `'unsafe-inline'`. It sets `data-cookie-answered` and `data-has-token` on `<html>` from localStorage before the first paint.
- In `app/globals.css`, those flags hide the banner's pre-mount copy and the login form while auth is pending. So the banner never flashes for someone who already answered, and the form never flashes for a stored session. That keeps MEH-1489's intent.
- `CookieBanner` starts visible with a `data-prehydration` marker and decides after mount. The footer re-open (MEH-3196) is unchanged.
- In `LoginClient`, only a small `QueryReader` suspends on the URL. `?redirect=` still goes through `safeInternalRedirect`. The authed redirect waits until the URL is read. `?email=` prefill and the `?reset=1` toast run once it is read.
- `<html>` gets `suppressHydrationWarning`. It covers only its own attributes.

The local build still prerenders `● /he/login`. Its static HTML now contains `login-email`, `data-auth-pending` and `cookie-banner`.

## Measured on the preview (`2b78b05ad`, median of 5, same harness)

| Page | staging | preview |
|---|---|---|
| `/he/login` | 5.50s | **1.70s** |
| `/he/map` | 6.40s | **1.97s** (the LCP is now a map image, no longer the banner text) |
| `/he/favorites` (guest) | 7.04s | 6.57s. The remaining time is the client redirect; #4997 removes it. |

## Tests

- New: `PrehydrationFlags.test.jsx`, 9 tests. Two of them fail on the old components (the banner is in the server HTML; the login form is in the server HTML while auth resolves). The others pin:
  - the script's keys against `cookie-consent.js` and `auth-context.js`
  - the two CSS rules
  - post-mount behaviour
  - a signed-in visitor never getting the form
- Changed: `AuthPagesAuthedRedirect.test.jsx` "while auth resolves the form is gated" now asserts the form is inside `[data-auth-pending]`, which the CSS hides for a stored session. This is the same intent, enforced by a different mechanism; the comment in the test says so.
- 42 files that touch the layout, globals.css or login: 524 tests pass. Local guards also pass: typed-new-modules, file-size, clone, test-honesty, rtl, z-index.

## Reviewer findings (fresh Fable subagent; auth-adjacent, so RED-tier reviewer) and changes (`2b78b05ad`)

1. **BLOCKER: a submit before hydration was a native GET, which put the password in the URL.** **Fixed:**
   - the form is `method="post"` and carries `data-no-native-submit`
   - the inline script blocks a native submit of such a form in the capture phase
   - this is pinned in `PrehydrationFlags.test.jsx`
2. **SHOULD-FIX: dead taps before hydration.** **Fixed:** `[data-prehydration]{pointer-events:none}`, so a tap lands only once React owns the control.
3. **SHOULD-FIX: a blank pane for a token holder while auth resolves.** **Fixed:** a «טוען» note shows under `html[data-has-token]`. This is existing copy, `auth.login.loading`.
4. **SHOULD-FIX: an early submit ignored `?redirect=`.** **Fixed:** `landingFor` reads `window.location.search` when the URL has not been read yet, still clamped by `safeInternalRedirect`.
5. **SHOULD-FIX: answering the banner, then a remount, flashed it again.** **Fixed:** `setCookieConsent` also sets `data-cookie-answered`.
6. **SHOULD-FIX: no-flash is checked only by a CSS regex.** Answered: the unit tests pin both the flag script and the rules. A Playwright no-flash case is a follow-up, because it needs a storage-seeded first paint, which E2E `addInitScript` provides only after the head script runs.
7. **SHOULD-FIX: CLS from `--cookie-banner-h` being unset until hydration.** Answered: the banner is `position: fixed` and does not shift content. The variable only pads BottomNav's offset after mount.
8. **NITs:** fixed the test filename citation. The outer Suspense is kept; it costs nothing.
9. **Docs:**
   - `docs/features/auth.md`: key file + test
   - `docs/SECURITY.md` §8-CSP: the second inline script added to the stage-3 nonce plan
   - the `30-login-journey-c.spec.ts` comment that said the server HTML has no login testids

The two new `set-state-in-effect` findings were removed: `mounted` uses `useSyncExternalStore`, and the URL handler is a stable callback. The eslint ratchet passes.

Reviewer: fresh Fable subagent; 1 BLOCKER + 6 SHOULD-FIX: 5 fixed, 2 answered (above).
Self-check: CI gate + Deploy gate green on the head 2b78b05; staging green (1596a3e, E2E run 44855100730); preview measured above.

Skills: mehamakor-dod, adversarial-review. No copy and no new UI pattern.

body:
The plug-in platform and marketplace tests repeated themselves. Three files (`marketplace_audit_test`, `plugin_services_audit_test`, `plugin_oauth_keys_test`) re-made the same requests as the endpoint tests next to them, just to check one more thing. Refusal cases were each written out as a separate test where one parametrized test would do. Several service tests repeated what endpoint tests already check through real requests, and some tests only checked constants or hand lists. This PR keeps every distinct assertion and moves each one into the test closest to the real request.

## Deleted (test → what already covers it)
- **`plugin_oauth_test`**
  - `test_a_key_the_plugin_never_registered_is_refused` → the `foreign-key-under-the-kid` case of `test_a_bad_assertion_is_an_invalid_client`.
  - `test_an_assertion_is_used_once` → `test_an_assertion_presented_twice_is_refused_and_written_down`, which now also asserts `invalid_client`.
- **`plugin_install_acceptance_test`**
  - `test_a_response_naming_people_costs_one_statement_cold_and_none_warm` → the cold/warm counts in `test_an_uploaded_picture_reaches_a_plugin_by_reference_under_members_read` and `test_a_response_mentioning_three_people_costs_one_statement_cold`.
- **`plugin_scope_dep_test`**
  - `test_the_dependency_carries_its_scope` → the probe route's request tests, since `ActorSessionDep` reads `route_plugin_scope`.
- **`context_jwt_test`**
  - The three JWKS publishing tests → `plugin_platform_test`'s key-set tests, which now also assert `use == "sig"`.
- **`registrations_test`**
  - Create, fingerprint, origin and fail-closed tests → `plugin_services_test` endpoint tests. These now also assert the fingerprint, and that `allowed_origins` follows the browser address on create, update and clear.
  - Listing/registration hand-over tests → `tuf_registry_test`.
- **`operator_catalog_test`**
  - Dropped-file, idempotent-rescan and missing-directory tests → `marketplace_test` rescan tests. The dropped-file test now also asserts `publisher`.
- **`tuf_registry_test`**
  - Tampered and not-a-bundle tests → `marketplace_registry_test` bundle-upload tests.
- **`bundled_dashboards_test`**
  - Three offer/install tests → `tenant_endpoints/marketplace_test.py`.
- **`definitions_test`, `contract_test`, `plugin_refs_test`, `plugin_data_test`, `plugin_api_test`, `tool_listings_test`, `widget_meta_test`, `service_plugins_test`**
  - Tests of constants, hand lists and derived sets.
- **Product code only tests called**
  - `catalog.listing_versions`, and `definitions.kinds_for_audience` with `LISTING_AUDIENCES`.

## Merged (test → test it folded into)
- **`marketplace_audit_test.py` (file deleted)**
  - Rescan audit record → `marketplace_test::test_a_dropped_file_appears_without_a_restart`.
  - Refused scans record nothing → `test_no_directory_configured_is_a_400` and `test_only_the_config_capability_may_rescan`.
- **`plugin_services_audit_test.py` (file deleted)**
  - Create, update, no-op, refused, delete and publisher audit records → the matching `plugin_services_test` endpoint tests.
- **`plugin_oauth_keys_test.py` (file deleted)**
  - Its tests, together with the suspended and declarative cases → `plugin_oauth_test::test_a_registration_that_is_not_live_is_an_invalid_client` (parametrized) and `test_a_key_set_published_at_its_address_authenticates`.
- **`plugin_oauth_test`**
  - Down-scoping and write-asked-at-read → `test_an_installation_token_carries_every_granted_scope`.
  - The four standing-level tests → `test_a_standing_is_carried_only_at_the_level_asked_for`.
  - Level-beyond-ceiling → the ceiling test.
  - Fifteen refusal tests and params → `test_a_token_it_will_not_issue_is_refused`.
- **`plugin_hub_test`**
  - Seven refusal tests → `test_a_call_the_hub_will_not_make_is_refused`.
  - Narrowed call and write-not-cached → the installation-call test.
  - Member-connections → `test_a_read_is_cached_per_actor`.
- **`plugin_installation_test`**
  - The token tests (none, member, switched off, no keys, another listing) → one parametrized test across all three routes.
  - Connections-never-name → the connections test.
  - Lookup → the write/read/remove test.
  - Shown-values read → `test_values_reach_whom_the_plugins_actions_would`.
- **`plugin_install_acceptance_test`**
  - Private-file share → the files read test.
  - Project-create refusal → the cannot-write test.
  - Placement, scope and switch revocations → `test_a_change_takes_effect_on_the_next_request`.
  - Members-read refusal → the member-search narrowing test.
  - Suggest narrowing → the narrowed-token test.
  - Suggest-kinds → `test_suggests_only_the_tasks_it_could_read`.
- **`plugin_member_tokens_test`**
  - Initiative-bound consent → the leave/revoke test.
  - Not-installed → the own-client-authentication test.
- **`plugin_sign_in_test`**
  - Refresh token spent only by its own plug-in → the renewal test.
- **`plugin_scope_dep_test`**
  - Guild-from-token → the routed-session test.
  - Write-covers-read and no-scope → one parametrized test.
- **`marketplace_registry_test`**
  - The status test → the refresh test.
- **`plugin_installation_entitlement_test`**
  - The repeat/lower-total test → the kept-total test.
- **`plugin_openapi_superset_test`**
  - Nineteen comparator tests → one parametrized test.
- **Service files**

## Rewritten
None. The service tests left are pure logic, boot paths or background sweeps.

## Totals
`git diff --numstat` against the branch base: **+1867 / -3991**, a net of -2124 lines across 41 files. Three test files are deleted.

## Tests run
- `cd backend && .venv/bin/pytest -q` on every changed endpoint file, plus `services/marketplace/publish_profile_test.py` and `catalog_test.py`: **390 passed**.

author: xuanwo
body:
# Which issue does this PR close?

Supersedes #7438.

# Rationale for this change

Non-append FTP writes stage the content before renaming it to the final path. The FTP backend currently stages every such write in the configured root. A nested write fails when the FTP account can write to the target directory and lacks write permission on the configured root.

# What changes are included in this PR?

Use the target file's parent for the temporary upload. Root-level uploads still use a relative filename so the FTP connection resolves it under the configured root. Cover root-level, nested, and special-character paths in a unit test. The FTP fix comes from @TennyZhuang's #7438. This PR omits the proposed `normalize_root` whitespace trim to preserve the path components as specified by RFC #7799.

# Are there any user-facing changes?

FTP uploads can write to writable subdirectories under a read-only configured root. The temporary file stays in the target directory until the rename completes.

# Local verification

- Reproduced on vsftpd 3.0.2 from `fixtures/ftp/docker-compose-vsftpd.yml`. With the configured root at mode `0555` and an FTP-owned `folder/` at `0755`, `Operator::write("/folder//example.txt", ...)` failed on `1cf276b88` with FTP `553 Could not create file`. The same write succeeded with the patch, readback matched, and the server showed only `folder/example.txt` after close.
- `OPENDAL_TEST=ftp cargo test --locked -p opendal --features tests,services-ftp --test behavior` produced 106 passes and 8 failures on both `1cf276b88` and this branch. With a fresh container and volume for each run, the same five list tests failed on missing directory entries and the same three append tests failed on missing final content length. The fixture used the FTP action's environment, loopback ports, and `RUST_TEST_THREADS=4`.
- `cargo test --locked -p opendal-service-ftp` passed all 4 unit tests and 2 doctests.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p opendal-service-ftp -p opendal --all-targets --features tests,services-ftp -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `hawkeye check`, `git diff --check`, and `python3 scripts/release_impact.py check` passed. The release check used a local PR event containing this description.

# Breaking changes

# AI Usage Statement

- Pi via T3 Code, `magpie/codex/gpt-6.2-sol`, `xhigh` effort. Traced the FTP writer, adapted the original fix, added unit coverage, and ran and compared the Docker and local checks.
- Pi via T3 Code, `magpie/agy-cli/gemini-4-neon`, `high` effort. Scoped the superseding change and identified the accepted RFC constraint.
- The FTP path logic carries forward work from #7438, whose AI statement identifies OpenAI Codex with GPT-5. That PR did not record an effort setting.

author: ferrematerialesnavarro
body:
## Objetivo
Cada ticket enviado a la impresora desde un teléfono se atribuye a una caja local y lleva su método de pago confirmado para el nuevo panel V12 de Windows, sin exportaciones JSON.

## Cambios web (opcionales y compatibles)
- Botón **Asignar caja a este teléfono** (CAJA_01, CAJA_02, etc.), guardado en localStorage por navegador/PWA.
- Añade `saleMeta` opcional (caja/método confirmado) solo al POST normal de impresión. NO cambia importes, contenidos de impresión, WhatsApp, SIFO, escáner ni carrito.
- Ante respuesta `recorded:false`, el teléfono advierte que Windows aceptó el trabajo pero no se guardó en el panel.
- La reimpresión queda con su comportamiento habitual y no se registra como nueva venta.

## Requisito antes de fusionar
Instalar y probar el paquete Windows **NAVARRO_CAJAS_AUTO_V12** sobre la versión V5 exacta del puente. El instalador valida SHA256, respalda, y puede restaurar el puente si falla. El panel V12 lee automáticamente `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NAVARRO360_PRINT\cajas_auto_v1.jsonl` cada cinco segundos y evita duplicar IDs.

## Límites
Registra solo trabajos aceptados en cola Windows, no WhatsApp/SIFO ni pagos bancarios reales. El código de caja es configurado por el teléfono, no autentica empleados. **Este PR se deja en borrador para evitar cambios en la web publicada antes de revisar la instalación y prueba real en Windows.**

Este PR pone orden en el repositorio y añade la función que faltaba para cumplir la idea original de la app: **eliminar fotos duplicadas**.

### 1. Consolidación de ramas
`experiment/crop-orb-ransac` ya contenía `develop` y todas las ramas `feature/*` y `fix/*`. Se une con `main`. El único conflicto estaba en el workflow manual: se conserva el selector de rama de `main`, ahora con `main` por defecto.

Cuando se fusione, `main` tendrá todo el trabajo y se podrán cerrar el PR #7 y las ramas antiguas.

### 2. Estabilización
- Se añade `icons/icon.png`. Sin él, `tauri::generate_context!()` fallaba fuera del CI.
- Se eliminan las advertencias de compilación.
- Se añade `package-lock.json` al repositorio.

### 3. Limpieza de duplicados (`cleanup.rs` + `DuplicateCleanup.tsx`)
- En cada grupo la app sugiere qué copia conservar: evita nombres tipo `(1)` o `copia` y carpetas Descargas/WhatsApp. El usuario puede cambiar la elección o excluir el grupo.
- Antes de mover nada pide confirmación explícita.
- Justo antes de actuar vuelve a comparar byte a byte con la copia conservada. Además comprueba que el archivo esté dentro de la biblioteca, que no sea un enlace y que no sea la copia conservada.
- Las copias van a la **Papelera del sistema** (crate `trash`). Nunca se borra nada definitivamente.
- Cada operación queda registrada en SQLite, fuera de la biblioteca, con el BLAKE3 del archivo. La pantalla muestra el historial con los botones **Deshacer** y **Restaurar**; al restaurar se verifica que el contenido coincide con el registrado.

## Pruebas
- `cargo test`: 19 pasan y 1 se omite (necesita las 65 fotos de prueba). Incluye una prueba de integración nueva que envía un archivo real a la Papelera (freedesktop, en Linux), lo restaura y compara el contenido.
- `tsc --noEmit` y `npm run build`: sin errores.
- La pantalla se revisó en un navegador con datos simulados.
- **Pendiente:** probar en Windows real. La restauración usa la Papelera de reciclaje de Windows y en este entorno solo se pudo probar en Linux.
